author: Igor Alexeev
title: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
original_content: For more than half a century, the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum (Lăng Chủ tịch Hồ Chí Minh) has been located in the Ba Dinh Square, where Ho Chi Minh, the first president of the Democratic Republic of Vietnam and founder of the National Liberation Front of South Vietnam, proclaimed the independence of Vietnam on September 2, 1945. The Mausoleum is a well-known attraction in Vietnam, including to numerous tourists. Visitor access to the mausoleum is open from 9:00, but I haven't managed to visit the mausoleum in my two visits to Hanoi. Evidently, I will have to come again. Ah, maybe not even once...
drawbacks: Couldn't visit the mausoleum in my two visits to Hanoi

author: Russ Lacuata
title: Historic and Cultural site
original_content: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is a powerful historical and cultural site that offers visitors a deeper understanding of Vietnam's heritage. I would highly recommend it to anyone interested in history, politics, or Vietnamese culture.  Features a well-maintained grounds, cultural importance, organized visitor experience. Consider long queues and strict visitor regulations.

author: Patty B
title: Worth Seeing
original_content: We chose this as part of our private tour.  Our driver picked us up early and advised we should do this first as it gets extremely busy.  He mentioned waiting in a queue for hours at times to get in.  We took his advice and were early enough to not have a wait.  The walk up to the mausoleum was far.  I just couldn’t imagine a long wait to do this when I saw how far it actually was.  We saw quite a few military members outside as well as in the mausoleum, they were quite intimidating looking.  Our guide told us to just walk quietly and respectfully past the glass enclosed sarcophagus to view his body.  As we were doing that I reached up to fix the Bobbie pin in my hair and it fell out.  I just kept walking, it was my only Bobbie pin, but I couldn’t risk even reaching down for it on the floor.  When we got outside a man from the group walking in front of us was being detained by one of the members of the military.  They took him away somewhere leaving the other members of his group standing there.  It was a little scary to witness that!   I knew then that I made the right decision to leave my only Bobbie pin behind.  We continued on with our tour to the other sights.

author: Andrea L
title: Interesting but not unmissable.
original_content: We visited the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum complex without going in to see the body. If you want to do it, organize your morning well because the mausoleum opens very early, at 7:30, but it also closes just as early, at 11:30.Access to the complex is free, but pay attention to your clothing: pants or skirts above the knee and tank tops should be avoided. Outside you will still find vendors selling sarongs: we bought one for 150,000 VND. For men, it seemed to us that there was a little less strictness, but it is still better to show up in appropriate attire.Inside the large complex, in addition to the mausoleum, you can visit the museum and the residences associated with Ho Chi Minh, including the famous stilt house. Be careful, however, because the various attractions have rather strict and not always continuous hours: it is best to check them beforehand to avoid finding something closed.Naturally, the classic photo in front of the imposing Mausoleum, with the large square that surrounds it, is a must.One last piece of advice, essential if you go in the summer: bring plenty of water. The heat and humidity can be really intense and the complex is very large. There are also some air-conditioned spaces where you can stop for a few minutes and recover from the heat!An interesting visit, especially to understand the historical and symbolic importance that Ho Chi Minh continues to have for Vietnam, but organize your schedule and clothing well before you go.
extracted_spaces: residences associated with Ho Chi Minh
drawbacks: various attractions have rather strict and not always continuous hours
heat and humidity can be really intense
highlights: interesting visit to understand the historical and symbolic importance that Ho Chi Minh continues to have for Vietnam
practical_tips: check the hours of the various attractions beforehand

author: Jean-Emmanuel R
title: Monument to the glory of Ho Chi Minh
original_content: Closed during our visit. Nevertheless, the monument is well highlighted on a huge square and surrounded by pretty flowers.Several other must-see attractions in Hanoi (including the One Pillar Pagoda and the Ho Chi Minh Museum) are located on the site.

author: Ezra L
title: Interesting stop, but not a must-see
original_content: I visited the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum on a hot morning and it was an okay experience overall. The security line was pretty organized, and I liked walking through the grounds a bit before going in. The marble building is impressive in its own way, and the area feels very formal and quiet compared with the rest of Hanoi. That said, the visit itself was very short, and once you’re inside there’s not much to take in. It felt more like something you do because you’re in Hanoi, not because it’s especially memorable. Worth seeing once, but I wouldn’t go out of my way for it.
drawbacks: felt more like something you do because you're in Hanoi
highlights: walking through the grounds a bit before going in

author: Tai L
title: Worth the visit, just go early
original_content: I visited the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum on a hot morning and it was one of those Hanoi stops that feels very different from the rest of the city. The grounds were calm and a bit formal, with guards everywhere and a long line of people moving pretty quietly through. Inside, it was very controlled and over quickly, but it did feel meaningful. I also liked walking around the surrounding complex and seeing the uniforms, the tidy gardens, and the big open square. My only real gripe was the strict rules and the wait, so wear something respectful and come early. Still, I’d recommend it if you want a bit of history while in Hanoi.
extracted_times: long line of people moving pretty quietly through

author: Travel Girl GR
title: It takes patience
original_content: Great trouble until you get into the mausoleum.The tail is huge so go very early when it opens.Remember that Monday is closed as well as three months from September until November that goes for maintenance in Russia.Be careful not to wear short pants and amane t-shirts, carry a scarf with you.You go through control and the water is banned.Backpacks are not allowed so lock them in closets after check.The tail is long but walking fast, it will take an hour to get in.Inside the mausoleum photos are prohibited and you just make a quick passage.

author: Kandis Post
title: A moving visit, but plan ahead
original_content: I’m glad I went, but it’s definitely a place to plan for. The area around the mausoleum is very orderly and the whole experience feels solemn, not touristy. I went early and still had to deal with a bit of a line, plus the security rules are strict, so wear proper clothes and leave bags light. Inside, it was quiet and a little surreal seeing Ho Chi Minh preserved like that. The square outside is worth a walk too, especially in the morning when it’s cooler. My only gripe is that it can feel a bit rushed, and if you’re not into historical sites, it may not blow you away. Still, I’d recommend it.
drawbacks: may not blow you away if you're not into historical sites
highlights: quiet and surreal seeing Ho Chi Minh preserved
practical_tips: visit in the morning when it's cooler

author: Roy Norvell
title: Worth visiting, but go early and expect rules
original_content: I’m glad I went, even though the experience was a bit more formal than I expected. The whole area felt very quiet and disciplined, with the guards, the big open square, and the line moving pretty slowly. Inside, it was actually more moving than I thought it would be, but you don’t get much time and there are a lot of rules, so it can feel a little rushed. I’d recommend going early because the heat and crowds build up fast. Also, dress modestly or you may have a problem at the entrance. Not my favorite stop in Hanoi, but definitely worth seeing once if you’re in the city.
drawbacks: a bit more formal than I expected
heat and crowds build up fast

author: Bandya Mama
title: Bandya Mama - The surrounding area forms a harmonious ensemble.
original_content: Visiting Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum again in February 2026, I was struck by how powerful the place remains no matter how many times one has seen it before. The architecture is simple yet majestic, built with clean lines and solid stone that express strength, dignity, and permanence. Standing in the vast space of Ba Dinh Square, I felt the same emotion generations of Vietnamese have felt—a quiet pride mixed with gratitude for the history that unfolded here.

author: dang d
title: Worth the visit, but plan for the queues
original_content: I’m glad I went, even though it was a bit more of a process than I expected. The whole area feels very formal and peaceful, and seeing the mausoleum up close gave me a real sense of the place’s importance in Vietnamese history. I liked walking through the grounds in the early morning before it got too hot, and the security checks were quick enough. That said, the lines can get long and the rules are strict, so be ready for that. It’s not really a leisurely stop, but it’s definitely worth seeing once if you’re in Hanoi.
highlights: seeing the mausoleum up close gave me a real sense of the place's importance in Vietnamese history
practical_tips: be ready for the lines and strict rules

author: Awilda R
title: Interesting visit, but a bit underwhelming
original_content: I went to the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum expecting something really moving, but it ended up being kind of mixed for me. The building is impressive from the outside, and the whole area feels very controlled and orderly. I did like seeing the guards and the strict atmosphere, and the nearby grounds were peaceful in the morning. But the visit itself felt rushed, and the no-photos, no-standing-around rules made it hard to really take it in. It was also pretty crowded, so I spent more time waiting than actually looking. Glad I went, but honestly it wasn’t the most memorable stop in Hanoi.

author: Emmie R
title: Respectful site, but the visit felt rushed
original_content: I was glad I went once, but honestly the experience was a bit disappointing. The mausoleum itself is impressive from the outside and the grounds feel very calm and respectful, which I appreciated. But the whole visit was more hassle than it needed to be. The line moved slowly, there wasn’t much clear explanation in English, and the security rules felt confusing if it was your first time there. It was hot, there wasn’t much shade, and the visit inside felt very quick and impersonal. A few more signs, better crowd control, and some basic context would make a big difference. Still, seeing the place in person was memorable.
highlights: grounds feel very calm and respectful
seeing the place in person was memorable

author: Ha Thanh T
title: Long wait, barely saw anything
original_content: I left pretty disappointed. We came early in the morning, stood in a long line in the heat, and then found out the mausoleum was closed that day. Nobody really explained it until we were already there, so it felt like a wasted trip across town. Even around the grounds, everything was super strict and rushed by guards, and you only get a quick look from far away. I was expecting a meaningful visit, but instead it was mostly waiting, shuffling, and being told where not to go. Maybe worth it if your timing is perfect, but for us it was a frustrating experience.

author: Necole B
title: Long wait for a closed mausoleum
original_content: I was really disappointed with this stop. I got there early, stood in a long line in the heat, and then found out the mausoleum wasn’t open to visitors that day. The security check also took forever, so by the time we realized it was closed, we’d already wasted nearly an hour. The square itself is impressive, but that didn’t make up for the fact that we couldn’t actually see the mausoleum. I wish the opening schedule had been clearer online or posted more prominently at the entrance. It felt like a lot of effort for very little payoff.
drawbacks: mausoleum wasn’t open to visitors that day
practical_tips: check opening schedule online or posted at entrance

author: Sacha B
title: Worth a look, but not a highlight

The mausoleum itself is very solemn and the grounds are well kept, with neat lawns and guards everywhere. It was hot and humid when I went, and the silence made it feel heavier. drawbacks: whole visit felt a bit rushed

author: Marc B
title: Interesting
original_content: Being there early in the day is the message otherwise you have long waits. Ho Chi Minh has been laid out here in a glass coffin since his death in 1969.

author: David L
title: Huge mausoleum
original_content: This mausoleum is a huge monument in central Hanoi, built in honor of the revolutionary leader, considered the father of Vietnam.  The mausoleum is one of the must-see places in Vietnam.  Recommended.

author: 845daljinders

author: roberto p
title: To see

It lasts about 20 minutes and is a nice ceremonial that compensates if you did not choose to visit the mausoleum that is open from 0900 to 1100.The ceremony is outdoors and is free

author: Gate88
title: Very moving experience!

author: Cruiser14548402596
title: President Ho Chi Minh – A place where elite and dignity converge
original_content: President Ho Chi Minh Avenue, in Hanoi is a sacred architectural work, which holds the monument of Bác Ho, the highest respected symbol of the Vietnamese nation. Opened in 1973 and completed in 1975, it is located in the historic Ba Ling Square, distinguished by its solid architecture, sanctuary and green spaces. The Lan Bác is not only a distinct architectural work but also a sacred symbol, where the people of the whole country and international visitors show their affection for the great leader. This is the place where an important historical mark was recorded, where I once read the Declaration of Independence.
highlights: highest respected symbol of the Vietnamese nation
distinct architectural work and sacred symbol

author: Jeremy C

author: DRBAUKE

author: Richard T

Only about a 5 minute ceremony.Also worth soaking up the atmosphere in the parade square.The mausoleum itself is very large and impressive and is a huge symbol for the Vietnamese.It is free to enter, but you have to go through security to get into the immediate square which causes delays at busy times.

author: Murton68

author: HamitGunesli

author: Alexis P
title: An essential but highly structured visit
original_content: There is no doubt that Ho Chi Minh’s Mausoleum is a major national monument in Vietnam. That said, I would like to highlight a few practical points about the procedure and share some helpful warnings.If you are dropped off at the main square in front of the building, be aware that the entrance is actually located at the back. We had to walk all the way around the mausoleum, which took about ten minutes.Security is strict. You are not allowed to bring water inside and will be required to dispose of it at the entrance. Visitors are also expected to dress respectfully, with shoulders and knees covered. Interestingly, some men wearing shorts were permitted to enter, while women with uncovered shoulders were not.Cameras must be placed in provided bags and left at a counter before entering. They are returned after you exit the main chamber, though there may be a short wait.Inside, you are given only a brief moment — around 15 to 20 seconds — to view Ho Chi Minh’s preserved body before being guided onward.Overall, this is an essential visit when in Hanoi, as it represents a central pillar of modern Vietnamese history. However, I found certain aspects of the procedure somewhat lacking in clarity and consistency.
drawbacks: procedure somewhat lacking in clarity and consistency
highlights: represent a central pillar of modern Vietnamese history
practical_tips: be aware that the entrance is actually located at the back
cameras must be placed in provided bags and left at a counter before entering

author: Talant2007
title: Ho Chi Minh City Mausoleum
original_content: The mausoleum building was built in 1975 for Vietnamese statesman and founder of the Communist Party of Vietnam Ho Chi Minh (1890 - 1969). Security on the approach to the mausoleum is very serious :)
drawbacks: Security on the approach to the mausoleum is very serious

author: Flyingred
title: An insight into Vietnamese history and culture
original_content: For the local population, Ho Chi Minh is a much-revered hero, who is held in high regard. We decided that as we were in Hanoi, we should go to experience the visit.. We arrived around 8am and the queue was quite short. It's an interesting experience, following the route through the square to the entrance of the mausoleum, passing the military personnel who are on guard duty. Entering the inner chamber and seeing his embalmed body was a unique moment that was powerful.The pedestrian route takes visitors past the Ho Chi Minh museum and the presidential palace, which has a collection of the former president's possessions. Entry is chargeable and as we didn't have any Vietnamese currency, we missed out on these.As we left the complex, many coaches with school parties were arriving (around 9 am) so my suggestion is to plan a visit before the buses of children arrive. The route to the mausoleum is covered so there is adequate shelter from the sun or rain.We used Google maps for the walking route. It shows a direct route that doesn't take into account the military checkpoints and guards, so we had to walk around the block to reach the visitor entrance.
drawbacks: Buses of children arrive around 9 am
highlights: Unique moment seeing Ho Chi Minh's embalmed body
Interesting experience following the route through the square

author: Steve_Grant1
title: A must see whilst in the city
original_content: This is a must see whilst you are in the city. Its not just about the Mausoleum but all the other historical sites around it. Be dressed correctly for the mausoleum and prepared to stand in a straight line to show your respect.

author: GlobetrotterMSK
title: Worth seeing
original_content: The tomb itself did not impress me very much, as I have seen Lenin's mausoleum and its creepy contents in Moscow before. I found the area of the memorial quite interesting. The official residence of Ho Chi Minh (originally built for the French governor of the colony of French Indochina) and its purpose-built buildings and other facilities are clearly worth a visit. Especially if you hire an expert guide who can provide additional information about the history of the museum.
extracted_spaces: the official residence of Ho Chi Minh
drawbacks: The tomb itself did not impress me very much

author: Tripad86
title: Surprisingly emotional
original_content: I felt surprisingly emotional when visiting the mausoleum, though I have no connection at all with Vietnam. The man is so revered. We arrived at 8 am,  with only a short queue to get through security.  We didn’t have any bags with us, which simplified things. The Google maps walking directions from our hotel were very inaccurate - you cannot enter where it said. The entrance is on the west side of the site and you cannot walk across the huge area to the east of the building. A long way round! We wanted to visit the palace and the museum too but these are cash only places and we had none. The huge parties of school children getting off coaches  were entertaining as they all wanted to practise their English and say hello. Definitely a worthwhile visit. When we left the site at just after nine the queues were enormous.
drawbacks: Google maps walking directions were inaccurate
Long way round to the east of the building
practical_tips: Be prepared for cash only places

author: FyingKiwi
title: Enlightening
original_content: A solemn and reverential experience which was enhanced through the tour guides descriptions of Ho Chi Minhs own philosophies. Much of what is portrayed of Ho Chi Minh in the western culture is contrary to what appears to be the more accurate portrayal of his life, reinforced by the displays of his work and wishes. Ho Chi Minh is described much more as a humble person with a passion for serving the people, rather than as one intent on radicalising the population against capitalism.What was learned by a visit here was that there was so much more to the social history of Vietnam than a vying for control, as is portrayed in the West.
extracted_spaces: displays of his work and wishes
highlights: humble person with a passion for serving the people

author: iPodsolnuh

The line moves pretty fast, everything is organized wisely. Prohibited items may be deposited in the storage room.

author: JuanMarco31
title: It's worth looking at - Changing the guard every hour.
original_content: In the wake of the visit to the temple of literature we went to the park where is the imposing mausoleum of Ho Chi Minh. The gardens are perfectly maintained by a myriad of women and one can see pretty buildings behind the esplanade facing the mausoleum , If you have some time , the two guards who are stationary under the entrance structure will be replaced , interesting sight to watch .
drawbacks: The two guards who are stationary under the entrance structure will be replaced

author: Silke105
title: Rare place of interest
original_content: The entrance with security check and backpack drop-off is located in the SW corner of the widely cordoned off area. Those who step out of the grave incorrectly are allowed to circle the outside of the complex. We were there on Saturday and there were many school classes and other groups of locals on site.After passing the security checkpoint (as at the airport :)) we went to the Mausoleum in a clearly regulated manner. Due to the organizationally short stay in the Mausoleum, the visit was completed after 45 minutes. Admission was free for everyone. Admission to the presidential palace grounds is 40,000 dong for foreigners. We weren't there, though.Overall, an interesting experience.
drawbacks: organizationally short stay in the Mausoleum

author: Chanda Pit
title: Peaceful Plaza at Ho Chi Minh’s Mausoleum
original_content: Standing at the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum felt truly special—the enormous plaza in front was a breath of fresh air! After days of navigating Vietnam’s bustling streets, it was such a joy to finally walk peacefully, carefree and surrounded by open space, with no cars in sight. Pure serenity in the heart of Hanoi!

author: Travel@1964
title: This visit provides the opportunity for us all to explore our own personal experiences and perspectives on our lives
original_content: This is a rare opportunity to visit idealistic vision of influences of an era of Vietnamese Struggles …  it’s very glimpse into history.

author: jw6969
title: Catch the change of guard
original_content: We managed to get there just before 12 noon. Purelly by fluke, at that time there is a very theatrical changing of the guard. Goose stepping and so on. It was really fascinating. The mausoleum itself was distinctly Soviet in appearance - bland and sombre, but it was all well worth seeing.

author: possagol
title: Vietnamese history
original_content: The mausoleum contains the embalmed body of ho chi Minh. It is an important place for Vietnamese. In the mausoleum it is not possible to take pictures and you visit it in line without being able to stop. We saw it early in the morning because then it is full of people.  Check the timetable carefully because it is not always open. Monday and Friday closed on Tuesday from 8 to 16.30 the other days only from 8 to 11.30 women covered and men with pants at least below the knees at the back of the mausoleum the buildings and accommodations used by ho chi Minh with its cars
extracted_spaces: Buildings and accommodations used by Ho Chi Minh
practical_tips: Dress modestly (women covered, men with pants below the knees)

author: KaG
title: A long wait in line....but worth the visit
original_content: The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum provides a sense of the Vietnamese admiration for this former leader, who is much admired by many Vietnamese.  It also provides an enhanced understanding of the culture and country's history.
highlights: sense of the Vietnamese admiration for this former leader
enhanced understanding of the culture and country's history

author: nicodenheijer
title: Nice but unfriendly security
original_content: Entire property beautiful to see. But the security on the ground is not exactly friendly. Jr bag also goes through the xray again.  Road bandage stuff. Bit of a charade.
drawbacks: Security on the ground is not exactly friendly
Jr bag also goes through the xray again
practical_tips: Go early to avoid security issues

author: Alex J
title: Great if you are a history buff !
original_content: Unless you are a history buff like me, you might find this a bit underwhelming.  I grew up during the Vietnam War, and he was the great hero of my childhood, so for me it was an emotional experience, BUT....for the average person who doesn't care much for history, this may not be all that good.  The queues are long, and it could be quite tiring if it is a hot day.  The buildings are impressive, especially the main building.  Also, Ho's embalmed body looks very very lifelike.  There are other buildings on the premises (Ho's residence during the war, etc....)  We went because it was part of our itinerary, we were on a conducted group tour. But if you are on your own, you might give this a miss if you are pressed for time, and if you are NOT a history buff.
drawbacks: Tiring if it is a hot day
highlights: Ho's embalmed body looks very lifelike

author: Glyn R
title: Informative and interesting
original_content: The site is impressive and the museum very interesting. The mausoleum was closed, but probably would not have qued anyway. Ho Chi Minhs stilt house worth a visit.
highlights: Ho Chi Minhs stilt house worth a visit
practical_tips: probably would not have qued anyway

author: Michel10000
title: Must see in Hanoi
original_content: Must see in Hanoi, because Ho Chi Minh has been so important for the origin and independence of Vietnam. Impressive that he's laid out there and looks like it. Beautiful Presential Palace and nice to see where he really lived and worked in the large adjoining garden.

author: Myca E
title: A moment of quiet respect in the heart of Hanoi
original_content: We visited the mausoleum early morning—solemn, orderly, and deeply moving. Walking past Uncle Ho in silence with our friends made us reflect on Vietnam’s history in a way no textbook ever could. A must-see, done with reverence.

author: Beppe Marini
title: Very interesting: to see
original_content: Monument of historical significance especially for the Vietnamese people, I would say not to be missed for a visit to Hanoi. An impressive marble building, it houses the remains of Ho Chi Minh City that can be visited in silence and in continuous procession. You can't take pictures. It is also worth admiring the imposing spaces around the mausoleum
highlights: houses the remains of Ho Chi Minh City

author: WHWhite
title: A must-see if interested in Vietnam's history
original_content: Free to enter. There is quite a long wait to get in. Staff impose a lengthy 'pause' so that a long queue builds up before letting people in, but at least you wait out of the sun. Cameras need to be handed in and reclaimed afterwards. You are kept moving as you go past the body, so you are through in a minute or two. The corpse is rather shiny / waxen in appearance, rather like Lenin as I recall seeing him in Moscow when I went there in my youth – similar techniques at work I suppose.
drawbacks: lengthy 'pause' so that a long queue builds up
highlights: you wait out of the sun
you are through in a minute or two

author: Frederique W
title: A peaceful and meaningful family visit
original_content: The grand architecture and serene gardens left a deep impression, especially on our children. Though solemn, it felt important to witness this piece of history. Well-organized and peaceful—a meaningful stop in Hanoi.

author: bhattesd
title: Must visit place
original_content: Visiting the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum Complex was a very moving experience. The place is beautifully maintained, and the atmosphere is solemn and respectful. It gave me a deep insight into Vietnam’s history and its beloved leader.

author: Xem Số Mệnh
title: Why No Trip to Vietnam is Complete Without Visiting Ho Chi Minh’s Mausoleum
original_content: A trip to Vietnam would be incomplete without visiting President Ho Chi Minh’s Mausoleum. This is where the body of a national hero, admired worldwide, is preserved. It is also the place where nearly every visiting head of state pays their respects.
highlights: preserved body of a national hero
place where nearly every visiting head of state pays their respects

author: TheLush101
title: Visiting Uncle Ho
original_content: Our tour of Vietnam included a visit to see Uncle Ho. We'd already been told that you needed to dress appropriately - in a similar way to visiting any religious site really - and to have covered shoulders and trousers on (not shorts). At the ticket entrance, there was security like at an airport. You then queue under walkways with a roof that keep the sun off. You then enter the main square and have a view of the outside of the Mausoleum. Again, we had to queue, but it does move as they keep people flowing through the complex. It's fairly small, you walk in and go up the steps - there are guards and cameras on the stairs. You then shuffle past Ho Chi Minh and work your way back out the other side - you're only in there 1-2 minutes max. I tried to slow down my walk a little bit and the guard politely said "please keep walking" so just bear in mind that they're always watching you! I'd already visit Lenin's Mausoleum in Red Square so had experienced something very similar. Our guide explained that it had been the same lab that had prepared Uncle Ho. This mausoleum and experience isn't on the same scale as the Russian one, but I think it's still important to see, and even if you don't enjoy it / think much of it, when you look around at what it means to the Vietnamese who will be visiting when you are, that says something.

author: Eli
title: A historical mausoleum in Hanoi.
original_content: A historical mausoleum in Hanoi. Quite solemn and has that classic monumental vibe. Learning more about its backstory was really interesting and surprising. If you’re traveling solo or on your own, you can use the Travellens AI app to explore it deeper.
practical_tips: use the Travellens AI app to explore it deeper

author: salvatore1964
title: Typical mausoleum of totalitarian regimes
original_content: When you enter the (vast) area of the Mausoleum, you must abide by a set of rules that would be indigestible in most of our maximum security prisons.For heaven's sake, maximum compared to Ho Chi Ming: but if I enter the mausoleum where the body is exposed! If instead I visit the gardens, the pond, the wooden house where it turned off, etc. (with humidity at 90% and a perceived temperature of 45 degrees centigrade), someone wants to explain why I have to wear long pants?!?Moreover, you can not approach the sidewalk leading to the stairs of the mausoleum (you are first reprimanded and then rejected by the unfriendly military of Giardia), just as you can not smoke in the gardens: in short, the classic place where you observe the most rigorous "personality cult" typical of totalitarian regimes.Personally, visiting Hanoi again, I would not return.
practical_tips: Be prepared for humidity and heat

author: AlexandraFlo
title: Worth it
original_content: Arrived at around 8am on a Tuesday, very busy. We were ushered into holding rooms which is unsure if that usually happens. After around an hours wait it was explained that there was a diplomat visiting and we couldn’t enter, thankfully that didn’t take too long and we were allowed through. Very happy we waited for the experience. After going inside there is an entry to pay around £1 to walk around the garden and visit his house see artefacts, this was great. Also thoroughly enjoyed the art we bought at the end as shown in photos.
drawbacks: couldn't enter due to diplomat visiting
highlights: very happy we waited for the experience
great to walk around the garden and visit his house

author: lilybt
title: View appearance only
original_content: This mausoleum houses the remains of Ho Chi Minh, the Founding Father, who was given a permanent preservation measure. The inside of the mausoleum is cumbersome to secure and the entrance time is quite short, which limits the sightseeing of the surrounding facilities, so we only saw the exterior.

author: Ileniasu
title: If you like history, a must.
original_content: It is not permitted to enter the esplanade with lighters (they must be picked up at the entrance without returning them) and you cannot enter with bare shoulders. No straps or you have to cover them with a scarf.If you forget them at the entrance, there are vendors who sell them.
practical_tips: Buy straps from vendors if forgotten

author: aurelieBou
title: Beautiful from the outside
original_content: We couldn't get in because we were in shorts. So let me say for the ladies consider taking a paraao so you can enter this place.
drawbacks: couldn't get in because we were in shorts
practical_tips: consider taking a paraao so you can enter this place

author: Fenzholt
title: Ho Chi Minh Memorial – Insightful visit
original_content: We did a guided tour of the Ho Chi Minh Memorial and really enjoyed it. The guide gave a clear and interesting explanation of Ho Chi Minh’s life, beliefs, and his huge role in Vietnam’s independence. He’s still deeply respected by the people, seen as a symbol of unity and national pride.We also got to see his old stilt house, which was simple but full of meaning—it really reflected his modest lifestyle. The garden around it is beautiful, with a peaceful lake full of fish and shady trees. There were also two of his old Russian cars on display, which was a cool touch of history.Overall, a great learning experience. I recommend to book a guided tour, or rent a “guide headset” to get most out of your visit.There is a security check at the entrance, they mostly look for lighters and stuff like that.We were allowed to bring our own water bottles.Definitely worth visiting if you’re in Hanoi, and if it’s not too hot :-)
extracted_spaces: Ho Chi Minh's old stilt house
drawbacks: mostly look for lighters and stuff like that
highlights: clear and interesting explanation of Ho Chi Minh’s life
peaceful lake full of fish and shady trees
practical_tips: rent a “guide headset” to get most out of your visit

author: Sayers Houston
title: A somber and poignant visit
original_content: The solemnity and respect shown here are palpable. It was an important history lesson for our children and gave us a deeper understanding of Vietnam's reverence for its leader. A truly profound and memorable visit.
highlights: solemnity and respect shown here are palpable
important history lesson for our children
deeper understanding of Vietnam's reverence for its leader

author: Andrew S
title: Impressive and Solemn
original_content: It is worth the long line.  It is a source of rightful pride to the Vietnamese.  And, a stirring experience for non-locals.  I was thoroughly move.

author: Claire C
title: Mausoleum unexpectedly shut
original_content: Turned up two days in a row but uncle ho wasn’t taking visitors and the mausoleum was shut. You could view the building from the outside. It was on days advertised as open on the website and in the morning. Disappointing.
practical_tips: Check the website for accurate opening hours

author: Katrin K
title: Imposing
original_content: The premises can only be entered through a security check. But that was relatively quick. We could only look at the mausoleum from the outside, as it was closed. It is very imposing with guards in front of it and you get an impression of how much Ho Chi Minh is worshipped. Opposite is the presidential palace, both built in a socialist style.
drawbacks: could only look at the mausoleum from the outside
highlights: get an impression of how much Ho Chi Minh is worshipped

author: Adam K
title: Unexpected and spectacular.
original_content: We were very lucky as there were no queues when we arrived. We were ushered in by tall handsome white uniformed soldiers as though we were VIP dignitaries straight into the mausoleum. This was def one of the highlights of our Vietnamese trip.
highlights: one of the highlights of our Vietnamese trip

author: Laura B
title: Pay your respects
original_content: How many places in the world can you see a world leader in such a state of rest?  Come here wearing respectable clothing (smart casual, I'm looking at you), take off your hat, walk the hallways to his resting place, then gaze respectfully.  Then go out and go to the museum right next door for the right history in context.  Worth a visit.
highlights: See a world leader in a state of rest

author: BorntocruiseUK
title: Don’t forget to cover your shoulders and legs!!!
original_content: I have visited before and managed to get into the museum but because of the limited opening times it closed on this occasion.I wore a t shirt and shorts and was made to purchase a shawl to cover my shoulders before I was allowed into the open air area in front of the building. This area reminds me of a car park. I could totally understand if I was entering the building but to just walk in the area seemed very strict. Lots of people were turned away as they didn’t have the correct clothes on. So be warned. There was a guy selling them by the entrance.Would I recommend going mmmm yes to tick the box.
drawbacks: had to purchase a shawl to cover shoulders
people turned away for not having correct clothes

author: Mark H
title: Goood places
original_content: Gooood places. We would like to visit one more time. This is a place where we can see the Ho chi minh’s body and explore a lot of things about him
highlights: place where we can see the Ho chi minh's body
explore a lot of things about him

author: John C
title: A must when visiting Hanoi
original_content: A must if you are visiting Hanoi. Large queues (both local and foreigners), but well organised - the line is always moving! It is worth the wait.When there, visit the museum as well.Check times before going to ensure it is open when you plan to visit.
extracted_times: well organised - the line is always moving

author: oldmtravel
title: Impressive monument
original_content: The mausoleum is only open til 10 in the morning so get there early as it is a really busy place. Men and women need to be covered to the knee and shoulders covered to and they are strict  on this and that includes access to the house on stilts and the museum as they are all in the same complex there is an admission fee to the house it is only small so will need some money, it is a beautiful complex and the mausoleum is very impressive and over stated and a great tribute to the man that is held in such hi regard by the people of Vietnam

author: Alban F
title: Walking to ho chi min mausoleum. Don’t forget to cover your arms !
original_content: We arrived on n a Friday afternoon to find point the mausoleum was closed, which was a shame as we would have liked to have seen inside.

author: John P
title: An Essential Experience to Understand Vietnamese History
original_content: To begin understand the 2,000-year struggle for Vietnam to be independent from invaders and colonial powers, visit the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum.  Get there early but only during the late fall, winter, and early spring when the body laid to rest in a glass coffin is not in Moscow for continued restoration.  The vast and sterile setting, long lines of silent citizens, and eventual passing by his preserved body from head to foot to head and out is somber and respectful.  I have passed the body of Lenin in his Red Square Mausoleum and Mao in his Tian'anmen Square Mausoleum are memorials to be understood in order to understand each of their national histories.
practical_tips: visit during late fall, winter, and early spring

author: corinne_prevost
title: TO SEE
original_content: It's a mausoleum with reinforced guard. As with airports, you have to go under security gates. The thing to see is the changing of the guard. For the opening of the mausoleum it is not possible to take pictures and all electronic equipment is confiscated at the entrance. Behind it there is a small pagoda and a small temple. A short walk but especially not in full sun because there is no shade around the mausoleum. Hot stroke assured

author: Amy B
title: A Solemn and Memorable Experience
original_content: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum in Hanoi is the final resting place of an iconic leader and a very important part of Vietnam's history. When I visited, I found it to be a large, solemn space in Ba Dinh Square, and it was clear that respectful attire and silence are crucial here. There might be queues, but it's worth the wait. Inside, the atmosphere is quite dark and quiet, and seeing President Ho Chi Minh's body preserved in a glass case definitely creates a solemn and emotional feeling. The grounds are lovely, with gardens and monuments, and nearby you can find attractions like the Presidential Palace and One Pillar Pagoda. Overall, visiting the mausoleum provides a unique and meaningful experience.
highlights: President Ho Chi Minh's body preserved in a glass case

author: GreGFlores
title: Skip this site.
original_content: Nothing to see except the closed mausoleum and a large flag pole when we went there. Maybe if there is a nice ceremony or event then it will be worth going to. Visit the nearby temples instead.

author: Eiffel
title: Vibrant tribute to Uncle Ho
original_content: We took the time to visit the mausoleum that houses Ho Chi Minh’s remains. It was an opportunity to share a moment with the Vietnamese people. Young and old come to pay tribute to their national hero, waiting in endless queues, until the body, kept in a glass tomb, is sneaked past. This is a solemn moment, a page in the rich and terrible history of Vietnam is before us, and this moment is unique.A little advice for those who do not want to queue for an hour and a half, you can arrive a quarter of an hour before the closing of the site (11:00 on Sundays for us) and you can access the tomb without queuing or at least much shorter.
highlights: opportunity to share a moment with the Vietnamese people
practical_tips: arrive a quarter of an hour before the closing of the site
access the tomb without queuing or at least much shorter

author: Harirajan Varatharajan
title: Visiting ‘Uncle Ho’
original_content: Visiting the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum was a profound and humbling experience. The atmosphere was solemn and respectful as we joined the queue of visitors paying their respects to Vietnam’s beloved leader. The mausoleum’s imposing structure, set against Ba Đình Square, reflected the significance of Ho Chi Minh’s legacy. Inside, the silence and precision of the guards added to the sense of reverence. Walking through the surrounding gardens and nearby landmarks like the Presidential Palace made the visit even more meaningful. It’s a must-visit to understand Vietnam’s history and the deep respect its people have for “Uncle Ho.”

author: rossbrownNottingham
title: Don't let the queue put you off.
original_content: We arrived at the Mausoleum at 9.06 am on a Wednesday. There was already a big queue there, but it was moving pretty quickly, we got through security, we had our water bottle confiscated which was fine, however, they did seem to be letting people through with mobile phones and smallish handbags. Long trousers, skirts and covered shoulders were acceptable but no headwear, we saw a woman get into trouble for having sunglasses perched on her head, the guard made her remove them.There were lines of Vietnamese primary school children also queuing to get into the mausoleum, their behaviour was impeccable, they had clearly been told how important this visit was by their teachers and parent helpers.Its very interesting to see the number of the military personnel around the mausoleum, a reminder that Vietnam is a communist country and that Ho Chi Minh is regarded as a great leader.We saw Ho Chi Minh lying in state and were out by 9.36 am, so a very slick operation, no one is allowed to stop. Well worth it to get a glimpse of another facet to life in Vietnam.
highlights: impeccable behaviour of Vietnamese primary school children
interesting to see the number of military personnel
well worth it to get a glimpse of another facet to life in Vietnam
practical_tips: dress codes: long trousers, skirts, covered shoulders, no headwear

author: mion369
title: De Grote Leider
original_content: Thousands of people are lining up, but actually it's making reasonable progress. We sat down for 55 minutes, including a visit to the grave. Everything is done with military precision, anyone who steps out of line is immediately reprimanded. Beautiful terrain, interesting information about life and work of Ho Chi Minh.
drawbacks: Steps out of line is immediately reprimanded
highlights: Interesting information about life and work of Ho Chi Minh
practical_tips: Go early to avoid long lines

author: Alison Townsend
title: Respectful
original_content: Very slick respectful experience, quite overwhelming.  So glad we did this tour/visit and into the gardens and the Stilted house.  Years on and Ho Chi Min is still so well regarded...

author: GIZMOKI
title: Unfortunately, it was Monday and I couldn't get in.
original_content: Unfortunately, it was Monday and we couldn't get inside, but we couldn't see the changing of the guard. There is a bit of distance from the old town, so I took a grab car.
drawbacks: couldn't see the changing of the guard

author: Ian R
title: Worth a visit
original_content: Free to enter (museum is a paid for visit), most of the site seemed to be closed.That said the mausoleum was impressive and the gardens nice.
drawbacks: most of the site seemed to be closed
practical_tips: check if site is fully open before visiting

author: MrDream688
title: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
original_content: The scenery is truly impressive and solemn. The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is a must-visit when in Hanoi. The surrounding area is well-maintained, creating a peaceful and sacred atmosphere. Visitors are very orderly, showing deep respect for the great leader. The flag-raising ceremony in the morning and the flag-lowering ceremony in the evening are particularly moving experiences. If you love history and want to learn more about Vietnam, this is definitely a place worth visiting!"
practical_tips: visit in the morning or evening for the ceremonies

author: vidijo
title: Not wanted by the deceased person himself.
original_content: For the northern Vietnamese a place of pilgrimage and a very spacious site where these people come to honor their idol. In order to fully understand this, you should read through the history of Vietnam. The building is 21.6 meters high and has a length of over 41 meters. Ho's dying wish was to be cremated has not been fulfilled. Hồ wanted his ashes to be spread throughout Vietnam. Very strict rules are set here. No photography or filming is allowed. There are also rules on clothing and behavior. For example, the legs should be covered, in both men and women. There is also a change of guard, less spectacular than in Greece, for example.
drawbacks: Strict rules on clothing and behavior
Rules on photography and filming not clearly stated
practical_tips: Read through the history of Vietnam to understand the significance
Be aware of strict rules on clothing and behavior

author: alessandro s
title: Even not.
original_content: Undoubtedly very important for the Vietnamese for the fundamental role of Ho Chi Minh in the history of the country.That said, to visit the interior you have to queue for over an hour (if there is unpleasant sun), airport style checks, absolute prohibition of photographs with a camera deposited at the entrance.The visit is a line up to Ho Chi Minh's embalmed body inside an imposing building but of zero artistic value.In my opinion, apart from being able to say you have been there, in the economy of travel it is better to spend a couple of hours more in Hanoi's old quarter, what is worth seeing of the Mausoleum can be seen from the street outside in front of the Parliament
practical_tips: spend a couple of hours more in Hanoi's old quarter

author: Sue M
title: Crowded and Tight Security
original_content: We came in the afternoon so no chance of going into the mausoleum, the complex is vast and security is tight.  A tourist tried to come into the complex with a knife through security, the military guards stopped everyone from coming in for a period of time until they were satisfied that no one else was involved.  We did go visit the Ho Chi Minh Memorial Complex to see Uncle Ho's stilt house and how simply he lived.
drawbacks: No chance of going into the mausoleum
practical_tips: Visit in the morning to avoid security checks

author: Jey
title: Worthwhile but very strict
original_content: It was very special to see the body of Ho Chi Minh and I am glad to have gone to the mausoleum however the staff were extremely rude. Everyone seemed to dislike tourists and had no interest in helping. This could be because perhaps they are unable to speak English but I don’t think that should stop them being kind. We were told you walk in two single filed lines and told not to walk too fast and not to step out of line but not really given more direction on where to go and then were yelled at for stepping the wrong way. You walk into the mausoleum and then around the body of Ho Chi Minh. You cannot stop you must keep walking and then back out again and there are guards everywhere. No photos and no talking. It was quite nice to be able to see something like this without people crowding around.You can walk around the grounds and see other information on Ho Chi Minh. I would recommend this but be aware, it is extremely strict and at the security screening many items may be taken off you and they are strict on dress code.
drawbacks: Dislike tourists and had no interest in helping
Strict security screening and dress code
highlights: Special to see the body of Ho Chi Minh
Nice to be able to see something like this without people crowding around
Can walk around the grounds and see other information on Ho Chi Minh
practical_tips: Be aware of the strict rules and security screening

author: Edward B
title: You need to allow alot of time
original_content: We had stayed overnight in Hanoi from Celebrity Solstice. We went to the Mausoleum but it was clear we were not going to have time to go through security and then the queue to see inside the Mausoleum and then get our transfer backWe walked around the outside and could see the Mausoleum and the Palace, which looked spectacular If you have more time than us then like us we will visit in future but allow the time to visit Next time we return then will be the first thing to do but you will need to queue early which we would not mind as we would have the time
drawbacks: queue to see inside the Mausoleum
not going to have time to go through security
highlights: saw the Mausoleum and the Palace

author: alessandra_biondi3
title: The great President Ho Chi Minh always lives in our lives
original_content: The Mausoleum is surrounded by 79 (in honor of his years) very long-lived Japanese palm trees that bloom every 15-20 years, stand the inscriptions praising the life of Ho Chi Minh forever in us and long life to the socialist republic of Vietnam.. the Mausoleum was built 4 years after his death in 1973 and finished in 1975, it is on the square overlooking the Ministry of Foreign Affairs office, Parliament, the Presidential Palace of the Party, all around there are bamboo plants. Ho Chi Minh was born 9.5.1890 to a Confucian and patriotic family, at 21 he left the country to move to France because he had to find his own path to save his country. He was a great leader revered by the people.
extracted_spaces: the Ministry of Foreign Affairs office
the Presidential Palace of the Party
highlights: the life of Ho Chi Minh

author: gfsc5
title: Imposing
original_content: We didn't enter the mausoleum as it was closed on the day we visited (Friday) which was ok as we mainly went to see the area and grab some photos.  It's an imposing building built up high and with lots of open area in front of including grassed and paved.
drawbacks: closed on the day we visited

author: OnAir38937315268
title: Good, Eclectic View of Uncle Ho
original_content: A Must See, the actual mausoleum, with the embalmed 'Uncle Ho' in it, has limited opening hours. It's located in a large complex of government buildings (Parliament, President's House, Ho Chi Minh's old house and more) so be prepared to walk around. Well kept, it provides a good view of Vietnamese history. Lots of security.

author: Thomas S
title: Focused Communism
original_content: Terrible. In the afterlife I think it was a total waste of time to see a dead dictator. This is communism at its worst. The soldiers there and the security guards are treating you like a criminal. The place is full of propaganda, and it was all just awful. How we had to stand in line and get crash orders. Have little sense for the whole experience. Steer away, read the bad comments.
drawbacks: The soldiers there and the security guards are treating you like a criminal.
The place is full of propaganda, and it was all just awful.
How we had to stand in line and get crash orders.

author: Shafinah J.
title: A Quiet Reflection of Vietnam’s History
original_content: Ever wanted to see a body that has passed on for more than 45 years? In Hanoi, you actually can. Believe it or not, the embalmed body of the much-revered Ho Chi Minh lies in a glass casket within his monumental tomb in the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, despite his wishes to be cremated and his ashes to be scattered in the North, Centre, and South of the country. Rules are strict in the Mausoleum though: no cameras, no bags, no talking, and no laughing. Oh, and take off your hat if you’re wearing one. Etiquette reads that it is rude (not to mention disrespectful) to wear hats indoors. A quick word of advice: do a check before visiting the Mausoleum. Apparently, Uncle Ho’s body gets packed off to Russia three months out of every year for major embalming maintenance. And wake up early too, because the last entry into this sacred Mausoleum is at 10.15am sharp daily.
highlights: See the embalmed body of Ho Chi Minh
Learn about the history and etiquette of the Mausoleum

author: Louise
title: Must See Be Patient!
original_content: If the experience didn’t feel like I was in North Korea this would be a 5 star attraction! If you’re in Hanoi this is a must but BE PREPARED! We have been to many religious sites and know about dressing modestly etc, my male partner was caught out for wearing shorts, we went across the road and got a pair of pants for about $5 AUD, no worries. We then got into the line with every other person local and tourists, to be screened by security more than the airports! Don’t bring any bottles of water or any big cameras, they will all be taken, cameras will be stored - to top it all off we get inside after the escapade of security and pants and see other people inside IN SHORTS!! As we go through the area we are marched in 2 straight lines for 40minutes! And might I mention no phones, photos or cameras - that’s fine totally respect it but honestly it was over the top and a double standard, tourists were being targeted and further only tourists have to pay. A small fee I know, but the negative attitude toward tourists put a slight damper on the whole thing! Nevertheless seeing the preserved body was amazing and such a feat, the communist influence throughout was very interesting to see and it was awesome to stand where many great political leaders have stood before! Would totally recommend but be prepared!

author: Maison Nhã
title: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
original_content: Visiting the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum in Hanoi was a deeply moving experience. Located in Ba Dinh Square, the site holds the embalmed body of President Ho Chi Minh, the leader who played a pivotal role in Vietnam's history. The atmosphere is solemn and respectful, with guards ensuring decorum.The mausoleum itself is an impressive structure, blending traditional Vietnamese elements with a modernist design. Inside, the atmosphere is quiet and reflective as visitors file through in silence to pay their respects. It’s remarkable how much care and effort goes into maintaining the site, reflecting the reverence Vietnamese people have for "Uncle Ho."I recommend going early in the morning to avoid long queues, especially during peak tourist seasons. Nearby attractions, like the Presidential Palace and Ho Chi Minh's Stilt House, add depth to the visit, offering insights into his simple and impactful life. Overall, it’s a must-visit landmark that encapsulates Vietnam’s modern history and enduring respect for its leader.
practical_tips: go early in the morning to avoid long queues

author: Passport38984184928
title: HA NOI: 8 Hours Tour Plan Recommendation
original_content: Here is a recommendation tour plan for 8 hours when you visit Ha Noi:13:00-13:30: Arriving to President Ho Chi Minh's mausoleum13:30-14:30: Visiting Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, Museum, and One Pillar Pagoda (note to dress politely and properly)14:30-15:30: Visiting the Temple of Literature15:30-17:00: Visiting Hoa Lo Prison17:00-18:00: Choosing to enjoy dinner with the dishes suggested by the tour18:00 - 19:15: Moving to watch the  Quintessence of Tonkin show19:15- 19:30: Buying tickets and check-in 19:30-20:45: Enjoying the Quintessence of Tonkin show20:45: End of schedule.I/ A few descriptions of the above locations:1. Ho Chi Minh's Mausoleum, located in Ba Dinh Square, Hanoi, is one of Vietnam's most important historical landmarks. It serves as the resting place of President Ho Chi Minh, the beloved leader who led the country to independence and unification. Constructed from 1973 to 1975, the mausoleum's architecture reflects the simplicity and solemnity of his spirit. Inside, President Ho Chi Minh's body is preserved in a special glass chamber, attracting millions of visitors annually. This site is not only a symbol of historical significance but also an educational space for future generations.2.The Ho Chi Minh Museum, located in Hanoi, is a grand tribute to the life and legacy of President Ho Chi Minh. Opened in 1990, the museum is designed to resemble a lotus, symbolizing purity and the revered leader's modesty. It houses a vast collection of artifacts, photographs, and documents that chronicle Ho Chi Minh's journey from his early life, revolutionary activities, to his leadership in Vietnam's struggle for independence. Through its exhibits, the museum offers visitors profound insights into the history of Vietnam and the enduring influence of Uncle Ho's ideals and vision for the nation.3. One Pillar Pagoda, located in Hanoi, is one of Vietnam's most iconic Buddhist temples. Built in 1049 during the Ly Dynasty, it stands on a single stone pillar, resembling a lotus blossom rising from a pond. The unique architecture symbolizes purity, akin to a lotus blooming in muddy water. Originally constructed to honor the bodhisattva Avalokiteshvara, the pagoda has become a symbol of Vietnam's rich cultural heritage. Despite being destroyed and rebuilt over the centuries, it remains a beloved landmark and a testament to the country's enduring spiritual traditions.4.The Temple of Literature - Quoc Tu Giam, in central Hanoi, is one of Vietnam's most significant historical and cultural sites. Built in 1070 during the Ly dynasty to honor Confucius, it became Vietnam's first university in 1076, training many talented individuals. This site symbolizes Vietnam's dedication to education and meritocracy. Its five distinct areas include Van Mieu Mon, Dai Trung Mon, Khue Van Cac, Bai Duong, and Hau Palace. A highlight is the 82 stone steles of doctors from the 15th to 18th centuries, recognized by UNESCO. Today, it's a venue for cultural and educational events and a place where students pray for exam success, showcasing Vietnam's long-standing respect for education.5.Hoa Lo Prison, centrally located in Hanoi, stands as a poignant symbol of Vietnam's history. Built by the French in 1896, this "Maison Centrale" initially held revolutionaries opposing colonial rule. Known as the "Hanoi Hilton" during the Vietnam War, it detained captured American pilots, including Senator John McCain. Despite its grim past, today it houses a historical museum displaying documents and artifacts from different eras. Attracting numerous visitors, the site highlights Vietnam's struggle and resilience, educating future generations about patriotism and the indomitable spirit of its people.6."The Quintessence of Tonkin" is a unique art program that authentically recreates the culture, history, and life of the Northern Delta region of Vietnam. Performed on an outdoor stage near Thay Pagoda, it attracts a wide audience. The program features a large water stage blending with nature, enhanced by modern lighting, creating a vibrant artistic space. It comprises six chapters depicting various aspects of Northern culture and history through dance, folk music, and modern theater techniques. Combining tradition and modernity, it utilizes lighting and projection technology alongside traditional elements like ao dai costumes and ethnic musical instruments. This program not only honors traditional values but also serves as a profound cultural lesson, promoting Vietnamese heritage and pride.II/ Transporting Recommendation:Travel by private rental car or book a taxi on the Xanh SM app (when visitors experience the quality of Xanh SM services, they will also learn more about innovation in using public transportation in Vietnam when traveling with a car company manufactured by Vietnamese people, it also helps save travel costs)III/ Recommended Cuisine:1. Cha Ca Thang Long Restaurant (21 Duong Thanh, Hoan Kiem, Hanoi) is renowned for its unique grilled fish, a symbol of Hanoi's culinary culture. Fresh fish, usually lentil or fruit fish, is marinated with turmeric and traditional spices, then grilled and stir-fried with dill and spring onion. Served with vermicelli, grilled rice paper, roasted peanuts, herbs, and shrimp paste with lemon and chili, this dish attracts both local and international diners eager to experience Vietnamese cuisine.2. Bun Dau Hang Khay (31 Hang Khay, Hoan Kiem, Hanoi) is a traditional dish and a must-visit for vermicelli with tofu and shrimp paste lovers. Located near Hoan Kiem Lake, it attracts locals and tourists with its fresh ingredients: crispy fried tofu, soft vermicelli, fragrant boiled meat, and signature spring rolls. The shrimp paste dipping sauce, seasoned with lemon, chili, and hot fat, creates an unforgettable flavor. Served on bamboo trays, the small, bustling eateries offer an authentic Hanoi atmosphere. For a true taste of old town cuisine, Hang Khay vermicelli and tofu is a top choice.3. Bat Dan beef pho (49 Bat Dan, Hoan Kiem district, Hanoi) is a traditional Vietnamese dish beloved worldwide. Originating from Hanoi, it features soft rice noodles, thinly sliced beef (often rare or thin), and a clear, sweet broth simmered from beef bones with spices like anise, cinnamon, herbs, ginger, and onions. This dish symbolizes the sophistication of Vietnamese cuisine, blending ingredients meticulously. Starting your morning with a hot bowl of beef pho promises a delightful experience.4. Co Vietnamese Restaurant & Vegan (21 Hang Can, Hoan Kiem, Hanoi) specializes in serving international guests with fresh, typical Vietnamese dishes. The menu features traditional flavors, including both classic dishes and unique vegetarian options. Whether you're exploring Hanoi's bustling streets or seeking a cozy dining spot, Co Vietnamese Restaurant offers a warm, inviting atmosphere for a memorable meal.IV/ Favorable weather and travel time:- Time: Because Hanoi's weather changes with the seasons, the best time to visit is in the fall and spring (from September to November and March to May).- The weather is comfortable, moderately sunny, not too hot or cold, and suitable for outdoor activities. V/ Estimated cost.1. Entrance ticket price:- Ticket price to Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum:+ Ticket price to visit Uncle Ho's Mausoleum: free+ Museum admission price: 40,000 VND (1.58 USD) + Ticket price to see One Pillar Pagoda: free2. Ticket price to visit the Temple of Literature: 70,000 VND (2.76 USD)3.  Ticket price to visit Hoa Lo Prison: 30,000 VND (1.18 USD)4. Meal prices:- Cha Ca Thang Long Restaurant: ranges around 300,000 VND (11.79USD)- Bun Dau Hang Khay: 30,000VND to 50,000VND (1.18USD-1.96USD)- Bat Dan beef pho: 50,000VND to 100,000VND (1.96USD-3.93USD)- Co Vietnamese Restaurant & Vegan: about 300,000VND/person (11.79USD)5. Ticket price the Quintessence of Tonkin show: - Silver seats (located on both sides of the stands): 320,000 VND (12.57 USD)- Gold class seats (located in the center area, in front of the stage): 400,000 VND (15.72 USD)- Platinum class seats (located in a private seating area with a central view of the stage, snacks served, and limited quantity): 640,000VND (25.15USD)6. Taxi rental cost: Vinfast VF 9 Eco 7-seat taxi rental: 2,300,000 VND/day (90.37USD)These are some suggestions for the 8-hour tour plan, hope it will be useful for you, and wish you a wonderful trip!

author: Yvonne S
title: A clone environment as compared to the Mausoleum of Mau in China
original_content: The Mausoleum grounds is where in September 1945 that Ho Chi Minh read Vietnam’s Declaration of Independence, and it’s here today that the national leader’s body rests within a massive granite mausoleum.  In his speech back in 1954 Ho used quotes out of the preamble of the US constitution to set the pace of getting rid of the French, who had moved back into Vietnam following the Japanese occupation during WW II, and where the country was split in two at the 19 th parallel (communist influence from Russia in the North and wester influence in the South). This area of the Mausoleum is somewhat like what we observed a few years back in Tiananmen Square in Beijing China with Charman Mau’s mausoleum, with a big national flag, and a single military guard under the flag.  Here in Vietnam, there was no solders standing under the national flag, but there were sure a lot of Soldiers at the Mausoleum entrance and posted around his body.We had to check our cameras (as no pictures are allowed inside the mausoleum).  You must remove your hat, and have your knees and shoulders covered, plus no sunglasses (all as a position of respect to the country’s former leader).The line to view the body of Ho Chi Minh, was very / VERY long (well over 1000), but we received a VIP pass and jumped right into the middle of the line.  The Mausoleum is closed on Mondays, and we were originally scheduled to stop here yesterday, but our great guide Henry just swapped the schedule.The setting of the body is very elegant of a well-preserved person.    Originally, Uncle Hoe had requested to be cremated and his ashes scattered over the waters, but following his passing in 1969, the government decided to display his body, as a symbol of the inspiration of a simplistic, modest educated gentleman that had inspired his nation to throw off the yoke of colonialism.The government wanted the body to be preserved like Lenin in Moscow and Mao Zedong in China, and thus approached the Russians for help.  The Chinees did not want the Russians to help as the Chinese and Vietnamese were at odds AGAINST one another, so the body was moved rom cave to cave until the Russians finally preformed the cosmetic preservation.After viewing the guards, flowers, the body of Uncle Ho (no pictures allowed), we continued to the Prudential Palace next door to the Mausoleum; viewing the massive building, and the plush grounds around it.  As part of the grounds, we viewed where Uncle Ho lived on the grounds in a masonry building during the war with a bomb shelter and underground tunnel over to the Citadel where communications to the arms was sent out.  After the war he moved into a stilt house on the grounds until his passing.
drawbacks: No pictures are allowed inside the mausoleum

highlights: Inspiration of a simplistic, modest educated gentleman
practical_tips: Have your knees and shoulders covered

author: FredoG11
title: Impressive filling
original_content: The mausoleum is currently closed, but the whole area is impressively beautiful and revealing . It provides a deep insight into the history of this proud people and their Uncle Ho.

author: Callmeducnguyen
title: Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum
original_content: It's better to have a guide to understand who Ho Chi Minh was and what he had done to Vietnam and how did he get so respected here rather than the fact he was a communist leader.Ho Chi Minh was humble but seeing the way guards there doing just disturbing me so much.The toilet is disgusting in this important area???
highlights: understanding who Ho Chi Minh was

author: Axbridgemum
title: Ho Chi Minh died September 2 1969
original_content: Honestly worth the very long queue. Very respectful shuffle past Uncle Ho's  body was unexpectedly moving, perhaps because he still commands such reverence from the very old to the youngest citizens of this unique country. The mausoleum is now closed until August 12 for his body to be 'maintained'
highlights: respectful shuffle past Uncle Ho's body

author: Onas
title: Imposing from the outside
original_content: Very imposing building from the outside. makes beautiful photos. Inside it is a little disappointing. We are guided to where Ho Chi Minh's body is. You can't take photos.
drawbacks: Inside it is a little disappointing

author: Ludo V
title: impressive but not very elegant
original_content: A mastodon-like gray structure is Ho Chi Minh's final resting place. Although he had expressed the wish to be cremated to save costs, the government decided to build this mausoleum for him. His body lies in state there, mumified by Russian specialists. It is flown to Russia twice a year for maintenance.The architects saw a lotus flower in their design. In my opinion, this requires a lot of imagination. We were lucky to experience the changing of the guard. A visit to the refrigerated room was not an option for us.
extracted_spaces: Ho Chi Minh's final resting place
drawbacks: a visit to the refrigerated room was not an option for us
highlights: experienced the changing of the guard

author: iayzit2
title: Must visit the Mousoleum
original_content: Must visit site! It is in Old Quarter and walking distance from any hotels you stay in this area. When we were there in early May 2024, the entrance was free. Usually, entrance fee is very minimal.
practical_tips: walking distance from any hotels you stay in this area

author: Dimitris L
title: Amazing experience.
original_content: The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is an amazing place. We went there early morning, as it is meant to be open only for a few hours early in the day. The day of our visit was a special one as it fell on a public holiday and thousands of visitors had already lined up by the time we arrived (around 9.00am)! The whole operation was conducted with military precision! Visitors had to line up, single file, and be exactly behind one another! Officials with loudspeakers were in charge. No bags or water could be taken and had to be left in storage for free and collected at exiting. Water fountains could be seen at various spots throughout and cups were provided, however we did not take up this opportunity! It was a very long walk around the whole area before we eventually reached the room with Ho Chi Minh's embalmed body, which was placed in what seemed to be a horse carriage, with his upper body slightly elevated so he could be seen easily by visitors. No photos were allowed to be taken inside. It was only a few seconds of viewing as we had to keep walking. It was very special and a moving moment. The Mausoleum is a beautiful building and photos of the building can be taken from a distance outside. The place is steeped in history and we could sense locals had a deep regard for "Uncle Ho" as they call him.
extracted_spaces: the room with Ho Chi Minh's embalmed body
extracted_times: a few hours early in the day
practical_tips: photos can be taken from a distance outside

author: Marc B
title: Super Super Busy
original_content: The mausoleum itself is impressive to look at but you have to wait about 3 hours to get inside. The other stuff in the park isn't particularly impressive and just not worth the investment of time. When I went it was super super busy, disgustingly so, which may have negatively impacted my view. I would advise people to skip this attraction if you are short on time in Hanoi. If you have the time or really want to go just have a look at mausoleum from the outside, do a quick lap around the park, and get out of there. Don't bother entering any of the paid attractions like the house or museum.
drawbacks: wait about 3 hours to get inside
not worth the investment of time
practical_tips: skip this attraction if you are short on time
look at mausoleum from the outside
do a quick lap around the park

author: Graham S
title: If you are in Hanoi this is a must
original_content: Wildly busy at weekends and closed Monday and Friday so we went for the opening time of 0730 on Tuesday morning (it’s only open 0730-1100 in summer). The queue was about 200 yards long. Predictably, everything ran like clockwork and we were moved forward to the door just before 0730. We were divided into two adjacent lines (tip: left-hand line is closer to the body). Total silence, guards everywhere, in you walk, keep moving, no photos and out by 0738. Amazing. And it’s free.Then into the stilt house (40000VND) and out by 0800. We didn’t bother with the HCM museum.Shock! When we left there was no queue at all so we could have had another 30 minutes in bed.Make sure you are dressed appropriately; no uncovered shoulders and no knees showing.Another freebie that we enjoyed was the lowering of the flag at 2100. Get there at 2045. You can also see the raising of the flag at 0600.

author: Felix F
title: History before your eyes
original_content: A piece of history! Went on a sunday when nearly all Vietnamese coming to see the founder of their current nation. Very interesting.

author: WanderingWilbur
title: Ignore the queues: its the best managed attraction I have been to!
original_content: I would just say that this is well worth a visit for a sense of history and the legend that is interwoven in the culture of this country. Plus, being communist, its free....If the queue looks ENORMOUS when you get there, take heart! It is so well managed by a plethora of police and military, that it takes so much less time than you may initially think. It took us 45 minutes, from halfway down the road outside of the start of the queue to being in the mausoleum itself. And when you emerge, staff are on hand to offer free water and snacks! Who would have thought?

author: George Severin
title: A monumental facility
original_content: The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum is a large memorial dedicated to the former Vietnamese leader Ho Chi Minh. The monumental building was built in the style of the Lenin Mausoleum in Moscow. There is a large area around the mausoleum that is monitored by the military. You enter the area after strict controls and regulations (such as dress code). When we got there, entry was no longer permitted. Therefore, we looked at this monument outside the area. If you are already in Hanoi, you should visit this mausoleum.
highlights: dedicated to the former Vietnamese leader Ho Chi Minh
practical_tips: visit this mausoleum if you are already in Hanoi

author: Peter B
title: Interestingly sureal.
original_content: Had always wanted to visit Ho Chi Minhs Mausoleum. First time we tried it was a Sunday, don't try on a Sunday totally packed ques massive. Finally got there on a Tuseday as they close on Monday's. Super sureal. Its free to enter and the ques though longish move well. Once you are in the Mausoleum its a 30 second walk past to view Ho Chi Minh, but surprisingly satisfying, in a strange way.  Be respectful in what you wear, plenty of info on do's and don'ts.
practical_tips: be respectful in what you wear

author: pieter
title: Confusing opening hours.
original_content: The opening hours of the Mausoleum are a bit confusing. We thought it was until 11 o'clock in the morning, but already at 10.20 o'clock we could no longer visit the mausoleum. After a 40 minute wait we were able to view the square in front of the Mausoleum and the house where he lived. You will be strictly checked (backpack had to go through the scanner).
extracted_spaces: square in front of the Mausoleum
drawbacks: backpack had to go through the scanner
highlights: view the square in front of the Mausoleum
view the house where he lived

author: Mie R
title: Sooooooooo impresive
original_content: I visited this destination at night and i was a great place to refresh some cool breeze, i do love the massive and green square grass. Next time I will visit it on daylight to have a chance to come in to the mausolem....
practical_tips: visit it on daylight to have a chance to come in to the mausolem

author: dianedinky
title: A bit strange
original_content: First off, the tomb is within a large complex so there is more to see than just the body of Uncle Ho.  And the surrounding area with the Palace, Gardens, Ho House, Pagoda etc is great for a visit.I titled this visit strange as it is a weird experience for a tourist.  Ho Chi Minh is revered by all of Vietnam so a serious and solemn event to be in this place.  As a Western tourist his reputation is not so golden so he didn't have that aura for me.  I also am not convinced it is his body preserved that you see.  He looks remarkably young considering when he died and even with the body being removed for a few months to Russia for 'maintenance'.  It could actually be a Lenin looky-likey in there...Glad I can say I was there but the security guards are very strict and too much for me.Note that the complex had many gift shops but they basically all just sell Vietnamese flag t-shirts or plates with Ho's face painted on.  Which was a bit of a let down.
drawbacks: Gift shops sell only Vietnamese flag t-shirts or plates with Ho's face painted on
highlights: The surrounding area with the Palace, Gardens, Ho House, Pagoda etc is great for a visit

author: Julian S
title: A moment of reflection
original_content: Visiting the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum was a somber but powerful experience. It offered a chance to learn about Vietnam's history and pay respect to a revered leader.
