practical_tips: walk in with your own water and beer

author: rangakmurthy
title: Best Pho!
original_content: After reading reviews on TripAdvisor, I had to try this place despite some concerns of cleanliness by reviewers. Yes, it’s not the most aesthetically appealing joint, but their Pho is worth it. I wandered into the place and realized I was among locals (no tourists at all). A local gentleman sitting in front of me said he loved this place and it’s very famous among the locals, and rightly so. I will confidently say that this was the best Pho I’ve had in Hanoi.
highlights: best Pho I've had in Hanoi

author: LuchinoBrooklynNYC
title: A winner!
original_content: Recommended by our tour guide, a lifelong resident of Hanoi. Superb beef noodle soup, on one  of the most fascinating, not touristy streets you will encounter in Hanoi. The soup broth, in which bones are steeped for hours, is outstanding.
extracted_spaces: one of the most fascinating, not touristy streets you will encounter in Hanoi

author: OurManIn
title: Our guides favourite Beef Pho cafe in Hanoi
original_content: Off the tourist track, a fabulous steaming hot beef Pho. Place was heaving at 8am with workers on their way in to work. Scruffy, ramshackle, but apparently a gold mine for the owners. For us, very tasty- added chilli and sauce woke up the morning taste-buds. A good cut above. Probably a taxi ride or motorbike pillion ride from the Old Quarter, some distance from the other end of the lake. Sorry about the crap pictures.

author: Al M
title: Interesting experience
original_content: The pho itself is ok, nothing special. The place is very full and popular among locals. Be aware:  it is very dirty.

author: Judy L.
title: Authentic and tasty beef pho, great local place
original_content: I rode on the back of an UberMoto moped at 6 in the morning to get to this place from the Old Quarter to make sure I would be breakfasting with locals.  The 10 minute ride was so worth it just to see the two chefs smiling, wondering what some tourist was doing in front of their restaurant at this time of day.  I've seen some reviews where people said the staff was rude or just ignored the tourists, but I find that a greeting in a country's native language usually helps to break the ice.  So, in my terribly accented Vietnamese I asked for one bowl of pho, "mot bat pho."  Please note that this restaurant does NOT serve pho ga (or pho with chicken), only pho bo (pho with beef), so it makes ordering much easier.  I got a thumbs up, and then I sat down on a long bench at a long table, where I shared breakfast with 8 other locals -- not a tourist in sight.  The broth alone justified the early visit -- great beefy flavor, not greasy, and a tad sweet from the meat and green onions.  I threw in some fresh chilis, a couple squeezes of lime juice and a lashing of the special chili sauce.  This is truly the breakfast of champions!
drawbacks: staff was rude or just ignored the tourists
highlights: not greasy, and a tad sweet from the meat and green onions

author: Dominic N
title: AMAZING
original_content: I can eat Pho Thin ALL DAY. The food was amazing and cheap. The place is a bit small but the food was amazing.You know a place is good when it is popular with even the locals.
drawbacks: The place is a bit small

author: Marco L
title: WOW!!!
original_content: Just fantastic, flavorful and very authentic! You would sit right next to Vietnamese people. That's when you know that the food is gonna be the best!

author: georgeu761
title: They sell beef pho and chinese donuts!
original_content:
This place is a no BS place.  They sell beef pho and you can have chinese donuts (油條) to dip into the soup.  That’s it.  They do both extremely well.  You pay first, you sit down, and then they give you a bowl of hot Pho Bo (beef). Pho will cost 50k VND and chinese donuts (油條) will cost you 10k VND for a basket of 5-8.  [these prices reflected as of 2018]

You’ll see a mixture of tourists and locals - which generally signifies that tourists see it as safe, locals see it as affordable, and both as good.
highlights: You pay first, you sit down, and then they give you a bowl of hot Pho Bo (beef)
practical_tips: Dip chinese donuts (油條) into the soup

author: ryantravelor
title: A bit far from old quarter Hanoi
original_content: The food is decent, but the location is a bit far from the old quarter Hanoi.  Its definitely a taxi ride from old town so it makes it less desirable being there are so many other options closer.

author: Travel235640
title: Good Pho but Cruel
original_content: I went here alone and ordered one pho to eat in, and one to go. Very little English spoken. Pho was good, but when I left and waited to pick up the to-go pho, there was confusion and I was blatantly ignored for 15 minutes. I was also subjected to invasive stares and comments directed at my bare legs (I was wearing shorts). I was then asked to pay again, very rudely. I refused, explained I had already paid, and was ignored again. Left without the second order. If you come here be ready to possibly be treated quite badly.
drawbacks: Subjected to invasive stares and comments
practical_tips: Be ready to possibly be treated badly

author: jackiejg
title: Simple and delicious Pho Bo.
original_content: We visited this place following a recommendation on a couple of different travel sites. It was worth the walk. We got there not long after midday and just in the nick of time as it turns out as we were the last to be served before they sold out! Tasty and delicious street food at its best.

author: TMLee2014
title: Wonderful pho
original_content: Simply yummilicious! Smooth yet firm rice noodles, light yet fragrant soup, tender beef strips 👍 Add in the home-made chilli sauce & u get a new wonderful spicy taste. Great to go with the deep fried dough stick (yau-char-gwai).  One minus point: very difficult to get seats & have orders come due to language obstacles.
practical_tips: go with deep fried dough stick (yau-char-gwai)

author: Nixek2810
title: Best pho ever
original_content: It’s the best pho I have ever eaten. The broth is clear yet sweet. The beef is actually nothing special but it’s the pho and broth that stand out. Went back to eat a second time before leaving Hanoi. Addicted!
highlights: best pho I have ever eaten
practical_tips: go back to eat a second time

author: MWoo
title: Good Pho, poor hygiene
original_content: While it surely looked like the restaurant had a good mix of locals and tourists, which is usually a good indication of a authentic restaurant. The hygiene was extremely poor, my kids ordered to bowls of dishes but no one tried them as sighted something not sanitary in the process. Will not be back
drawbacks: saw something not sanitary in the process

author: J Russell W
title: Limited Pho Choice
original_content: It is kinda a cross between a street food and a small greasy spoon. Communal tables, noise and local flavor and tourist alike. When we went, they told us no Pho Ga (chicken) only Pho Bo (beef). I could of swore I saw a chicken parts being boiled for Pho stock So be prepared to know and order what you want quickly, not much tolerance for us tourist.
practical_tips: know and order what you want quickly

author: Tung Dao
title: Overpriced and overated
original_content:
I'm an Hanoian and has been here for several times and while the Pho here was good it's nowhere the best Pho place in Hanoi. Too many green onion and the broth is too fat, the beef is stir fry before adding so this is absolutely not the original way of making Pho.
And you can buy 2 bowls of Pho from other vendor for 1 bowl here.
drawbacks: Beef is stir fry before adding
practical_tips: Buy 2 bowls of Pho from other vendor for 1 bowl here

author: Danielle S
title: Best Pho!
original_content: We came here as our first meal in Hanoi and were not disappointed. It had set the bar for all other Pho. You walk into this tiny cramped aromatic spot and are ushered to a seat where you are quickly served a bowl of steaming hot pho.  They give you a really generous protein helping which is super important to us who are used to getting in a lot of protein and less carbs in our macros and suffer a huge inverse of this in Southeast Asia. So the big portion of meat was a wonderful surprise and it was delicious! I added the various spices available and I almost wish I didn’t because the broth is so perfect as it is. Find time to go here during your stay!

author: Jocelyn H
title: Above average Pho
original_content: It's pretty good. Unfortunately, there's no menu only one type of pho (tai) and its well done when it's arrives your table. The fried donut comes but is extra. A small and narrow joint for most locals its a quick stop for a fast bite. They even bottle and sell that hot sauce. Worth stopping for If your in Hanoi
highlights: Quick stop for a fast bite

author: Jessiekan
title: Best pho
original_content:
During this trip, I have been to 3 famous pho shop, Pho Gia Truyen,  Pho 10 and Pho Thin. I personally like this the most, also because I like spring onions, this pho has lots of spring onions on top. And I found this soup base more sweet, I mean the sweet taste from the beef. And it has more beef than noodles ! 

One thing is the shop rather difficult to find , they don’t have a shop sign at the top. At first, we kept looking up at the top of the shops, but we couldn’t find and after that we realised there was just a little sign standing there.
drawbacks: no shop sign at the top

author: Sarah M
title: Best pho in all of Vietnam
original_content: We absolutely loved this Pho.... the broth was so delicious that we didn't really need to add anything but some chilli. The taste is so different than the pho we had in ho chi Minh and hoi an. We were also told to order some fried bread like sticks and dunk in the pho till it soaks the juices and omg it was absolutely delicious and I have not seen this anywhere! If you are in Hanoi, please try and get to this place as it is Amazing!
highlights: different taste than in Ho Chi Minh and Hoi An
fried bread like sticks with pho is delicious
practical_tips: try the fried bread like sticks with pho
get to this place if you are in Hanoi

author: luckybemery
title: Just walk in holding up the right number of fingers
original_content:
Sought out this place after arriving in Hanoi. Came with solid recommendation and didn't let us down. We stood outside sheepishly waiting for some attention before copying the locals, walking in, "xin chao, three please".

Delivered in seconds, quickly followed by green lemons and cold "Churros". Fish sauce and chilli on the table. 

Really amazing authentic experience (so busy following school pick up time). In slurp it down, then out! No beer, no plesentry, efficient. Even refused a tip of a couple of quid and retained a tip of local appropriateness. 

Very friendly on the way out - hopefully because we all, including my 12 year old, demolished the lot.

Recommend!

author: GM8868
title: Pho Thin
original_content: We had a good pho dinner here in this very authentic pho restaurant and all was very tasty with good service and basic bench seating

author: angusm9410
title: Authentic Pho!
original_content:
We were recommended this place as one of the best places in town for authentic Pho. The recommendation did not disappoint! The Pho was the best we have had so far!

The restaurant is bare bones and more of a street food style with common tables that can be shared.
 
Highly recommend to visit during your stay in Hanoi! The price was excellent aswell, approximately 2 USD per Pho.
highlights: Pho was the best we have had so far!
practical_tips: Visit during your stay in Hanoi

author: Sarah F
title: Amazing Pho!!!
original_content: Don’t be scared off by the seeming lack of hygiene in the place lol the food was amazing, best pho I had in Hanoi. Only one type so just sit down and they will bring it right away. I’d recommend to add the chili sauce!
practical_tips: sit down and they will bring it right away

author: R K L
title: It was not faux pho...
original_content: We were staying at the Hilton Garden Inn Hanoi and were turned on to the Pho Thin Restaurant by one of their excellent front desk clerks. The restaurant was literally across the street, looked like just another small local store front but was an absolutely amazing culinary surprise. It was not faux pho in even the smallest way. We had never tasted better! The service was friendly, fast and efficient...the restaurant just casual and fun. There was nothing that could be pretentious about this place. They just had GREAT pho! We actually returned multiple times for a late night snack during our Hanoi stay, even when we were staying at the Hanoi Hilton a few more blocks away. Their prices were incredibly inexpensive so don't tell them!
practical_tips: go to Pho Thin Restaurant for great pho

author: Spring T
title: OMG good
original_content: This pho is definitely in the top five for me. The broth is delicate and delicious, with lots of yummy meat and spring onions. Ample limes on the table, and a great chili sauce. They only do one dish so just find a seat, sit down and they will bring you a bowl of deliciousness - no need for ordering! 50,000 a bowl, great price for great food.
highlights: lots of yummy meat and spring onions
practical_tips: sit down and they will bring you a bowl of deliciousness - no need for ordering!

author: Kamil
title: Unexpectedly good pho in simple place
original_content: Full of taste pho, delicious pasta. Pretty difficult to find, but worth to look for. Good, fixed price.

author: hannostamm
title: One of the better Pho places
original_content: I have lived here for 20+ years and during that time have had a Pho or 2. I prefer Ha Noi Pho and would rate this as one if the better ones I have had. Disregard comments about lack of hygiene, it is a regular local restaurant with a turn-over ensuring the food is fresh. Pay at the entrance (VND 50,000), grab a plate of bread sticks (VND 5,000), add a dollop of their excellent chili sauce (free) and have some Pho bliss head your way.
practical_tips: grab a plate of bread sticks

author: David O
title: Simple breakfast
original_content:
I really enjoyed my Pho Thin at the Helio cafe at Ly Thường Liet and Phan Chu Trinh Road junction.
The stock, stick dough and chicken are fresh and it is not salty non sweet.
Enjoy watching the morning rush while sitting on the elevated terrace under the bright red umbrella.
extracted_spaces: Ly Thường Liet and Phan Chu Trinh Road junction
practical_tips: go early to watch the morning rush

author: Stektan
title: Great street Hanoi pho
original_content: Not all Pho are created the same.. The north and the south have different styles of Pho and its often a debate about which is better. In the north however, there's one street pho that dominates here. Very popular with both tourists and local alike, this place has been around for a while. It's not the typical Vietnamese restaurant that made it good and now renovated itself to tourist standards. The place is still dirty and the extension comes with low tables, low chairs and dirty floors. Not recommended for the fussy tourist looking for a clean, hygienic place. But if it's the food that you only care about, the Pho is very tasty. It's very unlike the ones from Saigon but the meat is juicy and the soup delicious. You pay slightly above the average for the street food but way below restaurants and hotel. Recommended for a stop over if you're not fussy about hygiene and cleanliness.
practical_tips: Recommended for a stop over if you're not fussy about hygiene and cleanliness

author: Emma C
title: Just good pho. Just worth to try it.
original_content:
Just a good pho bo. Dunno difference between 
Soup was great, but lil bit sweet and sour to my taste. Kinda think soup, strong flavour, chewy beef and soft noodle. If you guys prefer mild soup and chewy noodle like us, find the otherwhere else. 
I heard here is really famous among Korean community and ma Korean friend recommended here but actually nothing special. However, we totally understand that this pho is Asian people-prefer-flavour. We actually saw so many Koreans and Vietnamese here except for just one western guy (and he left most of food). 
If you like spring onion, try to go there.

한국인 친구가 한국에서 유명하다며 추천을 해주어서 엄청 오래 걸어서ㅠㅠ (20분?) 왔어요.  Pho Thin Bo Ho와 Pho Thin 이 무슨 관계인지는 모르겠지만, previous one이 닫아서 여기로 왔어요. 

국물은 대파때문에 새콤한맛이 나고요, 고기국물 자체의 단맛이 있어요.
다른 집에 비해 국물이 thick하고 간이 쎄서 아시아인/한국인이 확실히 좋아할 맛이었어요. 대파 많이넣은 갈비탕국물이랄까? 저희 맛은 아니었어요ㅠ

실제로 손님 10팀중 4팀은 베트남 5팀은 한국인 1팀은 서양인이었어요. 국수먹다가 서양인하고 친해졌는데 웨스턴사람 맛은 아닌가봐요.ㅋㅋ 저희처럼 간 센거 싫으시고 싱겁게 드시는분, 마일드한 국물좋아하시는 분들 비추천이구요.
면이 부드럽다고 하시는데, 저희 입에는 불은 면 이상 이하두 아니었어요.. 호불호 갈릴듯 하네요.

튀김빵은, 맛없다는 평을 듣고 왔지만 정말루 맛이 없어요...ㅋㅋㅋ 

가게는 깨끗하지 않고, 바쁘면 테이블도 치우지않고 그대루 두니까 알아서 치우시고 앉아야하는점 기억하세요ㅠㅠ
확실한거는, 너무 기대하면서 오래 걸어서 찾아오지는 마시라는거...
drawbacks: 국물이 새콤한맛이 나고, 고기국물 자체의 단맛이 있어요.
간이 쎄서 아시아인/한국인이 확실히 좋아할 맛이었어요.
국수먹다가 서양인하고 친해졌는데 웨스턴사람 맛은 아닌가봐요.
highlights: 국물이 thick하고 간이 쎄서 아시아인/한국인이 확실히 좋아할 맛이었어요.
튀김빵은, 맛없다는 평을 듣고 왔지만 정말루 맛이 없어요...
practical_tips: 간 센거 싫으시고 싱겁게 드시는분, 마일드한 국물좋아하시는 분들 비추천이구요.
가게는 깨끗하지 않고, 바쁘면 테이블도 치우지않고 그대루 두니까 알아서 치우시고 앉아야하는점 기억하세요...

author: s b
title: Late lunch
original_content: Went here based on reviews. Did not disappoint. Set price 50 000 dong for the best pho in Hanoi...so far.

author: Aliza D
title: Proper street food
original_content: Amazing pho down a tiny alley in Hanoi, almost would have walked past. Sit at the one table and pick a size of bowl and they'll provide you with delicious food!

author: Duc Huynh
title: Taste is good
original_content: Not a fan of Pho but this Pho is good, I like it. But the environment is not: small, hot, crowded and untidy. This is just a place for eating, you cannot stay for chatting coz there are always lots of people queuing and staring at you.

author: Jadex3
title: Good pho (beef)
original_content: You walked in and pay up front when you make an order (Cost 50,000VND). Be sure to request for the fried bread. They are free and you're supposed to eat it by soaking it into your pho soup.  Definitely must visit and try when you come to Hanoi. (Warning: The place lacks a bit of atmosphere and hygiene)
practical_tips: eat it by soaking it into your pho soup

author: HidehikoMURAO
title: "Phở Bò" is very good !!
original_content:
I was brought to a store by a friend living in Hanoi. Most of the customers are Vietnamese. 
I arrived at the shop around 9:30 am, but already a lot of people were eating phở and it was full. 
I ordered "phở bò". The soup is very tasty, the noodles are thick and delicious. 
Vietnamese people were eating "quay" soaked in phở 's soup. It looked very delicious, so I want to try it next time. 
I ate on the outdoor seating. If you squeeze the lime after eating about half, you can enjoy a refreshing different taste.

author: Huy L
title: good Pho bo
original_content:
yeah a good taste of Vietnamese famous Pho bo (beef noddle) that attracts many locals and tourists. maybe some still concern about the hygiene, the quality of the pho thin is confirmed through many years. 

you should try Pho Thin when you visit Hanoi
highlights: good taste of Vietnamese famous Pho bo
quality of the pho thin is confirmed through many years
practical_tips: try Pho Thin when you visit Hanoi

author: Joshua D
title: Pho-sure!
original_content: Good Pho! The atmosphere is very simple with benches & no air conditioning other than fans. However, the Pho is worth the lack of atmosphere.
highlights: Pho is worth the lack of atmosphere

author: Khiem Vo
title: Not hygiene, may use MSG
original_content:
Firstly the chef and the staffs used the same hands they touch the money to touch the food and serve you.

The soup is delicious because maybe they used MSG. We're both super sensitive with MSG, it makes us super weak and sleepy instantly so we know.
drawbacks: The chef and staff touch the money and then the food

author: jfavril
title: Excellent soup but only soup
original_content: It is a fix price of 50k for the pho that you pay before you enter. Typical Vietnam canteen, so not very nice decoration neither very clean but the Pho is one of the best ever. Includes meet so not good for vegan

author: Sue Ann L
title: Delicious cheap Pho - must try Vietnamese street food
original_content: Was introduced to this place by the local tour guide. Easy to miss entrance, very basic set up. Very cheap and flavourful bowl of Pho for $2. Pots of broth boiling over burning coal. Rumoured to be the 1st ever Pho stall in Hanoi since 1956. No upset tummy after - big win!
highlights: Very cheap and flavourful bowl of Pho for $2
practical_tips: Go early to avoid missing the entrance

author: Andrew G
title: Great food, what a place!
original_content:
We got advise to go here from a local.

It was fan-bloody-tastic !

So ... we saw the sign and thought it was down the alley. We didn't realise that it was the alley!

We sat and ask for 2. They brought us the most delicious pho that we had ever had. Huge bowl each with spices, corianders and greens that we could add if we wanted 

It was dead basic but super yummy. Proper food!

author: Cornelius L
title: Excellent Pho, friendly people
original_content: A family run stall that serves amazing pho. The owner was super friendly and advised us on how to properly enjoy pho. Great food great experience

author: Zoe S
title: Delicious!
original_content: One of my favorite Pho in Hanoi. Pho with beef was delicious, I like the broth very much. It is more tasty with the sauce, everything just simply melted in your mouth. However, the alley is quite hard to find but still highly recommend!
drawbacks: The alley is quite hard to find
highlights: everything just simply melted in your mouth

author: misspink1976
title: Local food, family run, good prices.
original_content: We went to this restaurant as part of a food tour. The food was amazing. The Dough Bread was delicious. The restaurant has been open since the 50's and was one of the first pho soups. Definitely worth a visit.

author: Davie_T_Edinburgh
title: Wow...worth seeking out
original_content: Our first proper street food experience that fulfilled our expectations. An easy to miss alley that you should make the effort to find. Small, standard or jumbo Pho Bo with a beer and a massively tasty and spicy jar of sauce on the table is a thoroughly satisfying experience. Be brave, street food is not for the faint hearted. You will be rewarded with delicious steaming hot soup and beer for little cost and a memory of food that will never leave you. Hanoi would not be Hanoi without it.
highlights: massively tasty and spicy jar of sauce
practical_tips: Be brave, street food is not for the faint hearted
Make the effort to find the alley

author: Benjamin O
title: Amazing experience
original_content: We had an amazing experience eating here. You go in and just ask for two as the only food they serve is Pho. It is packed with locals and you find a seat on the busy tables and the food is served to you very quickly. Location wasn't amazing but it is very cheap to get an Uber or I would say it is worth walking. I would definitely recommend this place if you want to fully experience the culture.

author: Crystal N
title: Simple yet pack with flavor
original_content: This Place is a hidden gem. They only serve one type of bowl here and once size. Beef with noodles. Its hot in the restaurant but you get pretty used to it. Restaurant is clean and service is fast and friendly. Definitely worth a try when you are in hanoi.
practical_tips: go when you are in Hanoi

author: Chris B
title: Hands down, the best pho in Hanoi
original_content: My wife and I love pho and we ate at many places in Hanoi. And this was the best. The. Best. The owner does something a bit different - instead of raw round or flank steak, he sautees the beef with garlic BEFORE adding it to the piping hot broth, and the meat becomes both chewy AND tender. It's wonderful. Add to it a bunch of flavorful green onions and a few spoonfuls of their chili oil / sauce...and you've got the best pho in Hanoi. We ate their twice...in less than 24 hours!
highlights: The owner does something a bit different - instead of raw round or flank steak, he sautees the beef with garlic BEFORE adding it to the piping hot broth, and the meat becomes both chewy AND tender.
Add to it a bunch of flavorful green onions and a few spoonfuls of their chili oil / sauce...and you've got the best pho in Hanoi.
practical_tips: Go to this place for the best pho in Hanoi

author: CoryMay
title: Amazing!
original_content:
I'm no master of Pho but I know when I stumble upon deliciousness. My airport taxi recommendes this place to me. After checking into my AirBNB, I walked right over to this place.
It was fairly easy to find, but the sign isn't above the door. It's a metal sign board as you can see in my photo.
You go in, just say how many pho bo you want, and if you want the bahn quay dough sticks. It's literally all they serve. You can also get tea and other drinks there.
The staff were super kind and service was super fast. On the table are condiments to add to your bowl. Vinegar with chillies, a spicy pepper paste, and slices of red chillies. Also some black pepper if you like. Make sure to also squeeze a wedge of lime and mix it all up!
The rice noodles were very light and nice. The meat was slightly tough, but had that good smokiness flavor to it. The broth is clean and light but had a depth to it. I wish I knew the recipe!
As you're eating, just drop a whole dough stick in and let it soak up the soup while you eat the noodles.
It was a great lunch! Highly recommend it!
highlights: The broth is clean and light but had a depth to it
The rice noodles were very light and nice
practical_tips: Make sure to also squeeze a wedge of lime and mix it all up!
Drop a whole dough stick in and let it soak up the soup while you eat the noodles

author: HungoverTT
title: Eat like the locals
original_content: street side eating experience and its very affordable. You shouldnt miss this when you are at hanoi.
practical_tips: Go when you are at Hanoi

author: Bazzamat
title: Authentic Hanoi experience
original_content: Hand in your 50000 Dong, scrabble to find a seat and wait for the only thing on the menu to be served. An amazing Pho Bo eaten shoulder to shoulder (literally) with the locals. Great find thanks to our guide and well worth a visit. My only advice - go steady on the Chilli sauce!
extracted_times: wait for the only thing on the menu to be served
drawbacks: wait for the only thing on the menu to be served
highlights: eaten shoulder to shoulder (literally) with the locals
practical_tips: go steady on the Chilli sauce

author: Christian G
title: The local experience
original_content:
Nice experience,  the entire communication with the staff was limited to holding up fingers and nodding appreciably.
The result: most delicious Pho Bo we had. Not a comfy place but very well invested 2  bucks for a local experience.
highlights: most delicious Pho Bo we had

author: HamidDR
title: Really simple but delicious food
original_content:
The place is small and would not win any design contests, but the service is quick, food is fresh and delicious. 
Great place for a quick bite.
practical_tips: Great place for a quick bite

author: sorrycoffey
title: Phở ăn được
original_content: The things are good, but it's rather expensive. Anyway i usually choose to eat whenever i go to hanoi.
practical_tips: eat whenever i go to hanoi

author: anjakeen
title: Straight forward, delicious, satisfying.
original_content:
Came here for my dose of Pho for breakfast. 
You sit. They bring your Pho. You eat. You pay. 
The best there is and very inexpensive. 
Not to be missed!

author: Marjorie E
title: Dirty but good
original_content: It's sad to see people that just throws out their rubbish on the floor, when they have the bin right next to them. The person that stand at the door collects the money upon entering and was quite rude. A good place to have a quick pho despite the mess & ambience. Pho was very delicious though, even without the vegetables that usually come with it on the side. One of the most tasty pho we have eaten here in Vietnam.
drawbacks: people throw rubbish on the floor
person at the door was rude
highlights: one of the most tasty pho we have eaten here in Vietnam

author: Igor Alexeev
title: Old Quarter of Hanoi: colorful...
original_content: The Old Quarter of Hanoi, also known as "36 Streets of Hanoi," is located north and west of Hoan Kiem Lake. Many tourists start their acquaintance with Hanoi from the Old Quarter. Including to ensure that the Old Quarter is a multitude of architectural, historical, and other attractions, public spaces, shops, stalls, restaurants, cafes, and other tourist attractions. And, of course, a huge number of people, especially in the evening. So, while walking through the Old Quarter, it will not be unnecessary to keep an eye not only at the sights but also at your pockets...
practical_tips: keep an eye on your pockets

author: COM Service Private Car Chauffeur Hanoi
title: Impressions of Vietnam's ancient towns
original_content: Hanoi’s Old Quarter is not merely a tourist destination but a living museum, preserving the heartbeat and soul of a capital city with a thousand years of culture. Spending a day strolling through its narrow alleys and enjoying a summer evening meal is the best way to truly immerse yourself in the pulse of Hanoi.

author: Rae L
title: Authentic Vietnamese charm in the streets
original_content: The avenues are stunning, offering a genuinely immersive experience of true Vietnam.

author: Patty B
title: A Nice Walk
original_content: We took a walk around the Old Quarter by day to see the hustle and bustle we had heard about.  Like most place we went to in Saigon and Hanoi it is vibrant and busy.  Shop and places to eat are plentiful.  We were just browsing and didn’t buy anything.  We just enjoyed people watching and seeing vendors and their wares.
highlights: plentiful shops and places to eat

Do NOT attempt to explore this area dragging large suitcases behind you.On our final afternoon, we had an 11:00 AM hotel check-out but our sleeper train wasn't leaving until 9:00 PM. Instead of being stuck or hauling bags through crowded alleys, we used Luggage Storage IO to drop our heavy family suitcases at a verified hotel front desk right in the Old Quarter. It was around $2.40 (50,000 VND) per bag for the day, monitored by 24/7 front desk staff and CCTV, and arranged in two minutes on WhatsApp without needing an app.Being totally hands-free made wandering the night markets and eating street food completely stress-free for the whole family. Highly recommend taking a slow walk through the 36 guild streets, just make sure you store your heavy bags first!

author: FrameTheWild
title: Hanoi City - great few days sightseeing
original_content: We had a private tour of Hanoi around the key places to visit, and had an absolutely wonderful time. What an amazing city - and although we arrived at the tail end of 'Tet' - the busyness of this made it an even more special visit.  Our guide took us to the Temple of Literature - definitely not to be missed; we also visited the mausoleum and paid our respects. With a visit to Ho Chi Minh's stilted house and also the One Pillar Pagoda.  Our tour included the Ho Loa prison - but due to the free entry because of New Year the queue was too long so we settled for a narrative and history of the prison from our tour guide. We also managed an inside visit of St Joseph's Cathedral.  The following morning we experienced a cyclo ride through empty streets (5.30am) and what a different view of Hanoi.  We saw the flag raising at the Mausoleum and then experienced local Pho noodle breakfast - not to be missed. And our final stop was the Hoan Kiem Lake and the Ngoc Son Temple. We were only in Hanoi for a few days, but managed to see all of the highlights.  And not to be missed was Train Street - which we were able to time perfectly with a track side seat in a local cafe, and an experience most definitely not to be missed.  All in all we had a wonderful time in Hanoi, and stayed in a wonderful hotel - The Capella.
practical_tips: time perfectly with a track side seat in a local cafe

title: The Old Quarter is best for first time visitors to Hanoi

Also, be careful in crossing the street as motorbikes and cars hardly stop to give way to pedestrians.

The streets glisten under the soft glow of lanterns and neon signs, creating a romantic and vibrant atmosphere. The sound of raindrops mixing with the hum of scooters and chatter from cozy cafés makes the experience unforgettable. Walking through the narrow lanes, the countless street food stalls serving steaming bowls of pho, sizzling skewers, and sweet treats, the air filled up with the aroma of fresh herbs and grilled meat, so tempting as we passed through. Small shops selling souvenirs, shoes and sandals, and handmade crafts, some closes early and some  stay open late, making it perfect for a leisurely stroll.We enjoyed a warm cup of Vietnamese coffee by the side of the lake watching the rain fall, it’s pure bliss. The Old Quarter in the rain feels like stepping into a living postcard—colorful, lively, and full of character.

author: Chirag Gupta
title: Immersing in the Soul of Hanoi: A beautiful Chaos
original_content: Stepping into Hanoi's Old Quarter is like entering a living museum of Vietnamese heritage. With its labyrinth of narrow lanes, centuries-old architecture, and vibrant street life, this historic heart of the city captures the true essence of Hanoi. By day, the neighbourhood hums with the energy of daily life—street vendors, scooters weaving through tight alleys, and the aroma of fresh fruits and Vietnamese street food.But it's after dark that the Old Quarter truly comes alive. The transformation is remarkable—softly lit, buzzing cafés, and an almost cinematic glow cast over the colonial facades. The atmosphere becomes electric, yet intimate, offering a deeper connection to the rhythm of local life.For those visiting over the weekend (Friday through Sunday), the night market is a must-experience. Stretching through the main thoroughfares, it’s a delightful blend of food stalls, local crafts, and live performances. More than just a shopping experience, it’s a lively, authentic way to engage with Hanoi's residents and soak in the spirit of Vietnamese culture.

author: Strike_right
title: Old Quarter, Hanoi on a Weekend Night
original_content: If you're in Hanoi on a weekend night, the **Old Quarter** becomes an unforgettable experience—a vibrant, chaotic, and deeply atmospheric immersion into Vietnamese urban life.### 🌃 AtmosphereAs night falls, the Old Quarter transforms. What by day is already a busy maze of narrow streets turns into a carnival of colors, sounds, and smells. Streets are closed to vehicles from Friday to Sunday night, allowing crowds to spill into the roads. The air buzzes with live music, laughter, and the clang of street vendors preparing food. Bright lights from lanterns, beer stalls, and souvenir shops give the place a magical, almost surreal energy.### 🍜 Street Food & DrinksThis is a paradise for food lovers. You'll find everything from steaming bowls of *pho* and sizzling *banh xeo* to exotic snacks like grilled quail eggs and sweet sticky rice. Plastic stools crowd the sidewalks where locals and tourists sit elbow-to-elbow drinking *bia hoi* (fresh beer) for less than a dollar. For those feeling adventurous, the food tour possibilities are endless—and delicious.### 🎶 Entertainment & CultureThere’s live music in the street, both traditional and contemporary. Impromptu dance circles form around performers playing Vietnamese instruments or acoustic guitars. The weekend night market, stretching from Hang Dao Street to Dong Xuan Market, offers clothes, handicrafts, and quirky souvenirs, often at bargain prices.### 🧑‍🤝‍🧑 Crowd & VibeExpect crowds—lots of them. It’s loud, energetic, and sometimes overwhelming, but that’s part of the charm. You’ll see families, young locals, travelers, and backpackers all mixing in one pulsating cultural cocktail. While it’s generally safe, watch your belongings and avoid scams, especially around bar areas.### 💬 Final ThoughtsA weekend night in Hanoi’s Old Quarter isn’t just an activity—it’s an **experience**. Whether you’re sipping beer on a low stool, listening to a street band, or weaving through the market crowds, it offers a rare blend of sensory overload and authentic cultural engagement. Not for the faint of heart, but absolutely essential for anyone wanting to feel the true heartbeat of Hanoi.**Rating: 9/10**(Best enjoyed with open senses and a flexible schedule.)
practical_tips: go with open senses and a flexible schedule

author: SB01
title: Unique Sensory Overload
original_content: My son and I spent 3 days in 2 hotels in the old Town. We could easily have spent a couple more days as there is so much to see and do. I don’t think I’ve ever been anywhere like this and for sure it won’t be for everyone. Yes, it’s dirty, noisy, chaotic, overcrowded. But it’s also friendly, authentic, great value, colourful and buzzing. The old quarter is a compact area, but other interesting sites - West Lake, the French Quarter, Ho Chi Min’s mausoleum are all within walking distance, or a low cost Grab - so it makes a good base. There are lots of good places to eat, with decent meals being available for less than £10/head. Or go for a blowout on one of the rooftop bars, where you may spend £30-40/ head. There are plenty of bars with beer around £1 a pint. You can pay less in the very congested bia street, but this is also the one part of the area that feels a bit sleazy and where you might get hustled to buy things. At night stroll over to train street and join the crowd flirting with disaster.

author: gfsc5
title: Chaotic delight
original_content: Situated at the northern end of Hoan Kiem Lake, the Old Quarter is a must-see destination for tourists.  Chaos abounds with motor bikes and scooters parked over the footpaths and whizzing along the streets with gay abandon.  They do tend to avoid running into people so the trick to crossing a road is to look straight ahead and walk at a steady pace from one side to the other.  Don't try to dodge them - they'll dodge you.Apart from the traffic (and the large number of people) there is lots to see.  Small shops abound with many of the streets specialising in particular goods whether that be silk or paper/decorations or shoes or whatever.  There is no grid pattern in the streets so it’s easy to get disoriented and lost.  That’s part of the adventure, of course.A great place to visit.

author: Shafinah J.
title: A Chaotic Symphony You’ll Want to Get Lost In
original_content: The 36 ancient streets that make up Hanoi’s Old Quarter are a maze of chaos and treasures. The streets are narrow and so are the houses, but that doesn’t stop the constant crush of motorbikes and, in an increasing number, cars mixing with bicycles, tourists and rickshaws known as cyclos. Despite the craziness, the Old Quarter should not be missed. Its lanes overflow with everything you need to fill your suitcase back home, from colourful kitschy trinkets to Vietnamese crafts to fine silks to hardwares and more. To fully explore the Old Quarter in Hanoi, prepare your feet for a day of walking street to street and taking in the locals’ daily life amidst these old-style narrow streets and houses. And if you have spare change, dining on these streets is a culinary requisite. more than just a tempting and adventurous bid – it’s actually required for a complete culinary excursion in Hanoi. It doesn’t take much effort to trace down an absolutely great bowl of humble Pho at ridiculously low prices.
practical_tips: prepare your feet for a day of walking

author: Patty B
title: Glad We Went

Laos and Cambodia were also heavily bombed.So…… a subtle distinction between good and evil is in order. Although the museum downplays the treatment of these pilots, suggesting that they (the pilots) didn’t have it that bad, physical and mental torment were the order of the dayP pop s

author: Katchamata
title: Well organized but historically very biased
original_content: The tour route is clear, the signs are interesting as are the exhibited objects. The main flaw of this museum is that one generally expects a factual and honest approach to history from a museum. Yet here the narrative is extremely biased, even misleading. They display on one hand the cruelty of the prison under the colonial regime, and claim elsewhere that under Vietnamese control, the prison resembled a sort of vacation center. author: Ben
title: Impressive and historically significant
original_content: A visit to the Hỏa Lò Prison (historically known as the 'Hanoi Hilton') is an impactful and thought-provoking experience. The museum provides a deep insight into the site's history, focusing heavily on the struggle of Vietnamese prisoners against French colonial rule, as well as the period during which American POWs were held here.The exhibits, including the preserved cells and the guillotine, are powerfully presented. The available audio guide is of high quality and provides essential historical context that truly enhances the visit; using it is highly recommended.Keep in mind that the information is presented from a specific national and political perspective, which is particularly noticeable in the section regarding the American pilots. Nevertheless, it remains an absolute must-see in Hanoi for anyone interested in Vietnam's recent history. The complex is well-maintained, and a visit takes approximately 1 to 1.5 hours.
drawbacks: The information is presented from a specific national and political perspective
highlights: deep insight into the site's history

author: Hailstorm12
title: Worth a visit for the Vietnamese narrative
original_content: This is mainly valuable to learn something about the Vietnamese view of this prison. With a western education, my knowledge of this prison is a place of POWs from the Vietnam War (which they call the American War). That's not what you will see here. The focus is when the prison was used by the French to house political prisoners. This is the history told there. There are a couple rooms set aside that talk about the American POWs including John McCain. This mainly tries to highlight how great they were treated, with photos of them playing sports and decorating Christmas trees. Our guide, a local, specifically commented on the difference of how the French treated the Vietnamese and how the Vietnamese treated the US. I've have my serious doubts about how the lucky the American POWs were, but I think learning about how other people tell their history is worth learning. I'm glad we went.
drawbacks: doubts about how the American POWs were treated
highlights: learn something about the Vietnamese view of this prison
how other people tell their history is worth learning
practical_tips: go if you want to learn about the Vietnamese perspective

Much of the prison is not accessible (off-limits), including the underground areas where the Americans were held. Multiple buses had just arrived, so it was “wall to wall” with little room to move and difficult to view the few exhibits and cells.

title: Interesting but a bit underwhelming overall

author: The Wandering Pair
title: A Powerful Insight into Vietnam’s Past
original_content: A monument to a troubled past, Hoa Lo Prison Relic is a must-visit in Hanoi for anyone wanting to learn more about not only the Vietnam War, but also the hardships endured by the Vietnamese people under French colonial rule.As you move through the cell blocks and read about the harrowing conditions faced by political prisoners, from overcrowded cells to accounts of torture and execution, it serves as a poignant reminder of the suffering many endured. The exhibits are well presented and help bring the stories of the prisoners to life.As you continue through the prison, you learn about the women who resisted colonial rule, the freedom fighters, and the revolutionary soldiers who dedicated themselves to the fight for Vietnamese independence. Their stories are both fascinating and humbling.The later sections focus on the prison’s use as a POW camp for captured American pilots during the Vietnam War and provide insight into this chapter of its history. Beyond this, the story of Hoa Lo continues through memorials and exhibits dedicated to those who fought for modern Vietnam.Visitors should dress appropriately, particularly when entering areas containing shrines and memorials. Shorts above the knee are not permitted, and it is important to remember that this remains a place of remembrance as much as a historical attraction.The museum is well laid out and easy to navigate, although be prepared to spend more time reading than walking. In a place with this much history, that’s certainly not a criticism.For anyone interested in history, Hoa Lo Prison offers an excellent opportunity to gain a deeper understanding of Vietnam’s past and a greater appreciation of the resilience of its people.Admission was 100,000 VND (£2.80) for two people, with an audio guide available for an additional 100,000 VND per person.Excellent value and a very worthwhile way to spend a couple of hours in Hanoi.
practical_tips: remember that this remains a place of remembrance

title: Must visit but might be one sided

The site recounts several harrowing episodes in Vietnamese history, from the French colonial period to the Vietnam War.The exhibition is clear and thoughtfully organized, making it easy to grasp the significance of what you are seeing. The museum effectively recreates the atmosphere experienced by prisoners, notably through the use of life-sized figures placed in reconstructed detention areas. The artifacts themselves are presented with restraint and honesty — few words are needed to convey the reality of their use.The captions accompanying the photographs are equally informative and provide helpful context throughout the visit.That said, I would approach the section on American imprisonment with some caution. author: Xem Số Mệnh
title: Hoa Lo Prison – A Haunting Remnant of Cruelty and the Unyielding Spirit of Revolutionaries
original_content: Visiting Hoa Lo Prison is not merely a historical excursion — it is an emotional reckoning. The moment I stepped inside, a chilling silence wrapped around me. It wasn’t the air that made me shiver, but the weight of suffering, resistance, and unspoken screams that still linger within these cold, oppressive walls.Built by the French colonists to incarcerate and break the will of Vietnamese patriots, Hoa Lo was designed as a living hell. Narrow, airless cells, heavy wooden shackles, and rusting iron bars speak of the torment inflicted. Instruments of torture — including the infamous guillotine — are preserved like grim witnesses to the brutality of a regime that sought to crush the human spirit through pain and fear.Yet amidst that horror, what struck me deepest was not just the cruelty, but the courage.As a traveler representing Xemsomenh.com, where we explore the fate, soul, and resilience of the Vietnamese people, I was deeply moved by how the revolutionaries transformed this prison into a cradle of strength and ideals. Names like Phan Boi Chau, Nguyen Duc Canh, and Nguyen Van Cu echo through the halls — not as victims, but as symbols of heroic resistance. Within these bleak cells, they turned darkness into light, turning torture chambers into classrooms, and nurturing hope in places meant to extinguish it.Hoa Lo is no longer just a museum. It is a place of remembrance — a shrine to sacrifice, and a testament to the iron will of those who laid the foundation for our independence. It reminds us that while colonists may have wielded chains and swords, they could not imprison the human spirit nor destroy the dream of freedom.Walking through these corridors, it is impossible not to feel humbled. You don’t just see history — you feel it. The pain is palpable, but so is the pride. Each rusted chain, each crude wooden door, tells a story that demands not only respect, but also reflection.At Xemsomenh.com, we believe that destiny is shaped not only by stars and numbers, but by the courage of those who dared to change their fate. Hoa Lo Prison is living proof. Here, fate was rewritten — not by surrender, but by sacrifice.If you come to Hanoi, don’t skip this place. Come with an open heart. Leave with a deeper understanding — not just of Vietnam’s painful past, but of the extraordinary spirit that rose from it.
drawbacks: The cruelty and brutality of the regime
The pain and suffering inflicted on the Vietnamese patriots
highlights: The courage and resilience of the revolutionaries
The transformation of the prison into a cradle of strength and ideals
The sacrifice and heroism of those who fought for independence
practical_tips: Leave with a deeper understanding of Vietnam's painful past and the extraordinary spirit that rose from it

The exhibition is mainly colonial, with instruments used for torture and a guillotine table with a blade attached, and there is a rather heavy atmosphere. It is impressive that the air conditioning crisis is bad for a lot of tourists, and it is so hot and humid that you might think it is a production.

author: AMsays
title: Light an incense stick to hopefully inspire a more peaceful future.
original_content: Sarcastically known as "Hanoi Hilton," this infamous prison was renowned for its harsh treatment of prisoners. French built in 1896; it is now mostly torn down and transformed into a museum with stark reminders of the era of its prominence. It was hard walking through there knowing some of the history which included the incarceration of Senator John McCain.  Originally the prison had 4 areas (A-D). Within those areas were the cramped cells, torture devices and the Guillotine Room. Today we see articles of oppression, the sewer used to escape and the POW exhibition area. Significant artifacts including haunting photos and prison objects. There’s newly created artwork and sculptures of prisoners. You can light an incense stick to hopefully inspire a more peaceful future. I did.

author: Deano1967
title: How to re-write history, Vietnamese style.
original_content: By all means visit the "Hanoi Hilton" but do your homework beforehand to learn the real stories of what went on in here because you certainly can't rely on the Vietnamese version of the truth being told.Making themselves out as latter-day saints, it's all the fault of the French and the Americans committing atrocities and torture against the valiant native population who were just freedom fighters.There isn't a single mention anywhere of what the Vietnamese did by way of torture to the American pilots who ended up here (do a Google search for "strappado" for one of the torture means, but you won't find a single reference to it in the totally one-sided presentation of history.We left feeling utterly at a loss because of the outright lies being told in this place. Yes, it's a Communist country but if you want Western money you're going to have to tell the truth because the truth is so very easy to find for those willing to see it.

author: joe v
title: "History" museum filled with falsehoods
original_content: As a museum on the history of Hoa Lo prison, there is a shocking lack of actual history. Instead the museum is dedicated to shameless propaganda for the Communist Party of Vietnam.The start of the museum showcases the horrors inflicted on Vietnamese prisoners when the museum was run by French colonials. You can walk through the inhumanely cramped rooms and see the barbarism of how prisoners were kept. Clearly the French built a nasty prison and committed numerous attrocities here and it would be a crime to continue it's use.However, skip forwards a few years, and the prison is now being used to house American POWs. Surely Americans being housed in the same prison must have also faced terrible conditions? They nicknamed the prison "Heartbreak Hotel," but no, according to the museum, American prisoners were treated like honored guests. They were free to enjoy Christmas feasts and games of basketball (as long as a cameraman was nearby to record for propaganda purposes).The museum that could be used to present history is now just a house of propoganda and untruths. This is somewhat unsurprising, as even during the war they concealed what was occurring here. Admiral Jeremiah Denton had to blink "torture" in Morse code while telling interviewers how great a time he was having for any information to get out.Tldr; The museum is preserved well and has a good setup, but any attempt at teaching history is overshadowed by posting blatant lies (that can be facts checked with a 10 second google search) all over the information boards
drawbacks: Shameless propaganda for the Communist Party of Vietnam
practical_tips: Skip the propaganda and focus on the history
Be aware of the biased information

author: Douglass Y
title: Harrowing history together
original_content: This wasn’t just another tourist stop; it was a raw dive into Vietnam’s harrowing history, told from a poignant Vietnamese perspective. The exhibits—photos, artifacts, and stories—pulled at our hearts in unexpected ways. We stood silently before rusted shackles, imagining lives once bound by them. It was somber yet enlightening, as if the walls whispered tales of resilience and pain. As a couple, we found ourselves reflecting deeply, discussing what freedom truly means. Some sections felt hard to digest, almost intrusive, but that’s the point—it forces you to remember, not forget. For all its emotional toll, Hoa Lo is unforgettable, leaving us with more questions than answers about humanity’s past mistakes.

author: James O
title: Eye opening demonstration of man's inhumanity to man
original_content: We visited mid-morning to avoid the tour crowds, and I would suggest the earlier the better, so as to experience the displays with the level of solitude it requires.I was astounded by the number of people who wouldn't pay a paltry fee for the self guided audio headset as it added so much clarity to the experience.It was shocking to see how a supposedly civilised country such as France treated their fellow humans, but then again, how many empires behaved in such a manor ? and how many countries still are today ?The displays were well laid out and numbered for ease of understanding with the audio  headset.I realise that this is Vietnam's story to tell, however, I thought it was a little cheapened by the constant maintenance of the party line through the French area when human emotion must have been to the fore of the poor Vietnamese, and the assertion that, in general, the American POWs were treated with such gentleness and compassion during that conflict. Obviously, the pictures and displays are authentic, however, I imagine selective portrayal was extensively used.I thought the narrative was weigted unnecessarily heavily in one direction, as what I assume would be a more accurate portrayal, would certainly be understandable to most people today.For me, both the story and site were lessened a little by such.I'm glad I went and would  recommend a visit to anyone visiting Ha Noi.Also, maybe it's just me, but I noticed a few people openly sobbing ??? Whilst its eye opening for sure, I certainly didn't achieve such emotion.
drawbacks: constant maintenance of the party line
narrative was weigted unnecessarily heavily in one direction

author: Voyage29672267144
title: Experience the Tour "Hanoi Essence: 6 Hours of Magic" - An Impressive Journey to Discover the Capital
original_content: Recently, I had the opportunity to join the tour “Hanoi Essence: 6 Hours of Magic” – a short but emotional and memorable journey to discover Hanoi. As someone who has participated in many tours, I was really impressed by the meticulousness and scientific arrangement of the schedule as well as the quality of service that the organizer provided.The tour started at 13:20 at Hoa Lo Prison – a famous historical site in the heart of Hanoi. Right from the gathering, I felt the professionalism when the tour guide briefly introduced the schedule and important notes. I was quite impressed with the way the staff took care of the tourists, from ensuring drinking water to welcoming them warmly. Hoa Lo Prison carries within it painful but proud historical stories. Under the guidance of the tour guide, each story and each artifact seemed to come alive before my eyes. Leaving Hoa Lo, the group quickly moved to Thang Long Imperial Citadel by comfortable and cool means of transport. The shuttle bus was very punctual, clean and fully equipped with drinking water for each passenger. At Thang Long Imperial Citadel, I felt like I was stepping into a space of the past, where the vestiges of ancient dynasties are still imprinted through each brick and each gate. The tour guide not only introduced historical information but also told interesting stories, making the tour not dry at all. After hours of exploring history, the group moved to Hanoi Old Quarter to enjoy the typical cuisine here. The time for cuisine was arranged reasonably, not too rushed. The tour suggested a few famous restaurants in the Old Quarter and I chose a small, pretty restaurant with typical dishes such as pho, bun, and spring rolls. Each dish had a strong Hanoi flavor, was fresh and delicious, and was served very attentively.In the late afternoon, the group experienced the feeling of sitting on a cyclo around Hoan Kiem Lake. This was probably the most romantic and memorable moment of the trip. When the city began to light up, Hoan Kiem Lake appeared sparkling with Turtle Tower and the bright red The Huc Bridge. Sitting on a cyclo, watching the narrow old streets, the street stalls, and the flow of people created a peaceful picture of Hanoi amidst the hustle and bustle of life.Next, the group stopped by Thang Long Water Puppet Theater to enjoy a traditional art performance. The wooden puppets were skillfully manipulated under the water, combined with traditional music to create an artistic space imbued with Vietnamese identity. The performances tell familiar yet captivating folk tales. The last stop on the journey is Indochine restaurant. The restaurant space is luxurious, cozy and the menu is diverse and attractive. I really like the attentive service of the staff here, always ready to meet all the guests' requests.Dinner took place in a comfortable, cheerful atmosphere. Delicious food, beautifully presented and especially a relaxing time after a long day of exploration.The tour ended at 19:30 and the tour guide did not forget to say goodbye and introduce other tours for those who want to explore Hanoi more deeply. Hanoi Essence: 6 Hours of Magic" is truly a short but extremely complete journey. From historical relics, cultural spaces to cuisine and art, all are arranged harmoniously and carefully. If you are looking for a tour to explore Hanoi in a short time but still full of experiences, do not hesitate to book this tour right away.

author: Phương Anh T
title: A Fascinating and Sobering Experience at Hoa Lo Prison
original_content: Visiting Hỏa Lò Prison in Hanoi was a truly eye-opening experience. As a tourist, I appreciated the well-preserved historical artifacts and the detailed information provided throughout the museum.What I liked:- The museum offers a balanced narrative about the prison's history, from its use during the French colonial period to its role in the Vietnam War.- The exhibits are engaging and immersive, with a mix of photographs, documents, and reconstructed prison cells that give a vivid sense of the harsh conditions faced by prisoners.- The storytelling was powerful, particularly the section on the resilience and determination of Vietnamese revolutionaries held there.- The air-conditioned interiors provided a comfortable environment for learning, even on a hot day in Hanoi.But I didn’t like something as:- Some parts of the museum felt a bit crowded, especially during peak visiting hours, which made it challenging to fully enjoy the exhibits.- While the displays were informative, I felt that certain narratives were a bit one-sided, particularly in the section dedicated to American POWs during the Vietnam War. Adding more perspectives would enrich the storytelling. Overall, Hỏa Lò Prison is a must-visit for history enthusiasts and anyone interested in understanding Vietnam’s complex past. It’s a sobering reminder of the struggles and sacrifices made during pivotal moments in history.

author: Ray Yantch
title: Better night markets in Vietnam
original_content: The market was the same as all the other night markets there wasn't as much food and with all the motorbikes cutting through we made it difficult to walk I would not recommend this one in Hanoi. The one in Da Lat was a lot better

author: Mohit B
title: Lots of people and a lot more vendors
original_content: Crowded but lots of stuff to buy! Don’t forget to bargain but be respectful. Most of them sell similar stuff but prices might vary

author: Jacky D
title: Bustling Market
original_content: Wonderful experience of the local market here. Amazing food n music to experience. Had fun interacting with the locals and knowing about their products.

author: ATH Theatre
title: Spacious but a Bit Rough Around the Edges
original_content: I visited Dong Xuan Market in Hanoi with my friends. The market has an old design, but it feels spacious and familiar. Inside, it looks quite nice, though the surrounding area is a bit dirty. This place mainly sells wholesale goods, so it’s hard to buy just one or two items. It’s a pity that the vendors weren’t very friendly. Still, it’s worth a visit to experience the atmosphere.
drawbacks: surrounding area is a bit dirty
highlights: worth a visit to experience the atmosphere

author: loonylou78
title: Night market.
original_content: Very large,busy but repetitive market.Great to wander along at the weekend.If you're lucky you can grab a bargain!Street food readily available too!

author: Shalini Lalwani
title: Great deals if you have the patience to crack it!
original_content: Huge walking market to be discovered on foot. Loads of food and things to be haggled on… colourful and vibrant street shops with great bargains.

author: Simon S
title: Hoi An Night Market
original_content: Really enjoyed a stroll through the night market in Hoi An. A good selection of merchandise. As you'll find throughout the world at night markets, some vendors were really pushy, others were good. Be prepared to say no thank you more than once at some stalls.
practical_tips: Be prepared to say no thank you more than once at some stalls

author: Matvl
title: Bustling market
original_content: The Night Market is great to explore. Sure mostly cheaper items, knock offs etc but this isn’t a market geared up for tourists. It was very busy. Plenty of food options too - both market stalls and small eating places that operate out of market times too. It’s definitely worth exploring if you’re in Hanoi over market opening days. Nice to combine with a walk around the lake too.
practical_tips: combine with a walk around the lake

author: Sharnee K
title: Atmosphere and food
original_content: The atmosphere was amazing and highly recommend for a look and great food choices but if you’re going for shopping it’s all the same things on repeat store  after store.
drawbacks: same things on repeat store after store

author: Thanh Xuan
title: Nơi mua sắm trải nghiệm tuyệt vời
original_content: Shopping at the night market was an unforgettable experience!The moment I stepped in, I was greeted by the colorful lights, the buzz of chatter, and the irresistible aroma of street food. Every corner was alive – with rows of stalls selling everything from handcrafted souvenirs to trendy fashion and quirky accessories. I found unique items I wouldn’t see anywhere else, and the best part? Bargaining with the friendly vendors made it all the more fun!There’s a kind of charm here you can’t find in big malls – it’s raw, real, and full of life. The energy, the people, the variety… if you’re in Hanoi (or Vietnam), don’t miss out on a night market walk – it’s more than just shopping, it’s a cultural adventure!

author: Willem B
title: Busy, busy market.
original_content: All markets in Vietnam seem alike, all items sold seem alike, but the experience is why I go the various markets. you see all kind of people trying to get the best deal, and that is what this market is all about. Very lively vibrant market, worth a try.
practical_tips: go to the market for the experience

author: Remi A
title: Okay experience
original_content: Nice but a little underwhelming when compared to other night markets. It does like variety in the goods being sold and some of the foods were not tasty. However, I will still recommend as it is a change in pace and something to do.
drawbacks: some of the foods were not tasty
highlights: variety in the goods being sold
a change in pace and something to do

author: corinne_prevost
title: HORROR
original_content: A night market where mopeds pass everywhere, nothing is controlled, an endless broom of mopeds that honk non-stop to pass. Prices are no more interesting than elsewhere

author: Kenlly Bowne
title: Overpriced and Too Crowded
original_content: The Hanoi Night Market is lively but overly crowded. Prices are quite high, especially for tourists, so be prepared to bargain. The atmosphere is fun, but the experience is not the best if you dislike large crowds. Worth a visit, but not a must-see.

author: akio9jp
title: Negotiating prices is imperative
original_content: The night market is held only on weekends (Friday, Saturday and Sunday) with traffic restrictions of approximately 700 meters from the rotary intersection on the north side of Hoan Kiem Lake to Dong Xuan Market.The area is packed with local citizens and tourists, selling a variety of goods such as clothing, accessories, household goods and souvenirs. However, there are many without price tags, and you basically have to negotiate a price to lose money, so you need wisdom and guts to get a good deal.
drawbacks: need to negotiate a price to lose money
highlights: packed with local citizens and tourists
practical_tips: need wisdom and guts to get a good deal

author: netnut2008
title: A nice change in the evening.
original_content: The Night Market is a nice change from the shops open during the day. Here you will find a lot and sometimes at significantly cheaper prices than during the day. However, the many fake brands have annoyed us a bit.

author: Keelyimps
title: Worth a visit, lots of nice things to buy.
original_content: Huge street market selling all sorts of stuff. Well worth going to and walking along looking at the different stalls. Grab yourself a bargain. 😄👏
practical_tips: Go and walk along looking at the different stalls

author: Louise
title: Worthwhile But Tourist Traps Lie Within
original_content: The first 50 or so meters of the market is great! However, the rest is the same - pretty much all sellers are selling the same products but it’s still worthwhile! You can get some great bargains, don’t pay more than 100k for a branded T shirt and 150k for a branded windbreaker - definitely lots of tourists traps here with sellers overcharging, just know your prices and you can get some great trinkets for back home.
drawbacks: sellers are selling the same products
highlights: can get some great trinkets for back home

author: BenZ
title: 100% Go Visit
original_content: If you want to visit a really good market visit this one in Hà Nội. There is so much to see and lots of bargains, it’s amazing to see how good the copies are they are literally 10/10. Amazes me how they do it, the market has a good buzz and always haggle. They will always give you a high price but most of the time you can get them down to 50%
drawbacks: They will always give you a high price

author: Sandrine F
title: A must do in Hanoi
original_content: Nice to see, great atmosphere, loads of good bargains. Perfect to buy souvenirs, do not hesitate to negotiate the price.
practical_tips: do not hesitate to negotiate the price

author: Rita N
title: Hanói night market, not to miss
original_content: Hanoi night market happens every friday, saturday and sunday. Hang Dao street is where you have to be. Busiest hour is between 19.00 and 20.30. I whas in Hanoi for 3 days and i found there all the best deals: under wear, sun glasses, sport wear (north face, Nike...), scarfs, souvenirs. No food strolls in this night market but in the streets around it. It is sure a "don't miss it" .
practical_tips: visit on Friday, Saturday, or Sunday

author: Sunil D
title: Great shopping experience in night market
original_content: great place to get some nice bargains for souvenirs and other stuff . the quality of clothes is good and this is one of the cheapest places in vietnam to shop ... YES... HCM is more expensive than this market
highlights: Cheapest place in Vietnam to shop
practical_tips: Go to this market for good bargains

author: Ros C
title: spectacular
original_content: exceptional a night visit must not miss The inhabitants are really welcoming Here you can eat and buy lots of fresh fruit
extracted_spaces: The inhabitants are really welcoming Here you can eat and buy lots of fresh fruit

author: Alessandro
title: Great for Evening Shopping
original_content: Characteristic Point of Sale where objects, clothes and food are sold. Famous brands Made in Vietnam are frequent for which the authenticity is doubtful. It remains open until about 11.30 pm Definitely worth a visit
drawbacks: doubtful authenticity of Made in Vietnam products

author: Rachelle C
title: Fun pedestrian zone, weekends in the evening
original_content: We kind of stumbled onto the night market in Old Town in Hanoi but were glad we did.  The lights were so much fun and the streets reserved for pedestrians  (finally no mopeds!) were filled with young families.  It was amazingly hot and humid in August, even at night, but we still had a great time.

author: RIchard035
title: Weekend night market
original_content: The night market in Hanoi takes place at the weekend and extends from Ho Hoan Kiem lake at one end along Hang Dao and Hang Duong streets. It a large market that seems to go on for ever. It is very well lit and seems very safe. We were there in the summer when the area around the lake is closed to traffic in the evening at weekends and the were many families with young children walking around. The market sells food, clothing, souvenirs, etc. Prices are cheap, particularly if you bargain. However, I found there seemed to be more items with fixed pricing than in other markets I have visited in Asia.

author: Julie M
title: Hanoi.
original_content: Due to the effects of the typhoon, the Yash Market has not been opened for 2 times. Follow schedule.
drawbacks: Due to the effects of the typhoon

author: Coyote-Travelerz
title: Pleasant
original_content: Compared to other night markets in Southeast Asia and Vietnam, this isn’t the best. Don’t let that discourage you from taking time out to enjoy the market. Each one is different and offers its own unique opportunities. We found wondering the streets and soaking up the atmosphere to be a very pleasant experience. It wasn’t too crowded (we didn’t feel like sardines) and we saw some interesting things on our stroll. It’s also a good opportunity to visit some of the historical places in the old section (like the gate or temples). As noted in other reviews, there are a lot of vendors selling knockoff products (which makes it a tacky experience) and not nearly as many street food vendors as you might see in other night markets.
drawbacks: not nearly as many street food vendors

author: these boots are made for walkin'
title: Tragic
original_content: Redundant (and oddly overpriced) fake garbage imported from China. The grossly underwhelming experience is tragically worsened by cranky retailers. I recommend a trip to Bangkok for anyone  interested in a good day/night market.
practical_tips: go to Bangkok for a good day/night market

author: D McNeish
title: Steer clear market
original_content: A market full of plastic junk  . Worst market I have ever been to . I Couldn’t leave quick enough. Not a pleasant experience.
drawbacks: Worst market I have ever been to

author: Skeets54
title: Average market for fake clothes
original_content: If you’ve never been to a night market before in any other part of Southeast Asia, you might think that this is really great however if you have been to other markets like those in Bangkok, Thailand or other parts of Thailand this market was quite poor in comparison. Firstly the street is not closed to motorbikes and they are still driving up and down incessantly whilst you were trying to shop which is really annoying. They should stop the street For All traffic including bikes. Secondly the stores are mainly clothing and fake goods which is fine if you want some counterfeit crocs handbags wallet belts and sportswear stuff but it wasn’t like other markets that had cute dresses or other types of interesting items. There were very little handcraft as well but the usual tat that you can find everywhere .Thirdly we found the market was significantly lacking in food options compared to other markets we’ve been to in Southeast Asia. There were a lot of reviews about the food so we came without eating hoping to to try a few things but we really couldn’t see anything apart from a few stools selling octopus tentacles and other things on a stick.  We were so disappointed by this market we thought that we went to early so then we went away and had some beers and came back again later in the night thinking that maybe more things would be open then however it was still exactly the same so all of the other reviews that we read about this market Were quite confusing. There were also very little places to sit and enjoy a drink or beer and watch the world go by all of the shops on the sidelines are clothing shops there’s only really one coffee shop but we saw that had a small balcony all in all probably one of the poorest, experiences.
drawbacks: motorbikes driving up and down the street
practical_tips: go to other markets in Southeast Asia

author: AJ2000
title: Fun night out with family of teenagers
original_content: So much fun with the family! Great for picking up some bargain clothing or cute souveniers. Gets very busy but is easy to navigate. Recommend finishing with a relaxing walk around the lake soaking up the atmosphere and enjoying some fun performances along the way. Also great after the intensity of the market.Teenage kids cut their teeth bargaining and picked up some decent bargains at the market (I think the stall owners were being kind!). We stopped at an ice cream stall on the lake during our walk which finished the night perfectly. Very squashy at the market and not recommended for prams, wheelchairs etc however plenty of space around the lake which would be wheelchair / pram friendly.
drawbacks: not recommended for prams, wheelchairs etc
highlights: great for picking up some bargain clothing or cute souveniers
relaxing walk around the lake soaking up the atmosphere and enjoying some fun performances

author: The Travelling Chef
title: A Must in Hanoi
original_content: Prepare for a pleasurable assault on the senses.If you love great food, street side grills of questionable tasty meats on a skewer, a bustling chaotic atmosphere, market stalls of counterfeit designer brands, garments, fruit and veg, fresh juice, toys, electronics just too many to list, live performances of traditional and modern music and pantomime, endless streets of packed bars and restaurants all inviting you in ,photo opportunities and a warm scenic walk around the lake.I highly recommend the night market to all travellers to experience.
highlights: warm scenic walk around the lake

author: Amy
title: Pocket Thieves
original_content: One of the better night market in Vietnam. Lots of vendors and activities. We got 15 toddler clothes set. 1 set (shirt & pant) for under $1 USA or 25k dong. Such a good bargain, I wish I got dresses too for my daughter, but we didn’t have room in our suitcase.Beware of pocket thieves! A guy tried to steal my phone in my bag not realizing I was holding on to my phone strap the whole time lol he was shocked and apologized for trying to steal my phone -_-

author: Varsha S
title: So much fun and fantastic prices!
original_content: During my final Sunday evening in Vietnam, I found myself wandering through the charming streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter and stumbled upon the Night Market. To my delight, I discovered that it offered everything I had purchased earlier, but at even better prices. In hindsight, I wish I had saved my shopping for this vibrant market experience. It's certainly a worthwhile addition to any itinerary, making it worth considering planning your trip around a Sunday evening in Hanoi.
highlights: Everything I had purchased earlier at even better prices
Consider planning your trip around a Sunday evening
practical_tips: Save shopping for Sunday evening in Hanoi

author: arpitam
title: Second to Danang night market
original_content: This is actually a busy thoroughfare throughout the day which turns into a night market after 7 in the evening. The flea market is good for tourists though preference would be to shop from the Dong Xuan wholesale market. The latter closes by 6pm. So if one has the evening only for shopping the night market is the good option.One may also club the Hoan Kiem lake - Nhoc Son Temple visit and finish off with night market.
drawbacks: preference would be to shop from the Dong Xuan wholesale market
practical_tips: go to the night market if you have the evening only for shopping
club the Hoan Kiem lake - Nhoc Son Temple visit and finish off with night market

author: Thanh N
title: Night Market in Hanoi
original_content: Great city to walk at night. They close off the streets Fri-Sun for pedestrians.  Much more chill than HCM but awesome all the same.

author: Arundev
title: It was an amazing experience in the night market
original_content: A must-visit place on your Vietnam trip. In fact, this is a weekend night market, open on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday from 6 p.m. to 11 p.m. Try to reach there around 6 p.m. and experience the arrangements for the night market. How they are changing a normal street into a night market where a lot of antique shops, street foods, dress shops, etc. are available. Vietnamese are very kind and always put a smile on their faces, which makes us more comfortable and gives us a feeling to spend more time there. Like everywhere, you need to bargain at some points. Sometimes, we may feel it is worth buying something at their cost. We stay there till the market closes. We had street food, bought many items, and talked to many local people. You need to add weekends to your trip to experience the night market. We put the night market on our last day for final shopping before going back home. This is a must-visit place to complete your Vietnam-Hanoi holiday.
drawbacks: Need to bargain at some points
highlights: Vietnamese are very kind and always put a smile on their faces
practical_tips: Try to reach there around 6 p.m.
Add weekends to your trip to experience the night market

author: Dan80_2013
