Children played and adults were sitting and relaxing

author: 944michelem
title: Overwhelming
original_content: We went to this market and we were a little disappointed. After being at street markets in Thailand and Peru, it was too many cheap knockoffs, clothes,shoes, glasses and bags! It wasn’t what we were expecting or hoping for. No local products available. Lots of food stalls and cheap beer everywhere and watch out for the motorbikes!
drawbacks: Lots of food stalls and cheap beer everywhere

author: Dawn H
title: Great for Shopaholics
original_content: The street has so many stalls - it goes on forever. Some close up by around 10pm.  Fantastic atmosphere.

author: Vivien
title: Crowded
original_content: It was quite crowded, and it was also raining when I was there, which made our trip to the night market less pleasant. There are a lot of shops and stalls by the road, but the prices are not like SUPER cheap, and I was expecting the place to have more night market food! I didn’t end up buying anything since it was not like really cheap compared to purchasing from an actual store and the items were not extremely attractive. But, I believe it’s nice to take a walk if you have nothing to do haha! I don’t think its necessarily a MUST go tourist spot, but I guess its a nice place to have a taste of the local Vietnamese culture. The streets were quite long and it is located next to the Bia Hoi Corner so you could go there and have a drink after walking the night market.
highlights: taste of the local Vietnamese culture
practical_tips: go there and have a drink after walking the night market

author: Phuketwergoing
title: Now this was fun. CHEAP CHEAP BIA HOI
original_content: Lots of stalls selling everything.  We got beer for around 50cents (AUD) a glass.Cold refreshing.....fantastic.Loved sitting on the little stools in the street watching people walk buy.Go.
highlights: Cold refreshing beer for 50 cents a glass
Sitting on little stools in the street watching people walk by

author: dejara
title: Bargain Paradise
original_content: Hanoi's Night Market is a nice place to buy all kind of souvenirs,clothing, shoes, T Shirts, electronics, cameras,headphones, glasses,jewelry and many items at bargain prices. Be aware that some electronics are not originals. I purchased a Bose headphone for $15 US dollars. It sells for over $150 in US. I found out later that it was a copy made in Pakistan, The  market is open only on week ends, ,
drawbacks: bought a copy of a Bose headphone

author: Emilygg
title: Funny
original_content: Had a fun time there shopping and eating. Busy but interesting. Found something cheap for kids back home.

author: Safemach
title: Loved it but not for the shopping
original_content: Amazing to see so many people having so much fun. I have no interest in buying stuff except the occasional mango in a bag, but I have never seen a city have so much fun with itself. Dancing, playing, fire eaters all sorts. Families, couples and everyone just enjoying themselves, great to see.Not for one second did I worry about my pockets or safety. Not a policeman in sight. Ok the guys pimping their neighbors daughter gets a bit annoying but they don’t pester.
drawbacks: guys pimping their neighbors daughter gets a bit annoying

author: sandymSeasister
title: A fun and vibey place
original_content: The weekend Market in the Old Quarter of Hanoi with a stroll around the lake, dinner at one of the many restaurants or coffee and ice cream at a pavement cafe is worth the time.  It’s fun and vibey and although I didn’t think prices were much better than you can barter for in the shops at the night market, it’s the ambience, the people-watching and the overall experience.  We actually stayed away from bargain hunting and rather watched street artists performing dance and music pieces, had a portrait done and were generally thoroughly entertained by the vibe strolling around the lake.
drawbacks: prices were much better than you can barter for in the shops at the night market

author: Robert M
title: Counterfeit Chinese tat.
original_content: This famous market thrives on selling counterfeit everything. Clothing, shoes, bags and top end electronic goods. Buy with humour, not with the view that you've bought a genuine bit of kit.The market is impressive though, taking up several streets, no stress busy atmosphere.We liked it, but we've seen enough fakes in our 3 week tour of Vietnam.

author: sally l
title: Plenty to see if you like markets
original_content: Markets aren’t really my thing. We went through the market on our way to a restaurant. It’s very busy with lots of stalls. Everything imaginable is on sale. In my opinion a lot of it isn’t particularly good but it’s horses for courses.

author: gordonj258
title: Sprawling market
original_content: The night market occupies many streets that have been closed to traffic. I found lots of things there that were cheap but also found that the stallholders were not prepared to really haggle as the base price is already exceptionally low.There are plenty of clothes, food and all the usual "souvenir" trinkets that you would expect. Very busy and an interesting way to spend a couple of hours.
drawbacks: stallholders were not prepared to really haggle
base price is already exceptionally low

author: Hardvision
title: Great bargains!
original_content: If you can accept that even if it says Abercombie & Fitch or Nike or Adidas, it is not the original and can bargain like crazy, this is the place. First of all the prices in local currency are crazy. Drop the last 3 zeros and divide by 23. That gives you the USD price. STart at about 20% of that price. In most of the places you can bargain and get the stuff for about 30% of the originally quoted price. Don't expect too much of quality. Quality does not come that cheap. The experience is worth it though. In the entire complex we saw only one shop which refused to lower the price and it was the most unusual of the shops over there.
drawbacks: Quality does not come that cheap
practical_tips: Start at about 20% of the original price
Bargain and get the stuff for about 30% of the originally quoted price

author: Heng How N
title: Special market
original_content: The market starts at 7pm and block traffic from using it. The place is converted to be place for many activities. It covers a big area from Hoan Kiem Lake towards the railway track.
highlights: converted to be place for many activities

author: Mark M
title: Haggle
original_content: At the weekend this street is closed off to traffic and stalls selling all kinds of merchandise are set up.We spent a good hour wandering the length of the market.Haggling is an absolute must. Offer 50% of the asking price to start the negotiations!
highlights: wandering the length of the market
practical_tips: offer 50% of the asking price to start negotiations

author: Rachael H
title: Busy, busy, busy
original_content: Really nice markets with lost of variety. There are both fake items and original items such as paintings. you are able to barter with the sellers to get more reasonable prices, really interesting place to visit

author: Traveller
title: Night market
original_content: The night market in Hanoi is only on the weekend, Friday - Sunday, 7pm-11pm.It’s one long strip of stalls in the middle of the road selling various things. One of the best things to experience in Hanoi.
highlights: one of the best things to experience in Hanoi

author: Edge Mirafuentes
title: Amazing food & Shopping
original_content: Open only on weekends from 7-10pm. This place is full of AMAZING food, entertainment & fun cheap haggle shopping!

author: carloscharmy
title: Just another SEA market
original_content: Coming from BKK I found nothing appealing in this market. Walked around it for 10 minutes and left. If  it is your 1st time in SEA give it a go.
drawbacks: walked around it for 10 minutes and left
practical_tips: If it is your 1st time in SEA give it a go

author: Becky & James
title: Typical Asian Night Market
original_content: I personally love the hustle and bustle of these markets - with the added fun of true Vietnamese bartering. Start bidding at 50% less than they ask for, and you can normally complete with a discount of about 30-40% off their price. Enjoy the bars and the old city gate whole you're in the vicinity.
practical_tips: Start bidding at 50% less than they ask for

author: b0rn2sh0p
title: Place for a bargain.
original_content: If you need cheap inflight carrier urgently, night market is the place for you. BigC market is twice more expensive than night market when it comes to carriers.
drawbacks: BigC market is twice more expensive
highlights: night market is the place for you
practical_tips: go to night market for cheap inflight carrier

author: iliketomoveandsee
title: Rubbish Market
original_content: I've been to many markets while travelling around Asia, and this was one of the worse. Crowded, scooters/motorbikes still riding down at speed even though the road is closed. The produce also isn't that great on the market - I wouldn't waste your time, to be honest.
drawbacks: scooters/motorbikes still riding down at speed even though the road is closed
The produce also isn't that great on the market

author: Bazza_752
title: Oversized china mall
original_content: Night market was essentially an oversized china mall... nice to see different environment - Lots of fake goods and knock-offs. I am not a fan of fake goods if you cannot afford the real item don’t buy a fake.
drawbacks: Lots of fake goods and knock-offs
practical_tips: Don't buy a fake if you cannot afford the real item

author: jongyungchoi99
title: nice
original_content: its long and having many gifts you can buy for your trip. and they are so cheap.you should see price which they write on paper and pay

author: fluffymonkey
title: Sunday family vibe
original_content: We visited the market on the Sunday evening, it was extremely busy so hold onto your kids if you have them! What really caught our eye though was the shear number of local families out with children enjoying a Sunday stroll and play around the top end of Hoam Kiem Lake. It was such an intoxicating atmosphere with kids playing the national sport (da cau), it involved kicking a weighted shuttlecock with feathers! and toddlers taking remote control cars for a spin (or rather the parents were controlling them!). Fascinating experience to see how Vietnamese go about their daily lives.
highlights: Shear number of local families out with children enjoying a Sunday stroll and play
Kids playing the national sport (da cau)
toddlers taking remote control cars for a spin
practical_tips: Hold onto your kids if you have them

author: Rui Jian Ng
title: Avoid Saturdays and go to shops with prices
original_content: Saturdays are very packed. If possible, head there on other days like Fri or Sun. Hectic place where you can get cheap clothes, shoes etc. Remember to bargain if possible but I reckon these days the vendors have placed their “best price” and hard to bargain down further. Word of advice: go for stalls with prices shown so you’ll at least have a benchmark and how to bargain. F&B: apart from the deep fried skewers, the sugarcane drink with lime is nice.
highlights: Sugarcane drink with lime is nice
practical_tips: Bargain at stalls with prices shown
Go for stalls with prices shown

author: webb s
title: Fun & crazy!
original_content: We were here on Sunday night. It was very crowded but exactly how I want it. There were many things to buy and many food joints to have some midnight snack. You might want a Vietnamese to accompany you or know enough language to get a raw deal. Still, everything is dirt cheap without a bargain. And the food is incredible as well.
drawbacks: You might want a Vietnamese to accompany you or know enough language to get a raw deal.

author: Siok H
title: Just feel the vibe
original_content: I went there to just feel the vibe but really got no patience to walk around with two young kids under my arm.  Goods are not interesting.

author: scubacol11
title: Shopping fun hustle and bustle
original_content: The market is open 19.00 to 23.00 Friday to Sunday nights,they close off several streets in the old town directly north of the lake so easy to find.The stalls are set up down the middle of the road in a back to back lay out so it is best to walk up one side then back down the other then you can look at the market stall and also the shop there too.My tip would be to walk all the way up and down first and get an idea of whats on sale and how many similar stalls and shops are selling the goods you may be interested in before you start shopping and haggling,a lot of the stalls are just extensions of the shops they are outside off and if they don"t have the exact item you want they will go to the shop and try to find it.Many of the stall are selling the usual fake designer goods but as long as you expect this you know they can"t be genuine by the low prices they are willing to sell them at,that said if you haggle you can get some bargains in clothes,shoes,artwork,ceramics,hiking wear and many souvenirs.There are many food stalls spread throughout the market so you can always get a snack if you are hungry but on some of the streets that adjoin the main avenue they are set out with many food and beer shops and there is a great atmosphere with plenty of choice of where to eat and drink and plenty of music to listen to.I found some prices far cheaper on the market than in the shops during the day as there was so much competition the vendors were willing to be haggled down more,Great fun if you enjoy the thrill of the haggling chase as I do,I see it as a participation sport and great fun and the stall and shop owners are not aggressive at all.Many people warn you to be careful with your wallets,but that"s the same anywhere in a market like this.
highlights: bargains in clothes, shoes, artwork, ceramics, hiking wear, and souvenirs
plenty of choice of where to eat and drink
practical_tips: walk all the way up and down first to get an idea of whats on sale

author: joanne h
title: your best option for a market
original_content: all the markets are now aimed a tourists, but this was the best out of all of them. If you are travelling in vietman Hanoi is much much cheaper than HO Chi Minh. They are not as aggressive at haggling as other Asian countries, its more like a reduction in price than a full blown haggle. We went at 8pm, still too early stalls just setting up.
highlights: best out of all of them

author: MMvet
title: Night markets
original_content: The usual hassle and bustle of markets.  Keep you wits about you and your valuables.  What was on offer can be purchased at any other market. We were fully prepared to barter but the sellers weren’t that interested in bartering, the would only knock a few dollars off the price or not at all, regardless of how much you may buy.
drawbacks: sellers weren’t that interested in bartering
would only knock a few dollars off the price or not at all
What was on offer can be purchased at any other market
practical_tips: Keep you wits about you and your valuables

author: Kalie L
title: Bit of bartering fun
original_content: Be prepared for banana shirts and matching shorts. All a bit of fun, we had a few beers on bir corner then went for a look. Quite good quality clothing, the usual bits and bobs like all markets. People were lovely. Watch your bag and keep it to the front of you, even the locals remind you....
drawbacks: Watch your bag and keep it to the front of you
practical_tips: Watch your bag and keep it to the front of you

author: antnChris
title: market okay but visit the lake as place is pumping
original_content: we visited night market Sunday night.they close off streets from 6.the markets nothing flash but we wandered down to lake where we saw amazing lights,  musicians , entertainment the kids out on the remote controlled cop cars tanks and diggers.great atmosphere and a wonderful walk.

author: Bhat P T
title: a nice experience
original_content: I was alone and could wander all the places  just out of curiosity. Since I don't eat meat or any non-veg items, I did not get a chance to enjoy street food. But I had nice cut fruits and sugarcane juice with a lot of ice. I could not resist the temptation, though worried about the quality and effect on my stomach.There are plenty of shops mostly selling cheap Chinese items. But I found a  few shops where they have put " Made in Vietnam" board and some stuff especially cloth for kids were good. Over all nice place to kill time. Loud music from Bars all over, people sitting on red plastic stools  and enjoying their drink and food. Not recommended for family. Couple is ok.

author: Alice M
title: Very hectic
original_content: The atmosphere of this place was very hectic. There were tons of shops and stalls selling fake brand clothing and shoes, as well as jewelry and some cheap, touristy clothes, like fruit shirts and elephant pants. Most of the places were pretty much the same, and just about everything was cheap and tacky. I didn't buy much because the clothing wasn't good quality and I was concerned about the origins of those clothes, I imagine their production involves a lot of underpaid, badly treated, overworked workers, potentially even slavery.
extracted_spaces: stalls selling fake brand clothing and shoes
drawbacks: concerned about the origins of those clothes
practical_tips: go early to avoid the crowds
be cautious of the quality and origins of the products

author: wanderlust_rambler
title: Just like any other night market in SEA
original_content: Market street is quite long but in the end hey all sell similar stuff. It gets very hot and humid fast and you walk along in the crowd. Full of tourists but not many items that interested us.Found that the shops nearby sold better quality goods. Don’t forget to haggle.
drawbacks: not many items that interested us
highlights: shops nearby sold better quality goods

author: Isabella B
title: Horror behind the facade of cheap goods
original_content: My partner and I went to the market and warn families not to come here.Behind the facade of glimmering lights and cheap goods is a horrific image. We witnessed a disfigured woman (not born with those disfigurements) crawling on her hands ( of which had been taken off so were just stumps) and knees attached like a dog on a leash to a pram full of heavy items, pushing a weighed down bucket with her head. A toddler was tied to her side. This woman crawled the whole length of the market on her bare skin. meanwhile we noticed shady looking men watching her on motorbikes, we assume to ensure nobody interfered. This is one of the most horrific sights I have seen in my life. Be warned this is not a sight for children and I’m horrified at what we saw. Absolutely terrible I cannot imagine the horrible life of this women, her fate is one which I don’t believe uncommon. Please be careful
drawbacks: disfigured woman crawling on her hands and knees
shady looking men watching her on motorbikes
practical_tips: warn families not to come here

author: Anne C
title: Go for the food, not the goods.
original_content: It was very crowded and the goods for sale are made in china, not vietnam. this place is not for tourists if you want to buy souvenirs. But the FOOD is excellent. street food everywhere. i would go here for  the food, not the goods.
drawbacks: goods for sale are made in china, not vietnam
not for tourists if you want to buy souvenirs
practical_tips: go here for the food, not the goods

author: Michelle Juul
title: Something you have to try
original_content: Nice to experience; a bit hectic and very busy. However, you don't spend alot of money, because you get "full" very fast.

author: Derek L
title: Nightly market visit
original_content: They block the roads off to cars, there are only a few scooters allowed through as well. Overall there was a lot of souvenirs to buy from here. It started to rain a little so bring an umbrella because there is little coverage. Everything from rings, shoes, food, clothes and knickknacks.

author: kisha m
title: Best of Night Market Experience
original_content: We were lucky enough to visit during the  festival and it was beautiful to see all the lighted boats and lanterns on the water. Worth a visit but be prepared for crowds. Still we hardly ever waited to order or eat at the restaurants or street vendors.

author: Jean-Emmanuel R
title: Somewhat mixed review
original_content: Very large night market that gave us a mixed impression. There is a good atmosphere there and it is pleasant to look at the different stalls.On the other hand, the choice for dining is very limited compared to the night markets we visited during our vacation in Malaysia in 2025. Here, you should expect a lot of clothes, jewelry, and souvenirs for tourists. The stalls sell roughly the same items (inexpensive, it is true) and in the end, there is nothing very authentic.Furthermore, the space to move around is very limited and unfortunately, scooters continue to drive in the street. I dare not imagine the chaos in high season.
highlights: pleasant to look at different stalls
practical_tips: expect a lot of clothes, jewelry, and souvenirs
be prepared for chaos in high season

author: Chrissie H
title: Fun shopping experience-bring cash!
original_content: Lots of great clothes, shoes and souvenirs and super fun atmosphere. Don’t forget to bargain and take cash :)

author: Travel Girl GR
title: You must be a weekend in Hanoi
original_content: The night market is held on the weekend only on the main street.You'll find everything, clothes, shoes, bags, souvenirs, food...

author: Rimjhim R
title: Awesome
original_content: Amazing vibes and goves the feel of vibrant Hanoi

author: thila2015
title: Safe, careful and comfortable.
original_content: Can get lots of stuff and souvenirs with reasonable price.

author: Jatin V
title: Hanoi taxi fraud
original_content: I have been to so many countries in europe and asia ...but in  hanoi i was told that there are so many pickpocketers and fraud.. i had terrible fraud experience in night matket grab taxi scam.. i took taxi from night market to my hotel ..that was showing grab lebel on the taxi...so i trusted...but when the driver dropped us ..He insisted to pay me without going out of the car and turned on blue light...and when i payed exact amount, he denied that it is not and asked me to show me my purse so he can help...and in the fraction of seconds he took big notes and put on the floor...and i caught him and he told me that accidentally fell ...and i saved my money..but that was the first experience in my life of this kind of fraud..
practical_tips: Verify the taxi's identity before paying

author: Jacqueline
title: If you enjoy markets, you'll love this.
original_content: We walked through the market but as markets and crowds aren't really our thing, it wasn't really for us.

author: Ray Yantch
title: Better night markets in Vietnam
original_content: The market was the same as all the other night markets there wasn't as much food and with all the motorbikes cutting through we made it difficult to walk I would not recommend this one in Hanoi. The one in Da Lat was a lot better

author: Mohit B
title: Lots of people and a lot more vendors
original_content: Crowded but lots of stuff to buy! Don’t forget to bargain but be respectful. Most of them sell similar stuff but prices might vary

author: Jacky D
title: Bustling Market
original_content: Wonderful experience of the local market here. Amazing food n music to experience. Had fun interacting with the locals and knowing about their products.

author: ATH Theatre
title: Spacious but a Bit Rough Around the Edges
original_content: I visited Dong Xuan Market in Hanoi with my friends. The market has an old design, but it feels spacious and familiar. Inside, it looks quite nice, though the surrounding area is a bit dirty. This place mainly sells wholesale goods, so it’s hard to buy just one or two items. It’s a pity that the vendors weren’t very friendly. Still, it’s worth a visit to experience the atmosphere.
drawbacks: surrounding area is a bit dirty
highlights: worth a visit to experience the atmosphere

author: loonylou78
title: Night market.
original_content: Very large,busy but repetitive market.Great to wander along at the weekend.If you're lucky you can grab a bargain!Street food readily available too!

author: Shalini Lalwani
title: Great deals if you have the patience to crack it!
original_content: Huge walking market to be discovered on foot. Loads of food and things to be haggled on… colourful and vibrant street shops with great bargains.

author: Simon S
title: Hoi An Night Market
original_content: Really enjoyed a stroll through the night market in Hoi An. A good selection of merchandise. As you'll find throughout the world at night markets, some vendors were really pushy, others were good. Be prepared to say no thank you more than once at some stalls.
practical_tips: Be prepared to say no thank you more than once at some stalls

author: Matvl
title: Bustling market
original_content: The Night Market is great to explore. Sure mostly cheaper items, knock offs etc but this isn’t a market geared up for tourists. It was very busy. Plenty of food options too - both market stalls and small eating places that operate out of market times too. It’s definitely worth exploring if you’re in Hanoi over market opening days. Nice to combine with a walk around the lake too.
practical_tips: combine with a walk around the lake

author: Sharnee K
title: Atmosphere and food
original_content: The atmosphere was amazing and highly recommend for a look and great food choices but if you’re going for shopping it’s all the same things on repeat store  after store.
drawbacks: same things on repeat store after store

author: Thanh Xuan
title: Nơi mua sắm trải nghiệm tuyệt vời
original_content: Shopping at the night market was an unforgettable experience!The moment I stepped in, I was greeted by the colorful lights, the buzz of chatter, and the irresistible aroma of street food. Every corner was alive – with rows of stalls selling everything from handcrafted souvenirs to trendy fashion and quirky accessories. I found unique items I wouldn’t see anywhere else, and the best part? Bargaining with the friendly vendors made it all the more fun!There’s a kind of charm here you can’t find in big malls – it’s raw, real, and full of life. The energy, the people, the variety… if you’re in Hanoi (or Vietnam), don’t miss out on a night market walk – it’s more than just shopping, it’s a cultural adventure!

author: Willem B
title: Busy, busy market.
original_content: All markets in Vietnam seem alike, all items sold seem alike, but the experience is why I go the various markets. you see all kind of people trying to get the best deal, and that is what this market is all about. Very lively vibrant market, worth a try.
practical_tips: go to the market for the experience

author: Remi A
title: Okay experience
original_content: Nice but a little underwhelming when compared to other night markets. It does like variety in the goods being sold and some of the foods were not tasty. However, I will still recommend as it is a change in pace and something to do.
drawbacks: some of the foods were not tasty
highlights: variety in the goods being sold
a change in pace and something to do

author: corinne_prevost
title: HORROR
original_content: A night market where mopeds pass everywhere, nothing is controlled, an endless broom of mopeds that honk non-stop to pass. Prices are no more interesting than elsewhere

author: Kenlly Bowne
title: Overpriced and Too Crowded
original_content: The Hanoi Night Market is lively but overly crowded. Prices are quite high, especially for tourists, so be prepared to bargain. The atmosphere is fun, but the experience is not the best if you dislike large crowds. Worth a visit, but not a must-see.

author: akio9jp
title: Negotiating prices is imperative
original_content: The night market is held only on weekends (Friday, Saturday and Sunday) with traffic restrictions of approximately 700 meters from the rotary intersection on the north side of Hoan Kiem Lake to Dong Xuan Market.The area is packed with local citizens and tourists, selling a variety of goods such as clothing, accessories, household goods and souvenirs. However, there are many without price tags, and you basically have to negotiate a price to lose money, so you need wisdom and guts to get a good deal.
drawbacks: need to negotiate a price to lose money
highlights: packed with local citizens and tourists
practical_tips: need wisdom and guts to get a good deal

author: netnut2008
title: A nice change in the evening.
original_content: The Night Market is a nice change from the shops open during the day. Here you will find a lot and sometimes at significantly cheaper prices than during the day. However, the many fake brands have annoyed us a bit.

author: Keelyimps
title: Worth a visit, lots of nice things to buy.
original_content: Huge street market selling all sorts of stuff. Well worth going to and walking along looking at the different stalls. Grab yourself a bargain. 😄👏
practical_tips: Go and walk along looking at the different stalls

author: Louise
title: Worthwhile But Tourist Traps Lie Within
original_content: The first 50 or so meters of the market is great! However, the rest is the same - pretty much all sellers are selling the same products but it’s still worthwhile! You can get some great bargains, don’t pay more than 100k for a branded T shirt and 150k for a branded windbreaker - definitely lots of tourists traps here with sellers overcharging, just know your prices and you can get some great trinkets for back home.
drawbacks: sellers are selling the same products
highlights: can get some great trinkets for back home

author: BenZ
title: 100% Go Visit
original_content: If you want to visit a really good market visit this one in Hà Nội. There is so much to see and lots of bargains, it’s amazing to see how good the copies are they are literally 10/10. Amazes me how they do it, the market has a good buzz and always haggle. They will always give you a high price but most of the time you can get them down to 50%
drawbacks: They will always give you a high price

author: Sandrine F
title: A must do in Hanoi
original_content: Nice to see, great atmosphere, loads of good bargains. Perfect to buy souvenirs, do not hesitate to negotiate the price.
practical_tips: do not hesitate to negotiate the price

author: Rita N
title: Hanói night market, not to miss
original_content: Hanoi night market happens every friday, saturday and sunday. Hang Dao street is where you have to be. Busiest hour is between 19.00 and 20.30. I whas in Hanoi for 3 days and i found there all the best deals: under wear, sun glasses, sport wear (north face, Nike...), scarfs, souvenirs. No food strolls in this night market but in the streets around it. It is sure a "don't miss it" .
practical_tips: visit on Friday, Saturday, or Sunday

author: Sunil D
title: Great shopping experience in night market
original_content: great place to get some nice bargains for souvenirs and other stuff . the quality of clothes is good and this is one of the cheapest places in vietnam to shop ... YES... HCM is more expensive than this market
highlights: Cheapest place in Vietnam to shop
practical_tips: Go to this market for good bargains

author: Ros C
title: spectacular
original_content: exceptional a night visit must not miss The inhabitants are really welcoming Here you can eat and buy lots of fresh fruit
extracted_spaces: The inhabitants are really welcoming Here you can eat and buy lots of fresh fruit

author: Alessandro
title: Great for Evening Shopping
original_content: Characteristic Point of Sale where objects, clothes and food are sold. Famous brands Made in Vietnam are frequent for which the authenticity is doubtful. It remains open until about 11.30 pm Definitely worth a visit
drawbacks: doubtful authenticity of Made in Vietnam products

author: Rachelle C
title: Fun pedestrian zone, weekends in the evening
original_content: We kind of stumbled onto the night market in Old Town in Hanoi but were glad we did.  The lights were so much fun and the streets reserved for pedestrians  (finally no mopeds!) were filled with young families.  It was amazingly hot and humid in August, even at night, but we still had a great time.

author: RIchard035
title: Weekend night market
original_content: The night market in Hanoi takes place at the weekend and extends from Ho Hoan Kiem lake at one end along Hang Dao and Hang Duong streets. It a large market that seems to go on for ever. It is very well lit and seems very safe. We were there in the summer when the area around the lake is closed to traffic in the evening at weekends and the were many families with young children walking around. The market sells food, clothing, souvenirs, etc. Prices are cheap, particularly if you bargain. However, I found there seemed to be more items with fixed pricing than in other markets I have visited in Asia.

author: Julie M
title: Hanoi.
original_content: Due to the effects of the typhoon, the Yash Market has not been opened for 2 times. Follow schedule.
drawbacks: Due to the effects of the typhoon

author: Coyote-Travelerz
title: Pleasant
original_content: Compared to other night markets in Southeast Asia and Vietnam, this isn’t the best. Don’t let that discourage you from taking time out to enjoy the market. Each one is different and offers its own unique opportunities. We found wondering the streets and soaking up the atmosphere to be a very pleasant experience. It wasn’t too crowded (we didn’t feel like sardines) and we saw some interesting things on our stroll. It’s also a good opportunity to visit some of the historical places in the old section (like the gate or temples). As noted in other reviews, there are a lot of vendors selling knockoff products (which makes it a tacky experience) and not nearly as many street food vendors as you might see in other night markets.
drawbacks: not nearly as many street food vendors

author: these boots are made for walkin'
title: Tragic
original_content: Redundant (and oddly overpriced) fake garbage imported from China. The grossly underwhelming experience is tragically worsened by cranky retailers. I recommend a trip to Bangkok for anyone  interested in a good day/night market.
practical_tips: go to Bangkok for a good day/night market

author: D McNeish
title: Steer clear market
original_content: A market full of plastic junk  . Worst market I have ever been to . I Couldn’t leave quick enough. Not a pleasant experience.
drawbacks: Worst market I have ever been to

author: Skeets54
title: Average market for fake clothes
original_content: If you’ve never been to a night market before in any other part of Southeast Asia, you might think that this is really great however if you have been to other markets like those in Bangkok, Thailand or other parts of Thailand this market was quite poor in comparison. Firstly the street is not closed to motorbikes and they are still driving up and down incessantly whilst you were trying to shop which is really annoying. They should stop the street For All traffic including bikes. Secondly the stores are mainly clothing and fake goods which is fine if you want some counterfeit crocs handbags wallet belts and sportswear stuff but it wasn’t like other markets that had cute dresses or other types of interesting items. There were very little handcraft as well but the usual tat that you can find everywhere .Thirdly we found the market was significantly lacking in food options compared to other markets we’ve been to in Southeast Asia. There were a lot of reviews about the food so we came without eating hoping to to try a few things but we really couldn’t see anything apart from a few stools selling octopus tentacles and other things on a stick.  We were so disappointed by this market we thought that we went to early so then we went away and had some beers and came back again later in the night thinking that maybe more things would be open then however it was still exactly the same so all of the other reviews that we read about this market Were quite confusing. There were also very little places to sit and enjoy a drink or beer and watch the world go by all of the shops on the sidelines are clothing shops there’s only really one coffee shop but we saw that had a small balcony all in all probably one of the poorest, experiences.
drawbacks: motorbikes driving up and down the street
practical_tips: go to other markets in Southeast Asia

author: AJ2000
title: Fun night out with family of teenagers
original_content: So much fun with the family! Great for picking up some bargain clothing or cute souveniers. Gets very busy but is easy to navigate. Recommend finishing with a relaxing walk around the lake soaking up the atmosphere and enjoying some fun performances along the way. Also great after the intensity of the market.Teenage kids cut their teeth bargaining and picked up some decent bargains at the market (I think the stall owners were being kind!). We stopped at an ice cream stall on the lake during our walk which finished the night perfectly. Very squashy at the market and not recommended for prams, wheelchairs etc however plenty of space around the lake which would be wheelchair / pram friendly.
drawbacks: not recommended for prams, wheelchairs etc
highlights: great for picking up some bargain clothing or cute souveniers
relaxing walk around the lake soaking up the atmosphere and enjoying some fun performances

author: The Travelling Chef
title: A Must in Hanoi
original_content: Prepare for a pleasurable assault on the senses.If you love great food, street side grills of questionable tasty meats on a skewer, a bustling chaotic atmosphere, market stalls of counterfeit designer brands, garments, fruit and veg, fresh juice, toys, electronics just too many to list, live performances of traditional and modern music and pantomime, endless streets of packed bars and restaurants all inviting you in ,photo opportunities and a warm scenic walk around the lake.I highly recommend the night market to all travellers to experience.
highlights: warm scenic walk around the lake

author: Amy
title: Pocket Thieves
original_content: One of the better night market in Vietnam. Lots of vendors and activities. We got 15 toddler clothes set. 1 set (shirt & pant) for under $1 USA or 25k dong. Such a good bargain, I wish I got dresses too for my daughter, but we didn’t have room in our suitcase.Beware of pocket thieves! A guy tried to steal my phone in my bag not realizing I was holding on to my phone strap the whole time lol he was shocked and apologized for trying to steal my phone -_-

author: Varsha S
title: So much fun and fantastic prices!
original_content: During my final Sunday evening in Vietnam, I found myself wandering through the charming streets of Hanoi's Old Quarter and stumbled upon the Night Market. To my delight, I discovered that it offered everything I had purchased earlier, but at even better prices. In hindsight, I wish I had saved my shopping for this vibrant market experience. It's certainly a worthwhile addition to any itinerary, making it worth considering planning your trip around a Sunday evening in Hanoi.
highlights: Everything I had purchased earlier at even better prices
Consider planning your trip around a Sunday evening
practical_tips: Save shopping for Sunday evening in Hanoi

author: arpitam
title: Second to Danang night market
original_content: This is actually a busy thoroughfare throughout the day which turns into a night market after 7 in the evening. The flea market is good for tourists though preference would be to shop from the Dong Xuan wholesale market. The latter closes by 6pm. So if one has the evening only for shopping the night market is the good option.One may also club the Hoan Kiem lake - Nhoc Son Temple visit and finish off with night market.
drawbacks: preference would be to shop from the Dong Xuan wholesale market
practical_tips: go to the night market if you have the evening only for shopping
club the Hoan Kiem lake - Nhoc Son Temple visit and finish off with night market

author: Thanh N
title: Night Market in Hanoi
original_content: Great city to walk at night. They close off the streets Fri-Sun for pedestrians.  Much more chill than HCM but awesome all the same.

author: Arundev
title: It was an amazing experience in the night market
original_content: A must-visit place on your Vietnam trip. In fact, this is a weekend night market, open on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday from 6 p.m. to 11 p.m. Try to reach there around 6 p.m. and experience the arrangements for the night market. How they are changing a normal street into a night market where a lot of antique shops, street foods, dress shops, etc. are available. Vietnamese are very kind and always put a smile on their faces, which makes us more comfortable and gives us a feeling to spend more time there. Like everywhere, you need to bargain at some points. Sometimes, we may feel it is worth buying something at their cost. We stay there till the market closes. We had street food, bought many items, and talked to many local people. You need to add weekends to your trip to experience the night market. We put the night market on our last day for final shopping before going back home. This is a must-visit place to complete your Vietnam-Hanoi holiday.
drawbacks: Need to bargain at some points
highlights: Vietnamese are very kind and always put a smile on their faces
practical_tips: Try to reach there around 6 p.m.
Add weekends to your trip to experience the night market

author: Dan80_2013
title: A large night market, good but nothing more
original_content: This remains to be done when you pass through Hanoi even if it is essentially the same items that the neighborhood stores display on stalls (clothes, shoes, etc.) and a lot of trinkets... Too bad there are no very little street food.People and a lot of “xe om” (two-wheel motors) who take the same single path of walkers. Less pleasant (night market not as good as other night markets in Vietnam...) but to do quickly once to see Hanoi.
drawbacks: night market not as good as other night markets in Vietnam

author: Vijay
title: nice long night 🌙 market
original_content: very nice market comparing other countries, had great time enjoyed bargaining ,u can buy souvenir, cloth ,and more made in vietnam items
highlights: can buy souvenir, cloth, and more made in Vietnam items

author: Taryn W
title: It was okay
original_content: honestly not a lot to say about the night market, go expecting to spend money even if you don't need anything or want anything. These lovely people know how to suck you in for a 'bargain'
drawbacks: These lovely people know how to suck you in for a 'bargain'
practical_tips: go expecting to spend money even if you don't need anything or want anything

author: Jenny Nguyen
title: Night Market
original_content: There are not too many options for shopping but the atmosphere is important when you go to the night market in Hanoi. Remember to bargain and be careful of pickpockets

author: Sarah
title: Awful night market
original_content: This night market is only held on weekends, but there was nothing I wanted there. It was winter, so there were a lot of shoes, socks, and winter clothes, which didn't interest me. More than anything, I was scared of the motorbikes rushing towards me, so I couldn't calmly look at it. I wish they would regulate motorbikes as well as cars. There were some interesting street food stalls nearby, which I found more interesting.
practical_tips: regulate motorbikes as well as cars

author: mayccm2018
title: Night market
original_content: Convenient location.   Lots of the stalls and numerous merchandises that you could purchase.   Prices were not very cheap.   Bargaining was necessary.  However, it was a great experience to visit Hanoi's night market.

author: Paperlapeipul
title: Mass gathering
original_content: Lots of people, lots of crowds and ten thousand things that nobody needs. You can hardly put one foot in front of the other.

author: Michael T
title: Lively Night Market
original_content: We were walking back to our hotel which was in the Hanoi Old Quarter after dinner at Bun Cha Ta restaurant.Along the way we passed by a busy pedestrianised area which was the night market. I could not remember the name of the street. It was a Friday evening. The streets were closed to traffic. Vendors set up stalls selling clothings, souvenirs, food, paintings etc. It was a lively place.The most prominent and most brightly lit building was the Ham Ca Map (which means teeth of the shark). That appeared to be the most photogenic and sought after spot for that instagrammable shot.The weather was cool that evening. We had so much fun just being outdoor and wandering around (when you don’t have to worry about motorbikes circling round you).
highlights: fun just being outdoor and wandering around

author: AJ2000
title: Average market, enjoyable lake walk away from the stalls.
original_content: This was pretty convenient for shopping but only if you already want to buy things. Our teenagers were happy expanding their wardrobe at good prices. Agree with others it is repetitive and a few stalls close by the lake are probably enough before it's all the same.Best value is in keeping it short and finishing off with a beautiful walk around the lake where the vendors are gone and is filled with activities and shows instead, all free and family friendly. A completely different and relaxed vibe! We had also been warned about pick pockets and shady vendors in the market area. I got ripped off like others! Someone recommended have lots of small change and only give exact money and this is fantastic advice. Heaps of chancers around.Is extremely crowded at the market, mayhem in the streets where the traffic is blocked, but really joyful around the lake.
practical_tips: finish off with a walk around the lake

author: Al37_11
title: A walk to take whether you have something to buy or not.
original_content: The street is occupied in its center by stalls and passers-by wander on each side. The approximately 2 km long market is held every weekend on Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays from 7 p.m.There you can find clothes, shoes, souvenirs, handicrafts and everyday items, most often at relatively affordable prices. On some stands it is possible to haggle, but not on all!It is also possible to eat there.There are crowds especially as the two side passages are not very wide.
extracted_times: every weekend on Fridays, Saturdays and Sundays

author: JnVSydney
title: Fave outing.....
original_content: This clearly, was our fave outing in old town Hanoi, 9for shopping) as the streets are closed and you can browse in relative piece away from, the hustle and bustle of the traffic, avoiding the infernal beeping, and craziness.The market itself is quite fun, everything you could possibly want concentrated in one area, a lot of the stalls are actually an extension of the shops that line the closed street which, is quite long, (extending from Dong kinh Nghia Thuc square to the Dong Xuan market),  we did most of our shopping here, to be frank at these prices, to question the authenticity is a bit naive.
practical_tips: Go to Old Town Hanoi for shopping

author: Abhishek
title: Better options, higher prices.
original_content: The night market is a celebration of everything that Hanoi has to offer. It takes place on Saturday and Sunday from 8 pm to 11 pm. However, prices on Sunday are better than that on Sunday. However, the prices you get on normal days in shop are better and in fact, the night market prices were quoted on the higher side. You must bargain a lot and not hope for anything authentic.
drawbacks: night market prices were quoted on the higher side
highlights: celebration of everything that Hanoi has to offer
practical_tips: go on normal days for better prices

author: duuuudi
title: Amazing
original_content: A very nice place to shop and buy clothes and gifts. We will find what you like at a good price after bargaining. Of course, it stays open until late at night. You will not be able to complete it in one night.
extracted_spaces: a very nice place to shop
drawbacks: You will not be able to complete it in one night.
highlights: find what you like at a good price after bargaining

author: Mark D
title: Not like Night Market in other Asian Cities
original_content: I thought there would be more food stalls at the weekend night market, but there was not. Just the same old stuff you can find everywhere around old town. Not really worth the hassle.
drawbacks: Just the same old stuff you can find everywhere

author: davelori
title: Seen it once no need to go back
original_content: First of all watch out for people who pick pocket. A lot of counterfeit things. Super busy, super hot. Just my opinion
practical_tips: watch out for people who pick pocket

author: dpghatak
title: Night market for all
original_content: A whole Street is shut down on Saturday & Sunday from 8 PM onwards. The street is opposite to Lake and Domino's. Series of stalls selling pin to elephant. Prices are not very low. Makes a late start and hence you should be prepared for a late night experience. I found it warming up at 9 PM and hence didnt hang around late night. All in all can pick up the experience but don't expect to make a killing
highlights: Series of stalls selling pin to elephant
practical_tips: Don't expect to make a killing

author: Chessie O
title: Visit store 33!
original_content: Visit store 33 if you go! Super friendly guy, great deals and lovely jewellery. Found my new favourite necklace that I’ll treasure forever. Thank you! Chessie and Joe

author: Aman Mehra
title: Shop your heart out and bargain!
original_content: We shopped our hearts out here. It's pretty big. Loads of shops with interesting stuff. Must visit to shop if you want shoes, clothes, bags, toys etc.
highlights: loads of shops with interesting stuff
practical_tips: go if you want shoes, clothes, bags, toys etc.

author: Sera-sgd
title: Na
original_content: Night market was so so. Selling the same stuff as the stores. Beware the donut lady seller pushing a trolley. She willRipped you off seeing you are a tourist
drawbacks: Selling the same stuff as the stores
Ripped you off seeing you are a tourist
practical_tips: Beware the donut lady seller pushing a trolley

author: Scott W
title: Hanoi Night Markets
original_content: If you're after a deal on clothes or souvenirs, then this is the place to go with lots of stalls and plenty of bargains on offer.
practical_tips: go here for deals on clothes or souvenirs

author: David D
title: Cheap market stalls not much different from what is in the shops
original_content: The night market is large but really no different from the many markets we have visited in Europe. Shops are open either side of the market and if anything we bought more from these shops than the stalls. It was raining when we went and once or twice the stall holders had to clear the collected water from the roof of the stall, we got wetter from that than the rain. The other issue is that the motorcyclists are allowed up both sides of the stalls , just have to keep your wits about you. Had to go but not the highlight of our Hanoi stay
drawbacks: stalls had to clear water from roof
motorcyclists allowed up both sides of stalls
got wetter from stall water than rain

author: Jobearoundtheglobe
title: Some bargains to be had! All in all great fun.
original_content: Not the 4000 stalls that you read online. Lots of things for sale but local shops around it will be cheaper. No consistency in the prices and you can often negotiate well in excess of 50% off (despite the 10-15% the guides say you will get) as long as you are polite to them.
drawbacks: Prices can be negotiated well in excess of 50% off
practical_tips: Negotiate well in excess of 50% off

author: Ali07London
title: If you like a market it’s worth a stroll
original_content: Lots of stalls. Some pretty things but lots of the same. Goes on forever!  Bought a pretty pair of earrings but the small shops are just as competitive.

author: Rini M
title: Overrated
original_content: It is overrated. You can find same products for cheaper price in shops. For foreigners they ask too much price .
drawbacks: You can find same products for cheaper price in shops
For foreigners they ask too much price

author: Silas E
title: After dinner walk
original_content: Went for a stroll around the market. Got something small to eat. Typical market. Good vibes tho :) Can recommend it for an after-dinner walk.
practical_tips: Can recommend it for an after-dinner walk

author: KTP310
title: Good atmosphere and prices
original_content: We enjoyed strolling through the night market which had a relaxed atmosphere, with no pressure to buy. We bought lots - the prices seemed even more reasonable than local shops. But do be aware, at one point we felt we were being followed, possibly by pickpockets.
drawbacks: felt we were being followed, possibly by pickpockets
highlights: prices seemed even more reasonable than local shops

author: Jonathan C.
title: hanoi night market
original_content: Beautiful night market in the old quarter. Walkable, plenty of stalls, food stands, restaurants, and shops.

author: Janelle
title: Ms. Anh Stall 39
original_content: Ms. Anh at stall 39 was such a fun lady and had a great shop. She was not pressuring at all and it was so fun bargaining with her. She gave us some great deals on numerous items. We got an adorable incense holder with the best incense over ever burnt. Loved her such a blast. My boyfriend and I still talk about Ms. Anh and how much she made us laugh. Highly recommend!!
highlights: Ms. Anh was a fun lady
practical_tips: bargaining with vendors can be fun

author: eileent3821
title: WEEKEND NIGHT MARKET IN HANOI
original_content: A very popular place among the local community, it is even more interesting to see it as a tourist. A wide variety of food - from meats and seafood, to food especially local snacks. You can get through it quickly if you do not have much interest in any of the products but you can also spend a reasonable time if the products are what you are after. Definitely worth a visit.
practical_tips: go through quickly if not interested

author: TravelinMan411
title: Fun night market!
original_content: A great night out! Many people, live music, plenty of shopping, they close off the streets so it’s nice to be able to walk around without looking for Motos!
practical_tips: close off the streets so it’s nice to be able to walk around without looking for Motos

author: Ali921
title: Market stalls for tourists mainly
original_content: It's a market. Most clearly aimed at tourists. Depends what you want and how you want to pay. Lots of cheap stuff - clothes, shoes, bags etc. Not for me. Once you seen one market you've seen them all
drawbacks: Once you seen one market you've seen them all
practical_tips: Depends what you want and how you want to pay

author: smewar
title: Must visit for weekend in hanoi
original_content: Lively market with food , live music, First copy of branded shoes, clothes, watches. Quiet a long, some shops have fixed price and some does bargain
drawbacks: some shops have fixed price and some does bargain
highlights: First copy of branded shoes, clothes, watches

author: Compudex
title: First Copy Biggest market
original_content: If you love value for money, its great place. If you're Brand Freak then you wont enjoy much. They have all Chinese made clothing and cutlery at cheap rate, (you must bargain a bit) I would call it all first copy market from Clothing, shoes, Watch, Belt and Toys !!we even bought new bag from here, after shopping :)
drawbacks: They have all Chinese made clothing and cutlery at cheap rate
They have all first copy market

author: G2Kpauly
title: Lovely night market
original_content: This is a really cool market to walk around especially on weekends it's so busy with locals and tourists. Look for the hotpot food stall on the corner it is amazing food. Also the meet on stick bbq stalls are nice. There is plenty of shopping to be done too and it goes along way this market.
practical_tips: look for the hotpot food stall on the corner

author: Felice Santiago
title: Walk and see around
original_content: Went to see and stroll around.. if you buy something try to haggle first (if you want) just like any market. Clothes, bags, shoes , souvenirs, coffee, food, can be found here. I remember it was a hot night too but all good :) I enjoyed sight seeing.

author: Travelove58
title: Big & colorful night market, with wide varieties of products.....
original_content: This weekly night market only opens from Fri-Sundays. Its a huge, huge market stretching to a few streets. We spent about 3 hours here . Quality of sports shoes & apparels here are good. Don't forget to bargain, as prices are always highly inflated. This is expected . Otherwise you end up paying ridiculous prices.We bought different sports shoes that were quoted 450K-500K but in the end , got it for 300K- 350K.
highlights: Quality of sports shoes & apparels here are good

author: Samantha H
title: Don’t miss Mr Thanh! Stall 34
original_content: What a fabulous experience this was.  So glad we came! Mr Thanh at stall 34 is a legend!  Great fun and so helpful.  Good prices and great choice.  Kind man with a lovely family.
practical_tips: Go to stall 34 for a great experience

author: 오 오
title: store recomendation
original_content: No.39 MsAnh wat really good and cheap!The owners were so nice and lovely!They are asking me to write it but it's good tohavecommuication like this.

author: Max H
title: Stall 34 is a great time
original_content: Stall 34 is well worth a visit. Lovely man running it who was very funny and I enjoyed chatting to him about the football. Really loved it!
highlights: enjoyed chatting to him about the football

author: Rory Huynh
title: Great Stall, Great Staff, Great time
original_content: Stall #34 was excellent! I visited the night market of Ha Noi and it was amazing! I was greeted by a lovely man who was helpful, funny and a down to earth guy. The stall #34 was so lovely and had many products for great value! I would definitely recommend visiting the place as the service was excellent as well as the stall.

author: David
title: So many people!
original_content: The Hanoi night Market is extremely busy! So many people! Other reviewers have suggested that it is s Fri, Sat and Sun night affair only - so worth coming on one of these days.A District of the old town is coroned off to all but foot traffic, which makes the area around the night Market a chaos of pedestrians, cars and motorcycles all coming to - or trying to bypass - the market.Recommend you go to the what is now the Old Town Restaurant and Pub and watching from the balcony aa another reviewer helpfully suggests.
drawbacks: chaos of pedestrians, cars and motorcycles
highlights: worth coming on one of these days
practical_tips: go on Fri, Sat, or Sun night
watch from the balcony at Old Town Restaurant and Pub

author: feltroneu
title: Crowded
original_content: The night market is very huge which have occupied few of the streets. The more impressive was the big crowd along the streets. Must be careful of your belongings and small kids. Some of the stalls selling very unique souvenirs but majority offered clothing. There were variety of choices maybe other night markets wouldn't offered. Be prepared to negotiate the price as the initial price they offered could be very expensive but it depended on your luck. It was one of the highlights of our Hanoi trip ended with a sweet memory.
highlights: one of the highlights of our Hanoi trip
practical_tips: be prepared to negotiate the price

author: Hana C
title: HUGE
original_content: Massive market, felt like it went on forever! So many cool things to look at - food, trinkets etc. Was super cool even in the rain.

author: Ann K
title: Nice stroll if you like busy markets
original_content: It's an nice stroll and you can see many different items for sale. Prices and items are geared towards tourists, so compare and bargain hard it you are interested in buying. Be aware of cheap quality and fake brands and keep your money and valuables in a safe place when steering through the crowds. If you are interested in street food, there's plenty of snacks to try! As the market is outside it is weather dependent and can get cold and wet, especially in winter.
practical_tips: keep your money and valuables in a safe place

author: Barry W
title: Generous Giving It 2 Stars
original_content: We have been to many night markets in the Asia Pacific region and this one definitely ranks as the worst. Mainly clothes, footwear, tacky jewellery, sunglasses, mobile phone covers etc. It is not a patch on Hoi An night market. I very rarely give low star ratings but this fully deserves it. Stay away.
drawbacks: Mainly clothes, footwear, tacky jewellery, sunglasses, mobile phone covers etc.
Not a patch on Hoi An night market
Worst night market in the Asia Pacific region

author: K&M rates plates
title: Worth a visit
original_content: Came here after a recommendation from our hotel receptionist. The night market is really cool and very authentic. It’s really busy but it’s good fun walking up and down haggling with the market traders. It’s definitely worth a visit
highlights: good fun walking up and down haggling with the market traders

author: LoBommer
country: The Royal Town of Sutton Coldfield, United Kingdom
title: Does what it says on the tin!
original_content: It's a market and it's dark! It must be a night Market!! Average but then I think all markets are average! Mostly clothes and some food stalls where they have a two tier price scale! It is incumbent upon one to visit these local markets even if it is just to say I went there!

author: TinaQ
title: Lively and noisy
original_content: This was my first experience as far as night markets go and I'm comparing it to other places I've visited since then throughout our travels around Vietnam, Laos and Cambodia. It's quite noisy, loads of stalls, loads of people, some street food and generic souvenirs. The best way to enjoy it is to find the Peachy Craft Bar, sit on its balcony and look at the hustle and bustle down below.

author: sg_anu
title: Massively crowded
original_content: Chaotic crowd with chaotic traffic thrown into it. Go only if you are comfortable moving in large crowds. Items sold are quite cheap but not of high quality. About 70 to 80% of the items sold are clothes out of which a large majority are brand rip offs. A lot of accessories and shoes are sold as well (again, lots of fake branded items). I have no interest in buying brand rip offs. With a lot of difficulty, found a pair of sports shoes for my daughter that didn't have Nike or Adidas written on it and they were actually quite good. A few places were selling curios and the prices looked quite good. But, honestly, it was a challenge deciding to buy anything in the huge crowd when you're constantly being swept off! I live in Asia and I've rarely seen that level of crowding.It's still a unique experience.
drawbacks: Items sold are not of high quality
A lot of fake branded items
highlights: A few places were selling curios and the prices looked quite good
Found a pair of sports shoes that didn't have Nike or Adidas written on it and they were actually quite good
practical_tips: Go only if you are comfortable moving in large crowds

author: epruuu
title: Everything you may want for shopping
original_content: This market is a colourful place in which you can find many different souvenirs, cosmetics, textiles, fruits, street foods. It is available Friday and Saturday evenings, I am not sure for Sunday.

author: JPollock311
title: Crazy busy & crowded, but fun
original_content: The old quarter and night market on the weekend is a must, they close the streets to cars and motorbikes and the streets fill up with families and vendors - it is amazing. We have been twice summer and winter, both were fantastic

author: Jay “flower” child
title: Just okayyyy
original_content: This is an okay night market. I’m comparing it to other major markets like Thong Sala in Ko Pha-ngan, Bangkoks night market and Hong Kong’s night market. This one is simply, okay.... there is not much food selection at all. Also, a lot of what is being sold isn’t unique to Vietnam and necessarily souvenirs but things like air pods and iPhone chargers. This just didn’t seem authentic when you compare it to other ones. I’m all about the food stalls and these ones were disappointing at best. If I’m not getting food I want unique handmade souvenirs and I didn’t get that either
practical_tips: Go to other markets for better selection

author: Kyra D
title: Eat All of the Street Food!
original_content: We loved the night market! We honestly didn’t know it was happening so we were lucky that we arrived on a Sunday (since it’s only open Fri-Sun). We were staying in the old quarter so we stumbled upon the market being set up when we were out and about. It’s pretty crowded but there are tons of great craft vendors and food vendors. We ate a ton of food and everything was so delicious. Specifically all of the dumplings. And it was easy to pop into the many bars along the market if we wanted to sit and grab a beer. Most of the places had outdoor balcony seating so we were able to look down on the market while taking a break. Definitely worth a visit if you’re there when it’s open!

author: Anine
title: Beautiful but crowded
original_content: The many multi colored lanterns that fill the streets are breathtaking and the reflection on the river even more so. The food at the night market are interesting and very tasty. There are some down sides to this night market though, it is packed with tourists and most of the stalls sell exactly the same merchandise and food. So while you are bumped and pushed through the street you are also looking at the same thing all the time. The big crowd kind of takes away from the beauty of this part of Hoi An.
drawbacks: most of the stalls sell exactly the same merchandise and food
bumped and pushed through the street

author: Candice
title: Worth a visit
original_content: If you're visiting Hanoi during the weekend, take a stroll along the night market street. Great walk with nice mixture of stuff. From shirt, souvenir, shoe, to hand make ice cream, street orchestra... A nice place to hang out after dinner. Stall starting to set up from 6+ to 7+ pm, by 8pm most of the stall is ready for the night.
practical_tips: Take a stroll along the night market street
Stall starting to set up from 6+ to 7+ pm

author: Ati
title: Chaotic, Crazy and Beautiful.
original_content: Perfect for an after dinner walk and buy loads of products for a quite reasonable prices. If you visit Hanoi this a must!!!Extra if you love a bargain.

author: Raymondale
title: Price quite reasonable
original_content: Last year Nov/Dec when i had my North Vietnam tour,i visited Hanoi night market twice,it is close to where i stayed.If compare to other night market in vietnam,hanoi night market is worth to visit,the price is reasonable,many stalls are fixed price,unlike Hoi an or other night market,you have to bargain,sometimes very hard.i bought some small things here,like mirror,mini umbrella,quilling arts,quilling painting...be noted that it only opened during weekends,and some roads will be closed,so better go there by walking.

author: Srirambalaji S
title: Street Market by the Night
original_content: Located at the one of the sides of Hoan Kiem Lake, this market comes to life by evening till midnight. Its like the street market in any country selling a large range of cheaper items. Do not get fooled by the branded logos as they are all fake products branded and displayed. There are lot of hawkers, so have the patience and negotiation skills to bargain for a better rate.As the place is crowded be careful with your belongings. Unless you are sure you want to buy and have decided on a rate in your mind do not show interest and you will be lured to buy in the products just at the hint of your interest on something.
practical_tips: don't show interest if you're not sure you want to buy

author: Harding N
title: tired
original_content: Do not expect something extremely authentic here. The things that you get in the stores close by - sneakers, Vietnamese souvenirs, fake jewelry, dresses - are somewhat better priced within this night market by approximately 10 20 % discount. You are able to negotiate/haggle more than the stores. It is just open Friday through Sunday later in the day. Stalls will begin opening around six pm but better to come after seven pm.

author: Abdur Rahman
title: Impressive... Mind blowing
original_content: I really enjoyed... Price are cheaper but you must bargain with the shop keepers. Souvenir items, street foods, cheap cosmetics, clothings everything you will found.
drawbacks: You must bargain with the shop keepers

author: Rose F
title: Night market mayhem
original_content: Spent Sunday night at the Night Market but didn’t stay long because I am not a big fan of shopping and I don’t need more ‘stuff’. #1 son bought a pair of Ray Ban sunnies for 100,000 Vietnamese Dong ~$6AUD  If you want cheap clothing watches, wallets, purses, bags, electronic gadgets, cards and souvenirs or doughnuts and frozen ice confections  then this is the place. Fun to do once as it was a lovely night and seeing families have fun around Hoan Kiev lake on a warm Sunday evening was delightful (a lot better than the market in my opinion!)
drawbacks: not a big fan of shopping
practical_tips: go if you want cheap clothing, watches, etc.

author: priya a
title: over priced
original_content: You will find a lot of cheap stuff in this market where most of the items are overpriced. Most of the vendors are not prepared to lower the price much. I suggest paying half of what they ask you.We didn't find any good deals here although it was fun looking around.
drawbacks: most of the items are overpriced
most of the vendors are not prepared to lower the price much
practical_tips: paying half of what they ask you

author: Jack S
title: best night market in SE Asia
original_content: The best night market in South East Asia with a huge range of items including (but not limited to) knockoff branded clothing, shoes and accessories, souvenirs, electronics and food. Certainly worth the visit. Note it is opened on Friday, Saturday and Sunday evenings but may close due to poor weather.
practical_tips: go on Friday, Saturday, or Sunday evening

author: Ald
title: Night Market
original_content: Lots of stalls selling the same stuff but the hustle and bustle of the place with all the lights, music and people made it an interesting experience.
drawbacks: Lots of stalls selling the same stuff
highlights: the hustle and bustle of the place
all the lights, music and people

author: Jessy
title: Below average night Market!
original_content: Mostly selling fake or imitation items. There is no clothes representing the locals or even street foods. We didn't find much things to buy.
drawbacks: Mostly selling fake or imitation items

author: Ginnyleeinwonderland
title: Night life at weekend
original_content: If you are a fan of buying cheap ( and fake) stuff, this is absolutely place for you. You can find there many cheap things including clothes, accessories for phones, cosmetics or food. You can enjoy night life at weekend of Hanoian but beware of the pick pockets. You should always keep your bag in front of you or just hold it. You can also find many traditional food of Vietnam there. Just enjoy life and use calculator to reduce price
practical_tips: keep your bag in front of you

author: Cindy Marie Azur
title: Only opens every Fridays
original_content: We’re very lucky to experience this night market. As usually it only open every Friday night and just happened that we’ve stayed till Saturday. Plenty of shops around selling good quality of imitated products and street food. A must visit place when you’re around the area Friday night. You can bargain to some but not all vendors.

author: QuaverT
title: Worst night in Asia
original_content: Hanoi market is an awful experience and it’s completely ruined the charm of Vietnam for me. I’ve had a superb time over the last few months in this country but this was by far the worst and stressful nights of my life. There’s only about 5 stalls which sell anything unique. Everything else is the same rip off bags/watches/plastic toys and the vendors are rude/ignorant. It’s incredibly busy so you spend hours doing a small shuffle rather than walking. It’s an absolute waste of time and has ruined my experience of Hanoi

author: Shahana
title: Cute market
original_content: Very touristic place but very cute. Once it’s night time all the streets light up with a lot of lanterns everywhere. Some places charge you when you want to take photos in front of their shops, but it’s like one dollar. You can also have a boat tour on the river, with little lights in the boat.Overall a good experience
drawbacks: Some places charge you when you want to take photos in front of their shops

author: DerriQ
title: Great night
original_content: We loved this market.  Its hard to miss if your staying in the old quarter so if you just head towards the lake you will find it on a Frid, Sat or Sunday night.  We went last Sunday night and really enjoyed it more than I thought we would after reading some of the reviews.  We got some good bargains and gifts for people back home.  Its a huge market and seems to go on forever and ever.  We kept walking and eventually found ourselves in beer street which was another amazing experience.  The stall holders all seemed nice and prices were better than I expected.  I didn't have to haggle anywhere near as much as other places like Bali and Thailand to reach an agreed price. Very packed but that's all part of the fun! If you have young children I don't like your chances of pushing a pram through the crown though!
drawbacks: Difficult to push a pram through the crowd
practical_tips: Head towards the lake to find the market
Go on a Friday, Saturday, or Sunday night

author: LinLing03
title: Great prices for mass-produced items
original_content: Don’t expect anything extremely authentic here. The items that you find in the shops nearby - sneakers, fake jewelry, Vietnamese souvenirs, dresses - are better priced in this night market by about 10-20% discount. You can negotiate / haggle more than the shops. It’s only open Friday through Sunday in the evening. Stalls will start opening around 6pm but best to come after 7pm. Most will open rain or shine as we experienced it while it was raining fairly heavy.
extracted_times: Friday through Sunday in the evening

author: Nia Sarrie
title: Interesting place to visit
original_content: you can't resist the ambiance..it feels like you will buy everything there..lol..take me back there :)

author: Libby C
title: Seriously disappointing
original_content: If you’ve been anywhere else in Southeast Asia, you’ve seen amazing markets.  Often they are filled with cheap but localish handicrafts, clothes and gifts specific to the region. If that’s what you are hoping for here, you’ll be disappointed.  It was all cheap t-shirts, ugly knock-off bags, electronics, plastic jewelry.  There was some food, but even that was mostly just fruit juice stands.  The only original thing I saw was some interesting greeting cards with 3D cut out structures.   Everything else was wildly uninteresting.
highlights: interesting greeting cards with 3D cut out structures
practical_tips: go elsewhere if you're looking for local handicrafts

author: Aneta B
title: Evening well spend.
original_content: It’s in the centre of Hanoi so you will definitely end up here no matter if you want to or not and I would say it was worth it. Yes, it’s packed with people and pretty noisy but the atmosphere is great. You can choose from different Vietnamese street food and also buy very cheap clothing - mainly dupes of expensive brands such as Adidas, Channel and other.

author: K5165XX
title: Very enjoyable
original_content: Amazing atmosphere as long as you don't have this every night. Good food and interesting shopping close to some of the high lights of Hanoi. Much better during the night but also interesting area during the day just lots of traffic...

author: Sarah
title: Noisy but cheap and good food
original_content: Small street with many people walking around buy food, souvenirs, clothes, shoes.... everything is cheap but i am worry about quality. But still nice

author: rearcardoor
title: Night market with 3 kids
original_content: I know this has had mixed reviews but we had a fun evening at the night market.  It’s not on par with some of the other South East Asian night markets but definitely worth a visit.  We browsed the stalls, ate some street food, had a drink at one of the outdoor bars on little plastic seats, and got some good bargains.  There is a lot of repetition in the stalls with so many selling trainers, electronics, clothes etc but towards the lake end, there are more stalls selling souvenirs etc.  There are lots of shops open alongside the market too and it gets quite busy as the evening progresses.  We got some incredible bargains and did not find the stall holders rude at all, it’s just all part of the game.  One example was a pair of trainers quoted at 1,350,000 dong and we got the price down to 500,000.  We got similar discounts for other items and had a lot of fun.

author: Paul's
title: tired
original_content: the night market is a really busy place and also a long i mean really really long market , hot and crowded took me 30m to find my way out

author: mistahfong
title: Beware of this seller
original_content: Don't buy food from this stall (near the crossroad at Hanoi Old Quarter nightmarket) , she cheated my money

author: psandhu1
title: Pleasant night market
original_content: Went here on Sunday evening at 7pm with my 8 month old baby in the sling. It is busy and the vendors are pleasant. My brother bought a Bluetooth speaker for £8. They sold mainly clothes, jewellery and footwear. Enjoyable.

author: Role
title: Market was nice if you haven’t been to one before
original_content: The markets are all ways cool great bargains some things are unique somethings repeat over and over. I would say if you e never been too a night market and it’s the weekend and you want something to do.  I would recommend you do the night market and walk around some. It’s safe and cool atmosphere. Hanoi is a little more laid back then southern Vietnam.
drawbacks: Some things are unique, some things repeat over and over
practical_tips: Go to the night market if you've never been

author: Andrew V
title: Busy
original_content: This is very busy with locals and tourists not a great deal of bargain to be had we did get a couple of good deals but on average most of the stuff is cheap knockoff that are not at a cheap price but if you’re in Hanoi it’s worth the look
drawbacks: not a great deal of bargain

author: Sherry Bischoff
title: Hanoi weekend night market
