original_content: Interesting stroll through the stalls. Was hoping for more locally hand-made items. Lots of clothing and food. Even though the streets were closed there were still a number of mopeds driving through the crowd.
drawbacks: Was hoping for more locally hand-made items
practical_tips: Go early to avoid mopeds driving through the crowd

author: Jun David
title: Great Bargain
original_content: The Night Market runs from Don Xuang Market to near Hoa Kiem Lake.Lots of knocked off items from bags, shoes and shirts. Lots of street foods. Lots of souvenirs. Most of the stalls are selling the same items though. All items are cheap but you need to bargain.Great experience.
drawbacks: Most of the stalls are selling the same items though

author: JustRose_CH
title: Not worth it
original_content: We arrived on a Monday and I spent the week looking forward to shopping at the night market. Other than a few stalls at the very beginning of the market, the end closest to the lake, the market was full of old clothes, underwear and generally things of that nature. The beginning had souvenirs for very reasonable prices, sometimes low enough not to bargain over. However I did not find anything at the night market I didn’t see elsewhere in Hanoi so if you are not there on a weekend don’t worry you are not missing anything. Note that the night market is only set up Friday to Sunday.
drawbacks: did not find anything at the night market I didn’t see elsewhere in Hanoi
highlights: sometimes low enough not to bargain over
practical_tips: don't worry you are not missing anything

author: Francis Martino
title: Worth a Visit in crowded place.
original_content: The Hanoi market at night is beautiful during the week end,Definitely worth checking out. Food and Goods all you can buy. Make sure to bargain, but start with at least 20-30% of the price they say you, stay strong when bargaining. If you don't get the price you move to stand the next one will give you your desired price.  It takes a bit getting used to to the big crowd,the kind you see in the market of the old quarter, and also hair bands, jewelry, watches, some toys and shoes,IT appliances and so on.Be careful of your belongings during walking and sightseeing in very crowded place.
practical_tips: Start with at least 20-30% of the price they say you

author: McCullough.Family
title: Good night out
original_content: Some of these reviews are very harsh. Do not get me wrong a lot of what is sold is the same but we never felt pressured into buying anything and no harm in looking for a couple of hours and most people will buy something
highlights: no harm in looking for a couple of hours
practical_tips: go for a couple of hours

author: Simona
title: Prepare to be scammed
original_content: Markets in asia are kind of sightseeing, however I'd recommend avoiding this one or be very careful. The vendors are rude, not willing to bargain and you feel bad if you ask for another size. This market ruined my night as one vendor has stolen 90k dong from me. I've bargained a price to 80k dong and have her a 100k bill. She returned me 10k dong and I've tried to explain that she should give me another 10k back. Then she started yelling at me and grabed my bag with the good inside. She have scratched my arm and was insanely rude. I didn't understand what have happened when she continued to yell at me and many people gathered around. I've tried to either get my money back or get my good but she left me with only 10k dong in my hand. Basically, the scam is that she blamed me that I've given her only 10k dong and that I owe her money. She started pointing at my friend's pockets and tried to reach out to them. A crowd of vietnamese sellers gathered around and we were screamed at in vietnamese. I don't care about the 100k dong. Just the overall concept of this scam is ridiculous and we've got a bit scared when we were surrounded by vietnamese crowd screaming at us. Recommend giving exact amount to the vendors to avoid this and be very careful in the market as it seems that they would do anything for a couple of dollars, even get violent.
drawbacks: Vendors are rude and not willing to bargain
Scam where vendor steals money and blames customer
practical_tips: Give exact amount to vendors to avoid scams
Be very careful in the market

author: Anas A
title: Weekend market
original_content: Hanoi's Night Market happens every weekend and it is very popular for both locals and tourists. Full of street shops which sell a variety of products. The quality of most products is cheap and copied from other brands. The problem with the market is that it is overcrowded.
drawbacks: The quality of most products is cheap and copied from other brands

author: Sebastián M
title: Overcrowded
original_content: Too many people at this place. Vendors offer the same products along the street. Not worth spending time here. But for the first time it is nice experience, to see how the night market in Hanoi looks like.
highlights: See how the night market in Hanoi looks like

author: Elsa C. L.
title: Fun and quite reasonably priced in Asia
original_content: Bargaining is necessary.  Naturally, vendors would like more profit.Highly unique wide assortment of Origami design cards for specific occasions or general are priced ranging from 20,000 to 35,000 Dong (US$1 = 22,500 to 23,000 Dong) depending on the size.Beautifully decorated fabric gift pouches approximately 5” X 6” are priced at 24,000 Dong.  When you buy five, you get one free.White cotton shirts with Vietnam attraction printed cost 40,000 Dong each.A native Vietnamese design colorful magnet is priced at 10,000 Dong.  My Vietnamese souvenir plate for my wall collection cost 100,000 Dong.Pork barbeque sells at 20,000.  As snack, three sticks would be satisfying for a person weighing 119 lbs as the pieces are not lean.No vehicle is supposed to go through the night market.  However, there were motorcycles.
drawbacks: Motorcycles were allowed in the night market
highlights: Unique wide assortment of Origami design cards
practical_tips: Buy five gift pouches to get one free
Pork barbeque is a satisfying snack

author: hansibrahim
title: Wash your eye
original_content: Held every Friday, Saturday and Sunday, Hanoi Weekend Night Market is a busy, bustling gathering of roadside stalls and local food vendors that brings huge crowds of locals and tourists. It runs through the Old Quarter district from 19:00 onwards, starting from Hang Dao Street and running north to the edge of Dong Xuan Market.
practical_tips: go on Friday, Saturday, or Sunday

author: tes108
title: Tacky junk
original_content: Our local friends told us that all the merchandise came from China. It did. Nothing remotely interesting and the place is devoid of charm.

author: Tabitha G
title: Crowded but enjoyable
original_content: Very crowded and a little overwhelming. Prices for the same item vary greatly, so be patient if you want something. If you’ve seen it once you’ll likely see it again. Get your best bargaining on, because you’ll need to cut the price by at least 70% to start. I found being patient and friendly works really well especially with young people. Lots of shoes, clothing and souvenirs. Also accessories (sunglasses, jewellery, make up and perfume.) Also electronic accessories. Remember- this stuff is all fake and the quality of the clothing in particular is very average. You’re just paying for the name brand. Overall a fun night out, recommended if you enjoy the market scene and crowds.
drawbacks: Prices for the same item vary greatly
Quality of the clothing is very average
You're just paying for the name brand
highlights: Recommended if you enjoy the market scene and crowds
practical_tips: Cut the price by at least 70% to start

author: Bulbul
title: Vibrant weekend in the city
original_content: If you haven’t booked the tickets for Vietnam yet, book it for the dates that include the weekend. The night market is held on Friday, Saturday, and Sunday starting from 19:00. The street is a lively gathering of the roadside stalls. These stalls sell almost everything right from pop up cards to shoes. The prices are reasonable too. However, negotiations seemed relatively unattainable here as compared to Don Xuan and the old quarter market. A good bet is to buy souvenirs from here. You get a great variety.

author: cinbkk
title: Shopping and food
original_content: A good place to while away the time in the evening from Fri-Sun. Lots of food, snacks, clothes, shoes, accessories and souvenirs. Some streets are too crowded for a proper walk, but it's a huge area and there's always somewhere to go. One end of the market ends at the Hoan Kiem lake, a good place to catch some fresh air.
drawbacks: Some streets are too crowded for a proper walk
highlights: Lots of food, snacks, clothes, shoes, accessories and souvenirs
practical_tips: Catch some fresh air at Hoan Kiem lake

author: Atlas1669
title: Fun but not much else
original_content: A bit of fun walking past similar stalls. It was really crowded and quite fun even though there was little to tempt us to buy. Worth going to see just for the experience.
drawbacks: little to tempt us to buy
highlights: worth going to see just for the experience

author: TonyMac64
title: Interesting but lots of the same stuff
original_content: We enjoyed our trip and the prices were comparative with other markets in Asia. My main criticism would be that all the clothing stalls had the same clothes, as did the jewellery and souvenir stalls etc. Worth it if markets are your thing but don’t expect anything out of the ordinary.
drawbacks: all the clothing stalls had the same clothes
jewellery and souvenir stalls etc. were unoriginal
highlights: prices were comparative with other markets in Asia
practical_tips: worth it if markets are your thing

author: Gordo4037
title: Not much variety
original_content: This was a busy market but not in the realms of Bangkok or Saigon. Very busy with many people and a lovely atmosphere abounded. There was a lot of street vendors selling snacks which on the main were fried foods but good to get a sample of a wide range of food for only 20000 dong. The stalls were a little disappointing as they carried virtually the same clothes, souvenirs and trinkets. By the time you got to the end you pretty much knew what the return trip on the other side of the road was going to be like, The stall vendors have pretty high prices do it is important to haggle with them and enjoy the experience- after all they can only say no and you will find the same item at the next stall or two anyways. Whatever price I was given I countered with 25% of that and usually we met at 30 - 40% of the asking price. All in all a good way to spend a few hours out and about with the locals and other visiting tourists.
drawbacks: stalls carried virtually the same clothes, souvenirs and trinkets
stall vendors have pretty high prices
highlights: wide range of food for only 20000 dong
good way to spend a few hours out and about with the locals and other visiting tourists

author: bunko007
title: Lots of people
original_content: It's good that we were accompanied by our Vietnamese supplier to this attraction.  The free guided tour made it easier for us to navigate the streets, where to find what we were looking for, and do translation for us with the vendors. The cool January weather made it comfortable for us to walk for at least 3 hours.  The crowded and lively atmosphere fascinated me, not with the stuff being sold.  Although I was able to buy some good quality neck ties, I couldn't find the trigger to purchase more as the options were really not interesting to me. Stalls selling similar products are bunched together so it's best to check around first before making the final purchase.
practical_tips: check around first before making the final purchase

author: Albywon
title: Busy night markets
original_content: All sorts of different goods and foods available - some are good deals and some are not. Before you go do your research and work out what price you could pay elsewhere and make sure you negotiate accordingly!

author: Zfy Ed
title: Huge Night Market with lots to see and eat!
original_content: Unlike it's counterpart the famous Ben Thanh Market in Ho Chi Minh City, this night market only operates from Friday to Sunday nights with the former everyday. But in terms of size and magnitude, this is a much bigger and long, stretching over 4 streets in perpendicular direction, that could add up to about 1~1.5 km.In the day time, the place was congested with motorbikes and cars but at night when the market started, it was flooded with lots of people, especially tourists. And so it's no doubt a touristy market.As one walks along, you will notice that most stalls were selling similar items, such as fashion clothings and bags, shoes, electronic and mobile items, toys etc, of course also street food. After a while, it's just like "repetition" everywhere with the same things on sale and the only different is that of the "prices", some selling higher and some lower prices. (But who knows they maybe from the same bosses as that was what some people told us). You may get tired of it.But it's a good place to indulge into the local culture and lifestyle of the people. We ended up buying some clothings and bags and our shopping spree ended slightly an hour and a half, which we spent quite some time in pushing our way through the crowd! :)As mentioned earlier, the place was very crowed with people walking in all directions, not to mention the oncoming motorbikes, despite the fact that the area has closed for all vehicles. And as a reviewer who posted earlier, when there are many people, there is an opportunity of crime like pick pocketing. However, to be fair, such crime does happen to any other city in the world and not only in Vietnam and so cannot condemn the city for it. Even in Paris, London, Brussels, Prague and Budapest, just to name a few, such act of crime is very common and evident.Well, it is personal responsibility to ensure that your personal belongings are well taken care of. In my so many visits to Vietnam in the last 4 years (more than 6 times), I had never experienced such thing or even scamming or cheating cases, which many travel reviewers have warned about when in Vietnam.Also, always be careful, keep a low profile (not wearing expensive things or carrying bag or even clothings) and avoid putting all the cash/cards in one place, and preparing small notes that will be easier to use, you should be safe!
drawbacks: repetition everywhere with the same things on sale
opportunity of crime like pick pocketing
highlights: good place to indulge into the local culture and lifestyle of the people
indulge into the local culture and lifestyle of the people
practical_tips: be careful, keep a low profile
avoid putting all the cash/cards in one place
prepare small notes that will be easier to use

author: Steve R
title: Beware !!
original_content: We went to the markets at about 8.30pm on a Friday night. Although the markets are Ok in terms of the shops and stalls, the issue here is crime. We were warned by our hotel to be careful of pick-pockets but I guess because we'd had only positive experiences in our 2 weeks in Vietnam so far and complacency, we thought they may be a little over cautious. Well, we were wrong. It happened so fast. The markets are very congested with people making it easy for pick-pockets, who are obviously very good at what they do.So some tips: 1... NEVER carry your wallet in your back pocket. Always use a secure carry bag around your body or neck, carried in front of you and zipped up closed.2... Only carry CASH, enough that you think you will need for the night. Keep your credit cards and other cash at your hotel - safe.3.. NEVER carry your PASSPORT unless absolutely neccessary. Keep it safe at your hotel4... PHONES are also a big target. When we were at the local police station reporting the crime, there was a steady stream of people coming in, reporting their phone had been pick-pocketed and in some cases, snatched from their hands by a thief on a motorbike.
practical_tips: NEVER carry your wallet in your back pocket
Only carry CASH, enough that you think you will need for the night
NEVER carry your PASSPORT unless absolutely neccessary

author: fizzy1991
title: Same thing everywhere you look but it's an experience
original_content: It is all the same tacky stuff, especially those awful banana shirts made out of cheap rayon fabric that sticks to you in the heat.  I guess if you have never been to a night market you should go but keep your money in your wallet and spend it on quality items in the light of day.
drawbacks: awful banana shirts made out of cheap rayon fabric
sticks to you in the heat
highlights: go if you have never been to a night market
practical_tips: keep your money in your wallet and spend it on quality items in the light of day

author: BC
title: Good Market
original_content: Lots of stalls here, all selling many different things, from bags to banana emblazoned shirts, to food. An eclectic mix, which was great to look around.

author: Seri L
title: Lot of eateries and fun shopping.
original_content: We stayed in Ha noi on friday and saturday so were able to visit the market for two night in a row. What a fun and interesting place to be. Wish they have it every night!! We will be back again in September and will certainly arrange to spend a week end there.

author: ozvpm_andy
title: Huge but a little bland
original_content: The night markets seems to stretch on for miles - but sadly, they are just stall after stall of the same old cheap bits and pieces. However, its still a nice atmosphere and something easy and cheap to do after dark in Hanoi.
drawbacks: same old cheap bits and pieces

author: Barb C
title: Worth a visit to get a taste of local culture
original_content: As others have said, it’s not a great place to shop compared to other markets throughout the world. We enjoyed a Friday night out on the town just to see the Vietnamese enjoying themselves at local pubs and restaurants.
drawbacks: not a great place to shop
highlights: enjoyed a Friday night out on the town
practical_tips: go to local pubs and restaurants for a night out

author: roam review
title: Go hungry and curious
original_content: The market was just bustling and literally up our street! The smells are amazing ( some are not) and the variety of food, clothes, bags, trainers and sunglasses will  keep you absorbed for hours. Some stalls are more open to haggling then others but I managed to sniff out a good few bargains, as soon as I got hot from all the rummaging we tried some of the liquid nitrogen sweets, they were odd but refreshing, definatly a new experience.
drawbacks: some stalls are not open to haggling

author: Aimee H
title: Crazy and worth a visit
original_content: The night market is a must in Hanoi - it is vast and at times we felt we didn't know where it was going to end! It's a bustling market with lots to buy, and lots of haggling to be done. Great for getting presents to bring home as well. Really fun.

author: Dianne S
title: Night Market
original_content: The Night market in Hanoi  was right outside our Hotel very busy and colourful lots of food selling and people.   Great for shopping.

author: Jalal Iqbal
title: nice market in the old town
original_content: i enjoyed the night market very much. a lot of nice small colourful shops. liked the festive environment. honestly price was a bit high. it was a pleasant experience to walk and see those shops.

author: Steve G
title: Well worth a visit
original_content: If you enjoy markets this is a good experience drifting along a whole street opened up with stalls of clothing, shoes, sunglasses, watches etc. My wife and I traveled with our two adult children and both had a great time finding all sorts of objects to buy!
highlights: finding all sorts of objects to buy

author: kpiddy
title: Combining markets in crazy busy streets
original_content: I am not a keen shopper or one to bargain and found no pleasure in the night markets in Hanoi.  The market stalls are set up beside the busy chaotic traffic and with shoppers passing by, the better times to shop would be on Friday to Sunday nights when the streets around Hoan Kiem Lake are vehicle free.  The stores sell clothing, luggage, handbags, souvenirs, toys and a whole lot more.
drawbacks: found no pleasure in the night markets
practical_tips: go on Friday to Sunday nights when the streets are vehicle free

author: debbieferr
title: Weekend night Market
original_content: The night Market was OK, a mix of cheap clothes, toys, souvenirs, jewellery, fruit and street food.I liked the fact that the roads around the market and lake were closed so everyone could be in the roads safely. Children played and adults were sitting and relaxing.
highlights: roads around the market and lake were closed so everyone could be in the roads safely
Children played and adults were sitting and relaxing

author: 944michelem
title: Overwhelming
original_content: We went to this market and we were a little disappointed. After being at street markets in Thailand and Peru, it was too many cheap knockoffs, clothes,shoes, glasses and bags! It wasn’t what we were expecting or hoping for. No local products available. Lots of food stalls and cheap beer everywhere and watch out for the motorbikes!
drawbacks: Lots of food stalls and cheap beer everywhere

author: Dawn H
title: Great for Shopaholics
original_content: The street has so many stalls - it goes on forever. Some close up by around 10pm.  Fantastic atmosphere.

author: Vivien
title: Crowded
original_content: It was quite crowded, and it was also raining when I was there, which made our trip to the night market less pleasant. There are a lot of shops and stalls by the road, but the prices are not like SUPER cheap, and I was expecting the place to have more night market food! I didn’t end up buying anything since it was not like really cheap compared to purchasing from an actual store and the items were not extremely attractive. But, I believe it’s nice to take a walk if you have nothing to do haha! I don’t think its necessarily a MUST go tourist spot, but I guess its a nice place to have a taste of the local Vietnamese culture. The streets were quite long and it is located next to the Bia Hoi Corner so you could go there and have a drink after walking the night market.
highlights: taste of the local Vietnamese culture
practical_tips: go there and have a drink after walking the night market

author: Phuketwergoing
title: Now this was fun. CHEAP CHEAP BIA HOI
original_content: Lots of stalls selling everything.  We got beer for around 50cents (AUD) a glass.Cold refreshing.....fantastic.Loved sitting on the little stools in the street watching people walk buy.Go.
highlights: Cold refreshing beer for 50 cents a glass
Sitting on little stools in the street watching people walk by

author: dejara
title: Bargain Paradise
original_content: Hanoi's Night Market is a nice place to buy all kind of souvenirs,clothing, shoes, T Shirts, electronics, cameras,headphones, glasses,jewelry and many items at bargain prices. Be aware that some electronics are not originals. I purchased a Bose headphone for $15 US dollars. It sells for over $150 in US. I found out later that it was a copy made in Pakistan, The  market is open only on week ends, ,
drawbacks: bought a copy of a Bose headphone

author: Emilygg
title: Funny
original_content: Had a fun time there shopping and eating. Busy but interesting. Found something cheap for kids back home.

author: Safemach
title: Loved it but not for the shopping
original_content: Amazing to see so many people having so much fun. I have no interest in buying stuff except the occasional mango in a bag, but I have never seen a city have so much fun with itself. Dancing, playing, fire eaters all sorts. Families, couples and everyone just enjoying themselves, great to see.Not for one second did I worry about my pockets or safety. Not a policeman in sight. Ok the guys pimping their neighbors daughter gets a bit annoying but they don’t pester.
drawbacks: guys pimping their neighbors daughter gets a bit annoying

author: sandymSeasister
title: A fun and vibey place
original_content: The weekend Market in the Old Quarter of Hanoi with a stroll around the lake, dinner at one of the many restaurants or coffee and ice cream at a pavement cafe is worth the time.  It’s fun and vibey and although I didn’t think prices were much better than you can barter for in the shops at the night market, it’s the ambience, the people-watching and the overall experience.  We actually stayed away from bargain hunting and rather watched street artists performing dance and music pieces, had a portrait done and were generally thoroughly entertained by the vibe strolling around the lake.
drawbacks: prices were much better than you can barter for in the shops at the night market

author: Robert M
title: Counterfeit Chinese tat.
original_content: This famous market thrives on selling counterfeit everything. Clothing, shoes, bags and top end electronic goods. Buy with humour, not with the view that you've bought a genuine bit of kit.The market is impressive though, taking up several streets, no stress busy atmosphere.We liked it, but we've seen enough fakes in our 3 week tour of Vietnam.

author: sally l
title: Plenty to see if you like markets
original_content: Markets aren’t really my thing. We went through the market on our way to a restaurant. It’s very busy with lots of stalls. Everything imaginable is on sale. In my opinion a lot of it isn’t particularly good but it’s horses for courses.

author: gordonj258
title: Sprawling market
original_content: The night market occupies many streets that have been closed to traffic. I found lots of things there that were cheap but also found that the stallholders were not prepared to really haggle as the base price is already exceptionally low.There are plenty of clothes, food and all the usual "souvenir" trinkets that you would expect. Very busy and an interesting way to spend a couple of hours.
drawbacks: stallholders were not prepared to really haggle
base price is already exceptionally low

author: Hardvision
title: Great bargains!
original_content: If you can accept that even if it says Abercombie & Fitch or Nike or Adidas, it is not the original and can bargain like crazy, this is the place. First of all the prices in local currency are crazy. Drop the last 3 zeros and divide by 23. That gives you the USD price. STart at about 20% of that price. In most of the places you can bargain and get the stuff for about 30% of the originally quoted price. Don't expect too much of quality. Quality does not come that cheap. The experience is worth it though. In the entire complex we saw only one shop which refused to lower the price and it was the most unusual of the shops over there.
drawbacks: Quality does not come that cheap
practical_tips: Start at about 20% of the original price
Bargain and get the stuff for about 30% of the originally quoted price

author: Heng How N
title: Special market
original_content: The market starts at 7pm and block traffic from using it. The place is converted to be place for many activities. It covers a big area from Hoan Kiem Lake towards the railway track.
highlights: converted to be place for many activities

author: Mark M
title: Haggle
original_content: At the weekend this street is closed off to traffic and stalls selling all kinds of merchandise are set up.We spent a good hour wandering the length of the market.Haggling is an absolute must. Offer 50% of the asking price to start the negotiations!
highlights: wandering the length of the market
practical_tips: offer 50% of the asking price to start negotiations

author: Rachael H
title: Busy, busy, busy
original_content: Really nice markets with lost of variety. There are both fake items and original items such as paintings. you are able to barter with the sellers to get more reasonable prices, really interesting place to visit

author: Traveller
title: Night market
original_content: The night market in Hanoi is only on the weekend, Friday - Sunday, 7pm-11pm.It’s one long strip of stalls in the middle of the road selling various things. One of the best things to experience in Hanoi.
highlights: one of the best things to experience in Hanoi

author: Edge Mirafuentes
title: Amazing food & Shopping
original_content: Open only on weekends from 7-10pm. This place is full of AMAZING food, entertainment & fun cheap haggle shopping!

author: carloscharmy
title: Just another SEA market
original_content: Coming from BKK I found nothing appealing in this market. Walked around it for 10 minutes and left. If  it is your 1st time in SEA give it a go.
drawbacks: walked around it for 10 minutes and left
practical_tips: If it is your 1st time in SEA give it a go

author: Becky & James
title: Typical Asian Night Market
original_content: I personally love the hustle and bustle of these markets - with the added fun of true Vietnamese bartering. Start bidding at 50% less than they ask for, and you can normally complete with a discount of about 30-40% off their price. Enjoy the bars and the old city gate whole you're in the vicinity.
practical_tips: Start bidding at 50% less than they ask for

author: b0rn2sh0p
title: Place for a bargain.
original_content: If you need cheap inflight carrier urgently, night market is the place for you. BigC market is twice more expensive than night market when it comes to carriers.
drawbacks: BigC market is twice more expensive
highlights: night market is the place for you
practical_tips: go to night market for cheap inflight carrier

author: iliketomoveandsee
title: Rubbish Market
original_content: I've been to many markets while travelling around Asia, and this was one of the worse. Crowded, scooters/motorbikes still riding down at speed even though the road is closed. The produce also isn't that great on the market - I wouldn't waste your time, to be honest.
drawbacks: scooters/motorbikes still riding down at speed even though the road is closed
The produce also isn't that great on the market

author: Bazza_752
title: Oversized china mall
original_content: Night market was essentially an oversized china mall... nice to see different environment - Lots of fake goods and knock-offs. I am not a fan of fake goods if you cannot afford the real item don’t buy a fake.
drawbacks: Lots of fake goods and knock-offs
practical_tips: Don't buy a fake if you cannot afford the real item

author: jongyungchoi99
title: nice
original_content: its long and having many gifts you can buy for your trip. and they are so cheap.you should see price which they write on paper and pay

author: fluffymonkey
title: Sunday family vibe
original_content: We visited the market on the Sunday evening, it was extremely busy so hold onto your kids if you have them! What really caught our eye though was the shear number of local families out with children enjoying a Sunday stroll and play around the top end of Hoam Kiem Lake. It was such an intoxicating atmosphere with kids playing the national sport (da cau), it involved kicking a weighted shuttlecock with feathers! and toddlers taking remote control cars for a spin (or rather the parents were controlling them!). Fascinating experience to see how Vietnamese go about their daily lives.
highlights: Shear number of local families out with children enjoying a Sunday stroll and play
Kids playing the national sport (da cau)
toddlers taking remote control cars for a spin
practical_tips: Hold onto your kids if you have them

author: Rui Jian Ng
title: Avoid Saturdays and go to shops with prices
original_content: Saturdays are very packed. If possible, head there on other days like Fri or Sun. Hectic place where you can get cheap clothes, shoes etc. Remember to bargain if possible but I reckon these days the vendors have placed their “best price” and hard to bargain down further. Word of advice: go for stalls with prices shown so you’ll at least have a benchmark and how to bargain. F&B: apart from the deep fried skewers, the sugarcane drink with lime is nice.
highlights: Sugarcane drink with lime is nice
practical_tips: Bargain at stalls with prices shown
Go for stalls with prices shown

author: webb s
title: Fun & crazy!
original_content: We were here on Sunday night. It was very crowded but exactly how I want it. There were many things to buy and many food joints to have some midnight snack. You might want a Vietnamese to accompany you or know enough language to get a raw deal. Still, everything is dirt cheap without a bargain. And the food is incredible as well.
drawbacks: You might want a Vietnamese to accompany you or know enough language to get a raw deal.

author: Siok H
title: Just feel the vibe
original_content: I went there to just feel the vibe but really got no patience to walk around with two young kids under my arm.  Goods are not interesting.

author: scubacol11
title: Shopping fun hustle and bustle
original_content: The market is open 19.00 to 23.00 Friday to Sunday nights,they close off several streets in the old town directly north of the lake so easy to find.The stalls are set up down the middle of the road in a back to back lay out so it is best to walk up one side then back down the other then you can look at the market stall and also the shop there too.My tip would be to walk all the way up and down first and get an idea of whats on sale and how many similar stalls and shops are selling the goods you may be interested in before you start shopping and haggling,a lot of the stalls are just extensions of the shops they are outside off and if they don"t have the exact item you want they will go to the shop and try to find it.Many of the stall are selling the usual fake designer goods but as long as you expect this you know they can"t be genuine by the low prices they are willing to sell them at,that said if you haggle you can get some bargains in clothes,shoes,artwork,ceramics,hiking wear and many souvenirs.There are many food stalls spread throughout the market so you can always get a snack if you are hungry but on some of the streets that adjoin the main avenue they are set out with many food and beer shops and there is a great atmosphere with plenty of choice of where to eat and drink and plenty of music to listen to.I found some prices far cheaper on the market than in the shops during the day as there was so much competition the vendors were willing to be haggled down more,Great fun if you enjoy the thrill of the haggling chase as I do,I see it as a participation sport and great fun and the stall and shop owners are not aggressive at all.Many people warn you to be careful with your wallets,but that"s the same anywhere in a market like this.
highlights: bargains in clothes, shoes, artwork, ceramics, hiking wear, and souvenirs
plenty of choice of where to eat and drink
practical_tips: walk all the way up and down first to get an idea of whats on sale

author: joanne h
title: your best option for a market
original_content: all the markets are now aimed a tourists, but this was the best out of all of them. If you are travelling in vietman Hanoi is much much cheaper than HO Chi Minh. They are not as aggressive at haggling as other Asian countries, its more like a reduction in price than a full blown haggle. We went at 8pm, still too early stalls just setting up.
highlights: best out of all of them

author: MMvet
title: Night markets
original_content: The usual hassle and bustle of markets.  Keep you wits about you and your valuables.  What was on offer can be purchased at any other market. We were fully prepared to barter but the sellers weren’t that interested in bartering, the would only knock a few dollars off the price or not at all, regardless of how much you may buy.
drawbacks: sellers weren’t that interested in bartering
would only knock a few dollars off the price or not at all
What was on offer can be purchased at any other market
practical_tips: Keep you wits about you and your valuables

author: Kalie L
title: Bit of bartering fun
original_content: Be prepared for banana shirts and matching shorts. All a bit of fun, we had a few beers on bir corner then went for a look. Quite good quality clothing, the usual bits and bobs like all markets. People were lovely. Watch your bag and keep it to the front of you, even the locals remind you....

Most of the places were pretty much the same, and just about everything was cheap and tacky. I didn't buy much because the clothing wasn't good quality and I was concerned about the origins of those clothes, I imagine their production involves a lot of underpaid, badly treated, overworked workers, potentially even slavery.

author: Isabella B
title: Horror behind the facade of cheap goods
original_content: My partner and I went to the market and warn families not to come here.Behind the facade of glimmering lights and cheap goods is a horrific image. We witnessed a disfigured woman (not born with those disfigurements) crawling on her hands ( of which had been taken off so were just stumps) and knees attached like a dog on a leash to a pram full of heavy items, pushing a weighed down bucket with her head. A toddler was tied to her side. This woman crawled the whole length of the market on her bare skin. meanwhile we noticed shady looking men watching her on motorbikes, we assume to ensure nobody interfered. This is one of the most horrific sights I have seen in my life. Be warned this is not a sight for children and I’m horrified at what we saw. Absolutely terrible I cannot imagine the horrible life of this women, her fate is one which I don’t believe uncommon. Please be careful

author: Gaza74
title: informative War history museum from the Vietnamese point of view
original_content: It was quite sunny/hot on the day we visited the very informative Vietnamese War History Museum (presented from the Vietnamese people’s point of view), A lot of things to look at outside, each exhibit was very well explained on individual signs, (Highly recommend a good hat & sunscreen), then we went inside the main building, the building was lovely, well air conditioned & very clean & tidy. We found the exhibition quite awkward & disjointed, with no direction as to where to go. The exhibition itself was excellent, everything was well described in English as well as other languages. I had no idea that the Vietnamese people had endured so much more war than what we know as “the Vietnam War that ended in 1973”,  We would recommend that visitors to this museum visit the reception desk in the main foyer to get a map, not advertised & or even signed. Feedback for the museum itself, i would suggest they paint or put stickers on the floor showing the direction & flow of the exhibit so it makes sense, failing that little free standing signs to do the same so you don’t miss anything.
extracted_spaces: reception desk in the main foyer
drawbacks: no direction as to where to go

author: The Graffster freelance travel writer
title: Real Life History
original_content: If you are a lover of military history and how Vietnam came into being do get the taxi ride to the Vietnam Military History Museum, you will not regret it. The newly built museum (it opened to the public in November 2024) is grandiose and magnificent. Inside and outside the impressive building there are thousands of artifacts from the time of the Chinese domination in the 900s to French colonisation in the 19th Century to the American invasion and repulsion in the mid-70s. If you like to be close up to military equipment such as planes and tanks you will not  be disappointed. When I went you witness genuine pride from Vietnamese people old and young who attend the museum knowing that it has suffered a tremoudous amount to be now a free and independent state.
highlights: thousands of artifacts from different time periods
close up to military equipment such as planes and tanks
practical_tips: get the taxi ride to the museum

author: samay Vora
title: Unveiling Vietnam's Past: A Must-Visit Military Museum Experience
original_content: The Vietnam Military History Museum in Hanoi is an absolute must-visit for anyone seeking to grasp the nation's profound history. Its "super structure" and extensive exhibits powerfully narrate Vietnam's epic struggles.You'll gain invaluable insight into the protracted conflicts against France, USA, and China, presented from a uniquely Vietnamese perspective. The sheer volume of genuine artifacts, from downed aircraft to personal effects, is deeply moving.The "super building" itself is a stark reminder of the resilience and ingenuity born from these wars. It's not just a collection of objects; it's a testament to the indomitable spirit of a nation.Prepare to be immersed in stories of courage, sacrifice, and ultimately, triumph. This museum is essential to understanding the very fabric of modern Vietnam. A truly impactful and unforgettable experience.
highlights: gain invaluable insight into the protracted conflicts
a testament to the indomitable spirit of a nation
practical_tips: Prepare to be immersed in stories of courage, sacrifice, and ultimately, triumph

author: Me_n_my_rucksack
title: New location out of town - a new modern museum well worth the visit.
original_content: Importantly - this Museum has moved ! It is no longer in the middle of the city.  It is now in the suburbs a 20 to 30 min drive out of the middle of town. (Using the Grab App its still only a few pounds) Head for the Vincom Megacity Smart mall (A moders shopping Centre) and its the other side of a dual carriageway with an underpass.The new museum is large - massive comcrete multi story building with large galleries (some of which were not finished when we visited.  The external displays are generally the ones which were previously displayed in the old museum in town.  As you enter the museum grounds to the left are US Aircraft and tanks, to the right Vietnamese aircraft SAMs and Radars.Fortunateley some of the political propoganda of the old museum has been toned down - after all somewhere claiming to be a Museum presents facts and artefacts not a one sided biased account.  The new museum is still a long way from being an impartial account of history but its better than the old one.When we visited the museum had been open a week, some of the galleries were empty and the escalators didnt work.  It was free for the first month and it was heaving with visitors.   The obvious bias aside this is an excellent museum displaying the tanks aircraft etc with lots of space around them and very accessable.  Very well worth the trip out of the City to visit it.
drawbacks: some of the galleries were empty

author: Art S

author: Susan C
title: A history of resistance
original_content: This was the first war museum we visited in Vietnam though not the last. It is an extensive museum that ended up taking the whole morning to complete. In the outside sections there are many examples of planes, tanks, rockets and artillery with clear signage. There are also interesting sculptures with some made out of the wreckage of bombers. This is also a simple way of visiting the Hanoi Flag Tower which gives you views over Hanoi and the museum from its first two levels.In the multiple buildings there are exhibits about the wars with China from 214 BC to 1789 and then the resistance against the French from 1858 to 1954 and the Americans 1954-1975. We saw again information on the 1972 bombing of Hanoi (there was also a temporary exhibition in Hoa Lo Prison). We sat through some tactical reconstructions of battles with AV presentations that lit up with lights showing offensive and defensive actions though the dialogue was only in Vietnamese. However, many of the signs include English explanations. On a practical note, some of these rooms are air conditioned and some use fans which were a relief in the September weather. This museum encapsulates the Vietnamese history of resistance to invasions and gives details of how they did it and the weapons and methods they used.
drawbacks: some rooms are air conditioned and some use fans

author: Rincewind
title: Great displays, especially the outdoor displays.
original_content: There are many museums in Hanoi covering different branches of the military (infantry, air-force, B-52 defense, etc). This one is the most centrally located, just to the west of the Old Quarter near Hanoi Train Street and Lenin Park. The museum has is split over several buildings with displays on the ground and upper floors as well as several areas outside for larger exhibits such as tanks and aircraft. Most of the museum covers the colonization by, and war with, France. Only a fraction covers the war with the US or China, although the outside exhibits are mostly from the war with the US.There is a general lack of narrative to the museum. It is mostly just a display of stuff in roughly chronological order. Here's a thing, here's its name, that's it. The only exception is the audiovisual display about Dien Bien Phu which does a decent job of illustrating the order of battle.The best part is the outdoor exhibit. There are a decent number of airplanes, helicopters, tanks and artillery pieces. Make sure to go right to the back of the museum because there is more tucked around the corner that you might miss.

One of my uncle was born there. They left in 1911. When France lost Vietnam in 1954 (with USA help). America took over telling us, you French you don’t anything, we are taking over, and you’ll see how to handle the problem! It’s going to be quite fast. What they did, sorry, a shame! To end the war in 1973. Then to put an embargo during 20 years! Then to say sorry! No! Sorry my Vietnamese friends.
