author: Mark
title: The Big One
original_content: I visited every military museum I could during my exploration of Vietnam and none even came close to the Vietnam Military History Museum, aka the "Army Museum". Hardware galore featuring as a centerpiece the distorted remains of an American B52 Stratocaster bomber shot down over Hanoi--grotesque modern art. It's a location you could easily spend an afternoon visiting. I slowly and methodically went through every gallery and spent an hour outside and felt I had seen it all, but it took nearly four hours. Right outside the gate I had a fantastic cup of coffee, but then--that's everywhere in Vietnam. Visiting Hanoi and missing this museum would be a big mistake. If you only see a single military collection, this is the mother of them all.
highlights: distorted remains of an American B52 Stratocaster bomber
practical_tips: visit Hanoi and don't miss this museum

author: Antonieta
title: Only on the outside
original_content: I didn’t enter, only wandered on the outside, that is totally worth it!So many USA planes!And learning that the US dropped more that 5kk tons of bombs on Vietnam is scary!

author: Pushpal P
title: Nice collection of aircrafts from Vietnam war
original_content: This place has a good collection of aircrafts from vietnam war. Will give you good feel of what was the air power then. They even have some destructed b52 bomber. The SAMs tanks mig 21 and helicopter. You can also climb the flag tower for a brids eye view. Good place military aircraft lovers
highlights: Climb the flag tower for a bird's eye view
practical_tips: Good place for military aircraft lovers

author: Raymondale
title: Learn something about military
original_content: This museum presents the First and second Indochina wars from a Vietnamese perspective.there are plenty of authentic war relics, weapons...Interesting attractions include the wreckage of an American B-52 bomber, an M107 self-propelled gun, and a military tank that had ploughed through the gates of Saigon’s Presidential Palace...even i am not a fan of military,still learn something from the museum.the Flag Tower is beside the museum,admission is free from the highlands cafe.Opposite the museum,it is Lenin park,if you have time can relax there.
highlights: Wreckage of an American B-52 bomber
practical_tips: Admission is free from the highlands cafe
Relax in Lenin park if you have time

author: BelgiumWdb
title: Amazing stop in Hanoi
original_content: For all who like military history. Interesting displays, impressive collection of airplanes and helicopter from the Vietnam war. A bit one sided: who can blame them. :-)

author: Susannah P
title: Average
original_content: Was rather looking forward to seeing the Vietnamese take on the war with America.  However this section of their history wasn't particularly well covered.However, it was reasonably interesting for a couple of hours
extracted_spaces: Vietnamese take on the war with America
drawbacks: section of their history wasn't particularly well covered

author: Mark M
title: Interesting collection
original_content: A great collection of military articles spanning the history of Vietnam, from tribal weaponry, cannons through to planes and helicopters from the American (Vietnam) War. Also some relevant modern sculptures and access to the flag tower.

author: KGB777
title: Interesting collection
original_content: We visited here together with the flag tower. There's a good collection of aircraft to see outside, which kept the kids entertained for a while.

author: Joe Clarke
title: Nice attraction but needs refining
original_content: After studying the History of Vietnam at university, my partner and I decided to visit this museum whilst on holiday in Hanoi. Whilst it was a lovely museum, with great indoor and outdoor exhibits. There are a few things which are incorrect; a lot of the aircraft plaques had generic captions such as calling numerous aeroplanes “helicopters” which was actually quite comedic after the tenth occurrence. Numerous pieces of military equipment were also labelled incorrectly such as calling an American M14 Rifle a “Vietnamese Rifle”. Other than these infrequent errors, my partner and I enjoyed our visit and would recommend it to others who are interested in military history.

author: leeoliver2018
title: The view from the other side
original_content: Quaint displays and a great explanation of Dien Buen Phu. Very interesting to see history from the other side’s perspective.  So this wasn’t a ‘Vietnam War’ museum and the US is the imperialist invader and its allies, including South Korea and South Vietnam, are puppet troops. Fascinating

author: John K
title: Worth A Visit - If Only For The Sculpture
original_content: a tremendous work of art - aesthetically rich - it's all there - form - texture - color - conflict - tension - balance - symbolism - and packed with triggers - whether intended or unintended - that hit you at your deepest - an intangible rightness prevailing - this gloating sculpture - of terror - of victory - of national pride - of humiliation - of destruction - of hubris - of ignorance - of death - this pile of junk - wreckage of French and American aircraft shot-down by Vietnamese troops in the resistance war against the French Colonialists and also in the United States Sabotage War in North Viet Nam - it's a big flip-off - perhaps rightfully so - and it is glorious -- so riveted - I was compelled to circle it - numerous times - and even after stepping away from the area - returning - to see it from all sides again - and again - as a whole - and then in sections - and finally small details - cracked windows - some equipment operating text - in English - spray-painted on what was the outside of a plane - the amount of smash in the smashed engines - element-worn wing-stars - scrapes and scratches - a head-height propeller jutting out beyond the guard line - long thin sheets of metal - able to catch enough wind to flap and sway but unable to tear themselves away - an - almost annoying in its nature-always-wins cliched self plant that has taken root amidst this chaos - and cherry-topping the entire heap - as if locking this all together - should you have any further questions - the torn-off - ill-divined - tail-end of an aircraft - a dunces cap - a peak - a shape - that from the symbols pounded into my head since before I am able to remember - conjures both Brazil's Christ the Redeemer - and Lebanon's Our Lady in Harissa - all here in this defiant - breathtaking work - in this bold abstract representation - of the other side of the story - on the other side of the world -
extracted_times: after stepping away from the area, returning
drawbacks: wreckage of French and American aircraft
practical_tips: return to see it from all sides again

author: Kieron Ball
title: History in front of your eyes
original_content: For years I had heard from my instructors about their time in Vietnam during the war so it was like seeing their history come to life for me as I hadn’t seen most of the hardware before . The exhibits are described in English as well as Vietnamese and it was awesome .
highlights: exhibits are described in English as well as Vietnamese
seeing their history come to life

author: Steve W
title: Brilliant museum.
original_content: An excellent collection of artifacts from Vietnam's military history that starts with internal fights during the formation of Vietnam, the several wars with different Chinese dynasties, French colonisation (twice), the Japanese in WWII, and finally the Vietnam War, (or the American War as it is known).Considering its size Vietnam has certainly held it's own throughout this history, surviving occupation and invasions.
highlights: Vietnam has certainly held it's own throughout this history

author: Govindan N
title: Excellent Museum
original_content: The Vietnam Military History Museum Hanoi houses a collection of weaponry that was used in Vietnam War. Notable attractions include the wreckage of an American B-52 bomber, an M107 self-propelled gun, and a military tank that had ploughed through the gates of Saigon’s Presidential Palace, thus ending the Vietnam War in 1975. You can also find improvised weapons and exhibits of artefacts dating back to the Hong Bang Dynasty.Entry ticket to Museum -VND 30,000  Camera charges – VND 20000 Museum Opening Hours: Daily 08:00 - 11:30 Tuesday – Thursday, Saturday & Sunday 14:00 – 16:00
highlights: collection of weaponry used in Vietnam War
wreckage of an American B-52 bomber
military tank that had ploughed through the gates of Saigon’s Presidential Palace

author: HistoryTravelSte
title: Interesting - Vietnamese perspective!
original_content: I really enjoyed the visit to this museum; it is well laid out, with a chronological approach to Vietnam’s military history. There is a fascinating range of artefacts on display, and some good models displaying key areas of the French and American Wars. As noted in many reviews already, much of the coverage is from the North Vietnamese perspective, but this doesn’t take away from a fascinating insight into the mindset of the Vietnamese people toward their military history. Highly recommend this museum for any fan of history.
practical_tips: Highly recommend this museum for any fan of history

author: Matthew P
title: Planes Tanks and Choppers
original_content: Interesting place to while away a good few hours learning all about the many atrocities that took place in what was the Vietnam war from the start, with conflicts with the French Imperialists from the early 1950's through to the 1975 liberation of Saigon and the reunification of this wonderful land.  There are also loads of old planes and other military hardware to look at from the US, China & what was the USSR.
highlights: interesting place to learn about the Vietnam war
loads of old planes and military hardware

author: Vignesh Srinivasan
title: Excellent museum with great displays
original_content: The museum had excellent open air displays of tanks, flights etc that were very realistic replicas of wartime. They also had a tall tower from where its excellent to view all the outdoor displays. The indoor displays depict wars from several centuries ago. There are 2 indoor museums. The only issue is that visitors may need to time their visit well - the museum opens late and closes by 4.30 PM.
drawbacks: visitors may need to time their visit well
highlights: excellent to view all the outdoor displays

author: 181ShellBell
title: Good Display and History
original_content: I took my 15 year old son to this museum which is in the same area as the Flag Tower.  We found this place interesting and enjoyed looking and reading what it offered.  I think it's worth a visit.

author: Denise S
title: Warmongering...... recent and past.
original_content: This Museum contains a lot of vintage, decommissioned, seized and destroyed machinery and vehicle from the different eras of the wars that occurred throughout the history of Vietnam. There was a lot of historical interest to be seen here,especially with the  remnants and whole machinery relating to the Vietnam War which mainly displayed captured American items.  There were also examples of Russian planes and equipment displayed. However there were artifacts and displays that encompassed from early precolonial history through to the First Indo -China war and the second. For me who loves old architecture, I was drawn to the Flag Tower of Hanoi which was built in 1812. I love flying so I was drawn to the planes and in particular the remnants of Aircraft wreckage assembled as monument. Quite sobering to look at the mangled machinery etc.There is a Highland Cafe, which is good for lunch or a coffee, and to have a rest before exploring the museum some more.  I would highly recommend visiting this museum as you can absorb the history through the Vietnamese perspective.

author: Jerzy N
title: Complete waste of money
original_content: All what’s interesting is outside for free. What you pay for is a propaganda how cruel French were and how humane Viet cong was. All on few photos and banners. Not worth money we paid.
drawbacks: Propaganda how cruel French were and how humane Viet cong was
Paid for something not worth it

author: John H
title: their side of the american war
original_content: this was rather too full of american hardware, although parts of a B52 have been used to make a sculpture.

author: HuahinCharlie
title: The American War
original_content: A nice walk from my hotel and stopped of to see the Flag tower and the incorporated Vietnam military history museum. If you are interested in this conflict and have seen Burns' documentary (among other things) then this is of interest with some 70's and earlier implements of war. The T34 inside was in great condition as was the A/C on the day I visited after depositing small rucksack at front desk. An APC was being worked on during my visit - must have been 40deg C + inside the hull.The downed US bomber was artfully arranged and there are a number of stalls for eats and drinks on site.
highlights: T34 inside was in great condition
downed US bomber was artfully arranged
practical_tips: Deposit small rucksack at front desk

author: Craig D
title: Very different to the War Remnants Museum in Ho Chi Minh- worth a visit
original_content: The Vietnam Military History Museum is not as polished as the War Remnants Museum, nor is it as 'in your face'. This museum highlights the strengths of the Vietnamese and the wars and struggles that they have endured and won over the millennia. The War Remnants Museum is a reminder of the atrocities perpetrated by the US and allied forces during the Vietnam/US conflict.
highlights: wars and struggles that they have endured and won over the millennia

author: Noam W
title: Good for those who have some knowledge
original_content: After 10 episodes of the epic Vietnam War documentary, by Ken Burns, this is a must see visit for the history of this sad war. Feel it from the eyes of the Vietnamese side. Exhibition it self isn't very much of a thrill, so an hour or two will be definitely enough to get the vibe
drawbacks: exhibition it self isn't very much of a thrill
highlights: a must see visit for the history of this sad war
Feel it from the eyes of the Vietnamese side
practical_tips: an hour or two will be definitely enough

author: Travelingjohn123
title: Nice museum
original_content: Nice museum of Vietnamese military history (which to 99% of people means the American and French Wars)Dien Bien Phu section of French history very good but I’m guessing most people are just interested in the US (and puppet South) vs North Vietnam. Very one sided propaganda version of events, which is at odds with the common US version of history - but the North won, so in this case they are allowed to write the story! Interesting displays and lots of tanks and jets outside. It is a bit neglected and the US jets in particular could use a coat of paint and some TLC, But otherwise an interesting museum if you want history from a different perspective.
drawbacks: US jets could use a coat of paint and some TLC
highlights: lots of tanks and jets outside
practical_tips: go if you want history from a different perspective

author: David Fredericks
title: Hanoi military museum
original_content: For anyone interested in the military history of Vietnam this is a must see. Many people will only comment on the Vietnam War (or more precisely the American War to the Vietnamese people) aspects of the museum but it covers the Vietnamese people's experience with war going back to the Chinese thousands of years ago and more recently the French in the 50s and 60s.Take your time to see all the exhibits and learn a bit about their rich history, not just the Vietnam War
highlights: covers the Vietnamese people's experience with war going back to the Chinese thousands of years ago
covers the Vietnamese people's experience with war more recently the French in the 50s and 60s
learn a bit about their rich history
practical_tips: Take your time to see all the exhibits

author: TheDaddyP1967
title: Great to walk round and see items and stories of the past history of this beautiful country
original_content: Lots of artefacts and articles about the wars the country has been through some great war items they had a mig Russian fighter as well as some scraps of American bombers and different tanks and weapons. Hot day walking around but really enjoyed it.
highlights: some scraps of American bombers and different tanks and weapons

author: Ian G
title: Worth Visiting
original_content: Lots of interesting things to see, a lot of artefacts from the American war on display as static displays. What i found fascinating is the displays devoted to the struggle for Independence against the French and how a grass roots movement grew into something that overthrew not only their colonial overlords but also succeeded in the American war as well.Interesting also to see a different slant on the American War to that of Hollywood and the popular media that we've been fed.i particulary like the central monument made from the remains from shot down aircraft, very effective i thought...
practical_tips: Go to see the Independence displays

author: Cathee
title: Interesting
original_content: There's an extended history of warfare in Vietnam. There's a saying " you've to be powerful or others are going to take you land". The museum houses parts from different wars were armies have taken the land of theirs and the Vietnamese have battled back. This extends back a quite a while. The greater recent Vietnam war is just a part of it.

author: Osgood
title: A must to see
original_content: I liked the museum as much as a place but at this point I'd gone to a few museums of the Military, Groundbreaking and Ho Chi Minh form in different locations in Vietnam and definitely the Prison Museum in Hanoi therefore I was somewhat tired of the propaganda and also the anti-American and anti-French bias as well as identical pictures. I suspect it will have made much more of an influence on me in case it was the very first one I'd been to. Nevertheless, it's a great museum of the kind of its, particularly in case it's the first of the kind that you visit.

author: Red
title: worth a visit
original_content: Interesting slant on Vietnamese military historical past from the early past to the current day. Nevertheless, in case you're extremely restricted, you are able to enter for free as there's a coffee shop adjacent with access from no restriction and the road on entering the museum campus. Once inside, your ticket isn't checked. having gone to the Hanoi Hilton earlier in the day' we paid our quid. You will find signs letting you know not to get on the exhibits, though I assume in case you cannot read English or maybe Vietnamese then you may think you are able to run riot! Hardly any information on the American war in this particular museum, virtually all of the exhibits are from the Chinese and french conflicts, nonetheless, the automobiles and planes come from the later battle. The Vietnamese are thin on specifics, exhibits simply let you know what the point is and often who donated it or maybe that glorious unit liberated it. Very little on the story of conflicts or perhaps any explanation of timelines or battles. Worth the coffee and an hour was excellent. The museum has toilets as well, which happens to be a bonus.
drawbacks: Hardly any information on the American war
Exhibits lack specifics on conflicts or timelines
Limited information on the story of battles
highlights: Interesting slant on Vietnamese military historical past
Automobiles and planes from the later battle
Worth the coffee and an hour
practical_tips: Enter for free if extremely restricted
Check signs not to get on exhibits

author: Eziechiele
title: Museum worth it
original_content: we have to see all points of reference to the history of ours. And it is not only around the impact on the war on Vietnamese but additionally the Americans and the children of theirs. The truth is quite thought provoking about companies and the contribution of theirs to wars as well as the American options in just how we battle them.
extracted_spaces: points of reference to the history of ours
the Americans and the children of theirs
highlights: thought provoking about companies and the contribution of theirs to wars

author: Carmen T
title: Biased
original_content: Cost about 40 000 VND to get in .  There are alot of things to see such as aircrafts, tanks,  weapons and even a flag tower. Its a cool place to check out the history however it is very biased so take it as a grain of salt.  Some images may be gruesome to see. It is worth checking out and reccomended to spend 90 mins there to see it all.
drawbacks: Some images may be gruesome to see
highlights: Cool place to check out the history
practical_tips: Spend 90 minutes there to see it all

author: CSQUARED
title: Cool museum and exhibits, very hard to navigate and too much propaganda
original_content: The museum has extremely cool pictures from the wars against the French and Americans. However, the text descriptions of what occurred during the wars were extremely vague and in embarrassingly broken english for a museum. Also, the propaganda in the way they portrayed the war against the Americans while dismissing the Southern Vietnamese as simply puppets was a little ridiculous. Was hoping to get the North Vietnam perspective of the war, instead just got a bunch of lies and misinformation.
drawbacks: Text descriptions of what occurred during the wars were extremely vague
Propaganda in the way they portrayed the war against the Americans

author: paul w
title: Very well organised and interesting museum
original_content: I must confess having a father in the military I tend to always be particularly interested in military history and artefacts. The museum is laid out across several buildings and floors in a chronological order (if you enter by the wrong door you’ve suddenly find you’ve skipped twenty years). Almost all of the exhibits have English translation - some incredible historic photos and a lot of very interesting facts and information provided. Found it very well balanced and for me, minimal propaganda against the various enemies they have faced over the centuries (and beyond). The are a number of tanks, planes etc in immediate view but don,t miss the hardware on display behind Building 3 ( it’s not that obvious)
practical_tips: don't miss the hardware on display behind Building 3

author: aaong86
title: Interesting history of Vietnam
original_content: The museum consists of various buildings. Different eras of Vietnamese military history are showcased in different buildings. The Flag Tower of Hanoi is within the bounds of the complex as well.The entire complex was huge and I spent quite a few hours walking around. There were thousands of exhibits (mostly artifacts) with English explanation.A must visit when you are in Hanoi!
highlights: A must visit when you are in Hanoi!
thousands of exhibits (mostly artifacts) with English explanation
practical_tips: spend quite a few hours walking around

author: Gary E
title: Very informative
original_content: We enjoyed the tour of the museum, it has plenty to look at.There is lots of artifacts, war information and military equipment. The musuem is reasonably priced, you need to time your visit as there is a lunch break for approx. 1 1/2 hours. A really excellent must do activity.

author: Patrick D
title: Vietnam Military History Museum
original_content: The Museum of Military History makes it possible especially to understand the Vietnamese history since 1945 until now. More than 2 thousand documents and precious objects give a glimpse of the evolution of the country from the time of the Hung kings to that of Ho Chi Minh. But it is especially the period of the wars of Indochina and Vietnam during which Vietnam sought to regain its independence against the French and then the Americans which is highlighted.The museum is divided into six parts: the Vietnamese heroic mothers, a heroic nation, the heroic people's army of Vietnam, the traditions of the Vietnamese People's Army, weapons and weapons manufacturing, the support of the international community in Vietnam during the war and relations between the Vietnamese People's Army and other countriesNational relics are exhibited such as the MIG 21 aircraft driven by Pham Tuan during the 1972 battle of Dien Bien Phu. tank 843 which broke the gates of the Independence Palace on April 30, 1975, ending the Saigon regime See also the citadel of Thang Long and the Flag Tower which offers a panoramic view of the city i. This observation tower built in the 19th century is one of the few ancient Vietnamese buildings that were not destroyed during the French colonial period. Very interesting museum because it presents the military strategies put in places, and one discovers there the technical dimensions of a warThe museum is opposite Lenin ParkEntry fee for foreigners: VND 40,000 / personSupplement for a camera, phone: VND 30,000Next to the museum, there is a cafe with a very large shaded terrace, possibility  to have a drink, (  very good pastry,)  restaurant
highlights: presents the military strategies put in places

author: Polisgirl
title: Really interesting
original_content: This is great for anyone interested in history.  The exhibits were really informative and the photo opportunities with the tanks and helicopters were good.

author: Christy V
title: Great place to visit
original_content: Interesting military history to learn about with many exhibits to view. A large outdoor collection of aircraft as well. We were glad we stopped by to tour.

author: Bangoe
title: Glimpse of history
original_content: Interesting place to visit to learn about the history of Vietnam. Rather well laid out. I just do not understand why they charge extra for "camera". Almost as much as for a person. Especially as taking photos with your phone seems to be free (everyone did it).
drawbacks: almost as much as for a person
taking photos with your phone seems to be free
highlights: learn about the history of Vietnam

author: Mike K
title: Cheap entry and worth a visit if your in Hanoi.
original_content: Spent a couple of hours here, lots to see including planes, helicopter, tanks and other vehicles.  The flag tower is also incorporated in this area.

author: gastronaut_11
title: Worth a visit
original_content: Good chronological history of the military struggles that Vietnam has undertaken through the ages. Most relics relate to the French colonialism era. Certainly worth a visit. Cheap entry fee. Watch out for the buses, which park immediately adjacent to the outdoor sited planes and armour.
highlights: Good chronological history of the military struggles

author: Andreaobrien1
title: History of wars in Vietnam
original_content: This museum takes you through all the history of conflicts that have impacted Vietnam from the Chinese occupation, french and Vietnam war in the 60s, 70s. Some great photos and images, like the prison much propaganda but you can see the struggle of the people and the country. Plenty of Russian, Chinese and USA military artefacts.

author: lucasjnl
title: Must see in Hanoi
original_content: Various buildings with extensive displays. Big choppers outside. Especially the French colonial war section was an eyeopener. The Dien Bien Phu presentation is very striking with a complete lightshow of strategic moves. Beware of the curious siesta opening hours. Complementary to the War Remnants Museum down in Saigon.
drawbacks: Beware of the curious siesta opening hours
practical_tips: Complementary to the War Remnants Museum down in Saigon

author: PETER J
title: A Must see to understand the country
original_content: An expected 1 hour visit turned to 3 plus . It's not so much the heavy equipment outside , it's the graphic photo's & the stories & numbers that go with them at this museum . I went from the top of Vietnam to the bottom by train , passing through all the farms & villages & this is what made this far more confronting to think what so many of Vietnam's people have lived through . Visit the Museum & i'm sure you'll have different outlook on both the people & the country .
highlights: different outlook on both the people & the country

author: Badger
title: Fascinating
original_content: Well worth a visit depicts the history of Vietnam for thousands of years and of course the 60’s:70’s , obvious North bias with references to the Puppet south but a very interesting visit that I recommend

author: ZBH88
title: Grizzly
original_content: A very deep and matter of fact portrayal of the war in Vietnam. Accurate as war is war and it doesn't discriminate. It's 40000 to enter each and younger children are free. Children of all ages are allowed but it's your choice if you feel it suitable as there are many colour photos and grapgic descriptions of deformities resulting from the use of agent orange, torture being carried out and dismemberment/dead bodies. We took our 2 year old but he is too young to pick up on it. There are a number of militarty planes, helicopters and artillery in the yard outside of the museum. There are toilet facilities on site and the odd gift shop.
drawbacks: Graphic descriptions of deformities resulting from the use of agent orange
Torture being carried out and dismemberment/dead bodies
highlights: Accurate portrayal of the war in Vietnam
practical_tips: Children of all ages are allowed but it's your choice if you feel it suitable

author: pratikshahi
title: Must visit for military history
original_content: i have always been fascinated with Military and war history, watching movies and playing games based war.  It was an absolute treat for me to see all the military equipment and ammunition. Everyone might not enjoy it as much as i did. But its a very cool place to explore.
drawbacks: Everyone might not enjoy it as much as i did
highlights: a very cool place to explore
practical_tips: go if you're interested in Military and war history

author: Karina P
title: War is over
original_content: I don't find war that intertaining, think it is sad. Costs 110.000 in all for 2 people with camera. It is quiet a big place, and guess you could spend a couple of hours there, 2 hours was enough for us. Non of the videos and audio worked. The most interesting was all the old airplans, choppers and tanks. You can also see the flagtower on this trip.

author: Vasudev68
title: A must visit
original_content: Located in old Hanoi city area, it houses various military equipment. It also has planes, helicopter, ammunition seized from Americans during their long battle. It has an in-house theater showing  small movie clip on early wars.

author: BC
title: Really Good
original_content: This was a really good visit, showcasing such of the military history of Vietnam, with many big planes and tanks to look at too. It was very sobering in places as it detailed the horrible acts of the americans, which really made you think. A must see.
highlights: showcasing such of the military history of Vietnam
many big planes and tanks to look at

author: Carolyn C
title: Amazing
original_content: Whilst we aren’t military people, we visited the museum whilst in Hanoi and OMG, this place blew my mind. It has so many artefacts and the history displays are so informative. My 11 year old son learnt so much and so did I. If you have time, make sure you visit, but note that it is closed at times during the day.
drawbacks: closed at times during the day
practical_tips: note that it is closed at times during the day

author: Alex C
title: Badly organised and uninformative
original_content: Really disappointed by this museum. The layout was so unclear we found ourselves skipping around chronologically quite a bit.I wanted to go to find out more about the first and second Indochina wars. To be honest, I learnt nothing (certainly nothing I didn't already know - which isn't much). There's a lot of pictures of Uncle Ho meeting with various parties, signing documents etc. but not enough content/text to really get an idea of what is going on. The second Indochina war (the Vietnam War) got a little bit tedious to be honest. Being neither American nor Vietnamese, I don't have ultra strong views on the war and I do have some sympathy for a Hanoi museum showing a bit of a one-sided picture. That said, there's a limit to how many times you can be presented with VC weapons used to bravely, annihilate the enemy excellently while similar looking US weapons were used to torture and kill and not got a bit bored.Of course, facts and artifacts don't lie. There were a number of military vehicles to look at. If you enjoy watching hoards of Chinese tourists trample over 'Do not cross' signs and clamber into the museum's private property (jeeps and planes) then this museum is a must see.
drawbacks: Learnt nothing about the first and second Indochina wars
One-sided picture of the Vietnam War
practical_tips: Be prepared for crowds of Chinese tourists
Watch out for 'Do not cross' signs

author: GWYN33
title: Sobering visit
original_content: Superb collection of military artefacts greet you - People forget that the Vietnamese were involved in a series of wars of liberation from the French and later US intervention - this is all chronicles here in an excellent museum. Well worth a visit.

author: ESVincent
title: Everyone goes and there is a very good reason...
original_content: This Museum is very much on the tourist trail both Vietnamese and International but having said that it never feels over whelming. The story told is unsurprisingly one of throwing off Colonial oppressors whether those are Thai from the 14th C, the French or later Americans. It is of course the French and American conflicts that dominate but their is long history of independence struggle and you do wonder how both the French and Americans misread the tide for independence for so long. The atrocities are one sided though and don't show the total picture.The Museum has an amazing range of vehicles, planes and items but not everything is explained. This is a worthwhile visit if only to look at historical folly . Fascinating
drawbacks: The atrocities are one sided though and don't show the total picture.
highlights: The story told is unsurprisingly one of throwing off Colonial oppressors
The Museum has an amazing range of vehicles, planes and items
practical_tips: This is a worthwhile visit if only to look at historical folly

author: Granduelle
title: Interesting but more explanations in English would be great
original_content: It's worth a visit, collection of some heavy machines like war planes and tanks, plus various smaller items like weapons, clothes and loads of pictures. A little effort in translating more if what's there into English would be nice.
extracted_spaces: collection of some heavy machines like war planes and tanks
drawbacks: A little effort in translating more if what's there into English would be nice

author: Andrea L
title: Something to do, but with some doubts!
original_content: Train Street is now one of the most famous attractions in Hanoi and, although it is definitely touristy, seeing the train pass at a very short distance from the tables is an experience worth having.Access, however, is not as immediate as it might seem. Do not think you can just arrive and walk freely along the tracks: there are checkpoints and a lot of police, and the entrances are closed, especially near when the trains pass. The simplest system is to choose one of the establishments that overlook the railway and follow the staff's instructions, who will accompany you inside when it is possible to do so.We went to the Hanoi 1990s Café and had a very good experience, so we recommend it. We arrived about 40 minutes before the train passed, ordered something to drink, and waited calmly, sitting practically right next to the tracks.When the train is about to arrive, you absolutely must follow the staff's instructions: tables and chairs are moved, everyone must stand in the indicated areas, and in a few seconds, the train passes at a truly impressive distance. Avoid taking personal initiatives or moving onto the tracks to try to get the best photograph.We chose an afternoon train and, in my opinion, it can be even more pleasant than in the evening: there is still light to see the whole street well, take photographs, and observe the surrounding environment, and we found less confusion than we expected.It has certainly become a very commercial attraction, but it remains one of the most unique experiences to have in Hanoi. I recommend checking the train schedules beforehand, arriving with some advance notice, and, above all, always following the instructions of the staff and the police.Be careful because there is no safety and the risk is high!

author: Вадим К
title: ✨ Compulsory to visit! Our best evening on the legendary Train Street at the Hương Lê Cafe ✨
original_content: ✨ Compulsory to visit! Our best evening on the legendary Train Street in the cafe Hương Lê ✨Had an unforgettable family evening (3 adults and 2 children) on the famous Train Street in Hanoi. Our journey to this place started from the Hotel L'heritage Premium: we walked for only about 10 minutes along the completely quiet, strict government street Lý Nam Đế to the marching music of the city garbage machine. And this contrast is astonishing – after absolute silence, we instantly plunged into the incredible, surging wave of emotions and capital high of Hanoi!At the entrance to the location we were immediately warmly welcomed by an active call and professionally escorted to the available tables at the Hương Lê.🟟� RESULTS OF OUR OPERATIONAL AUDIT:▪▪ Comfort and ergonomics: Sitting was incredibly comfortable, despite the fact that it is the very center of tourist activity. Directly above our tables, the fans worked at full capacity, creating a pleasant coolness on a tropical evening.▪▪ Orders and cuisine: Prices on the menu range from quite high to quite adequate for such an iconic attraction. We ordered 4 bottles of cold beer, traditional Vietnamese iced coffee (Ice Coffee), 2 milkshakes for children and chocolate ice cream. Everything came in quickly, the drinks are excellent quality and perfectly refreshing. The total bill was VND 640,000. Cash payment on the spot.▪️ Interactive and traditions: We arrived about 50 minutes before the train arrived. This is the perfect time: the people gather very quickly, and by X-hour there were no more seats available at all. Waiting for the train is a separate pleasure, we have made wishes by laying coins and bottle caps directly on the tracks!▪️ Top level security: Ten minutes before the train arrived, all the cafe staff mobilized instantly. We were asked very sternly and clearly to change seats, and all tables and chairs were moved quickly to a safe distance so that the train would not be guaranteed to hit anyone or anything. The team's coherence at this moment is admirable.🚂 CONCLUSION AND SUMMARY:Running literally thirty centimeters from your knees, a huge train is one of the brightest, most memorable and adrenaline-filled rides in all of Vietnam! It's pure magic from the night of Hanoi. Thank you very much to the Hương Lê team for the welcome, atmosphere and safety of our children. Place must visit absolutely every traveler!
drawbacks: Prices on the menu range from quite high to quite adequate
highlights: Incredible, surging wave of emotions and capital high of Hanoi

The South Train Street (Lê Duẩn / Khâm Thiên)Location: Located south of the main train station, accessible via Alley 224 on Lê Duẩn Street.Vibe: This stretch is less crowded and more authentic, offering a quieter look at local residential life, though it still features a handful of local businesses and coffee shops.&...The little resto called 28 TRAIN TRACK FOOD AND DRINK HANOI --- delicious food, great service!!!

author: Grace-Aguiar
title: Captivating & Travel-Inspired
original_content: Visiting the famous Train Street in Hanoi is one of those experiences that stays with you long after you’ve left. Tucked between narrow houses and lively cafés, the railway cuts straight through a tiny neighbourhood where life carries on just inches from the tracks. When the train approaches, you can feel the energy shift—locals pull in their stools, tourists press against the walls, and suddenly the whole street hums with excitement.The moment the train passes is both thrilling and surreal. It’s loud, close, and heart-pounding, yet there’s something strangely beautiful about watching daily life pause and then instantly return to normal once the train is gone.Beyond the train itself, what makes this place special is the atmosphere. Friendly café owners invite you in, offering egg coffee or cold drinks while sharing stories about the street’s history. It feels authentic, chaotic, and uniquely Hanoi.

author: Caroline WSL HYZ
title: Hanoi Train Street – A Unique Experience with a Few Tips
original_content: Visiting Hanoi Train Street is definitely a must-do when you’re in the city. The atmosphere is vibrant, and the experience of watching a train rush past just inches away is unforgettable. To make the most of it, I recommend arriving at least one hour early. This gives you time to grab a good spot, snap some great photos before the train arrives, and enjoy a cocktail or coffee at one of the local cafés.There are many cafés and bars along the tracks. Some places have upstairs seating for a better view, but personally, I’d suggest sitting downstairs to really feel the excitement up close — it’s much more immersive.Toilets are usually available at the shops, but don’t expect them to be very clean or well-maintained. If that’s a concern, plan accordingly.You’ll also find many souvenir vendors nearby. Prices can vary a lot, so bargaining is a must. Once you’ve made a purchase, it’s a good idea to let other vendors know — some can be quite persistent, even a bit pushy. In general, interactions with shop owners can be hit or miss; some are friendly and welcoming, while others may come off as rude.Overall, Train Street is a fun and unique slice of Hanoi life — just come prepared, be patient with the crowds and vendors, and enjoy the ride (figuratively)!
drawbacks: Toilets are usually available at the shops, but don’t expect them to be very clean or well-maintained.
Some shop owners can be rude.
Crowds and vendors can be pushy.

practical_tips: Arrive at least one hour early

There were clearly empty seats available, but she refused to let us sit without any proper explanation, speaking in a very unkind and dismissive way.What made it worse was that, at the same time, another staff member from the same shop was actively calling and inviting other customers in. The inconsistency and unprofessional behavior left us feeling very unwelcome. We understand rules and limitations, but basic politeness and respect should never be too much to expect.
drawbacks: Unwelcome and unkind behavior from staff
practical_tips: Be prepared for potentially rude staff
Check for available seating before being approached

author: Redback_Venom
title: An experience not to be missed
original_content: We walked to the train street from the Vincom Centre not too far away. It was a hot and sticky day, and when we neared the railway crossing, a lady bustled us down the street and toward what we can only suggest was her family's cafe. We were quickly given seats and small tables, and were served on quickly for food or drink. We ordered smoothies and soft drinks - all reasonably priced for a cafe in the area.We were initially told the train was not far away, but then after 30min had elapsed, were told it was still 45 min away! Oh well. More drinks!Our family of 5 (3 kids) fell in love with the cafe owner's small dog which thankfully kept them occupied as we waited. And then, the train came, and went in the flash! Was it worth it? Yes it was as there is no way you would ever be able to do this in Melbourne or anywhere in Australia!
drawbacks: Train was not far away as initially told
highlights: Cafe owner's small dog kept kids occupied
practical_tips: Go to the cafe for a drink while waiting for the train

author: Lily
title: A thrilling encounter with trains
original_content: The thrill of trains zooming past just inches away was exhilarating! We loved sipping coffee at a tiny café, watching the world go by as the vibrant energy of the street enveloped us. A must-see

author: Chris Anderson
title: Thriller on Train Street
original_content: We visited at 9.30 in the morning - no crowds, good egg coffee and a thrilling experience. I'm sure it's great  at night when it's all lit up but fewer people made it better for us.
practical_tips: visit at night when it's all lit up

author: Evered Cincinnati
title: Hanoi's craziest coffee break
original_content: The chaotic and crowded atmosphere is part of the charm, we suppose. Seeing the trains passing surprisingly close is both thrilling and a little terrifying. We squeezed into a small cafe right on the tracks. It felt like a scene from a movie. It's a bit touristy, but definitely a unique memory from our trip.

author: Rachel H
title: Cool experience in Hanoi, easy to navigate and get a good spot
original_content: Worth visiting whilst in Hanoi. We did lots of research but ended up just walking in really easily, finding a table quickly and having a great view. The cafe prices weren’t as high as we were expecting either so overall would recommend. We went late in the evening.
highlights: cafe prices weren’t as high as we were expecting

author: Ronan Q
title: Our visit to train street
original_content: Me and my girlfriend visited train street when we first arrived in Hanoi. As you can expect, it’s a street where a train passes by you. It’s cool. The bars are a bit more expensive but it’s not that dear, about 50K VND for Hanoi Beer. Although you can put the cap on the track and keep that as a memory. It’s a cool first time experience, would do it once and then probably not again as you can expect.
drawbacks: Bars are a bit more expensive
highlights: Can put the cap on the track and keep that as a memory

author: divya
title: One time experience.
original_content: * It was a 15-20 mins walk from our hotel * Get there 30minutes early to get a good spot with a seat at a cafe/restaurant. * Check the train timings on google(could change) .They have additional trains running on weekends in the evenings. Just pick a bar to sit you are comfortable in. You can enjoy a beer,coffee or something to eat while you wait for the train. Very pricey
highlights: Get a good spot with a seat
Enjoy a beer, coffee or something to eat while you wait
practical_tips: Check the train timings on google
Pick a bar to sit you are comfortable in

author: Global Wanderers
title: Worth a visit
original_content: Lower quality coffee at twice the price as elsewhere but it is a pretty unique experience. Watch out for the locals who help you cross the busy street then show you the best coffee shop. We sat and watched it happen time after time.
practical_tips: Watch out for the locals who help you cross the busy street

author: Gina R
title: A must-do in Hanoi's Old Quarter
original_content: If you're in Hanoi's Old Quarter, it's a unique experience that you shouldn't miss. Trains mostly run in the afternoon and evening, so just text one of the many cafés — we loved Hao Hao Coffee — to find out the exact time and, if you want, book a table. Make sure you arrive early, as the road is closed when the train is about to arrive. If you are in the curved section of the street, choose the café well to get a better view. Trains arrive from both directions, and the bars usually also have an upper floor from which the view is completely different, with the atmosphere changing a lot with light and darkness.
practical_tips: text one of the many cafés to find out the exact time

author: John V
title: Unique tourist attraction
original_content: Original idea. Everything is on the pricey side but we were willing to drop some dough to support this interesting tourist attraction. It is a lot more organized than we imagined even with a guard to call people out and clear the area ahead of the train passing. We arrived at about 2:30pm and the train does come as predicted at 3:20. It’s worth it coming in a bit earlier to get a spot because there are lots of folks popping up really close to the train time. Be nice and support the locals, spend a bit of money here.
drawbacks: everything is on the pricey side
practical_tips: arrive a bit earlier to get a spot
be nice and support the locals, spend a bit of money here

author: Creeping_Death_LA
title: As Ozzy sang Crazy Train
original_content: This is a must see while in Hanoi, you can get the schedules from your hotel staff. We went a couple of times during the day and each time was an experience. Expect to see many tourists kicking back along the route either drinking beer, coffee, you name it the locals serve it. Just be aware that mixed drinks are pricey compared to a local cheaper bottle of beer. We could never have this train experience in the USA because too many stupid locals would get drunk fall on the tracks end up dead and the family would sue due to negligence.
drawbacks: locals would get drunk and fall on the tracks
highlights: many tourists kicking back along the route
practical_tips: get the schedules from your hotel staff
be aware that mixed drinks are pricey

author: Christopher L
title: Better than Thailand

cram you in the closer the time gets

author: Desiree
title: Hanoi Street train
original_content: Tom our guide took us to the Hanoi Train street. What an experience. Highly recommended. This is an experience you must have!

author: Dao Matcha - 143 Phung Hung Train Street
title: Hanoi Train Street

practical_tips: This place is perfect for watching the train pass by

author: Bernie T
title: Brilliant
original_content: What an exciting experience.  You arrive,  loads of great restaurants on the track. The staff know the train time and adjust the seating to protect visitors. There was a near miss some yrs ago, the Vietnam equivalent to health and safety closed the street to visitors.  We arrived not that long after the resteraunters requested it reopening. They certainly look after you as its in their interest to do so.
practical_tips: arrive not that long after the resteraunters requested it reopening

author: Laura B
title: Ignore the hustlers
original_content: The train tracks run straight through the cafes and shops of this street.  We sat on a shop on the second floor and enjoyed some sodas while people watching.  The train comes 2-3x per day; while we were there, the schedule of the day was 11:50am, 3:20pm, 7:40pm.Just make sure to ignore the people hounding you and preventing you from getting close to the train to take photos even though they are just shop owners trying to "trade" your going to their shop with train access.  We figured this out later after the train had sadly passed us by.
drawbacks: preventing you from getting close to the train

author: Linda H
title: Silly, but fun.
original_content: This is so fun.  It’s a train that runs down a street of shops.  A lot of the shops serve food and drink while you wait for the train.  I have to say that the coffee I had in both shops was the best coffee I had in Vietnam.  They get it from Saigon.
highlights: best coffee I had in Vietnam
practical_tips: go to the shops that serve food and drink

author: sarah zeke
title: Too crowded
original_content: Too crowded and food was expensive there. There’s limited time when train pass by and its only short. Worth the visit but wont be coming back again, not worth the hype and trouble.
drawbacks: not worth the hype and trouble

author: TUMBO10
title: Excellent
original_content: This is a great thing to see. Initially I thought it would be quite Instagrammy and over hyped but I actually enjoyed it. We went at night and seeing the lights from the bars either side of the track made for a great atmosphere.Staff from businesses will try and get you into their bars - prices are double what we found nearer the lake but still only 50,000 VD for a beer, which is just over £1.70 is still good.We got lucky and arrived about 2 minutes before a train arrived but I recommend seeing what times trains are - your hotels typically know this answer.
extracted_spaces: bars either side of the track
drawbacks: prices are double what we found nearer the lake

author: Lee_family_219053
title: Overhyped and don't get conned by the eateries that you gain entry only thru them
original_content: We were at the Train Street Mural and followed the rail track to train street to see what the fuss was about. When we approached a few people started asking us to go ro their drinking places as that's the only way to get access to the train track. We saw a barrier and someone controlling access up to the track. DO NOT get conned or follow them but walk further down and you'll gain free access to the train track and walk along the narrow alley with drinking places on both sides. The owners will try get your business by saying train coming and sit down have a drink. Do note the train timing and be ready to get out of the way. Enjoy your time there taking photos and the atmosphere.
highlights: free access to the train track

author: Hugary1
title: Hanoi Train Street
original_content: One of the most unique tarin experiences in a major city of 92million you will ever see. Train comes on schedule and some people lock up their doors. The shop owners are obliged to keep you out of harms way. You can have a beverage and food inside along the track and watch the train pass, around 30 sec's. Can't imagine how people sleep as the trains run all the time. The Unification railway was completed after the war and connects Saigon and Hanoi.
drawbacks: Some people lock up their doors
highlights: Can have beverage and food inside

author: KAVITA BERRY
title: Electrifying
original_content: It was an electrifying experience -- a must do  for everyone---the train passed so close-- atmosphere was charged with excitement

author: AMsays
title: A Moment of Magic, but overall, I think it is overrated...
original_content: Yes its unique, sitting trackside as a train goes by, but its momentarily magical.  There's the hustle beforehand, the jostling for position, the uneven sidewalk, the expensive drinks and what of the surly service. I don't know, maybe my server was having a bad day but overall, I think its overrated....
highlights: sitting trackside as a train goes by

author: vtex001
title: Please research carefully and be patient!
original_content: Reviews of the various cafes are difficult to use because individual experiences vary considerably and there are hundreds of themscattered across several areas where trains come through.I have attached a screen shot from google maps of the area we would recommend but be careful because lots of people will try to convince you that you are in the 'wrong' place and they can get you to a better place for a small (inflated) fee via taxi or scooter. The train times seemed about right but don't be surprised if it's late. Get there a little early (45 mins) but be prepared for some of the train street cafes to be closed or setting up. We were about to accept one when lots of local people appeared and started pulling tables and chairs from everywhere, this resulted in crowds heading down the previously quiet street. The prices are fairly standard and all of the reputable cafes will give you a menu to choose from. Don't buy unless see a menu with prices.You will also see the late-comers trying to push in to cafes where there is clearly not room. The staff are excellent at moving them or'encouraging' them upstairs.Even though I had seen videos I was still surprised at how close the train passes. While it is 'touristy' I would definitely recommend it, the staff at our cafe were excellent hosts and it is their livelihood. They played their part in the safety aspect too as the police are swift to kick people out of the street for non-compliance. We had a guy offer a 'back-street' view which was genuine but had we been caught the police would have moved us. Stick with the bigger streets with lots of cafes. The guy got very worked up and started shouting when we looked sceptical and he told us to leave - don't take offence, smile and wave!Overall, it will take an hour and a half all-in. It is safe and easy, the most difficult part will be timing and choosing a drink!Highly recommended.

author: Funlovinfella

author: Ian R
title: A 'Must Visit" experience
original_content: We were obviously planning to visit this street having heard so much about it beforehand.As it was we stumbled upon it after visiting the jail and subsequently stopped for a drink. Not expecting to see a train we had another drink and a snack when all of a sudden lots of movement by bar owners ahead of a train coming through.Wow. What an experience to be sat track side as the huge locomotive and carriages rumbled through.Most people left the street at this point, and as we settled in for another beer were told more trains were coming through.Such a great experience.
highlights: sitting track side as the huge locomotive and carriages rumbled through

author: SB01
title: A Must Do for Train Enthusiasts
original_content: This is an unusual attraction in that it is nothing more than a single line of railway track. However, the proximity to housing and the opportunistic bars that line the passageway make this an edgy and exciting thrill. The train literally passes within centimetres of the punters, including ourselves, who lined the street. At the southern end of the viewing area there are only bars on one side, so the effect is less claustrophobic, so personally I would try and sit further north, where the road crosses the line, as you get a decent view of the train approaching and departing. There are a few chancers who try and direct you to bars, but you could do this without buying anything, but personally I think you get a better view from a chair alongside the track.Train times are erratic,  but usually there are some between 8 - 10 pm. An official blows a whistle and he and cafe owners attempt to clear a path as the train approaches. Make sure you are not in or near an excitable group….
drawbacks: chancers trying to direct you to bars
highlights: decent view of the train approaching and departing

author: mrsmcdlt
title: Not again
original_content: This was unsettling, and not the way we'd imagined it.  The street is visually amazing, and the train passing by is a thrilling experience, but the night we were there, something wasn't right.As the train was anticipated, a woman appeared, who started screaming at people in the "front row".  She was frantic, and although those people were moving as requested, she continued to bark at them.  A young family near us were attempting to gather their things and their young son, when a police offer came by and started shouting at them (they were not in the first row, so we couldn't understand the problem).  When he didn't feel they were moving fast enough, he grabbed their table, sending their drinks flying, and walked away with it.  Once the train passed (which was awesome), we sat back down with our drinks, only to have the woman return, literally pushing us and yelling that it was CLOSED.  People had full drinks in their hands, and were totally confused, as we were pushed out of the area in a big hurry.We ended up standing on a street corner finishing our beer, and wondering what had just happened.It all seemed terrifically aggressive, and I can only imagine how scared the little guy felt when a police officer yanked away their table and sent his drink flying.

author: Yo13
title: What to do See for fun
original_content: How not to take an hour of your time and land while enjoying a Hanoi beer or a coffee with egg while waiting for a train, which you will never take.... it is to be seen once in a lifetime, I advise you. I expected the train to idle, but be careful....
drawbacks: land while waiting for a train

author: Skyrose77

author: gfsc5
title: Amazing experience
original_content: We stumbled upon Train Street when we were heading back to our hotel after a morning of sightseeing.  Our timing was very good as we only had a 20min wait before the train arrived.Essentially, it's a train track running down a narrow street with small cafes/coffee shops on either side.  The walking isn't easy as there is no real paving.We found a cafe and ordered a Vietnamese milky coffee, peach tea and a chicken banh mi and sat at a table adjacent to the rail line.A warning signal is given before the train arrives to give owners time to move any chairs that are too close to the line.  It also gives people the chance to get to safety.  The train is a full size train with many carriages and it doesn’t go slowly.  And it passes within touching distance.  Amazing.Recommended.

Vietnamese milky coffee, peach tea and a chicken banh mi

author: S&O
title: Especially pretty in the evening
original_content: In the evening it is especially pretty, as it is very cheesy, nicely lit. At 7.30 pm and 9.15 pm the train comes through in the evening, at a very decent pace. Very worth experiencing. 1 std before existence and secure a good seat in a cafe in the front row.

author: Nahid Kaleem
title: Exploring Hanoi's Train Street: A Must-Visit Experience
original_content: Hanoi’s Train Street is a must-visit attraction where visitors can enjoy coffee while witnessing a train pass just inches away. There are two train streets in Hanoi, but the Old Train Street is the most authentic and historically rich.  To make the most of the experience, visitors should arrive 30 minutes before the train’s arrival to take photos and soak in the atmosphere. The most popular section is Phung Hung Street, accessible by foot, motorbike, or taxi. Key train timings vary between weekdays and weekends, so checking the schedule locally is essential.  While the experience is thrilling, safety precautions must be followed, including staying off the tracks, respecting cafe guidelines, and being mindful of the train’s timing. Visitors should avoid gathering in large crowds, sitting on the tracks, or placing objects too close to the railway.  This unique mix of culture, history, and excitement makes Hanoi Train Street an unforgettable experience for travelers.
drawbacks: Placing objects too close to the railway
highlights: Witnessing a train pass just inches away
Unique mix of culture, history, and excitement
practical_tips: Arrive 30 minutes before the train's arrival

author: Keelyimps
title: Great experience.
original_content: Get there early to grab a decent seat outside a café. We asked one of the café owners what time the next train was first and waiting an hour but this was fine enjoying a couple of beers and people watching. The train does come very near you 😀

author: eliza248
title: Better than it sounds

Definitely worth going to watch and go about 30 mins earlier to secure any of the cafe seats in the middle of the street.
drawbacks: Would never happen in the UK!

author: Happy Eater 😀
title: Train on time
original_content: No20 train street , arrived and had egg coffee at 2pm and advised the train was at 230 , although other places said was at 315 , at 225 whistles started going and train was on time , Lovely coffee and great service

author: dennisalexandrov1976
title: One step from the train
original_content: This is undoubtedly one of the main attractions of Hanoi, can only be in Asia. In countries where safety standards are at a different level, this is hardly possible when there are dozens of cafes on a narrow street where people sit within a metre of the tracks on which trains of passengers and freight regularly run. And it's not a special show, it's a real road where trains run, for example, to southern Vietnam. There's a schedule, it's best to come in advance to take a comfortable seat in one of the many cafes. We got on two trains: the first day was a very long freight train, and the other time, we barely had time to run into the track area and greet the passenger train. And as soon as the train passes, crowds of people pour onto the tracks, locals even burn things, life boils over and this is how people live with the trains. And nobody's bothering anyone. Be sure to go!!!
drawbacks: crowds of people pour onto the tracks
highlights: comfortable seat in one of the many cafes
practical_tips: take a comfortable seat in one of the many cafes

author: Igor Alexeev
title: West Lake, in Hanoi...
original_content: West Lake or Tay Lake (Hồ Tây) - the largest body of water in Hanoi, with a coastline of about 17 km. The lake shores are a great place for walks and relaxation. On these shores, there are, of course, many attractions, including the Chancuo Pagoda (Chùa Trấn Quốc)...
highlights: great place for walks and relaxation
practical_tips: go for a walk along the lake shores

author: Renate H
title: Highly recommended in Hanoi
original_content: I would be happy to stay at this special hotel with very friendly staff and a delicious breakfast buffet again anytime.

author: Jean-Emmanuel R
title: Pleasant lake west of old Hanoi
original_content: Pretty lake which, as its name suggests, is located slightly to the west of old Hanoi. You will find a pretty pagoda there, but also a very pleasant and well-shaded promenade along the water. Much more peaceful than Hoan Kiem Lake, this lake is also located within walking distance of the embassy district, the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum, and the One Pillar Pagoda.

author: Keren W
title: Nice place for a slow Hanoi afternoon
original_content: I spent an afternoon walking around West Lake and liked it more than I expected. The breeze off the water was a nice break from Hanoi’s heat, and there were plenty of little cafes and street stalls nearby where I grabbed a strong iced coffee and some grilled snacks. It felt calm in spots, especially along the quieter sections, but the traffic around the lake can get pretty noisy and crossing streets is still a bit of a hassle. Some parts also looked a little messy, so it’s not exactly postcard perfect. Still, I’d recommend it if you want a slower, more relaxed side of the city.
drawbacks: traffic around the lake can get pretty noisy
crossing streets is still a bit of a hassle
some parts also looked a little messy

author: Eddie F
title: Peaceful lake with a few rough edges
original_content: I spent an afternoon walking around West Lake and really enjoyed the slower pace compared with the busier parts of Hanoi. The breeze off the water was nice, and I liked seeing locals jogging, fishing, and hanging out at the little cafes. I stopped for a cold drink and watched the sunset turn the water kind of silvery, which was lovely. That said, some stretches felt a bit chaotic with traffic and construction, and a few areas near the road weren’t exactly relaxing. Still, if you want a break from the crowds and don’t mind a bit of urban mess, it’s worth going. I’d recommend it, just not for a pristine lakeside experience.
drawbacks: areas near the road weren’t exactly relaxing
highlights: watched the sunset turn the water kind of silvery

author: Benjamin A
title: Hanoi in autumn is truly wonderful.
original_content: One beautiful afternoon in Hanoi, I was reminded of my trip there last autumn. Today, as I was going through my travel photos, I found this picture and felt compelled to share a review. Hanoi is truly a wonderful city, with delightful autumn weather and incredible food.

author: Jazz Gumbo
title: On a sunny day, its a nice walk.
original_content: Came to stroll around the area & even took out one of the swan boats which was reasonably priced and a nice way to wile away an hour. Fascinating architecture surrounds the lake, well worth visiting.
highlights: nice way to wile away an hour

author: sekjr0521
title: Enjoyable Walk
original_content: No matter where you are in the Old Quarter, it is an easy walk through colorful streets to get to West Lake.,. There is so much activity going on it is hard to keep up with it all.  So no matter how many times you go you'll always find something new to see.  They are always changing different displays that border the perimeter of the lake... Plus, on your walk, you'll find yourself attracted by many other things along the way including the Water Puppet Theater. At the lower end you'll find a number of restaurants including McDonald's, which was my hangout because at least i knew what i was eating.... I think... It is about a 30 minute walk, and more enjoyable at night with all of the lights and music...
highlights: Nighttime atmosphere with lights and music

author: AbhimanyuSinghi
title: Scenic View with Pagodas Around It
original_content: The lake was a short walk from Pan Pacific Hotel. We could even see it from our room. The view is quite scenic especially around sunset. A few pagodas line up one side and are worth a shot visit. You can also take a boat ride in the lake I think.

author: Em Happy Travelling Folks
title: Pagoda Times - be aware
original_content: Visited the pagoda today and a few things there dampened our joy - and it wasn’t the most amazing storm ever as we travelled over in the awesome rickshaws. On arrival we said no to people selling ponchos (as we had umbrellas and our own coats), however it was like no wasn’t acceptable. They “sold” us 4 ponchos, 2 we didn’t want. This made us cranky as we were being respectful. Then after paying different prices for the same product, we got to outside the entrance and a man groused at one of our party for having her phone out.  Ok - so again, judgement re photos. Tourists use phones for everything now, not just  taking pictures - eg using google translate! Sometimes we use them to look up history and information also when there is not English explanation. Anyway, she put it away respectfully. Then when inside we literally walked around for 5–10 minutes, a lady pointed to her watch at quarter to 11 and basically shushed us out of there. So we walked out thinking we had gone to the trouble of ensuring correct clothing and no singlets etc and saw very little for the effort it took to arrange getting out there. Such a shame. Check their breaks times as they matter. The Lake looked beautiful - even with the lightning striking directly down over it!
drawbacks: People selling ponchos and not accepting 'no' as an answer
Different prices for the same product
Being shushed out of the pagoda at a specific time

author: BalkrishnaShroff
title: Nice One !!
original_content: This beautiful lake is located about 6 km from city center. After visiting oldest Buddhist temple Tran Quoc Pagoda in Hanoi, which is next to lake, we stopped here for some time. It's beautiful lake ideal for photo opportunity. Three were few few vendors around selling souvenirs. We had cold fresh coconut water which was very nice.Worth visiting for few minutes...

author: AngeK
title: Best Pho ever!
original_content: Went to this place on a food tour and then went back on our own as well just had to try the fried Pho with beef and veggies again. Absolutely 10/10 recommend Pho Cuon Hung Ben! And the Standing Bar has loads of different beers, cider and yummy small dishes to share. Head upstairs for a great view of the lake
