author: Strike_right
title: West Lake Hanoi
original_content: Go for a lively environment, nice picnic, a weekend brunch a beautiful sunset, a lot of sunset pictures, and a long walk.Avoid for evening pollution.

author: Văn Lâm
title: I would like to introduce you to a wonderful tour of Hanoi
original_content: HANOI CITY TOURDURATION: 8 hoursDEPARTURE: DAILY - MEANS OF TRANSPORT: CAR On this Hanoi City tour, you will visit Uncle Ho's Mausoleum - the great leader of Vietnam. Visit the first university of our country - Temple of Literature, visit and take pictures of Hoan Kiem Lake and Ngoc Son Temple - the heart of Hanoi capital, ... A journey to explore the capital of Hanoi promises to bring you the most unforgettable experiences. HIGHLIGHTS OF THE PROGRAM:• Visit the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum relic site with Uncle Ho's Mausoleum, Stilt House, and Uncle Ho's fish pond and visit the One Pillar Pagoda.• Visit the Temple of Literature - the first university in our country.• Visit Tran Quoc Pagoda - a pagoda with a history of nearly 1500 years, considered the oldest in Thang Long - Hanoi. • Admire the massive architectural work, built by dynasties in many historical periods - Thang Long Imperial Citadel. • Visit and learn about Hoa Lo Prison. • Enjoy the specialities of the capital Hanoi. Tour program8:00 am: The car picks you up at the Hanoi Opera House to start the tour of the capital Hanoi. (Bread and water are provided for you to have a snack in the car)8:15 am: The car arrives at Tran Quoc Pagoda, the group gathers and visits• Tran Quoc Pagoda - located on an island east of West Lake (Tay Ho district). The pagoda has a history of nearly 1500 years and is considered the oldest in Thang Long - Hanoi. The pagoda's architecture has a harmonious combination of solemnity, and antiquity with elegant scenery amidst the tranquillity of a vast lake. It was the Buddhist centre of Thang Long Citadel during the Ly and Tran dynasties.9:00 am: The car picks up the group to go to Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum9:15 am: The group gathers at the Mausoleum and visits• The Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum relic site with Uncle Ho's Mausoleum, Ho Chi Minh's stilt house and fish pond and visits the One Pillar Pagoda.10:20: The car picks up the group to go to the Temple of Literature - Imperial Academy10:30 am: The group gathers and visits the Temple of Literature - Imperial Academy• The Temple of Literature - Imperial Academy. Vietnam's earliest university is regarded as the Temple of Literature-Imperial Academy. Built on a rather big scale in October 1073, this historic building is still standing today. Confucius, the originator of Confucianism, and Chu Van An, the principal of the Imperial Academy, who stood for the lofty moral concept of Vietnamese education, were worshipped at the Temple of Literature.11:45 am: The group has lunch at the restaurant ... (eat Hanoi specialities)13:00 pm: The car picks up the group to visit Thang Long Imperial Citadel• Thang Long Imperial Citadel is a complex of relics associated with the history of Thang Long - Dong Kinh Citadel and Hanoi city starting from the pre-Thang Long period (An Nam protectorate in the 7th century) through the Dinh - Tien Le period, strongly developed under the Ly, Tran, Le dynasties and Hanoi city under the Nguyen dynasty. This is a massive architectural work, built by the dynasties in many historical periods and became one of the most important relics in the system of Vietnamese relics.14:15 pm: The car picks up the group to go to Hoa Lo Prison14:25 pm: The group gathers and visits Hoa Lo Prison• Hoa Lo Prison was formerly a prison located in Hanoi, Vietnam, also known as the Central Prison or ironically the Hanoi Hilton. It was built when Indochina was an inseparable part of the French Empire. Partially destroyed in 1990, it is now used as a museum. 15:10 pm: The car picks up the group to go to Hoan Kiem Lake 15:20 pm: The group gathers and visits Hoan Kiem Lake• Hoan Kiem Lake, also known as Guom Lake, learns about the Vietnamese and French architecture around the lake area. You will visit and take pictures outside Ngoc Son Temple worshipping Van Xuong Saint and Tran Hung Dao - a famous general in Vietnamese and world history and The Huc Bridge. If you want to go inside the temple, you will pay for the entrance fee. 16:00 pm: The vehicle will return you to the Hanoi Opera House at the end of the Hanoi City Tour, or you can depart independently.
highlights: Visit the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum relic site
Visit the Temple of Literature - the first university in our country
Admire the massive architectural work, built by dynasties in many historical periods - Thang Long Imperial Citadel

author: David Roy P
title: Great Fun
original_content: Took a ride on the Pedal Boats on the Lake . Very Cheap for 1 Hour , only $3 AUD .Great Fun but exhausting . Had to give up after 45 minutes as our legs ached too much . The Lake is quite big and is a bit Polluted . Noticed Several Dead Fish floating here & there . Lots of people were fishing

author: Hoi An Free Walking tour & Cycling tour
title: The largest lake in HaNoi
original_content: The largest lake in HaNoi, where you can cycle. Especially, there are a lot of exercises activities in the morning around the lake. However,  the water of the lake is polluted,  there are a many fishes that died around the lake. Luckily, young generation of HaNoi,  they are taking care of environment at every weekend.  That' s a good point,  more and more people verlunteer to clean the lake. Hopefully,  it will get cleaner in the near future 🙏💯❤️
highlights: young generation of HaNoi taking care of environment
more and more people volunteer to clean the lake

author: Chris M.
title: Beautiful lake. Nice run.
original_content: Beautiful lake, did a nice run! Would recommend it to others that are into running abroad. Plenty of shades in the hot weather. Be aware to bring some drinking water because of the humid climate!

author: OHKSO
title: Open-top bus tour
original_content: This time, we took an open-top bus around the city centre to and from Thanh Nien Street, which divides it from Checkback Lake. Despite the size of Westlake from the bus's 2nd floor window, it was a quiet surface because it was not the ocean. Also, Thanh Nien Street seemed to function as a walking course.

author: Michelle M
title: Enjoy the lake view
original_content: I found a nice spot for people who love cycling in Hanoi. I could rent a bicycle for $2 and pedal around the serene lake for 3 hours. It was magical, especially at sunset. After cycling, I stopped at a charming coffee shop along the lakeside for a delicious cup of coffee with a stunning view. It's the perfect way to unwind and immerse yourself in the beauty of West Lake.
practical_tips: stop at a charming coffee shop along the lakeside

author: John L
title: Walk is interesting but be careful.
original_content: You can walk around the lake, which more than 17km. It takes 3-4 hours of walking. Some areas are well planted but others are not. You will walk across some lotus patches, restaurants, schools, cafes, parks etc.. in the summer time lots of dead fishes and it emits bad odor, the water is polluted year round but you still see people swimming in it and fishing even signs everywhere prohibited.

author: Crumpled Nomad | Travel Intelligence
title: Largest lake in Hanoi
original_content: The biggest freshwater lake in Hanoi. Many hotels and restaurants are located around this lake. We dined at the eastern and oriental tea house which overlooked the west lake from where we were sitting at the cafe. We even went closer to the lake to take more beautiful pictures. Many sites around the lake for picture taking.
highlights: many sites around the lake for picture taking
practical_tips: go to the Eastern and Oriental Tea House for a good view

author: Alex Phạm
title: West Lake
original_content: As the largest freshwater lake in Hanoi, if you have time, you should rent a bicycle to go around the lake and enjoy the beautiful sunset here.

author: Dimitris L
title: A lake with views
original_content: West Lake is a nice area to walk around and enjoy the scenery. There are many sellers selling all kinds of things in the area and many tourists as well. The water however is not something one would admire.
drawbacks: The water is not something one would admire

author: Nami L
title: West Lake
original_content: Windy West Lake on a summer afternoon.The beautiful scenery here is captivating.I'll take you there next fall.Reviewing our old love storyLove Hanoi

author: Francoise D
title: Top on the way home
original_content: Great hotel! Many facilities. Nice location if you have already done 'old quarter' etc. I stayed here on my way back home. It was still wonderful to enjoy it.

author: Sofia
title: Dirty water, unimpressive scenery.
original_content: Renting bikes around West Lake was a disappointment. The water was dirty, the air wasn't fresh, and the scenery was pretty boring. We couldn't find a decent spot for our picnic, so ended up eating street food back at our hotel.
practical_tips: Go somewhere else for a picnic

author: Tom Mubarak
title: A lakeside picnic and bike ride
original_content: We rented bicycles and explored the scenic West Lake (Ho Tay). The fresh air and serene atmosphere were perfect for a romantic picnic. We found a quiet spot by the lake and enjoyed delicious street food while taking in the beautiful scenery.
practical_tips: find a quiet spot by the lake

author: Shruti Pramod Reddy
title: Walk around
original_content: Walked around this lake for an hour on Dec-23,2023, exploring Vietnamese people.Nice insight into the local life as I saw some sunset shoots happening & people sitting & some food stalls and cafes nearby too.
highlights: nice insight into the local life
people sitting & some food stalls and cafes nearby too
practical_tips: go early to see sunset shoots

author: dragonflyazul
title: 100 % POLLUTION !!!
original_content: This is a very big lake ,  lake is very  polluted and full of dead fish.  Lake smell and dirty Not worth the visit. The area around the lake is also not very attractive , the road is dirty very hard to walk around, cause of motorbikes blocking footpath. NOT a tourist attraction.

author: Monika K
title: Could be beautiful if cleaned
original_content: Unfortunately, slightly disappointed with the lake. There is a nice coffee shop and nice pagoda but other than that- lake is very dirty and crowded. As previous comments mentioned a lot of dead fish and plastic trash floating.
drawbacks: dead fish and plastic trash floating

author: André K
title: Polluted Lake
original_content: Very big lake , polluted and full of dead fish. Not worth the visit. The area around the  lake is  also not very attractive , definitely not a tourist attraction.

author: Loretta M
title: Worth riding a bicycle around West Lake👍
original_content: Enjoyed our bike ride around West Lake. It was a good challenge and best done clockwise around the lake to be on the lakeside side of the road. Rented bikes from Bike Plus 150,000d for two hours which included helmets. A nice change in activity from walking Old Quarter.

author: Nick K
title: Potential but NO
original_content: YUKKKKCan't walk around cause of motorbikes blocking footpath.  Lake dirty and smells. Road is busy around and pollution

Road is busy around and pollution

author: Annette Dupont
title: Very beautiful !
original_content: Big lake, picturesque landscape. We took many photos here. The sunset is truly magnificent. We also tried the ice cream. But you have to wait a long time before you can queue.
drawbacks: You have to wait a long time before you can queue
practical_tips: Go early to avoid long wait times

author: Heidi Watkins
title: Tranquil Delight at West Lake: A Must-Visit in Hanoi
original_content: Just had an amazing time at West Lake in Hanoi. The peaceful vibes by the water and the beautiful pagodas were a treat.Loved how I could take a relaxing stroll, watch Tai Chi, and enjoy the sunset. And the local food around the lake?Delish! If you're in Hanoi, don't miss this gem.

author: campfamily50
title: Twin Dragons of West Lake
original_content: Twin Dragons of West Lake. This was an impressive sight and if you visit West Lake its a “must-see”.  These twin dragons are colorful, cool and large.  With the back drop of the lake, it almost looks like they are the Guardians of the Lake and welcoming you to this beautiful area. We loved it.

author: Shelley M
title: disappointed
original_content: Nice to escape the crowds in old quarter.  A much larger lake with a lot of housing and shops around.  The day was so smoggy that you really couldnt see very far and what you could see had so much rubbish floating in it was rather sad to be fair.

author: Phi Somchai
title: Peaceful place
original_content: One of the most famous place in Hanoi.  It is very scenic with lots of eatery and residences around the lake.The surrounding is rather peaceful here and great place to get away from the chaotic Old Quarter.
highlights: great place to get away from the chaotic Old Quarter
practical_tips: go to get away from the chaotic Old Quarter

author: Soko37
title: Famous place
original_content: Dominant of Hanoi, neighbouring with Truc Back smaller lake, pagoda or governmental attraction very close near by. Nice to walk around almost in any weather. We walked around a bit and being lucky to have low temperature slightly above twenty degrees. We did walk only part close to another small lake as this is very big one
highlights: nice to walk around almost in any weather

author: Jain G
title: Ha Noi West Lake
original_content: There are several places to rent bicycles around the West Lake. You could also rent bikes and start cycling from the Old Quarter.  That was fun
practical_tips: start cycling from the Old Quarter

author: Leonhkny
title: Lung of Hanoi
original_content: This is one of the very few options to escape the crowd in Hanoi. West Lake is a vast waterfront area offering a relaxing, peaceful atmosphere as well as some precious open spaces for a stroll. Good to take a rest when traffic of the Vietnamese capital becomes unbearable.

author: Ugrid M
title: Bicycling in Hanoi
original_content: This was one of my several times to Hanoi. But the distinguished experience was my first time to ride bicycle in Hanoi where the traffic condition is unique. My experiences  in bicycling in Hanoi was exciting. West lake is a good place for bicycling around. There are good hotels, coffee shops and street food stalls around the Lake. Friendly, hospitality, worth for money at many shops I visited. I took 2 days there before leaving by air back home after finishing 7-day touring bicycling from Thai-Laos border to Laos-Vietnam border and then to SAPA.My impressive accommodation is A25 Hotel 109 Truc Bach, Ba Dinh, Hanoi near West Lake. Clean, well-equipped and hospitality.My impressive bike shop is 2Cycle Bike Shop, 154 Yen How, Tay Ho, Hanoi. Excellent services.

2Cycle Bike Shop, 154 Yen How, Tay Ho, Hanoi

Visit 2Cycle Bike Shop, 154 Yen How, Tay Ho, Hanoi

author: Ali921
title: Nice views
original_content: West Lake itself is not historic in itself. It's probably too large for most people to walk around as well. A lot of the locals just sit down on chairs and look at the view. It's visited mainly because of Tran Quoc pagoda which sits within it. Alongside is another lake Ho Truc Bach - more famous because Senator John McCain was shot down into that lake

author: wombatdavid
title: Enjoyable walk
original_content: We enjoyed a walk up to the lake from the Old Quarter. It is a bit dirty and the air was very polluted. But we walked around some of the lake and saw the pagoda. A nice spot in Hanoi if they could just clean up somewhat…

author: G2Kpauly
title: Nice to wall around
original_content: I had a very enjoyable walk around part of this lake. It's worth going to to enjoy some fresh air, take some photos, walk around and watch the locals enjoying life.
practical_tips: go to enjoy some fresh air

author: Gon Freeces
title: Best place in Hanoi and I want to live here
original_content: The neighborhood consists of some of the best attractions in Hanoi. There are several spots where you can get a great view of sunrise and sunset. Bars, pubs and some restaurants serving the best Vietnamese foods and drinks. Streets are clean.  That’s why some 5 star hotels are located here.

author: Travelove58
title: Really it's just a normal lake.......
original_content: This is basically just a very normal lake, just as in many places all over the world, with the usual activities people do around & along it. And the usual street seller selling their stuff. Nothing special.Visit only if you have time to spare
practical_tips: Visit only if you have time to spare

author: Mozzie93
title: Glad we survived this bike ride!
original_content: We rented bikes and cycled round lake. It was a long way (2 or 3 hours) and mixed. Some parts were nice and relaxed, but other parts were on roads and felt a bit dangerous. Lots of cafes to stop for refreshments luckily. Pagoda and interesting buildings. After cycling round, we were too exhausted to go to the botanical gardens.

author: CKF
title: Fun but sweaty and a bit dangerous
original_content: Our tour company arranged for us to rent bikes to ride around the 17 km perimeter of West Lake.  It was a fun experience, and there are a few temples and statues to stop and see along the way.  Warning: you are on regular traffic rounds with all kinds of vehicles.  Because of this, the experience was more dangerous than I expected.  But we had decent bikes with good gear shifting and we enjoyed the afternoon.
highlights: few temples and statues to stop and see

author: Mawa N
title: Beautiful sunset at the lake
original_content: Amazing sunset overlooking the west lake in Hanoi capital. Drink cocktail and watching the sun disappear in the west so beautiful

author: LoBommer
country: The Royal Town of Sutton Coldfield, United Kingdom
title: Not worth a visit
original_content: We had walked from the old quarter via the Mausoluem, botanical gardens and the B52 Lake and were looking forward to a nice walk around this large lake, unfortunately there were no lakeside footpaths and the water was dirty and smelly with dead fish floating in it. The Truch Bach lake nearby was marginally better and we found a lovely spot to have a beer and a banh mi.
highlights: lovely spot to have a beer and a banh mi

author: Jason S
title: It’s not a must do
original_content: West lake is ok to visit love to walk around lakes and parks when I travel to other cities you can get a sense of local life.For me it was ok if staying in area then most certainly go over and walk around the lake or part of it.If staying in old quarter don’t think it’s that special to go and see.Temple and pagoda is a nice touch for lake and it’s fairly dirty and smelly bit that goes for most lakes on Hanoi.
drawbacks: Not that special to go and see
highlights: Love to walk around lakes and parks
Temple and pagoda is a nice touch

author: steverichhudd
title: Didn't get the attraction
original_content: We got to the lake from the Botanical Gardens.  We were expecting a beautiful lake to walk around. The part we first encountered smelt terrible and had dead fish floating on top. Some guys were fishing and we saw their catch on the side. We walked past the pagoda but felt no need to go any further. The areas we saw were dirty. Perhaps we had over expectations of West Lake or not seen the best parts (and am very happy to be proved wrong), but this and the Truc Bach Lake next to it were not places I would recommend.

author: Rajalakshmy M
title: Beautiful lake with fantastic vibes
original_content: Beautiful lake. Amazing atmosphere around the lake activities, tai chi, badminton, runners, tourists. In the weekends it gets even better.

author: 422iana
title: Morning run
original_content: An enjoyable run towards the lake and there was wide paths around the lake. Head to the pergola. Busy roads to cross.

author: Raymondale
title: Biggest lake in Hanoi
original_content: it is bigger than Ho Hoan Kien,it is hard to walk around the lake.i went here for Tran Quoc Temple,so no time to admire the lake and its surrounding.better stay close to the lake,then you have time to see the beauty of the lake.be note that there are some peddlers around the lake,they want ask you to try to carry baskets on shoulder pole,and take pics of you,it is not free,and the price is not cheap.if you want to try,ask the price first,and bargain with them.

not free, and the price is not cheap

author: chiangmaicharlies
title: Not worth the time
original_content: The biggest lake in Hanoi, but it's smelly, dirty and not picturesque.There's a pagoda and temple at one point on the lake, which is where most tourists go.Don't bother unless you have time on your hands and like dirty lakes.It's an easy walk from Hanoi centre, but not worth it.
practical_tips: Don't bother unless you have time on your hands and like dirty lakes

author: JimboOz
title: Tran Quoc pagoda
original_content: In the 15th Century, the Emperor borrowed a magical sword from the sacred turtle who dwelled in Hoan Kiem lake.  It's inspiration encouraged the Vietnamese warriors to defeat the invaders from Mongolia . On returning victorious, the Emperor was boating around the lake, and the Turtle rose up from the depths and snatched his sword back from the Emperor's grasp.At this Pagoda I purchased a baby turtle and put it back into the lake, gaining merit for my next reincarnation
practical_tips: Go early to see the turtle

author: parksemin
title: Nice view
original_content: We went to West Lake and really enjoyed the sunset. And then, we walked around, visited temple and pagoda. Nice place to vistit. Should try

author: Hoang Do
title: Best Lake in Hanoi
original_content: West Lake is pretty big that if you ride a motorbike around the lake it will take 40 minutes. The place is very good for people going on a date. You can ride around the lake and stop at one of myriad coffee shops and restaurants. The lake is truly full of possibility if you stay creative.
highlights: good for people going on a date

author: michael p
title: Pretty haven in the city
original_content: Hanoi is a busy city ruled by motorbikes which are noisy at all hours and take up any available pathways.  The lake (2 lakes actually) are a haven though even here it is not possible to walk around without using the road and without having motorbikes use the paths. The small lake is good for a 2-3 km run, the big lake is 17km.  There are a few restuarants around the lakes.  The main attraction is the pagoda, which you can visit or take photos of from outside.
drawbacks: difficult to walk around without using the road

author: Andy Nguyen
title: Found the fresh air among busy capial
original_content: I think most of you know West Lake, Hanoi, Vietnam 🇻🇳 This is the most "fresh" place in Hanoi. I found it when Hanoi was in the worst polution ever and there are many people have to bear it :((Fortunately, Hanoi has West Lake, which bring a lot fresh air to refresh Hanoi. When I reached here, I felt like I escaped successfully from a polluted monster. Really love it 😍 You can visit West Lake if you want to find your own fresh space :)))
practical_tips: visit West Lake to find your own fresh space

author: John E
title: Expat hangout
original_content: This is the area where most expats live and hangout so there is a lot to do as far as restaurants and stores and hotels. NIce area to walk around and get a feel for lifestyle.
extracted_spaces: area where most expats live and hangout
highlights: Nice area to walk around and get a feel for lifestyle
practical_tips: Go to this area for a feel of the local lifestyle

author: Chunker M
title: Exclusive!
original_content: It absolutely was a breezy and wonderful evening. Strolling on the lake and enjoying seeing neighborhood people dance is a wonderful knowledge. If you are an animal lover you are going to think it's a lot more fascinating because you are able to purchase different species of animals because of their host walking around there. The pet therapy is employed as well as you're competent to possess a peaceful and harmony walk.

consider purchasing different species of animals

author: Gavin M G
title: Well it IS a lake:-)
original_content: It is good to see any water expense in Hanoi. West Lake is no exception. It is a good place to go and sit for a coffee, and to take a stroll. I could not find any pedestrianised area or quality Western coffee around the lake - still its an OK place to go for an evening walk.... I think that it has massive potential as a really great space to chill and be out, but this potential has not been tapped at all.. that said, sure its OK for a visit.
drawbacks: no quality Western coffee around the lake
highlights: good place to go and sit for a coffee
good place to take a stroll
massive potential as a really great space to chill

author: Epic-Traveller
title: Ho Tay (West Lake)
original_content: This is a large and beautiful lake in a busy part of the City of Hanoi. There is a nice temple at one end and a pagoda with various other things half a mile further.We had a nice stroll along the lake under the shade of trees and visited the pagoda in the middle.
practical_tips: visit the pagoda in the middle

author: Ajax7925 -Steve W
title: Ho Tay - west lake
original_content: I have been here many times.  It's beauitful to see.  So many high in places to eat .  I have been to Hanoi 4 times and every time I go to West lake.

author: Elysee
title: Remarkable beach.. should go
original_content: Took a stroll up together with the lake. Such as a lot of Hanoi, the purely organic attractiveness is some spoiled by the litter and additionally the mad website traffic all about you. On the fringes on the lake, it was quite a bit of quieter and we are able to stay on benches and ease up and talk just a little, consequently it was ultimately an enjoyable experience. We in addition walked across the key bridge after which discovered the pagoda which was interesting in the very own right of its. author: Conney
title: Very relaxing place
original_content: We walked approximately the sofitel and also took a drink within their roof top bar to view the sunset over the lake drinks were english prices for cocktails but worthwhile for the point of view, we also liked some good tapas there. Nice temple on how though a sign says no shorts so we did not go in therefore in case you're planning that perhaps take a sarong. Relaxing walk in place along the lake

author: Stefan O
title: West Lake
original_content: West Lake in Hanoi is so nice situated so close to the city centre and a great walk along the lake on a sunny day!!

author: aaong86
title: Largest body of water in Hanoi!
original_content: This is another must visit when you are in Hanoi esp when you are visiting the Tran Quoc Pagoda which is located at the lake. The perimeter of the lake is around 18km which is possible to walk around the entire lake but it will probably take you a few hours to do so. Perhaps you could spend a few hrs to walk around the entire lake.

practical_tips: spend a few hrs to walk around the entire lake

author: Bulbul
title: Ideal to spend time away from the bustling old quarter
original_content: The lake is situated in Tay Ho district. The area is posh and clean. Spend a couple of hours in the evening here if you want to experience some peace away from the bustling old quarter. You can also choose to ride swan shaped pedal boats in the lake. The cost is around 100000 VND for an hour.
highlights: peace away from the bustling old quarter

author: sangeeta68
title: beautiful
original_content: we were there and loved the sunset one day while strolling down the side, there is not much else to do here
drawbacks: not much else to do here

author: Ellen B
title: Stroll along the lake and Tran Quoc pagoda
original_content: The pagoda is beautiful but today there was too much building going on. The whole footpath was out and lots of drilling. Very dusty. But apart from that it was really nice to see. The lake is huge and has lots of cool coffee places to enjoy. 13 km to bike around if you fancy that.
practical_tips: bike around if you fancy that

author: SeeMoreLiveMore
title: Know what you are looking for before you come ...
original_content: This is more a district around the Lake rather than a tourist spot in itself. The lake is hardly picturesque. But there are a few interesting temples and buildings around it. There are many good local eats in the area as well. But know what you are looking for before coming will make it easier to navigate the area.
practical_tips: know what you are looking for before coming will make it easier to navigate the area

author: Jalal Iqbal
title: big lake a bit far from the city
original_content: the lake is big, clean and nicely maintained lake. located a bit away from the city. has nice walkways beside it. u gonna like it, especially in the afternoon and evening. has a cool pagoda and some nice colorful places around it. i spent a nice evening here and liked the entire place.
practical_tips: go in the afternoon or evening

author: Nick Andreeff
title: Should see
original_content: Just in case you'd love to get some expats into the life of yours here is the house of yours. Yes on weekends a few Vietnamese can be found here to go walking and exercise but usually its full of countless expats. The water isn't actually neat and so even though you may see several Vietnam folks swimming I am going to have a pass on it. It is excellent in the views of its as well as has a few of decent restaurants nearby.

author: JnVSydney
title: Largest lake in Hanoi
original_content: However not the prettiest, for us that title goes to Hoan kiem Lake (see review), west lake is huge about 17k’s of shore line. The attraction for us was visiting Quan Thanh Temple and Tran Quoc Pagoda. author: blackeaglejim
title: riding around West Lake
original_content: Originally a lagoon that was separated fro the Red River by landfills and embankments in the 11th century, West Lake is the largest body of water in Hanoi.  A causeway alongside the eastern shore, built in the 17th century, created Trúc Bạch, the small fishing lake on the other side.  In the past, the lake was a popular site for royal pleasure cruises, palaces and temples.  Today the whole area is built up, but it’s worth a ride around the lake by bicycle or motorbike, 13 kilometers circumference, for the quiet getaway spots and interesting temples.       Beginning at the bottom of Thanh Niên Street, the Quan Thánh Temple is on the right, originally built 11th century, dedicated to the Guardian God of the North Trân Vp and worth a look inside for the big, black 17th century bronze statue of the god.  Further up offshore on the left is the Trấn Quốc Pagoda, Hanoi’s oldest, moved here early 17th century from its original 6th century location downriver.  A little further on, turn left along the lake and pass by Yên Phụ Temple and then several nightclubs, restaurants and bars, with the option of lakeside tables.  Further on is Kim Liên Temple, a fine classic Vietnamese building.  Further on, turning left on the Tây Hồ Peninsula theWest Lake Palace is at the end, dedicated to  Liễu Hạnh, the chief deity in the Holy Mothers pantheon.       Rounding the northern end you pass by the big amusement park as you turn down Lạc Long Quan Road along the lake’s western shore.  There a few quiet temple compounds along the way, each different in architecture and layout from the others.  At the south end you turn left and follow the shoreline Nguyễn Đình Thi Road back to Quan Thánh Temple.  There are other temples, broad views of the lake and many options to eat along this route.
drawbacks: the whole area is built up
practical_tips: ride around the lake by bicycle or motorbike

author: Ernest W
title: Smoggy
original_content: The first impression you get when you arrive on the shores of the West Lake is that it is extremely smoggy. You really can't see a thing. It is entirely surrounded by buildings, but half of them are not really that visible because of the smog. It is also muggy. If you've ever been to the West Lake in Hangzhou, China, you'll see that this one is pretty similar. But it has less attractions in that there's only one pagoda (Chua Tran Quoc). Also, Hanoi's West Lake is far smaller than Hangzhou's, making it seem more cramped and urbanized. At least if you're in the middle of Hangzhou's West Lake, depending on where you are, you may need binoculars to see the buildings in the distance and realize that you're still in the middle of a highly urbanized area. With Hanoi's West Lake, there's never any doubt about that. There are benches situated around the lake for one to sit on and just relax. But, like many other places in Hanoi, the streets are filled with cars and motorbikes, and the constant honking will give you a massive headache before you've had time to settle down and enter a state of zen. Still, I have fond memories of the ice cream kiosk just across the street from Chua Tran Quoc. A very refreshing coconut cream ice cream cone can be had for only 7000.  After walking back toward the old quarter with it, I got so enamored I turned around and got another one!

We were taken to see a beautiful pagoda and temple which we paid homage to it by placing food and pretend money, said a prayer and then burnt the offerings of money. The tour guides that we were with were wonderful in explaining the history of the temple and surrounding area's....

author: Germ54
title: Tay Ho and West Lake area Great to visit
original_content: You will experience many international and western style restaurants and hotels in this area. Many prices equal to prices in the USA

author: Alex B
title: Pleasant Walk Around the Lake
original_content: West Lake is the largest lake in Hanoi, about 30 minutes walk from the old quarter.  It's a long walk to go around the lake but it is a pleasant walk, not so crowded (midweek when I went there).  There's pagoda (forgot the name) which closes at 1130 am.  The walk from the old quartier to the West Lake passes through the more genteel, expensive neighborhood of Hanoi.  In all in all a very worthy effort on my part.  On the return I just a taxi back to my hotel which cost me 35,000 VND.

author: sakazaan
title: A pleasant escape from the chaos
original_content: What a beautiful, calm part of Hanoi. I went specifically to look for homeware goods at YNOT. In the process, I discovered Pingpong with some unique furniture pieces and Oriberry coffee shop with a good selection of ceramic cups and plates. My highlight was the discovery of a gorgeous cafe between YNOT and Pingpong. It is a place with delicious healthy food, coffee roasted on site and a lovely ambience with seating in the garden or in the three storey building.
practical_tips: go to YNOT for homeware goods
check out Pingpong for unique furniture pieces

author: Kevin V
title: Chilling around
original_content: Take your bicycle and cruise around the West Lake. There are a lot of benches to take a seat and some pictures.

author: rgeffken
title: A must see if only for the John McCain monument
original_content: For a war veteran like myself who could not have visited Ha Noi except under the worst of circumstance in 1970, this placid lake where John McCain landed must be seen

author: DCTravelers69
title: Eh
original_content: We walked by here on the way to the botanical gardens.  It's fine, but i would never go out of my way to see it--
drawbacks: would never go out of my way to see it

author: Geoff G
title: Good to cycle round
original_content: Did a loop of the lake on push bikes as part of our Intrepid tour.  Lots of things to see, some quiet sections but also plenty of traffic to contend with.
drawbacks: plenty of traffic to contend with

author: Rihonann
title: Peaceful place in Hanoi
original_content: This lake was very peaceful. It helped me to escape the hustle and bustle of the busy city. Felt so relaxed when walking around this lake.

author: hungodd94
title: Nowhere give me calm like West Lake
original_content: This is the only place in Hanoi that still give me calm everytime i get by. the water, the breeze, the smells of flowers. A remote place among one of the most busiest city in Vietnam
extracted_spaces: one of the most busiest city in Vietnam

author: Anil L
title: Biggest Lake in Hanoi
original_content: A good place for morning jog and evening walks. Also, a nice spot to polish your photography skills.

author: jessmoss871
title: Calm
original_content: I wanted to get away from the hustle and bustle of the old quarter in Hanoi and West Lake was the perfect escape.

author: DAVID L
title: The Big Lake ...
original_content: Another of the picturesque lakes of Hanoi, this being the largest one. Pretty greenery all around and restaurants and concessions along the periphery. Lots of young grads out getting photos adds to it all.

author: Parimal M
title: Nice lake and lot of people in the evening
original_content: A lot of activity with street shops and street food in the evening. Part of the street around the lake is closed to traffic in the evening

author: Ada E
title: It was a Lake, bit grubby.. but interesting Pagoda situated on the banks worth a visit.
original_content: Didn't think much of the folk selling baby turtles so that you could throw them back into the lake..
drawbacks: Didn't think much of the folk selling baby turtles

author: Jen78703
title: Nice place to walk around
original_content: This lake is pretty big. I really enjoyed walking around and seeing the side walk vendors as well as just getting out from the craziness of old town. It's quiet and not busy at all

author: Coryy20
title: Most besutiful
original_content: West lake is in the heart of Hanoi and is the biggest lakes in Hanoi. Lots of restaurants around  and shopping.Walking around or jogging the scene is just breathtakingly beautiful and peaceful. Find a beench sit and just enjoy the scenery.
practical_tips: Find a beench sit and just enjoy the scenery

author: Xerxes R
title: Beautiful walk around the lake
original_content: We are here now and although the weather is a damper we  enjoyed our walk here. We crossed the highland coffee and the pagoda also walked past the John Mc Cain memorial and liked that as well. Enjoy your walk here.

author: Mandinka_11
title: West Lake
original_content: we decided to walk round the lake as we couldn’t check into our hotel, arrived early from train station at 5:45 . What a walk this was, 11 miles ! We stopped at a couple of bar/restaurants on the way round. It is worth having a stroll around part of the lake, there isn’t  a lot to see otherwise than the lake, unless you walked into the built up areas.We were fortunate that it was a lovely warm/sunny day.Enjoy, note good walking shoes are a must, oh and don’t forget umbrellas for any showers.
drawbacks: unless you walked into the built up areas
highlights: good walking shoes are a must

author: Peter F
title: Nice walk
original_content: A pleasant walk around lake. Some good photo opportunities. Lots of cafes etc around lake in nearby streets. The restaurant on lake is fantastic. Excellent food and service, looks pricey but is quite reasonable.
practical_tips: go to nearby streets for cafes
looks pricey but is quite reasonable

author: Mktpro99
title: Beautiful lake
original_content: Lots of restaurants and bars in this area. Nice. Ideal for sunsets across lake. Very romantic. Watch traffic crossing street.

author: heinzhuynh
title: Hanoi biggest lake
original_content: I came to visit Tran Quoc pagoda and it situated right the west lake. Nice and cool place for a couples shot of pictures
highlights: good for couples shot of pictures

author: Nicki P
title: Very pretty
original_content: A nice breath of fresh air in a busy city. Highlands Coffee was a good place to rest. Good place to walk.
practical_tips: go to Highlands Coffee for a break

author: DeltaWhiskey
title: The Famous John McCain Lake
original_content: Hanoi is a city of lakes, this one being perhaps its largest with restaurant boats and lined by residences & some hotels. Usually hot-humid-windy during the late Spring, Summer, & early Fall.

author: Enkidu-backpacker
title: Huge, beautiful from far/Dirty from near
original_content: its a huge lake located north of hanoi. the location is where expats chose to live and is quite beautiful to sit and have a tea, beer or coconut juice while looking at the lake but the water is really dirty and u could find anything possible floating on water such as dead fish.

author: VikingLogarta
title: Smoker-friendly
original_content: I am always thankful for smoker friendly restaurants and bars, though I've been trying to quit for some time. The food was good and the service was acceptable.
drawbacks: trying to quit for some time

author: vampslayer01
title: Great Area
original_content: Nice area and really great to walk around, there is lots going on around from some temples to locals swimming and different parts of the city to see

author: Cyprusclaret
title: Known as west lake byvthe ex pats
original_content: This is the expat area of hanoi, you will find many bars and restaurants here with a varied mix of cuisines.There is an expat shop where British an get a few comforts of home ie. Tea bags, marmite etc but at a big premium. It's situated around a lake so mosquito bites are part of the course.A nice area non the less and not far by cab you the old town
practical_tips: get a few comforts of home at the expat shop
not far by cab to the old town

author: karlo a
title: Nice place for foreigners to chill
original_content: The are is teeming with western themed restaurants, take advantage also of visiting Trấn Quốc Pagoda if your in the area. Admission is free, but be sure to wear appropriate clothes as it is an active shrine.

author: ColonelBangkok
title: Great Collection of Restaurants
original_content: I enjoy staying near Westlake and take advantage of the many VN and Western restaurants that surround the lake, many with alfresco dining. The area is easy to find and makes for a pleasant visit.
practical_tips: take advantage of the many VN and Western restaurants that surround the lake

author: Nunngo
title: Bike riding around the West Lake
original_content: Put your life into the hands of the local Hanoi drivers and get on a bike for a ride around this lake.  We hired bikes and with a local friend who knew the safest way and 'technique' to get around the lake on a bike, off we went to experience bike riding in the crazy traffic of Hanoi.  It was an amazing experience and believe it or not, quite safe.  I think the local drivers allow for the bike riders and they do not display the same impatience and 'road rage' as drivers in western countries.  The day (2 October 2016) we rode around West Lake was an interesting one. It was late afternoon and I could see what looked like floating dead fish.  The weather was hot, as usual for Hanoi, and as we rode around towards where the five star hotels are situated on the lake there were literally thousands and thousands of dead fish on the lake.  It was an incredible sight, in that it was so unusual and bizarre.  Our Hanoi friend explained that this is something that happens occasionally in the lake because of the hot water temperatures and the lack of oxygen in the water which is over populated by the fish.  Needless to say what the smell was like.  Interesting!The ride around the lake was a great way to see many local sights, it is a very beautiful lake highly populated with restaurants, bars, cafes, temples, high rise apartments and high end accommodation.
practical_tips: go with a local friend who knows the safest way

author: SlowlyinAsia
title: Nice to Have a Cool Breeze
original_content: Took an off the cuff motorbike tour ( I was not the driver ) of HaNoi and ended up at West Lake at one point.at the Tran Quoc Pagoda. Unfortunately, the Pagoda was closed on that day but I still enjoyed mingling with the locals as the milled around, watching the fisherman. One gentleman caught a whopper carp, must have been around five kilos and quickly sold it to someone waiting for such a moment. I had a great time just hanging out.
drawbacks: The Pagoda was closed on that day

author: jenabaintheworld
title: Beautiful esp early or at sunset
original_content: We live along west lake so we are spoiled with the  beautiful views.   The lake is esp nice for walking or biking early morning or around sunset.  It's 17km around or you could walk certain sections that are more picturesque.   Just 10 min taxi from old quarter.
practical_tips: Walk certain sections for more picturesque views

author: minimize940314
title: Bigger than Hoan Kiem
original_content: West lake is way bigger than Hoan Kiem. You will see local people fishing and jogging. The temple at the shore of the lake is wonderful.
highlights: The temple at the shore of the lake is wonderful

author: Trang B
title: Other image of Hanoi
original_content: Large, much more beautiful if you visit in summer with lotus flowers . There are lots of restaurants and shop around for you to choose( Vietnamese and European). There are lots of expats stay in this area as more quite than in the centre, then you can easily find out that so many foreigners around.
practical_tips: Visit in summer for lotus flowers
Choose from Vietnamese and European restaurants

author: rsm920
title: Hire a bike
original_content: This was one of my highlights of Hanoi - hire a bike and cycle around the lake.  Takes a couple of hours, but is such a peaceful experience, even with the mopeds weaving around you (it never felt unsafe!).  Such a contrast to the the hustle and bustle of the Old Quarter - a must!

author: electrixbubble
title: Biggest Lake in Hanoi
original_content: You might know that Hanoi is a city of lakes. This is the largest one. During the hot summer in August, you might need to visit here because the place offers you chill-axing vibe. 360 degree views are also a plus. A friend took me there riding around the lake, it was the best feeling after being in the chaotic city. The activity here you can do is riding a swan boat. I did not try and clueless how much they would charge.
drawbacks: clueless how much they would charge

author: PeterM-Sin
title: Dirty lake with dead fish inside
original_content: Nothing special to see. Just a dirty lake where we saw a lot of dead fishes floating on the surface. Not worse the trip outside the lovely old and french quarter area in Hanoi
extracted_spaces: lovely old and french quarter area in Hanoi
drawbacks: dead fishes floating on the surface

author: Katie Henry
title: Regarding bike tours
original_content: The lake is a lovely location and around are lots of interesting sites that are definitely worth visiting. However for those thinking of doing the bike routes around it, be mindful that it is not as easy as it may sound. All of the route takes place on the busy roads which made us feel a little unsettled, so it probably won't be enjoyable for anyone not confident with cycling. Also the lake is very big so it will take a while. We had to stop halfway as it was too long, and concentrating on the road meant you don't see the lake as well. Definitely go and see the lake but probably better on foot.

author: Janine F
title: Not great
original_content: The best part is the Pagoda, after that nothing great. Ladies selling turtles that you can release into the lake. Hoan Kiem Lake in the Old Quarter is much better.
highlights: Ladies selling turtles that you can release into the lake
practical_tips: Go to Hoan Kiem Lake in the Old Quarter instead

author: PacoGlasgow
title: Stayed on West lake
original_content: Having stayed on the westlake at intercontinental hotel we soon realised we were a good bit away from all the tourist areas....old quarter. We decided to move in to centre of Hanoi. Not really much to do apart from walking round the lake.
practical_tips: Move to the centre of Hanoi

author: adstone888
title: comparable to Hangzhou West Lake
original_content: Hanoi West Lake is as good as Hangzhou West Lake. I was quite taken with the setting of Hanoi Lakes; West and Central Lakes. I feel the I can enjoy better strolling around the lakes. Firstly, there are not as crowded as Hangzhou where people pushes each other. You can relax and enjoy the view and setting without being push on. There are plenty of eateries around the Lakes; especially good quality coffee everywhere.Lastly I feel the whole atmosphere around the lakes are excellent and a real tourist attraction. I would take my time walking and taking in all the good feeling and wash my mind clean of stress.

author: albertosR7320AZ
title: On my free time i am driving with my bike!
original_content: On shunning days i ride aroud the lake! It takes one hours! Is one of my wy to relax! Try to explore more about hanoi!
practical_tips: try to explore more about hanoi

author: Lydia Farmer L
title: Fun!
original_content: While visiting our son and his girlfriend, we visited this area. We had a meal and rode around to an outdoor bar they frequent. Lots of expats and good cold beer!

author: strongdavid0184
title: BIG LAKE
original_content: Nice walking around west lake with walking city .There are many people but many studens play music . So you feel happy and interesting . Many bar and coffee shop are busy . the food is expensive but good .The traffic is crazy .

author: Diane D
title: Worth Cycling round
original_content: As part of our trip organised through Selective Asia was a 17km bike ride around West Lake.  Unfortunately this wasn't on pedestrian walkways but on fairly busy roads which was a bit hairy at times but worthwhile.  There are interesting Pagodas, gardens and you see a different side to Hanoi away from the bustle of the Old Quarter
drawbacks: bike ride on fairly busy roads

author: Melfish13
title: Such a contrast to the centre
original_content: I loved West Lake and we went for two out of three days during our trip to Hanoi. We rented bikes for just 60,000 dong each and cycled round the whole things, which is beautiful and the roads are very good. There is loads to see and do as you cycle round, so I'd completely disagree with some other reviewers of the Lake. There is a water park where we spent 4 hours! There is a 50m swimming pool right next to the lake, loads of different cafes and lunch stops, pedalos and that's just on the lake shore.

author: Miller J
title: Airy and nice view
original_content: We had a motorbike ride going around West Lake. There is nothing too interesting to do in this site but I like the peaceful and romantic scenery of this lake, specially its fresh scenery in the morning. We also found out some stalls selling street foods nearby the lake. They are really tasty.

author: Hanoidave
title: West Lake - The Ex Pat enclave of Hanoi
original_content: West Lake is a large body of water to the northeast of Hanoi city.In Vietnamese it is called Ho Tay.  The area to the north of the lake is where most western restaurants, bars and hotels are located including the 5 star Sheraton and intercontinental. The lake itself is popular for fishing, boating and even rowing.The shores of the lake abound with cafes and small eating establishments.You can travel around the lakeshore by car, motorbike and bicycle. You will enjoy the cool breeze; and select a cafe with seats right by the lake for coffee, beer and snacks .Recommended by Hanoidave.
practical_tips: travel around the lakeshore by car, motorbike and bicycle
select a cafe with seats right by the lake for coffee, beer and snacks

author: SEVENSEAS_Media
title: Quiet, residential
original_content: Don't expect too much from this. I went looking for the lotus flowers and I was clearly in the wrong spot. It's nice and a great place to stay apparently but I wouldn't go out of my way to go there
drawbacks: I was clearly in the wrong spot
I wouldn't go out of my way to go there

author: Michel C
title: The most impressive lake of Hanoi
original_content: Now surrounded by houses and condominium for rich people and expatriates, the west lake, when night arrives, is one of the spot of Hanoi preferred by lovers. Some restaurants around the lake propose good food.

author: Alireza Z
title: heart of hanoi
original_content: this lake is calm on 6 am poeple are excercising in around the lake . (good for photography ) they do thai chi . there are a lot of stores near the lake and you can find anythink near this place. i think near the lake is best choice for choosing hotel

author: moonlotus18
title: Two big lakes with nothing much to see
original_content: The west lake may be the biggest lake in the city but apart from that, there is nothing much to see. There is a walking path around it but be aware some parts of it needs maintenance (rickety or broken or uneven). There may be some vendors selling wares in the area. It gets quite hot during the day time so bring a hat/shades. The lake itself is nothing much to see, rather polluted unfortunately. Apart from that, there is the nearby pagodas to visit and the famous spot where John McCain's plane was shot down during the war. Nevertheless if you have nothing much to do, it will serve as a good stroll to take in the local scene.The best thing there was when we stumbled on the Highlands Coffee place located on a 2 storey boat nearby. Very refreshing stop - as it was air conditioned and nice restaurant inside -  in between walking around the lake.
drawbacks: Ricketty or broken or uneven walking path
highlights: Refreshing stop at Highlands Coffee place
practical_tips: Be aware of uneven walking path

author: Cathe G
title: Lovely scenary but not alot to do ...
original_content: This was a welcome break from the hustle of Hanoi old quarter, we were amidst large houses and tropical palms with a generous lack veiw and much quieter roads.This is clearly a wealthy area with lots of expats visible and trappings of wealth in the cars driven.We walked around different sides of the lake and its clear development is ongoing with luxury flats being built amongst some traditional markets.There was not alot to see however and on foot there was minimal access to a small number of  restaurants, and alot of casual cafes with warm beer and full of young foreign english teachers but in terms of things to do or see the shopping was very limited and expensive.
drawbacks: shopping was very limited and expensive

author: enjayaitch
title: Friday night
original_content: Friday night they block traffic around the lake to allow the community to do their thing. You'll be surprised at the goings on that include a variety of street musicians, community involvement in a variety games and the ubiquitous salesperson.

author: Lou N
title: Skyline view of hte business dsitrict,
original_content: Not a must see but the lake and view make a nice area to stroll with good places to stop for a refreshment.
highlights: good places to stop for a refreshment

author: LarryG392
title: Amazing sight
original_content: I was surprised to find this huge lake in the midst of Hanoi. It is surrounded by hotels. Also the Tran Quoc Pagoda was very impressive.

author: tony4307
title: Some Things to Do and See
original_content: Several restaurants and even a shopping mall in close proximity to where we stayed.  Nice area to take a stroll, stop in for a brewski, or whatever.
highlights: nice area to take a stroll

author: Barbara M
title: Rather boring residential lake,
original_content: particularly by comparison with Hoan Kiem.  Actually the comparison is completely unfair but, if your time is limited, rather focus on the area around Hoan Kiem.
practical_tips: focus on the area around Hoan Kiem

author: Ken c
title: Not much to see here as a tourist
original_content: We went around the whole lake because we were interested in the Vietnamese real estate market but I wouldn't do this as a tourist and there is little to see here.

author: Myranda B
title: Full of energy, the food is so-so.
original_content: Tahien is a city that never sleeps, always full of energy. The food was just so-so, but drinking a cold Czech beer in the lively crowd was exceptional. It's worth visiting at least once!
highlights: drinking a cold Czech beer in the lively crowd

author: Travel Girl GR
title: Indifferent road
original_content: Road with shops for food and drink.Nothing special since you can find decent stores anywhere else in the city
drawbacks: can find decent stores anywhere else in the city

author: Knuckles
title: Excellent Hanoi Food Tour with Minh
original_content: Excellent Hanoi Food Tour with MinhOur walking food tour with Minh was a real highlight of our time in Hanoi. Minh was informative, relaxed, and incredibly knowledgeable, sharing great insights into the city’s food, culture, and history without ever making it feel formal.What made the experience special was how friendly and genuine he was — it felt more like exploring Hanoi with a friend rather than being led by a tour guide. The food was fantastic, and we discovered places and dishes we would never have found on our own.Highly recommended for anyone wanting an authentic and enjoyable food tour in Hanoi. ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐
practical_tips: go with a guide like Minh for an authentic experience

author: 黄佳琪
title: Lively beer street for the hustle and bustle of you
original_content: It's a beer street crowded at night, so buzzy that it's almost inch-deep. If you love the hustle and bustle and enjoy the beer culture, it's really worth exploring. However, street solicitation is more common and requires psychological preparation.

author: Mamie F
title: Vibrant Music Bar Street Safe and comfortable
original_content: The ambience is great, the energy is high! The music is pleasant and the environment safe and secure. Bars gather here to pick your favourite tunes and moods, and enjoy one or more great nights~

author: Vy H.
title: Bars in Hanoi, Vietnam
original_content: Fun area to hang out and drink!  Very energetic vibe, lots of music blasting and tons of people.  If you don’t mind the chaos, this place can be lots of fun!
practical_tips: go if you don't mind the chaos

author: TravelingFoodie
title: Fun and worth it
original_content: Ta Hien Beer Street offers a fun and energetic glimpse into Hanoi’s nightlife. We visited in the evening and found the street packed with people sitting on small stools, enjoying beers and street food in a very informal setting. It gets loud and crowded, and vendors can be persistent, but this is all part of the experience. A lively place to stop by if you want to see a youthful, social side of Hanoi.
highlights: fun and energetic glimpse into Hanoi’s nightlife

author: Berte Haul
title: Perfect pit stop by the night market 🍺
original_content: Plenty of seats at 6 p.m., packed by 7! Nearby vendors invite you in but don’t pressure—places fill up fast. Prices are fair, making it perfect for a bite and a beer, a stroll through the night market, and a relaxed drink on the way back.

author: Furchtlos und Treu
title: Worth it
original_content: I can only think of the following: typical Vietnam... go, order beer, sit and watch the hustle and bustle 😅 There is actually always something to see, you get used to the noise level

author: Umberto
title: Worst place we've eaten for 1000000 dong.
original_content: Worst place we've eaten for 1000000 dong. The food was just crap and not worth the price.  Attracted by the name, never again.

author: Lily
title: Backpacker buzz with heart
original_content: We hit Ta Hien Street for cheap eats, cold beers, and spontaneous laughs—and got all three in spades! The energy is infectious, the locals are friendly, and late-night banh mi runs became our group’s favorite ritual. Pure Hanoi chaos, and we loved it!

author: Song Mi-rae
title: Hanoi Old Town
original_content: In the northern and vibrant city of Hanoi, you must walk through the old streets or by cycling. Through narrow, maze-like alleys, shops and the everyday lives of locals who have preserved hundreds of years of history, you can feel the true charm of the city. Especially in the morning sun or in the evening noise, you'll get deeper into the unique atmosphere of Hanoi.
practical_tips: visit in the morning or evening

author: 李强
title: A beer, a bunch of friends, an "international street."
original_content: Towers Street is a backpacker's paradise! We sat on plastic benches in the evening, drinking ice beer for 20k Vietnamese dong per capita, and watching tourists from all over the world talk and laugh. The street kebabs aroma, the music swirling, lively but not noisy. Laughing late into the night with your friends in the evening wind - that's what travel looks like!

author: raybrahms1964
title: Beer Street party section a total abomination!!!
original_content: We first visited Hanoi 12 years ago and absolutely loved the place. We are back here at the moment and this review is solely for the god awful section of beer street that is absolutely horrendous. It's like running a gauntlet with elderly men watching girls dancing on tables wearing next to nothing while you are harassed by boys shoving menus in your face trying to drag you into their bar. I don't know what the hell the authorities were thinking of when they gave their approval to this section of the street. It is an absolute abomination  and has no place in Hanoi. Whoever is responsible for allowing this should hang their heads in shame. If Hanoi continues in this direction and decends into a place akin to Pattaya on acid then we will not return. If the authorities read any reviews on TA like this then they need to sit up and take notice as they are overseeing a transformation that has absolutely no place in beautiful Hanoi!!!
drawbacks: eldery men watching girls dancing on tables wearing next to nothing
harassed by boys shoving menus in your face trying to drag you into their bar

author: Cordy
title: A chaotic & fun date night!
original_content: We grabbed tiny plastic stools, ice-cold Bia Hoi, and just people-watched for hours. It's loud, energetic, and incredibly fun. The perfect place to laughing 😂

author: Nicolette Torso
title: Chaotic, fun, and unforgettable!
original_content: We dove headfirst into the madness of Ta Hien! Sitting on tiny plastic stools, drinking cheap local beer, and soaking up the insane energy was a highlight of our trip. It's loud and crowded :))))

author: Nona D
title: Wild and fun nights
original_content: Ta Hien Street is an absolute must-visit for a fun-loving couple! The energy is electric. We squeezed onto tiny stools, drank cheap, fresh beer, and just soaked in the chaotic, bustling vibe. It’s loud and crowded, but it was one of the most memorable nights of our trip. A truly unique Hanoi experience.

author: MMA Hà Đông
title: Enjoy night life in Hanoi
original_content: Great place to enjoy Hanoi nightlife, there are many private and open bars, especially lively on weekends with walking street with affordable prices and lots of activities. The downside is that it is not for people who like to go to bed early or are allergic to alcoholic drinks
drawbacks: not for people who like to go to bed early
practical_tips: avoid if allergic to alcoholic drinks

author: Paul P
title: Get ready to be pestered
original_content: Noisy and annoying. But I guess you have to experience it if you're in this part of the world!!!Beer is cheaper than UK obviously but slightly pricier than other places nearby.

author: corinne_prevost
title: THE HOT NEIGHBOURHOOD OF HANOI
original_content: We didn't know where the warm neighborhood was we found it while walking. Beers galore + girls + rabateurs. The winning trio on this street. You have to eat, drink and more so affinities.
practical_tips: You have to eat, drink and more

author: akio9jp
title: Nekki Munmun
original_content: It is a drinking district in the heart of Hanoi's Old Quarter, with shops, clubs and bars serving alcohol on both sides of the street, just 200 meters long. There's a lot of pop music going on and it's a Fever. I had the impression that there were more Western tourists than locals. It's for energetic young people, and the over-recent father doesn't feel good.
drawbacks: It's for energetic young people, and the over-recent father doesn't feel good
highlights: shops, clubs and bars serving alcohol

author: 지후 한
title: Perfect combination of authenticity and vibrant atmosphere
original_content: With our friends, we visited Hanoi's Ta'an Street and it was an unforgettable experience! This place is filled with authentic local atmosphere, and the energy of the lively streets in particular captivated us. Drinking local beer and enjoying the bullshit of the street was a really special experience. It was the perfect place to enjoy a variety of foods and drinks and to spend time with friends and friends. Ta'in Street is a place where you can feel the true charm of Hanoi, and I would definitely like to find it again!
highlights: perfect place to enjoy a variety of foods and drinks

author: Kent
title: Street beer so fun
original_content: I come here on weekend one time per month with my friends. 9 life for all guys, street beer, street food, street music - The vibrant is so fun. I love it all :))

author: Willy Sims
title: Cheers to colorful nights
original_content: This vibrant beer street buzzed with life, and we couldn't resist the delicious street food wafting through the air. We sipped cold beers while soaking in the colorful atmosphere, surrounded by laughter and chatter. Each corner offered something new, from mouthwatering snacks to friendly locals eager to share stories. It felt like a celebration every night!

author: Maddie T
title: friendly locals and lively beer streets
original_content: The street is a lively place, full of tourists and friendly locals. We tasted a variety of delicious beers in the small bar and the atmosphere was relaxed and pleasant. Although it is somewhat touristy, it is this enthusiasm that gives us a sense of Hanoi's unique charm. The night's lights and laughter were intertwined as if time had stood still. If you come to Hanoi, don't miss this vibrant beer street!
practical_tips: Don't miss this vibrant beer street

author: Giorgio
title: Lovely Nights in Ta Hien
original_content: Traditional architecture took us back to the past, and the lively Cheap Beer Street was perfect for relaxing with budget beers. The lights and vibrant atmosphere made our visit an unforgettable experience in Hanoi. We'll definitely be back!

author: Mamie F
title: Harnoy's Taching Street expedition.
original_content: The atmosphere is great, the bars and stalls are full of lively crowds. As a famous beer street, it feels great to have friends drinking beer together! The locals are also friendly and helpful, making us feel warm. Still, the streets are a little crowded, and sometimes it's hard to find a quiet place to rest. Overall, this is a place to experience!
drawbacks: hard to find a quiet place to rest

author: Amara B
title: Amazingly
original_content: A bustling, bustling place in the heart of the old town. There are so many diverse colors in this place. My sister loves dancing to music with bottles of beer at roadside stalls
highlights: dancing to music with bottles of beer at roadside stalls

author: 周星
title: The usual experience of lively nightlife
original_content: The small bars and stalls down the street offer authentic food and drinks that do give us a hint of the authentic Vietnamese touch. However, the number of tourists makes it difficult to find a quiet corner to enjoy this uniqueness. Although we tasted several local drinks, it wasn't particularly stunning. Overall, it's a great place for tourists who want to feel the nightlife, but don't expect too much.
extracted_spaces: small bars and stalls down the street
drawbacks: difficult to find a quiet corner
highlights: great place for tourists who want to feel the nightlife

author: Jaymee Elf
title: A night of flavor and fun
original_content: We dived into the lively atmosphere, sampling delicious street food and sipping local beer. The vibrant energy was contagious as we mingled with fellow travelers. Laughing and enjoying each bite together made for an unforgettable night filled with flavors and memories we’ll cherish!

author: Germaine Kope
title: The heart of hanoi's nightlife scene
original_content: Ta Hien Street, aptly nicknamed "Beer Street," offers an electric atmosphere after sunset. We loved sitting on tiny plastic stools, enjoying fresh beer and watching the world go by. The mix of locals and travelers created such a vibrant vibe. It's chaotic and crowded, but that's part of its charm. A must-visit for experiencing Hanoi's authentic nightlife.

author: Dot P
title: The vibrant nightlife
original_content: The laughter of locals and fellow travelers filled the air, creating an inviting atmosphere. We shared stories with friendly vendors, discovering hidden gems amidst the chaos. It was the perfect blend of culture and fun.
highlights: perfect blend of culture and fun

author: Adriana
title: Hanoi's Beer Corner
original_content: This bustling beer corner came alive at night with endless rows of tiny plastic stools filled with locals and tourists alike. Sipping fresh beer while people-watching and sampling street food made for an authentic Hanoi experience. The energy here is simply contagious!

author: Blondell C
title: La Rue de la Bière
original_content: Sitting on our little stools, we shared bia hoi with the locals. The atmosphere is electric, especially in the evening. One tip: try street skewers, they are divine with cold beer!
extracted_spaces: The locals' area where we sat

author: ouchene
title: The Pulsating Heart of Hanoi’s Beer Culture! 🍺
original_content: Wow, what an unforgettable evening on Ta Hien Street! This historic alley in the heart of the old quarter has totally thrilled us. The famous Bia Hoi tastes fantastic here, especially when sitting on the typical small plastic chairs. The atmosphere is electrifying - everywhere cheerful people enjoying life! The mix of tradition and modern nightlife is unique. An absolute must for any Hanoi visitor!
highlights: The atmosphere is electrifying - everywhere cheerful people enjoying life!
The mix of tradition and modern nightlife is unique
The famous Bia Hoi tastes fantastic here
practical_tips: An absolute must for any Hanoi visitor!

author: Sue V
title: Load and chaotic
original_content: This place is an assault on the senses. Load music and lights emanating from every venue. Street vendors hassling and hawkers trying to get you in to every bar. Not for the faint hearted.
drawbacks: hawkers trying to get you in to every bar

author: Krisha
title: Vibrant nightlife
original_content: We were swept up in the lively atmosphere of this iconic Hanoi destination.  Inexpensive local beers flowed freely, making it easy to mingle with fellow travelers and soak in the electric ambiance.  The street food stalls lining Ta Hien offered a tempting array of affordable eats, perfect for fueling a night of revelry.

author: Explore37315798840
title: Horrible experience
original_content: We visited a few places like this in Southeast Asia (Siem Reap, Phnom Penh, Saigon) and enjoyed the atmosphere, but this one is very disappointing and vulgar. The cacophony generated by the loudspeakers of the multitude of small bars competing as well as the flappers of the latter (which are more harassing than inviting) pushed us to cross it as quickly as possible and go have fun elsewhere. In addition, we were repeatedly asked what we were looking for by putting videos of young girls undressing under our noses. This is a shame because it projects a negative image of the city.
drawbacks: repeatedly asked what we were looking for

author: Shtarker
title: Sheer Craziness
original_content: Visited "beer street" in Hanoi's old quarter on a Saturday night.Although we have watched it on YouTube, the crowed, loud technology music & every second vendor trying to drag you into their bar or restaurant was something that we are totally unprepared for.  Finally we sat down at Coco Bar for a drink, seems to have less people around that area, but still have to constantly fighting off street vendors trying to sell items to us, one of them was a kid looked under 10 yrs old selling cigarettes.Definitely not our cup of tea!
drawbacks: Street vendors trying to sell items

author: Crumpled Nomad | Travel Intelligence
title: Busy busy busy street on a Saturday night
original_content: A famous street in Hanoi where one can find many pubs, bars and drinking holes along the street. They even sat on the road with low chairs sipping ice cold beers. It was extremely busy and packed on a Saturday night and as I walked along, I was constantly bombarded with people touting. I found this rather unpleasant and tried to walk as fast as possible. It’s just not something for me but it’s strictly my opinion. I’m sure many will find this place interesting. For someone who’s not into drinking and loud music, this may not be the place for you. But I enjoyed walking along it, just once to soak in the bustling atmosphere.

author: Sshuddho G
title: A diff experience..
original_content: ..cold and fresh draught beer sitting on small street side chairs after a long day of touring can be quite therapeutic..cheers

author: BrakiWorldTraveler
title: Pattaya style party area
original_content: This street is commonly known as Hanoi Beer street and is set in the northern part of Old Quarter. It comes alive at night with dozens of cafes, night clubs, eateries, massage parlors, etc....much reminding on such in Pattaya or Phuket.Music is very loud, coming from every, tiny and small club one by another, so while walking you hear only unrecognizable mixed music noise. We just walked through without any desire to sit somewhere, even our teenage daughter didn't like it.
practical_tips: avoid if you don't like loud music

author: Departure48409439286
title: A wonderful experience at Hoang restaurant
original_content: The restaurant serves delicious food, super delicious food, friendly and enthusiastic staff. Daisy was the one who took care of my table, she was very kind and friendly. Will recommend the restaurant to many of my friends and will come back again and again

author: PW14513
title: chill chill
original_content: Busy street and ideal place to hang out with my friends. There were a lot of souvenirs shops and restaurants surrounding
highlights: Ideal place to hang out with friends
practical_tips: Go to the surrounding souvenirs shops and restaurants

author: Rutland Auckland
title: Not worth the effort to go to - it’s just hyped up
original_content: Sorry not for us. A tourist trap. Overpriced. Underwhelming. It reminded us of Magaluf or some other seedy European nightlife.Save your money and go to any of the myriad of better places
practical_tips: Save your money and go to any of the myriad of better places

author: Mobile40517000222
title: Bia street for travelers
original_content: Such an interesting place for gathering and chilling with friends. Good for Hanoian and travelers to enjoy the bia hoi

author: HIROYUKI SHIMIZU
title: Extraordinary
original_content: I went there on a Friday and it was crowded with tourists and locals. Cars and motorbikes were passing by nearby so we had to sit and drink on the edge of the seats, music was blaring, people from all over the world, vendors... it was chaos. If you want to feel the power and heat of Asia, this is the place to go.
drawbacks: had to sit and drink on the edge of the seats
highlights: feel the power and heat of Asia

author: Siddeeque Hassan
title: Beer + Positivity = Ta Hian
original_content: Ta Hien Corner is also known as The Beer Street, is a great food street. The weekends in Ta Hien is so much positive vibe and positivity. A great place of weekend hangout for both tourists and natives. A must visit place for sure.

author: Scott W
title: Beer Street
original_content: This place is amazing, bars everywhere and the sights and sounds are an assault on your senses. A great place to go for a drink with lots of 'happy hour' offers.
highlights: great place to go for a drink

author: Vthc4
title: Great atmosphere
original_content: We went on a Thursday evening and it was bustling - a total change of the street in the day. Great atmosphere with loud music with many diners seated on both sides of the street.

author: SK
title: Nice area to visit for the nighttime
original_content: One of the must-go, it is crowded and fun. Just remember to not drink too much and make sure you always check prices.

author: Jacky29292
title: Nice place but very crowdes
original_content: Njce place for drink beer and have some food. The price ia a bit expensive. It is very crowded but fun to go there

author: The Baobab Republic
title: Awesome
original_content: One of the places you must visit when coming to Hanoi is the old quarter of Ta Hien.  Here is famous for the shops selling food, drinks, bars and many specialties of Hanoi.  And there are many delicious dishes.  And Banh Mi Co Nga is one of the dishes that you should try.  A little pate, sausage, chicken eggs are stir-fried in a pan with a little fat.  Add a little soy sauce and chili, serve with bread.  A great experience in the old town.

author: alebeth
title: It’s a no from me
original_content: Also known as beer street. This place is crazy busy and reminds me of Bangla Rd, Thailand. I really disliked this place and didn’t enjoy it. Maybe better suited to a younger crowd who wants to get on the drink and balloons.

author: EdM
title: Everything is happening
original_content: A great spot to have a beer and watch the action. We found the junction was better than the bars higher up the street. And cheaper

author: Pulkit C
title: Crazy party street, unlike seen anywhere else!
original_content: Oh what a street. Extremely crowded, beer revellers filling on the street sitting on small benches. What a vibe! Must visit if you love beer or not. The place to party in Hanoi. Street was alive till midnight on a weekday. Locals as well tourists flocked onto the small drinking joints lining the street, my top rated place in Hanoi for night life!
highlights: Top rated place in Hanoi for night life

author: Rob Nesbit
title: The place to be on a Saturday night
original_content: The place to be on a Saturday night in Hanoi. Might be an idea to let the crowds dissipate after a few hours and wait in a bar, then the fun can begin as the adult-kids go home..........
practical_tips: let the crowds dissipate after a few hours

author: G2Kpauly
title: Cool street
original_content: A popular street in Hanoi to walk down, chill and eat and drink if you want.  It gets more busy on weekends and you will get hustled by every bar restaurant as you walk down. It's pretty narrow too.
drawbacks: get hustled by every bar restaurant

author: MinT
title: Great place!
original_content: Perfect place to drink and enjoy the crowded people go passing by you on the street. The beer, the street foods, everything from here was great.

author: alexander
title: Good
original_content: The place to be if you want to party in Ha Noi! By night it is a “walking street”  but given so many scooters and the occasional taxi I wouldn’t exactly say it’s a walking street haha.
