author: Killian W
title: Bun Cha to discover!
original_content: Excellent food, full of flavor, I took Bun Cha Full Option, as recommended on the menu, a treat! Beautiful discovery

author: Federica D
title: Bun Cha Gluten Free very tasty
original_content:
Perfect spot to cheers with friends and enjoying amazing time with friends. 
First time trying Bun Cha Gluten Free and fried spring rolls … really tasty!! 🥰🥰 all of their menu meals are gluten free , such a good news for us as celiac! 🥰🥰
highlights: all of their menu meals are gluten free
practical_tips: go to a place with gluten-free options

author: Thomas G
title: Best Food Experience in Hanoi
original_content: This was the best food experience in Hanoi so far. Local was incredibly cosy and rich in tradition. The host was very friendly and accessible. The food was the best we've had in Hanoi. We ordered a number 2 and a number 10. It was perfect amount for two people and the food tasted absolutely amazing.
highlights: food was the best we've had in Hanoi
practical_tips: order number 2 and a number 10 for two people

author: Stephanie M
title: Great spot for some delicious food
original_content: This is a great spot to try some delicious bun cha. Awesome atmosphere and good hospitality, and the food was incredible! Extremely reasonably priced as well, would definitely recommend

author: Russ Lacuata
title: Authentic Flavors
original_content: Truly is a hidden gem in Hanoi serving one of the best Bun Cha if not the best. The Bun Cha is an authentic combination of sweet and salty broth with the smoky flavor of the grilled pork. The rice noodles are thin and soft but not mushy. The herbs and vegetables are piled high and they are fresh and crisp. This is highly recommended.
highlights: one of the best Bun Cha
authentic combination of sweet and salty broth
smoky flavor of the grilled pork

author: Rubén G
title: Rich Bun Chá and egg coffee.
original_content: Good place to eat Bun Cha; you can also combine it with rolls on a menu. Egg coffee is also quite delicious here if you want to try it.

author: Tommaso V
title: Bun Cha at Bun Cha Ta - Must do!
original_content: Tried Bun Cha for the first time and loved it! Service was quick and friendly, the manager explained us how to eat it and we had a nice convo. But most importantly Bun Cha is extremely tasty and quite a different dish from the ones i tried during my ten days in Vietnam. Highly recommend Bun Cha Ta 👍🏼
practical_tips: go to Bun Cha Ta for Bun Cha

author: Emča H
title: Delish
original_content: I really recommend this place for people who haven’t tried Bun cha and want to make sure that their first experience will be a good one. The service is great and atmosphere very relaxed. Price is to be expected for the quality.
practical_tips: try Bun cha for the first time

author: Maria Anna M
title: Simple, comfortable and Fairly priced
original_content: Authentic bun cha in a more comfortable setting, especially on a hot humid day like today. It was not intimidating to eat the soup since they have a friendly staff, especially Nam, who enthutiastically taught me the best way to enjoy it. I loved the soup as is, just the right sweetness plus the smoky flavor of grilled pork. The noodles thin and soft. The fried spring rolls were good and filling. I came just before the peak hour so I was able to savor the food and the place, but soon got crowded with mostly food tour groups. Fairly priced, with a bonus of the gleeful assistance of their staff. Definitely worth it!

author: Francesca Z
title: Ottimo Bun Cha
original_content:
They made us sit on the second floor with traditional tables. We chose the traditional bun cha with fried pork, pork spring roll, vegetables and rice noodles.
Everything should be mixed together and enjoy!
highlights: traditional bun cha with fried pork, pork spring roll, vegetables and rice noodles

author: David T
title: Bum Cha Ta"A Hidden Gem"
original_content: Bun Cha Ta is a hidden gem in Hanoi, serving the best Bun Cha in town. Despite its simple setting, the restaurant was bustling with customers, a testament to its popularity. My wife and I loved the authentic flavors. Highly recommend for anyone craving this iconic dish!
practical_tips: Highly recommend for anyone craving this iconic dish!

author: W128
title: Bun Cha-tastic
original_content: Bun Cha-tastic. How great was this place. Went upstairs. Aircons, fans and cold beer. Then combo 1. Bosh. Bosh. Bosh. Fresh noodles. Greens. Charcoal griddled pork. Dip Into the bowl of garlic - whack it on lettuce and greens, bung a piece of pork in and wrap and then eat.  Nom nom nom. Greens into broth. Noddles into broth. Chilli Billy. Nom nom more. Cracking cracking place. Get involved!!!

author: Phillip
title: Good food and nice atmosphere
original_content: Very good food. Will definitely recommend taking nutshell soup with pigs. Cool atmosphere and nice staff. Great prices in the center

author: Ka S
title: Local cuisine to try
original_content: We had dinner at this place the first evening we arrived in Hanoi, on the recommendation of the hotel receptionist. Street food served in a simple restaurant, on two floors, they made us sit on the upper floor; before entering the room you take off your shoes.
highlights: Street food served in a simple restaurant
practical_tips: Go to the hotel receptionist for recommendations

author: Dev D
title: Cheap and delicious
original_content: This spot is absolutely perfect for a quick dinner. The Bun cha was absolutely delicious  (the spring rolls particularly). It comes with all the usual accompaniments (fish sauce, chilli, garlic) so you can tailor it to your flavour pallet). Service was friendly and the food also came really quickly.

author: Egay M
title: Our Bun Cha Ta Experience
original_content:
Came here for lunch.

Classic Bun Cha
Grilled Pork with Noodles. Pork was mostly lean. Well seasoned. Grilled well done. Soup is delicious, inherits the smokeyness of the grilled pork. Noodles slippery smooth. Vegetables and herbs fresh. Lime and a bit of chili enhances the flavor.

Fried Spring Rolls
Doesn't look pretty but tastes good. Good accompaniment to Bun Cha.

Overall, Bun Cha Ta is a good experience.
highlights: Pork was mostly lean. Well seasoned. Grilled well done.
Soup is delicious, inherits the smokeyness of the grilled pork.
Noodles slippery smooth. Vegetables and herbs fresh.

author: SerpentSermon
title: Great Lunch Out
original_content: This place was so interesting, because it's like you're sat in the floor of the first floor of somebody's house. The stairs are defiantly a bid steep. However, it's not really a negative until after a few beers. The food is fantastic, full of flavour and very fresh. The staff are friendly and very quick. It feels very personal because there are only 3 or 4 tables upstairs. The price is insane! I couldn't believe how cheap this was for such good food. You are talking about £35 for 5 people including beers. Unreal. Would highly recommend!
extracted_spaces: the floor of the first floor of somebody's house
drawbacks: the stairs are defiantly a bid steep
highlights: the food is fantastic, full of flavour and very fresh
the staff are friendly and very quick

author: Marc B
title: Great Food, Allergen Friendly
original_content: The best food I ate in Hanoi. They specialise in Bun Cha as per the name and nail it. Everything is gluten free which was great for me as someone with dietary restrictions. Price is cheap. The girl at the front is lovely and speaks great English.

author: PHOAustralia
title: Not what we expected
original_content:
We first experienced with Bun Cha was 15 years ago in Hanoi and we loved it.  We have had it many times in Melbourne. 

However, the style of BunCha at this place was not to our liking as the pork was already soaked in a bowl of sweet soup. I prefer the style where you build your own bowl with noodles, lettuce, herbs and dipping sauce.  The spring rolls were nice. 

I also didn’t like taking off my shoes (top level of the place) for the seating particularly as it directly outside a toilet that is need of a very good clean.
drawbacks: pork was already soaked in a bowl of sweet soup
taking off my shoes for the seating
toilet that is need of a very good clean
practical_tips: build your own bowl with noodles, lettuce, herbs and dipping sauce

author: Kevin C
title: Upset stomach; dirty; inattentive!
original_content:
Place was dirty and full of tourists! Cash only? 

The guy who was in charge of showing me to my table sat there and did not pick up the dirty plates and mess left by the other customers. Instead his phone was more important!

I also ended up with an upset stomach after the visit. 

Never again and I recommend you head elsewhere. 

Michelin? Maybe they were confused with rating it against their tires!
drawbacks: dirty plates and mess left by other customers

author: sandy
title: Delicious, fast and friendly
original_content: They are super, super quick with the food and respond when you have any requests. The food is super delicious!!! The service is very friendly. So I would definitely recommend it! The spring rolls are an absolute hit!!

author: DXB_Maple
title: Best meal in Hanoi
original_content: This was our favourite meal in Hanoi. The flavour was delicious and it tasted so fresh!  Our non-advenurous eater (tween) also loved it. The whole family agreed!

author: nicolasfre
title: A must
original_content: For less than 6 euros you surely have the best bun cha there is. To do absolutely. Recommended by a tire guide and we know why!

author: ciaran1sheridan
title: Good Bun Cha option in Hanoi
original_content: Tasty Bun Cha experience in Hanoi Old Quarter. Good paced service, helpful staff & generous helpings. Worth a visit & recommended.

author: Inna
title: Delicious lunch in a cozy cafe
original_content: On the first day in Hanoi, we drove around a lot, looked for where to change money, and looked around the city. We were very hungry and wanted to try some local Vietnamese cuisine. We did not regret choosing this cafe. We were greeted well by the staff and escorted to the place where we should eat. The room was not very large, on the second floor. You had to take off your shoes before entering the room. We were seated at a large table that could accommodate more than 10 people. As a result, people of Asian appearance sat next to us and had a nice conversation. We asked the girl what she could recommend to us from the menu. In the end, we settled on the traditional bun cha dish. I chose with pork, my companion with chicken. The dish included noodles, fresh herbs, spices and a rich, sweetish hot broth. I recommend visiting this cafe, it is very cozy, they will tell you about traditions, and you will have a good time and eat delicious food
practical_tips: try the traditional bun cha dish

author: NTN
title: Michelin Meatballs
original_content: It is no coincidence that in the Michelin guide everything is amazing and everything is 100% Local, the meatballs are a must and the price is the lowest possible

author: B L
title: Recommend.
original_content: Found this place through Trip Advisor and it didn’t disappoint. I ordered the local Hanoi bon cha soup with the sampler spring rolls plus beer and rice whisky. My food was yummy and fresh. The place was clean and the hosts nice.  Recommend.

author: Caroline
title: Delicious and tasty
original_content:
Super delicious food, we all bought their signature dish which consists of a pork soup with rice noodles and spring rolls on the side. It was really delicious and even the clear soup had a lot of flavor.

The staff were also really nice and smiling.
highlights: staff were really nice and smiling

author: Meilan
title: First meal in Hanoi
original_content: First meal in Hanoi and it did not disappoint! We had the Bun Cha and an order of spring rolls. The broth was savory with tiny hints of tanginess. The grilled pork was cooked perfectly and accompanied so well with the fresh herbs and noodles. Meant to take pictures, but was so hungry that I devoured most of the food before I remembered to take a pic. Overall a very satisfying meal. Very reasonable prices, but cash only.
highlights: Bun Cha was savory with tiny hints of tanginess

author: lnk1402
title: Disappointed
original_content: Extremely disappointed, the food was acceptable, and great value. Do not understand the Michelin recommendation at all
drawbacks: Do not understand the Michelin recommendation at all

author: Emma H
title: Must try Hanoi’s Bun Cha here!!!
original_content:
Perfect place for authentic bun cha. There are multiple storeys where you can sit on the floor or on lowered tables depending on your comfort. The food was made from such fresh ingredients. Bun Cha is a must try in Hanoi! 

Thank you to Vinh for teaching us how to authentically eat Bun Cha!!
highlights: Perfect place for authentic bun cha
The food was made from such fresh ingredients
Bun Cha is a must try in Hanoi!
practical_tips: Thank you to Vinh for teaching us how to authentically eat Bun Cha!!

author: Ella
title: The best meal I ate in Vietnam
original_content: As a coeliac, I loved eating here as everything on the menu was gluten free! I'd highly recommend the bun cha with tofu and ordering extra vegetable spring rolls. It was amazing to eat spring rolls without fear of cross contamination. The menu is not labelled as gluten free, but I first came here as part of a food tour where my Vietnamese tour guide spoke with staff to confirm it was safe to eat as a coeliac. I loved the food so much we visited again on our last night. This restaurant has an interesting layout, as the tables and chairs are set into the floor.
practical_tips: ask staff about gluten free options

author: BunchOfLilies
title: THE place for bun cha
original_content:
In my top 3 meals on our whole Vietnam trip. Excellent quality bun cha and absolutely delicious. The spring rolls were also exceptional. Service was flawless and prices reasonable. There was a food tour here when we came so also a good sign how great it is. Wonderful dining experience I could not fault a thing.

If you’re looking for bun cha in Hanoi, this is the place.
practical_tips: If you’re looking for bun cha in Hanoi, this is the place

author: George M
title: Excellent
original_content: Local color and food to write hone about. The soup was spectacular. Service was great and prices are extremely reasonable Highly recommended

author: Laura
title: Everything gluten free and so good
original_content: You have to try it! Everything is gluten free (the fried spring rolls too) and it is so yummi. It is so great to find a place were you can eat safely when you have celiac’s disease. We went there twice because we liked it so much. Plus, the location is pretty lovely
practical_tips: go there twice if you like it

author: Helen Carr
title: Bun cha specialty restaurant
original_content: Traditional authentic restaurant.  Small menu. Must visit to try the local specialty of bun cha. Family owned and operated.
highlights: Must visit to try the local specialty of bun cha

author: AndreasBrok
title: Excellent street food type place!! Must eat!
original_content: The place is quite underrated when you see it from outside. But going in is something that you must do. The choices are simple but they are super rewarding. I have never eaten pork grilled like that anywhere in Vietnam. Super tasty!!!

author: iznogoodgood
title: To discover
original_content: Very warm welcome and fast service in this restaurant where the specialty is Bun Cha which I did not know. Soup composed of several ingredients (meatballs, rice noodles, spring rolls, salad, etc.). It’s surprising but, for my part, I liked it without more. To discover.

author: Michael T
title: Authentic Vietnamese food
original_content:
When I mentioned to friends that we’d been to Bun Cha Ta, their first reaction was “not the one Obama had been to”!

Wife and I didn’t know which restaurant the former president had visited but we love the food at Boon Cha Ta. It is a very popular local restaurant which has a very simple menu.

We’d ordered their signature white rice noodles with fried pork and side dishes of fried spring roll (seafood and vegetarian versions). 

The white noodles and vegetables were served separately so we dipped the noodles and vegetables into the pork soup. Tasted really delicious.

Bun Cha Ta is located in the Old Quarter and was within walking distance from our hotel at Hoan Kiem area.

Staff are friendly and prompt. 

Overall this is a recommended place if you’re in Hanoi.
practical_tips: go to the one in the Old Quarter
try the signature white rice noodles with fried pork

author: Vicki H
title: Fabulous Bun Cha!
original_content: It’s a small unassuming place to eat but seriously great Bun Cha alongside excellent service.  We thoroughly enjoyed our visit and we would definitely recommend and return!
extracted_spaces: a small unassuming place to eat

author: M3Traveller
title: A great place to experience local lunch or bun cha!
original_content:
Read about here on Michelin Guide, rated Bib Gourmand and wanted to try something traditional and local to Hanoi.

A very “rustic” feel - we were seated upstairs and it’s shoes off and seated at sunken floor tables. 

The food was delicious - we had the traditional house dish (bun cha, obviously!) and flavours were excellent. Staff explained what it was and how to eat it (add garlic and chilli!).

A great experience for relaxed lunch - and very very reasonable!

author: Fatima C
title: Tasty food
original_content: Super attentive staff, they recommended the dish to us, the price was very good and the place was very simple. We were sitting on the ground floor but the lady told us to go up and stay on the first floor (more pleasant). It's really worth it because the food is very tasty and fresh.
highlights: food is very tasty and fresh
practical_tips: go up and stay on the first floor

author: Mari K
title: Great food, multiple floors
original_content: Cozy place, great food!The restaurant is bigger than it looks from the street as there is a second (and a third?!) floor! We had spring rolls and bun cha - yum!

author: GenieC
title: Don't miss this!
original_content: Few items on the menu but DELICIOUS from first bite to last.  Don't miss this if you're near old town.  If I had three thumbs, I'd give them 3!!
practical_tips: Don't miss this if you're near old town

author: Clayton J
title: nice tradional food
original_content: nice restaurant serving a traditional food in Hanoi.This kind of food is so famous, the Us president had used it when he came to Vienam

author: MartK
title: The best is the view from the second floor
original_content: We didn't like it. The beef was stringy and greasy, untypical for beef. The fried spring rolls were too. Overall, too expensive for the quality. The visitors were all tourists, mostly accompanied by tour guides. The stairs up to the second floor are dirty and sticky. The view from the top of the bustling street is interesting, but that's not enough for a good rating.
extracted_spaces: the top of the bustling street

author: Alwyn
title: Full of flavour
original_content: We tried a few places but this was our favourite bun cha.  Very flavourful gravy, the grilled and minced pork were to perfection in my view.  The owner and service staff were very knowledgable and polite.  We were there for 5 days and when here 3 times.  the place is small so be a bit patient or go a little off hours.
highlights: the grilled and minced pork were to perfection
the owner and service staff were very knowledgable and polite

author: karoo91
title: An explosion of flavors
original_content:
I went to bun cha to taste my first bun cha. No regrets about my choice, the dish was excellent, as were the spring rolls.
The young waitress was very friendly and smiling and very available to explain how to eat this dish.
Excellent value for money 130,000 dg bun cha + 2 spring rolls + 1 beer
practical_tips: Ask the waitress for guidance on how to eat the dish

author: cassie h
title: Bun Cha at it's BEST
original_content:
Absolutely fantastic. We were recommended a few places to give Bun Cha a red hot crack as the dish of Hanoi and this was by far the best. So good we wen't back twice in 24 hours. (And yes, this is way better than Obama Bun Cha which we was good but not worth the hype). 

Food was balanced and fresh. Served in a cute two storey family run establishment, 100% ask for a seat upstairs - you'll see why! 

Service was on point with our orders taken quickly and food delivered within minutes. I would recommend enjoying the #1 combination bun cha & 2 x spring rolls. I have never had spring rolls as delicious - will really struggle back in Sydney now!

Bonus points - the team did not even ask for a review which for anyone who has travelled Vietnam will know is a rarity and why so many places are rated so highly (sometimes unjustly). Makes it very challenging to find the best spots. 

Hope you enjoy as much as we did :)
practical_tips: Enjoy the #1 combination bun cha & 2 x spring rolls

author: Fangqi_A
title: Great introduction to Bun Cha
original_content: Went for a late lunch. We ordered grilled pork bun cha, which was served in a soup with plate of vegetables. Grilled pork was flavorful and tasty. The host was patient in explaining how to eat the bun cha. Will recommend this eatery.
highlights: grilled pork was flavorful and tasty
host was patient in explaining how to eat the bun cha

author: Yolanda R
title: Success
original_content: We went to try the typical bun cha and we were right. The place has charm, the staff is friendly and explains how to proceed. The food is abundant and tasty.
highlights: The food is abundant and tasty
The staff is friendly and explains how to proceed

author: Carlota
title: Great! A must in Hanoi
original_content: Great food! Original Vietnamese restaurant with very good bun cha. We didn’t expect such a great atmosphere and welcoming. Definitely recommended! 😊

author: Lars V
title: Very tasty food and friendly service
original_content:
Very tasty food and friendly service.
Fair price and large portions. I can definitely recommend it!

author: Marie R
title: A very good place to taste Bun cha Hanoi
original_content: Very good Bun cha Hanoi, we really enjoyed our meal! Prices have increased slightly (110,000d). A charming welcome as often in Vietnam!

author: familieX
title: Tasty Bun Cha
original_content:
Our guide took us to this restaurant to let us taste Bun Cha. The open space on the 1st floor is nicely decorated.
The Bun Cha with grilled pork was tasty.
highlights: tasty Bun Cha with grilled pork

author: Eva
title: Bun cha at the top
original_content: Awesome food, friendly staff, delicious bun cha. Loved the top room with table carved in the floor. Rolls are deli too. Highly recommend

author: mr g
title: be careful of the vegetarian bun cha
original_content: The pork bun cha was good, nice and balanced.  The vegetarian bun cha broth was way too sweet and barely edible (I think they kept the sugar the same but left out the fish sauce).  Stick to the carnivore offerings.
drawbacks: The vegetarian bun cha broth was way too sweet and barely edible
highlights: The pork bun cha was good, nice and balanced

author: mamacita1001
title: Very disappointing,,,,
original_content:
This is a TA place. You don’t need to go.

Bun Cha is just disappointing.
It can’t be 100,000 for that quality and the portion.

Deep fried spring roll isn’t good at all as it isn’t filled with much meat and veggies. I found a lot of space in it. And they are rather small.

Bun Cha doesn’t come with many vegetables in the soup and on the side. 
I don’t get why and how this place has got good reputation. 

Far from "best" Bun Cha, this is my opinion.

Tiny amount of Vietnamese rice wine is served in the end as complimentary but the price of it should be already included in the price of Bun  Cha.  (100,000 dong)
As I had to wait for my room (of a hotel) to be ready, I had egg coffee as well. It is also disappointing. You can’t tell if it is just coffee or egg coffee. If you have already tasted authentic egg coffee, you won’t think it is egg coffee. It is just sweet coffee.
drawbacks: Disappointing quality and portion for 100,000 dong
Deep fried spring roll not filled with much meat and veggies
Bun Cha doesn't come with many vegetables in the soup and on the side

author: Sadie M
title: Fantastic food -and helpful staff
original_content:
Recommended by our hotel - helpful staff, nice dining room upstairs , they ask you to remove shoes . Restaurant with ac.
Food was great- we went option 1 which was rice noodles and herbs that add into a clear soup with pork (meatball and strips of pork) . Accompanied by 2 fried spring rolls . You can add garlic chilli ginger fish sauce as condiments to taste which worked great for the teenagers . Option1 cost  120 000 vnd
practical_tips: add garlic chilli ginger fish sauce as condiments to taste

author: Steven
title: Good buncha
original_content: Great food, fast service, reasonable and clear pricing. Visited here three times during my 1 week stay.

author: benjaminng2016
title: Enjoyable lunch
original_content: The place is clean and the food is tasty. The price is reasonable and the service is good. The local goes there too besides we tourists.

author: Sophie P
title: Would definitely recommend
original_content: Our first experience of Bun Cha and it was a good one! The service was amazing, we loved the food, and tried their rice wine whisky and got a taste of their dads home brew - delicious.

author: Sholto D
title: Good place for Bun cha
original_content: Grill pork and spring rolls were excellent. It's very close to our hotel then easy to go. Highly recommend!

author: KeithChan69
title: Great tasting local street food in the comfort of a restaurant.
original_content:
This is the first time I tried Bun Cha after seeing many on the streets. 
With couple kids in tow this restaurant was a great place to accommodate our needs and taste buds yet without the hustle and bustle of the streets.
The food were so good we finished every bit.
highlights: accommodate our needs and taste buds
practical_tips: go to Bun Cha for a good meal

author: Camper52591290704
title: Good
original_content: Bun cha is a traditional Vietnamese dish that is very delicious, the water and vegetables are very fragrant, the restaurant is clean, and there are delicious drinks

author: dmct123
title: Don’t go anywhere else for Bun Cha
original_content:
Recommended by our guide and also seen the reviews on Tripadvisor and it certainly didn’t disappoint.
Incredible and authentic.
If you visit Hanoi…this place is an absolute must try!

author: Richard W
title: How many 5 star reviews for Bun Cha Ta.
original_content: Looking for a good place with traditional food I found Bun Cha Ta in Hoi An. I read the reviews and thought surely it can't be that good, but we gave it a go and WOW, the food was fantastic. Simple broth, noodles and pork slices and patties, but the taste of each element was amazing. We had traditional spring rolls as a side dish and an explanation from the staff of "Bun Cha". The restaurant may seem a bit far out of the old town but from the waterfront it is probably less than 10 mins walk and you won't be disappointed.
highlights: the taste of each element was amazing
an explanation from the staff of 'Bun Cha'
practical_tips: go to the waterfront for a 10 min walk

author: Piotr M
title: very good food
original_content: very good and tasty food served in this restaurant, not too big choice, but that's good because the dishes are great

author: Thuy
title: The best food in Hanoi !
original_content:
Food was pretty amazing. We had the Bun cha with seafood nem. 

We stayed in Hanoi for 3 days and everyday we went back here each day. The customer service was so nice!

author: Andreas
title: Amazing food and atmosphere
original_content: Authentic and amazing Vietnamese food. We had the Bun cha full option and everybody loved it. Plenty of food to a reasonable price. The atmosphere was also really good and the service was great.
highlights: Plenty of food to a reasonable price
The atmosphere was also really good and the service was great
practical_tips: Go for the Bun cha full option

author: Grace R Saporsantos
title: Bunchafave!
original_content: one of our favorite food in Vietnam the Buncha! we will miss this and we will definitely come back because of this dish!

author: Alyssa B
title: Amazing gf traditional food!!
original_content: Came here after seeing all the reviews and we weren’t disappointed!! Such a cute restaurant with friendly staff, the whole menu is gluten free so I felt very safe eating there. The Bun Cha was so good we came back for dinner again the next night. Highly recommend the deep-fried veggie spring rolls and tofu!!
highlights: deep-fried veggie spring rolls and tofu

author: Marthafebi C
title: Good location and experience! Tasty food and coffee
original_content:
Unique taste. The meat is tender and grilled perfectly with white noodles and lot of veggie. But soup is sweet - might not suitable for savory lovers like me. 

You can find traditional, or seafood spring rolls. Although not so distinguished in term of taste. 

The sticky yoghurt is so gooood. Love it!!
The coffee is good
The chocolate is too sweet

But worth the visit since the location is strategic and near every where
drawbacks: soup is sweet - might not suitable for savory lovers like me
not so distinguished in term of taste
highlights: The meat is tender and grilled perfectly
The sticky yoghurt is so gooood
practical_tips: worth the visit since the location is strategic

author: Melissa O
title: Best Bun Cha in Hanoi!
original_content: Wow. The Bun Cha was sooooo incredibly delicious. 2 bowls and 2 sodas for $12 USD. You cannot beat that. And the waitstaff was lovely. Highly recommend for a quick, casual meal!!
highlights: The Bun Cha was sooooo incredibly delicious
practical_tips: Highly recommend for a quick, casual meal!!

author: hanz95
title: Great place for first timers
original_content: Great place to try Bun Cha for the first time. The menu is set up for first timers, and the friendly staff tell you how to eat it when it is served. We shared one between two as the serving sizes are generous! Probably a bit pricier than other places but given the service I think that’s warranted!

author: Mamouchka
title: Delicious food!
original_content: Went there to try the Bun Cha as many forum recommend it. Well… it was worth it. The bun cha and the spring rolls were delicious. The service were great (as expected). Make a stop if you close by, you won’t regret it.
highlights: The bun cha and the spring rolls were delicious
practical_tips: Make a stop if you close by

author: Jollyjumper22
title: Bun cha experience
original_content: I ate bun cha in Hanoi and every place I went to, serves delicious bun cha. This place was no exception. The only difference is that this restaurant probably visited by many tourists so the price is quite more expensive than other bun cha restaurant.
practical_tips: go to other bun cha restaurants

author: Krishna
title: Must try restaurant at Hamoi
original_content:
Must try. I would have certainly missed something incredible if I hadn't visited here for dinner. 

Food style is something I have experienced for the first time. Seating arrangement is also quite unique and soothing.

author: Amanda
title: Yummy for lunch
original_content: In love with buncha. So tasting with fish sauce flavor.  You must try spring rolls. Nice staff and lovely place. We will come back

author: Janine T
title: Best Bun Cha Ta
original_content:
Based on our love of Bun Cha and reading reviews decided to walk to BunCha Ta. 
Chose Bun cha full option and was 5/5 for flavour. You are able to select chilli and garlic to your own comfort level. 
The staff gave instructions to us and others how to mix the spices, noodles and herbs into the broth.
At the end she gave everyone a small shot glass of Vietnamese white wine whisky??? and got us to say Một, hai, ba, dzô!’ Nice way to end the lunch. 
Definitely recommend this place!!!!
highlights: able to select chilli and garlic to your own comfort level
Nice way to end the lunch

author: Piotr H
title: Best bun cha in Ha Noi
original_content: This is the best meal I’ve had in Viet Nam so far. The meat was tender and flavourful. The soup was rich. Spring rolls were to die for. Highly recommend!
highlights: The meat was tender and flavourful
Spring rolls were to die for

author: Ron Chio
title: Best Bun Cha. Must try!!!!
original_content: They have a restaurant in Hoi An which was amazing. I coincidentally stopped by their restaurant in Hanoi. Absolutely amazing 😋 Ha was so nice and very cheerful. The Bun Cha here is one of the best I’ve had ever. I totally recommend this place. I’ll be coming back for sure.
highlights: Ha was so nice and very cheerful
one of the best I’ve had ever

author: Eric H
title: One of the best meals in Hanoi
original_content: Extremely friendly staff and amazing food! Without a doubt one of my favorite meals I’ve had so far in Vietnam. Bun Cha was super flavorful and the price was fair at 100,000 VND.
practical_tips: go to this place for a fair price

author: Soo
title: not recommend
original_content:
food just so so, nothing feel wow about this bun cha, very pricy and many bloger wrote on them but i think they paid for them. not even a local visit their restaurant, we ordered all their expensive meal which have their bun cha and all type of spring roll, but they dont taste any better than the street food, i really not recommended.

没什么好吃的，食物普普通通，和街边的没什么分别。没本地人吃，都是游客客。和外面的贵2倍，我点的都是些最贵的，没什么特别。每个客人我看他们都吃了两口就跑了。不推荐
drawbacks: don't taste any better than the street food

author: SS2510
title: One of the best meals in Vietnam
original_content: Amazing meal thanks to our food tour. But loved it so much that went back another time. For a vegetarian they were amazingly accommodating. Strongly recommend - choose #1 for meat lovers and #6 for vegetarian (remember to tell them no fish sauce). Thanks Jenny for taking us
practical_tips: choose #1 for meat lovers and #6 for vegetarian
remember to tell them no fish sauce

author: Peter
title: Bun Cha Ta Hanoi
original_content:
It was based on Google reviews that led us to Bun Cha Ta. The staff is friendly and welcomed us with cheerful smiles. The soup is somewhat sweet for my liking but otherwise it is quite delicious. The price is really cheap, Vdn 100,000 to 125,000. I tried several other bun cha better than this and its the reason I would not rank this  as
more than 3 stars. No harm checking it out if you have no idea where to go.
There is another bun cha which the locals called it Bun Cha Obama. That’s because Obama and Anthony Bourdain ate there.
drawbacks: Not as good as other bun cha places
practical_tips: Check it out if you don't know where to go

author: bethiahope
title: Delicious simple food with such kind people
original_content: We were recommended to eat here by our hotel on our first night in Hanoi. It was our first meal in a six week tour of SEAsia and I still Renner how lovely the people were and we really enjoyed the meal. It was delicious, a sweeter broth than expected but that’s what travelling is about. I highly recommend this restaurant. Thank you for being so kind to us as fresh westerners!🙏🏻

author: Sean C
title: Best Bun Cha in Hanoi
original_content: Best Bun Cha we’ve had in Vietnam. Staff are friendly, food was delicious and the vibe was lovely. A must do if you’re in Hanoi.
highlights: Best Bun Cha we’ve had in Vietnam
practical_tips: A must do if you’re in Hanoi

author: Christian
title: Best Bun Cha in town
original_content: Excellent dish, good service, literally, full of food, everything is awesome. Tasty and super yummy, worth to visit. Highly recommend!

author: fal3
title: Delicious!!
original_content:
A great way to try Hanoi’s most famous dish!

The meat was very tasty. I’m not a fan of rice based noodles but I really liked this. Note this place focuses solely on bun cha, and I can imagine the the sweet and sour flavours may not be for everyone. The only complaint was the food wasn’t that hot.

The staff were excellent and spoke English very well. They clearly get a lot of foreign visitors. A true example of great customer service, which is rare in Vietnam these days.
highlights: The staff were excellent and spoke English very well
practical_tips: Note this place focuses solely on bun cha

author: fnarby
title: Excellent quality and service
original_content: Thank you for an excellent meal of Bun Cha this afternoon. The food quality was excellent and our server was wonderful. Thank you for the rice wine to celebrate the new year. I highly recommend this place.

author: TonyM277
title: Worth a visit
original_content: Lovely food, good size servings.  Friendly helpful service.    A variety of options available and positively it was a completely Gluten Free menu which was helpful for some of the family. Appears to be a tourist only establishment
drawbacks: Appears to be a tourist only establishment
practical_tips: Go to a place that is not tourist only

author: CrabisGOOD
title: Linh is awesome! Great bun cha!
original_content:
We randomly chose this restaurant and it did not disappoint. We sat on the second floor and ordered number 1 and number 10. The service is EXCELLENT! Linh is awesome. His English is excellent. He was so helpful. Made suggestions on what to eat and made the experience so great.

We sat on the second and had to take off our shoes, which wasn’t something I liked, but overall it was well decorated with good ambiance.

It is affordable!
drawbacks: had to take off our shoes

author: Bruce2467
title: Yummy Bun Cha!
original_content:
They serve the best bun cha in town. Quick and friendly service!
My family went back 3 times in a week. Can't get enough of how good Bun Cha is!

author: Lou
title: Copious good and pleasant service
original_content:
One of my favorite Bun Cha, I often take the recommended dish (the first one) I make discover it to each person who comes to see me in Vietnam because I find the setting very nice! Go to the floors if you go there.
All the waiters are very pleasant and especially very nice.
I highly recommend it!

author: vivianPham
title: Best Bun Cha in Hanoi
original_content: This restaurant is a must. They get a lot of tours and bookings from influencers for their food popularity. Our family was recommended by a guide book. We went and didn’t leave the restaurant disappointed. The Bun Cha was so delicious and fresh that our family came back the next day to have more of it!
highlights: The Bun Cha was so delicious and fresh

author: llhleon
title: Last dinner of our Hanoi trip
original_content:
Really like this place, which we went to for our last dinner during our Sapa/Hanoi holidays. It's located not far from our hotel in the old quarters. Made a booking via whatsapp which was promptly attended to. Arrived earlier than appointed time but was seated without issues. Service from the young-ish staff was friendly and welcoming.

We ordered the 'full option' plus a seafood springroll. I only remember having bun cha once before on a previous trip to Vietnam, but i certainly don't remember it being this good. When served, we were told how to enjoy the dish. The herbs, and rice vermicelli, the springrolls and BBQ pork sang in unison when dipped in the sauce (primarily fish sauce). Really good.

After the meal, we ordered 'happy drinks' of rice wine whisky. Smelled potent, but thankfully, it did not come close to knocking us out.
highlights: The herbs, and rice vermicelli, the springrolls and BBQ pork sang in unison when dipped in the sauce

author: CCTEXAN08
title: Awesome food
original_content: The food was fresh and flavorful.  Cool seating arrangement, the staff was super polite and friendly.  Highly recommend this location.  Ms. Ha was very friendly and welcoming! So delicious we went back for more!
highlights: staff was super polite and friendly

author: Lindsay N
title: Wonderful experience
original_content: I had a very tasty vegetarian meal here and Jenny who served us was delightfully pleasant and very helpful. An all round great experience.
highlights: Jenny who served us was delightfully pleasant and very helpful

author: Samantha C
title: Great food and excellent service!
original_content: We came here as it was highly recommended by our hotel. Excellent food and the service by Anna was great!

author: Mathilde L
title: Favorite restaurant in Hanoi!
original_content: So delicious I went back 3 times! My favorite Bun Cha in Hanoi. Vegetarian options were just as delicious as meat options. Staff was exceptionally friendly and attentive. Cannot recommend enough!
highlights: Vegetarian options were just as delicious as meat options
Staff was exceptionally friendly and attentive
practical_tips: Go back 3 times for Bun Cha

author: Cat
title: Amazing bun cha!
original_content: I fantastic restaurant to taste Hanoi’s signature cuisine.  Delicious food and wonderful staff. Great for celiacs!

author: Aylin
title: Great
original_content: Anna is super friendly hehe. It was actually my first bun cha and I really enjoyed it. Very nice food, very good service. She gave us some advice for activities. ☺️

author: Nicky S
title: So good!
original_content:
This was our first Bun Cha experience and it did not disappoint. The food was delicious and we loved the spring rolls. Service was great, shout-out to Anna who answered our questions promptly and ensured e had everything we needed.

Thank you!
practical_tips: ask for Anna for good service

author: William munro
title: 21 Nguyen Huu Huan street
original_content: Great traditional very friendly restaurant . Staf were lovely espciallally Anna our server . The food was fresh and delicious as well as reasonably priced . Will definite be back for more.

author: Cheryl Wang
title: Unexpected delicious street food!
original_content: The food is just fantastic and Anna is super nice taught us how to have the spring roll in the right way. Exellent experience!

author: Pien K
title: Lovely restaurant great food and service from Diem
original_content: We had a really good time at this restaurant. The service from Diem was great, she made sure we had everything we wanted. Would totally come back.

author: Sofia M
title: Very good food
original_content: The food is simple and delicious. The waitress super nice. I recommend a visit to the restaurant in Hoi an. ❤️
practical_tips: visit the restaurant in Hoi an

author: Joseph T
title: Absolutely Scrumptious
original_content: If you are looking for good Bun Cha in Hanoi, look no further! Bun Cha Ta Hanoi serves delicious, well-made Bun Cha in an air-conditioned room with attractive decor and friendly staff. We enjoyed the food, the banter and the overall atmosphere of this place and will be coming back next time we visit. At the end of our meal, they even offered us a small shot of local alcohol as a traditional chaser to the dish. Five stars!
practical_tips: go to Bun Cha Ta Hanoi for good Bun Cha in Hanoi

author: Nita
title: Delicious food and lovely staff ^^
original_content:
first time for eat bu cha.
staff name is “diem” explained about food and good service to me.
Bun cha very delicious. !!!

author: Honor E
title: A very popular place for authentic Bun Cha!
original_content: What seems to be a very popular place to eat in Hanoi! Great to experience authentic Bun Cha! The service was 5*, Diem (the girl serving us) was super helpful and attentive…we even got a complimentary sample of their Vietnamese rice whiskey!
highlights: complimentary sample of Vietnamese rice whiskey
practical_tips: go to a popular place to eat in Hanoi

author: Emer
title: Fabulous Food and Staff
original_content: We just ate here this evening and the food was amazing. Our waitress Diem was so helpful and friendly. Such a lovely girl and a lovely place to eat. Very reasonable also. I recommend Bun Bha Ta very much and thank you Diem for great service.

author: Leannie
title: Seems very popular
original_content:
We came here early evening on sundat and were initially concerned we would not get a seat at all the tables were taken, but we were then instructed to follow the waitress up two flights of stairs to the third floor where eventually we found a floor with space!
The menu was varied and I liked the bun cha with spring roll combo with a few cold beers. The only thing that was a little off putting for me was the lady assigned to our floor every time she took an order just stood at the top of the stairs and shouted the orders at the top of her voice to the kitchen - was a little annoying, as well as just standing there by the door watching everyone eat - a little bit off putting! But overall not bad bun cha and nice spring rolls especially the seafood ones.
drawbacks: the lady assigned to our floor every time she took an order just stood at the top of the stairs and shouted the orders at the top of her voice to the kitchen
just standing there by the door watching everyone eat
highlights: bun cha with spring roll combo
nice spring rolls especially the seafood ones

author: Jit Wei K
title: Fantastic food
original_content: The broth was extremely flavourful and the spring rolls were great. The waiter also gave everyone in the restaurant a shot of their house brewed rice wine (on the house of course!) which was a nice touch. Definitely recommended!
highlights: nice touch with house brewed rice wine

author: Claire A
title: Best food in Hanoi
original_content: We found this place after looking at a bunch of reviews on the internet and I can honestly say it was the best meal we had in Vietnam. If you’re in Hanoi this place is a must visit!
highlights: best meal we had in Vietnam
practical_tips: If you’re in Hanoi this place is a must visit!

author: Richard Koh
title: Hanoi Authentic Food in Old Quarter
original_content: Went to this restaurant from a recommendation of our hotel front desk staff.  They serve authentic Vietnamese food, e.g. rice flour noodles, grill pork fried spring roll, grill seafood spring roll etc.and has been open for over a decade. Their service was great, food was good and located at the Old Quarter. The owner, Ms Ha, was very wonderful. A truly recommended restaurant for you!
practical_tips: go to a restaurant recommended by hotel staff

author: kilimama
title: Flavorful local food
original_content:
Excellent local food. The dining area is air-conditioned and very nice. The Bun Cha was delicious. The waiter Kai was so helpful and sweet. We enjoyed him as well.
Don’t miss sampling this local dish in the old Quarter of Hanoi
practical_tips: Don't miss sampling this local dish

author: M&M
title: The BEST Bun Cha in town!
original_content: Without doubt the best Bun Cha i ate in Vietnam. Beautiful little restaurant with super friendly staff. I honestly think this was one of the best meals ive had ever. Absolute must visit and 10/10. Amazing.
highlights: one of the best meals ive had ever

author: Travelove58
title: Cozy, bright & nice decor, friendly service & good food......
original_content:
Street food in a very nice restaurant setting. We sat in a 2nd floor room, very cozy, with beautiful nice decor/ambience. The young man serving us was very enthusiastic & friendly.  Besides guiding us the right way to eat, he sat with us throughout & asked lots of questions.
The food is very good. Worth a visit if in Hanoi
highlights: young man serving us was very enthusiastic & friendly
practical_tips: Worth a visit if in Hanoi

author: Allie Gone Away
title: Excellent, EXCELLENT
original_content:
Such an approachable way to test the street food waters in Hanoi! Delicious, clean, and such quick service. Food was ready in minutes.
Vegetarian options are abundant and delicious!! Ask to sit upstairs for the best experience. 💕
practical_tips: Ask to sit upstairs for the best experience

author: Issy F
title: Bun cha ta-stic
original_content:
Walking away from Bun Cha Ta for the 2nd time in my first week in Vietnam, I can strongly recommend this restaurant to anyone in Hanoi who finds themselves bewildered by the variety of food on offer. Bun Cha Ta is the perfect place to start your journey - quintessentially Vietnamese cuisine with friendly, outgoing service. Khai, our waiter, even explained how to go about eating it! The staff are welcoming, the atmosphere is lovely, the interior (sunken tables and no shoes) immersive, and the food even better! 

***Bun cha is soup with noodles, greens, spring rolls and pork but it is so much greater than the sum of its parts.***
practical_tips: go to Bun Cha Ta for quintessentially Vietnamese cuisine
ask for help from the staff

author: Sean I
title: Good quality of food, clean, polite servers
original_content:
If you are looking for the best restaurants in hanoi, you should come and enjoy :)
The server is really polite, talkative and she speaks english perfectly

author: Keon A
title: Great Food!!
original_content: I had never previously had the specialty Bun Cha Ta and safe to say I was blown away. The pork was really tender. The broth was swimming with flavour and the spring rolls were some of the best I’ve ever had. I would highly recommend coming here for a meal if you get the chance. The staff was also super friendly and attentive.
highlights: The broth was swimming with flavour
The spring rolls were some of the best I’ve ever had
practical_tips: Highly recommend coming here for a meal

author: Ralf M
title: Great place for authentic Bun Cha
original_content: Authentic Bun Cha in Old Quarters Hanoi. Food was fresh and tasty! Staff was very friendly and helpful! Highly recommend!

author: Juan V
title: Best Authentic Experience
original_content: Had a blast eating at this place. The staff is super friendly, and the food was amazing. They teach you how to mix the food together and the flavor just blows your mind. Highly recommend.
highlights: teach you how to mix the food together

author: Sid
title: Excellent and wholesome flavours
original_content:
The only one of two restaurants we came back to twice during our trip to Hanoi. The Bun Cha is excellent and extremely flavourful. A little on the pricier side compared to competitors, however, the portions are hearty. I suggest trying the “Traditional Bun Cha” over the other options on the menu. 

Pros:
1. Very clean and enclosed restaurant.
2. Very flavourful food with hearty portions.
3. Excellent service.

Cons:
1. None that I can think of.
practical_tips: try the 'Traditional Bun Cha' over the other options on the menu

author: Chris M
title: Excellent Local Food and History
original_content: We are a family from the US. The hostess at the restaurant spoke fluent English and was happy to share the history of local cuisine while explaining the menu.  The food was excellent the the price is reasonable.
practical_tips: ask the hostess for menu explanations

author: Silje B
title: Delicious Vietnamese food and authentic experience
original_content: Delicious Vietnamese food and great service! Really recommend for those who want to eat typical local food in a have a more authentic experience.
practical_tips: Recommend for those who want to eat typical local food

author: Harps D
title: The best bun cha in Hanoi!
original_content: The bun cha at this restaurant is absolutely delicious and it's definitely the best I've had in Vietnam! I have already been here 4 times because it was so tasty! The family that run the restaurant are super nice and really helpful! For instance they will tell you how to eat the dish correctly if it's your first time having it.
highlights: The bun cha at this restaurant is absolutely delicious
The family that run the restaurant are super nice and really helpful
practical_tips: Ask the staff for guidance on how to eat the dish correctly

author: agnese A
title: Best Buncha ever and lovely Amy!
original_content:
We found out Buncha Ta by chance, just browsing on the internet for the best Buncha in Hanoi, we couldn’t be more happy with what we found!

The food is amazing, we went there 3 days in a row and I still have cravings for it after 2 weeks back in Singapore! Go for the “Full Set” option to experience the full Buncha package, they also have vegetarian or pork free option that is not so common to find!

Aside the lovely food, Amy and her family’s kidness played a huge part!
Moved by her passion, Amy made sure everything was all right all the time, took her time to explain us how to enjoy at the best our meals and chat with us!

we are very thankful for the beautiful experience that you provided us and we really looking forward to visit you again as soon as possible! Take care Amy :)
highlights: kidness of Amy and her family
practical_tips: Go for the Full Set option

author: Melanie B
title: Go Here!
original_content: It was suggested by our hotel that we go to this location for Bun Cha whereas many go to the one most known since Obama went.  However, this place is truly authentic and feels like such a local experience.  Food was fabulous and the server had good English and couldn't have been friendlier!
extracted_spaces: the one most known since Obama went
highlights: feels like such a local experience
practical_tips: go to this location for Bun Cha

author: Robin1087
title: The best Bun Cha in Hanoi!
original_content: We craved for food and heard Bun Cha is a speciality in Vietnam. So we went to Bun Cha Ta. What an amazing experience. Thor - the restaurant owner - was so friendly and explained a lot about the food in Vietnam and how to eat Bun Cha. She was amazing! The food was incredible too! The broth and the pork were delicious and tasted fresh with all the herbs and rice noodles. We have limited time here in Hà Nội but when I come back I’ll visit this place again! Thanks a lot Thor! ^_^
highlights: Thor - the restaurant owner - was so friendly and explained a lot about the food in Vietnam and how to eat Bun Cha.
The food was incredible too! The broth and the pork were delicious and tasted fresh with all the herbs and rice noodles.
practical_tips: Go to Bun Cha Ta for an amazing experience of Bun Cha, a speciality in Vietnam.

author: Kiah N
title: Yum!
original_content: Delicious meal. The portions are huge, easily shareable. The servers teach you how to eat the dis which was fun. We tried the traditional version as well as the vegetarian option. Both were excellent.

author: TravellerRumi
title: What a find!
original_content: Never judge from the outside! We were sceptical going in as it was empty but it actually became full whilst we were eating. The food here is so authentic and genuine! It seems like a family run cafe/restaurant and they were very friendly to us. I'm coeliac and showed my coealic card so they made my food fresh. Didn't get ill afterwards!

author: Cel
title: Don't be fooled by the lack of people
original_content: I first ate here 2018 and it was PACKED all the time, nowadays it isn't very busy but it's still as AMAZING as before! As most places in Hanoi, this specialized in one thing only.  On this trip alone I ate 3 times (would've gone more if my family wanted something else lol). TBH don't even know what bun cha tastes like at other places because once I try and love something I tend not to try it somewhere else. Parents liked the passion fruit juice but I thought it was too sweet. The lady is also very sweet.
drawbacks: Parents liked the passion fruit juice but I thought it was
highlights: once I try and love something I tend not to try it somewhere else

author: MartinH
title: Excellent Food & Service!
original_content: We went to Bun Cha Ta in early evening hours before the Water Puppet Show. The food was superb. Fresh, authentic local dishes, and very tasty. We each had spring rolls + pork or vegetarian soups with rice noodles and salad. The service was quick and friendly. Would also recommend the egg coffee there. Martin

author: Warren
title: Grilled Pork Rib and Spring Roll Soup at its finest!
original_content: If visiting Hanoi you absolutely must have lunch or dinner at this tiny but fabulous restaurant. And you must order the Bun Cha Ta Full Option. Eat slowly and enjoy immensely!!

author: TOSH22
title: Excellent food and service
original_content:
Most delicious bun cha with unlimited supply of fresh herbs , everything is just right in terms of taste and ambiance. Lovely setting and comfy place and we got to taste the seasonal homemade apricot drink and the owner, Amy, surprise us with a happy drink, Vietnamese whisky that hits the right spot.
Must visit 🤗💜

author: David
title: OK.
original_content:
Visited for dinner in Apr 22. The place focuses on a few menu items, so I went for what I now understand to Bun Cha.

It was pleasantly flavoured but I'm not a big fan of Pho/Noodle soup style dishes, so not something I'd normally go for, were it not for the restaurant's speciality.

Customer service was very good.

A downside was thay they didn't have any coca cola or pepsi zero/diet/light. A shame - all restaurants should stock it a low cal cola abd and they even have it on their menu.
drawbacks: No Coca Cola or Pepsi Zero/Diet/Light available

author: Andrew
title: Bun Cha Ta
original_content:
Came here in the evening to find an empty restaurant. We have to asked is the restaurant opened?

I always feel uneasy with empty restaurant, is it the food is bad or expensive?

To my surprise the food is rather good. The restaurant is empty because locals only eat it for breakfast or lunch & not much of foreigners because the country just opened after 2 years of lockdown due to the pandemic.

The nem or spring rolls are tasty. Meats are BBQ just nice.

Good Bun Cha restaurant in Hanoi.
drawbacks: locals only eat it for breakfast or lunch
practical_tips: go during breakfast or lunch hours

author: Adrian K
title: Absolutely Wonderful!
original_content: My family & I had the pleasure of dining here twice on our Feb 2020 Vietnam vacation and it was our favorite restaurant of our entire trip!  The Bun Cha was absolutely amazing and the best we’ve ever had!  The atmosphere was nice (we had the room on the second floor with about only 6 tables).  We had the same waitress, Thuy, both times and she was simply an amazing person.  She was so nice and took the time to get to know her customers.  We had some great conversation with her and even got to know the people at the table next to us.  The price was a bit more than most places we eat, but it was totally worth it!  We also had a meal at Bun Cha Huang Lien (the famous place where Obama dined with Anthony Bourdain), but Bun Cha Ta has them beat, so if you have the choice, go to Bun Cha Ta instead, you wont’ be disappointed!
drawbacks: price was a bit more than most places we eat
highlights: Bun Cha was absolutely amazing and the best we’ve ever had!
waitress, Thuy, was simply an amazing person
practical_tips: go to Bun Cha Ta instead of Bun Cha Huang Lien

author: ndcoach
title: Very good
original_content: I will start by saying I went to the place our president Obama had lunch today also I will compare the two first of all displays for the exact same meal was 40,000 dong more I would rate the other place at a 9 1/2 and I would rate this place had a solid eight or five stars to 4 1/2 stars for this page I will return here many many times since it’s only a five minute walk from my hotel and the other place is a 25 minute walk from my hotel everything was great I am just doing the solid comparison since I ate at both places in the same day
extracted_spaces: The place our president Obama had lunch
drawbacks: 40,000 dong more for the exact same meal
highlights: only a 5 minute walk from my hotel
practical_tips: go to the other place if you want to save money

author: Lucy
title: Lovely staff.
original_content: After looking up online where was the best place to have Bun Cha we decided to come here, and we were glad we did. Bun Cha wasnt our favourite Vietnamese dish but Bun Cha Ta made it taste good. We found the staff were really friendly and helpful too.
drawbacks: Bun Cha wasnt our favourite Vietnamese dish
highlights: staff were really friendly and helpful

author: Westportone
title: Fantastic local place
original_content: Excellent quality local Vietnamese bun cha. Basic restaurant with high quality food. Bun cha was flavors one and the combo spring rolls (we tried both pork and crab) were some of the best we experienced in Vietnam. Inexpensive for a traditional experience. Only one annoying point was one of the waitresses playing music on her iPhone right behind us.
drawbacks: One of the waitresses playing music on her iPhone right behind us
highlights: Excellent quality local Vietnamese bun cha
Combo spring rolls were some of the best we experienced in Vietnam

author: Rochi7
title: Great place to eat vietnamese food!
original_content:
Food was really good! If you go, go upstairs, it's very quiet :)

People there was really nice, specially Thuy who taught me how to eat what I ordered and recommended me some cool places/restaurants.

author: Brian H
title: Street food at it's best
original_content: A small cafe with a small menu, under ten items on it. The food was  delicious pho based pork or vegetarian noodles with herbs and greens. Started our Hanoi experience here and finished it here too. Well worth a visit.
highlights: delicious pho based pork or vegetarian noodles with herbs and greens

author: Ralf Oliv
title: Very delicious Bun Cha
original_content: The food was delicious. The server named Xuan showed how to eat the Bun Cha at the vietnamese way and how to pronounce the most important vietnamese phrases. I recomend this place to anyone who want to have a special experiance insted of just have a normal dinne
highlights: The server named Xuan showed how to eat the Bun Cha at the vietnamese way and how to pronounce the most important vietnamese phrases
practical_tips: I recomend this place to anyone who want to have a special experiance insted of just have a normal dinne

author: Rachel A
title: Tasty Bun Cha!
original_content:
Tasty Bun Cha with help how to eat if you’ve never had it before. Can get with different types of spring rolls on the size too. 100,000VND for Bun Cha and 2 classic spring rolls. Perfect. 
Went here for the first time on the Hanoi Street food tour and had to go again!
practical_tips: Ask for help on how to eat Bun Cha if you've never had it before

author: Kimberley
title: One word: Disgusting
original_content:
We had time for one final meal in Hanoi after travelling all over Vietnam and enjoying this country's incredible food and ate here after googling the best place in the city for bun cha, our fave dish.

I have no idea why this place has such good reviews - the menu is tiny, the restaurant is small and looks dirty and the food was absolutely disgusting. Our bun cha arrived with stale noodles, broth that smelled like pond water and meat that was squishy and looked like it had gone bad. After this meal we had to take a 16 hour flight back to London where we live and I was absolutely terrified that I was going to spend the entire flight throwing up. The worst meal we had in our entire time in Vietnam, don't eat here!!!
drawbacks: broth that smelled like pond water
meat that was squishy and looked like it had gone bad

author: Cédric Ng
title: So good
original_content:
The food was so good and the staff was kind.
We saw this restaurant on a youtube video and we were no Disappointed

author: Simon0602
title: good food, very affordable and decent seating
original_content: If you want Bun Cha, this was the best we ate in town. Yes you can get a very good option at the roadside for VND45,000 (inc. spring rolls) rather than the VND100,000 you'll pay here but, for me, the herbs were fresh and more varied and you can get a beer to wash it down. It's on the food tour guides route when hosting Europeans but it's not a sterile westerners destination.
practical_tips: Consider visiting roadside options for better value

author: Georgie
title: All round wonderful dining experience
original_content: Delicious spring rolls, fresh herby vegetables, generous serving of fresh noodles, and tasty condiments. Additionally, wonderful service from Thuy, our waitress, who even explained how to eat the bun cha properly. Loved the quaint wooden seating arrangement on mats the second storey.
practical_tips: Ask for Thuy as your waitress for proper guidance on eating bun cha

author: Sandra G
title: Tasty food, great value, 0 customer service
original_content: Great food for a reasonable price. Big portion. Customer service was quite poor. They seated us upstairs which was quite cold. We were the only customers sitting upstairs and the owner was hammering planks of food right next to us whilst we were trying to eat. We ate here because it was close to our hotel and we were quite hungry after a day of travel.
drawbacks: They seated us upstairs which was quite cold
The owner was hammering planks of food right next to us whilst we were trying to eat
highlights: Great food for a reasonable price
practical_tips: Go here if you're close to your hotel and hungry

author: Kristina
title: The best Bun Cha Ta
original_content: The best Bun Cha Ta in Hanoi. I highly recommend! Here you can find very Good price and hight quality!

author: Wendy
title: Best food I’ve had in Vietnam
original_content: Best food I’ve had in Vietnam.  Highly recommend - very tasty and delicious.  Easy to find in the Old Quarter.

author: Linbaba
title: Very good bun cha in a characteristic place
original_content: Not much more to say beyond the title of this review. I really liked it as I liked the idea to share the table with other people. Many tourists but also some locals. I would definitely do it again.
highlights: liked the idea to share the table with other people

author: Ana
title: Great traditional meal
original_content:

Recommended!
practical_tips: try one of our first traditional dishes

author: Ash Cole
title: The best buń chà in Hanoi!!!!
original_content: The best buń chà in Hanoi!!!! Staff are super friendly & helpful. I restaurant is unique & clean. I recommend ordering the tofu in tomato. I’ll definitely be back!

author: Priya G
title: Great food and ambience
original_content: We went to Bun Cha Ta after reading a ton of reviews online and were very excited. Were we satisfied - YES! The second floor has an interesting set-up for seating and we really enjoyed the authentic experience. Our server was friendly and went above & beyond to make a friendly conversation with us. The bun cha was tasty in my opinion. My husband, who is not a fan of bun chas, thoroughly enjoyed his meal!

author: Garden B
title: Not clean area. Not delicious as so many places that I've visit. Don't recommend. Low service quality.
original_content: Not worth visit. Not clean area. Not delicious as so many places that I've visit. Don't recommend. Low service quality.

author: Adventure05703998509
title: Good restaurant
original_content: Good cuisine from Hue, the place is a landmark of locals (the person does not speak English). We recommend it for those who want something authentic.

author: Nargajuna Pillai
title: Beef Noodle with Hue style
original_content: My 1st time try this noodle and it's wasn't dissapoint me. I kinda like the taste of the noodle and also the soup. Especially this contain a pig leg (i guess), look strange but very tasty

author: john
title: Excellent food, good prices, popular restaurant for residents and tourists
original_content:
It's probably my favourite little restaurant in Ha Noi. The Nem Lui is excellent, skewers of meat, served with salad vegetables, pineapple strips, mango strips and noodles and rice paper, so you can make pancakes of the fillings, comes with a peanut dipping sauce.

It can be busy as it is popular, rightly so due to the excellent food and good prices.

author: John74gr
title: Delicious
original_content: Wow, excellent food, really delicious. We had different dishes and surely I don't remember the names of them. The lady serving was so helpful and friendly. I would say the restaurant is a must visit for every visitor

author: Nicole
title: Cheap eat
original_content: Mainly came to this place with friends for the Bun Bo Hue noodle soup. multiple options of spices on the table for anyone to increase the heat on their dish based on preference

author: justinkieu1994
title: Average tasting
original_content:
We went here around 9AM in the morning. They recently changed location so it’s about 3 to 5 mins walk from the old location. 

The Bun Bo Hue was ok. Tasted kinda bland and watery 

But the desert that we got: Che Thai and Che Buoi was amazing. Not too sweet and hit the right spot!

author: PnP Wiz
title: Bun Bo Hue O Xuan - Good and Reasonable Price
original_content: This is a good local restaurant with a Vietnam Central region taste.  It is a local restaurant with a minimal English.  The food is very tasty and good with a Vietnam Central region ingredients. The prices are reasonable, and friendly services.  The restaurant has an average clean, and very crowd in the morning and lunch time.  It also has varieties kind of food from the central region, and so you can try different things.  We went there couples of times, and would definitely come back.  It is also a recommended place to eat if you visit Ha Noi.

author: Benjamin C
title: Good cheap eats
original_content: No English spoken, point and nod works. We just got the special on the front; came with different meats, meatball, a cube, think there was pork and noodles. Very good. 1 bowl is plenty for one person. Many many locals in there, so it must be good!

author: Love2Travel17a
title: good basic food eaten with locals
original_content: Twp people can eat (water + a main dish) for under £5 total.  No English was spoken but we chose from a menu with pictures.  Meat on skewers with rice pancakes & veg especially recommended.  When I tried to leave a small tip, the staff rushed out into the street with my money, thinking I had forgotten it.  Very basic but we liked it
highlights: Meat on skewers with rice pancakes & veg especially recommended
practical_tips: Choose from a menu with pictures

author: juliana74
title: Authentic Local Eating
original_content: First sign that you are eating with the locals is that the wait staff don't speak English. But thank goodness they had a menu with photos. I sort of knew what I wanted (Bun Bo Hue), but was presented with various options. I just took a chance, pointed at one photo and knew I'd get something delicious. And I did! If anything, I wish I could have asked for a bigger bowl of noodles!
practical_tips: Bring a translation guide or use a menu with photos

author: moonlotus18
title: Excellent and affordable local cuisine
original_content:
This restaurant was a great tip from our hotel staff. We made an effort to find it and was not disappointed. The crowd size during lunch time attested to its popularity with the locals. There is upstairs seating which is cooler than the seating downstairs. We ordered a selection of local dishes and loved the noodles, wraps, and even yummy desserts that they have on menu. The waiter showed us how to wrap the spring roll which was really helpful.
We came back a second time as we loved it so much. Don't miss this place during your time in Hanoi.
practical_tips: ask the waiter to show you how to wrap the spring roll

author: Steven S
title: Something different, beef noodle soup
original_content: This is not pho. Good for a change of taste. Beef noodle very similar to pho from the outside, but the soup base is more like tom yum than beef soup. The mix also have beef balls and pork knuckle. The more protein the better I guess. The address has moved from the one marked on Google Maps, so do watch out for it. Location is another part of Hanoi so it's a nice change of pace also.
drawbacks: The address has moved from the one marked on Google Maps
highlights: Beef noodle very similar to pho from the outside, but the soup base is more like tom yum than beef soup
The mix also have beef balls and pork knuckle
practical_tips: do watch out for the new address

author: tmbernong
title: Special noodles with grilled meat, meatball, hardened blood
original_content: Many types of meat, meatballs, one domesticated animal blood cube with mint leaves, vegetables, beansprouts, garlic as garnishes. Staff in blue uniform but bad timing as 2 female staff shouting for very long time arguing which is super annoying!
practical_tips: go early to avoid staff arguing

author: consultantck
title: Delicious noodles and yummy side dishes
original_content:
The main dish offered by this little local eatery is the soupy 'bun' noodles served with:
- meatball
- pig trotter
- a cube of pig blood

The second time I returned, I only asked for meatballs and there were 2 meatballs served with some pork slices which I appreciated far better. 

The side dishes were starchy cakes that were steamed and eaten with a fish sauce concoctions. 

Nice light meal overall
drawbacks: The second time I returned, I only asked for meatballs and there were 2 meatballs served with some pork slices which I appreciated far better.

author: J K
title: Heaven in a bowl
original_content:
Bun bo Hue is easily my favorite Vietnamese dish. And I came to Vietnam with a mission - not just to eat, but to experience a bowl of bun bo Hue. Since I was not going to be visiting Hue, there was no hope of having the real thing at the real place. But my foodie tour guide assured me that this place was the closest thing available in Hanoi. Very authentic, she said, and the lady who owned the shop was from Hue. She apparently had two locations but this was the better one. 

We came here on our last night in Hanoi. I could not leave Vietnam without having this at least once while we were here. The sidewalk was packed with diners on low tables and even lower chairs. This was eating out Vietnamese style. 

We found corner of a long communal table, sat down and ordered right away. Three bowls of bun bo Hue, an order of banh beo, an order of banh ram it. Memories of our earlier food tour came flooding back.

A separate vendor sat at the far end of our table, selling drinks. We got a couple bottles of Hanoi beer to share, along with glasses of ice, because it was an impossibly hot and humid evening. All the same, I was going to have my bowl of steaming hot noodle soup, come hell or high water!

The food was delivered quickly, faster than I would have expected given the size of the crowd that evening. Banh beo came first - steamed rice cakes in little dishes topped with condiments. Pour a little fish sauce over it, scoop it up with a little metal soup spoon. Goes down like oysters (but do remember to chew). Banh ram it were next - little (rice, I believe) crackers with a blob of sticky tapioca starch steamed on, again topped with condiments. Dip in fish sauce and eat.

Finally, the piece de resistance, the stuff of my dreams, my unicorn -- a bowl of bun bo Hue the size of a small wash basin was placed before me. Except the order was messed up. My dining companions had requested no blood cake. I stopped our guide before she could send it back. I would happily have their blood cake. And it was the best blood cake I've ever had, and a generous cube of it too. The noodles were perfectly chewy, the broth delicate yet flavorful. Heaven in a bowl. What happened next was kinda hazy to me. I remember chopsticks flying, sips of beer, mouthfuls of melting beef, a bowl too big to finish. All I knew was that I did not want the experience to end.

I want to note that other places where I've had it, the bun bo Hue broth here was not served spicy. There's a chili paste and other condiments on the table that you are welcome to add yourself. Although I did end up spicing up my soup, I will say that it really wasn't necessary. The soup was full of flavor and well-balanced all on its own. 

Several waiters wearing t-shirts that bore the shop's name milled around, so you could easily tell whose attention to get. I can't really speak to the service, since our guide was with us and did all the ordering (and corrections) in Vietnamese. But they seemed amenable and responsive to her requests. 

Four girls swooped in and grabbed our spot as soon as we stood up. I'm chalking this one up as mission accomplished.
highlights: best blood cake I've ever had
practical_tips: add chili paste for extra spice
