author: kpiddy
title: Park near Hoan Kiem Lake with a historical meaning.
original_content: At the southern end of Hoan Kiem Lake near the Post Office is the small park, Ly Thai To Park, the park gets its name from the large bronze statue in the centre, the Emperor Ly Thai To.  He was the founder of the Ly dynasty of Vietnam from 1009 to 1225, he founded the city of Thang Long in 1010 which in time would be known as Hanoi.  On our first visit to the park on a Sunday evening a marketplace surrounded the park, on another visit the park was being prepared for some sort of event.The park is well placed just away from the noise and rush of the surrounding streets to take a short break.
drawbacks: being prepared for some sort of event
highlights: well placed just away from the noise and rush of the surrounding streets

author: saul g
title: beautiful
original_content: While doin your own "Discover Hanoi Hoan Kiem Lake area) walking/strolling tour , allow yourselves to enjoy this lovely square with the towering statue of Ly Thai To in its center . Not as crowded as the promenade along the lake , but still - many tourists and local are hanging around , willing to talk to you . Great for people-watchin and some action with your cameras .. Only a couple of minutes from the lake , from Tap Hoa Phong Tower and the impressive  Hanoi Municipal People's Committee building .The area is "only pedestrian" on weekends . Hve your cameras ready  .
practical_tips: allow yourselves to enjoy this lovely square

author: shiraziwine
title: weekend Dance area
original_content: This park around the lake is really a peaceful area in Hanoi, very beautiful place for evening or morning walking. in the weekend all sq and streets around were close to the traffic and it was open just for pedestrians. in each corner a group of people were dancing, singing, doing acrobatic things etc. i saw a real happiness there and really enjoyed the weekend in Hanoi style.
practical_tips: walk in the morning or evening

author: iliketomoveandsee
title: Extra bit of park
original_content: Lovely little add-on area of the park to the lake. This area is also a walking zone on a weekend, which makes exploring and wandering around a lot more enjoyable.

author: nellielim
title: Popular recreational area
original_content: Located opposite Hoan Kiem Lake, this is a popular exercise and recreational area for the locals. The park is an ideal place to enjoy some fresh air and relax. A memorial to the first Ly dynasty king stands here.
highlights: ideal place to enjoy some fresh air and relax

author: Bruinman
title: Wonderful place to engage with Hà Nội.
original_content: I'm lucky enough to have the opportunity to visit Hà Nội about every other year, and I always make it  a point if I'm out on a stroll on my own to visit this park. Aesthetically, it's nothing special, but as is common in 23 September Park in Sài Gòn as well, young Vietnamese will often approach foreigners to practice their English. I've met some very warm-hearted people here and had genuinely wonderful cultural exchanges here that have always made my trips to Hà Nội and Viet Nam that much more unique.
practical_tips: visit this park on a stroll on my own

author: John M
title: Good place to people watch in the center of Hanoi.
original_content: This is the recreational space for the people who live here, and a good place to people watch in the center of Hanoi.

author: Rui Li A
title: brings back kampong vibes!
original_content: This place is definitely worth a visit **ON SUNDAYS, only on sundays, the roads will be blocked out for families and people of all ages to be roaming  around the streets - chilling, walking dogs, dancing, singing, playing childhood games. It was an amazing feeling and we were truly heartened.

author: Greg W
title: A lovely public place
original_content: We watched families and young people enjoy this space over the public holiday weekend.  It's in the Old Quarter and part of the lovely walk around the lake.

author: ruthandvern
title: Greatest public space in Hanoi!
original_content: I think this is where this review should be placed. A lot of the pictures depicted the huge vibe of happiness, community, sharing. We walked down our 1st evening in town, a Sunday evening. Almost every few feet there were games, dancing, musicians, children in tiny cars (all together away from others) picnickers, friends and lovers. It just lifted my heart and filled my spirit. I don't recall ever encountering that in a public park. We took 122 pictures and videos as we walked around enjoying each new space we came across.

author: kenl461
title: Ly Thai To Park
original_content: Enroute with our tour group to Hoan Kiem Lake, we past by Ly Thai To Park, with a large statue of its namesake.  If I had paid attention to our guide, I would have learned that Ly Thai To is the 1st King who founded what is known as "Hanoi" today.Good place to see what the locals do in their daily lives & spare time.  A nice break from the hustle, bustle & noise from the city.  Nice & clean.
highlights: Good place to see what the locals do in their daily lives & spare time
A nice break from the hustle, bustle & noise from the city

author: santo t
title: Nice park at the perimeter of Hoan Kiem Lake
original_content: Located in the east side of Hoan Kiem Lake perimeter in the far side perimeter, a small park with a big and tall statue in its centre, Ly Thai To Park with Ly Thai To statue, a memorial to the first king of the Ly dynasty who had moved his seat of power to Hanoi. Nice break after busy walk in Hanoi Old Quarter, locals use this park for their daily exercises, yoga and tai chi, and hang out place for youngsters, free park for everybody. Tourists can relax here while watching how locals spent their leisure times for fun and exercises.
highlights: Nice break after busy walk in Hanoi Old Quarter
Locals use this park for their daily exercises, yoga and tai chi

author: Shi
title: Good to walk around
original_content: We enjoyed walking around the park, mostly saw local youngsters hanging out, some of them skateboarding and displaying some pretty daring stunts. There seems to be tai chi classes held in the park, really good place if you want to observe a bit of local life as it happens. The park was never really crowded during our visits, certainly recommend if you are after a relatively quiet stroll.
highlights: good place to observe local life

author: hannostamm
title: Great spot for people watching
original_content: Dedicated to the founder of Hanoi, the park is popular with locals of all ages. Early in the morning, the elderly come for Tai Chi and dancing, later during the day it is the skate boarders and many students, especially during graduation for the obligatory graduation photo. Bring your camera.
highlights: popular with locals of all ages

author: Xanerin
title: Local History
original_content: What a lovely area just a short walk along the lake.  I think the statue is some famous king but more intriguing was the locals enjoying this space.  Young ones skateboarding and showing off their skills, others exercising - think it was tai chi and older generation just sitting and enjoying the atmosphere.  Beautiful place.
practical_tips: go for a short walk along the lake

author: Esther R
title: History
original_content: Well i am not really know who is he.. but i love to see and hear that he is one of inspirative man in vietnam. Walk about 20 minutes from hotel at hang bong street

author: John S
title: Early morning exercise
original_content: Great place to start your day.Our group came and took part on Laughter yoga, the locals were friendly and welcoming and assisted us in getting it right. Great fun, don't fancy that then there is ballroom dancing nearby or you could join in one of the various aerobic groups that seem to spring up everywhere . A must do place to visit
practical_tips: join in one of the various aerobic groups

author: DAVID L
title: Park by the Lake
original_content: Nice mixture of green space open areas dedicated to a famous Vietnamese king of the same name. It’s a happy place for locals who gather here, for exercise, family outings or just lounging about.

author: rzsz
title: Early morning tai chi
original_content: Come in the early morning (5:30-7) when local people are there doing aerobics, ballroom dancing, tai chi, soccer. We joined in the tai chi and it was an amazing start to the day.
extracted_spaces: local people are there doing aerobics, ballroom dancing, tai chi, soccer
highlights: joined in the tai chi and it was an amazing start to the day

author: Nunngo
title: Lovely park
original_content: You can't miss this park, it is directly opposite Hoan Kiem Lake.  It has a large memorial statue of King Ly Thai To.  It is always crowded with locals, families predominately out enjoying down time and play time with their children.  Locals also use it in the mornings and evenings to gather for group exercise.  It is worth a visit to in the morning and at night, two opposing times of day when the parks use is different and equally as entertaining.
highlights: large memorial statue of King Ly Thai To

author: minimize940314
title: Simple park
original_content: This is a simple park but you can see the statue of the former king ly thai to. The park was named after that king. Ok place to take a rest
extracted_spaces: Statue of the former king Ly Thai To
highlights: Statue of the former king Ly Thai To

author: hueyleng
title: Local atmosphere
original_content: Just opposite the Hoan Kiem lake, you won't miss the giant statue of Ly Thai To in the square. We came here during early morning and it was packed with locals doing exercising there. A few big groups doing aerobics while blasting different work out songs away at the same time. Some were playing soccer in the middle. Some were dancing, and a big group was doing a mixture of warm up while listening to instructions thru the loudspeakers, intermittently they held hands and did funny faces and moaned (uniquely local thing and interesting to watch). This place used by mostly adults turned into a playground for children at night, a completely different view. Worth going both day and night to have a glance on locals' lives.
highlights: watching locals exercising and playing games
practical_tips: go early to see locals exercising
visit both day and night for a different view

author: Philipp H
title: Laid-back, local atmosphere
original_content: The park itself isn't that beautiful. But we went there in the evening and liked the laid-back atmosphere. There was an outdoor photo exhibition on display, which we really enjoyed. Moreover, some Vietnamese ladies were dancing to pop music.
drawbacks: the park itself isn't that beautiful
highlights: some Vietnamese ladies were dancing to pop music

author: d_titzova
title: Hanoi statue Lý Thái Tó
original_content: Statue Lý Thái Tó (974-1028) of first Emperor dynasty Ly is a large bronze sculpture. Was made in 2004, weighs 12 ton and atop a 20 ton pedestal, high 10.10 metres. Monument is located in Indira Gandhi Park (popular by the local people) near Hoan Kim Lake.

author: Llewellyn53
title: The Statue makes it special
original_content: Right next to the lake it makes crossing the road worthwhile. A large open space dominated by a statue but it would have been handy to have a bit more information on display to explain what it was all about. Some rubbish bins would also help reduce the amount of litter
practical_tips: consider bringing rubbish to dispose of

author: New Era
title: For relaxing or moving
original_content: Large outside space for many people go dancing, exercise. Group of friends meeting, family,.... Can come any time.
highlights: large outside space for dancing and exercise

author: G C
title: Monument to Vietnam's famous leader
original_content: The Ly Thai To Park lies close to the shores of Hoan Kiem Lake and memorializes this famous location plus Vietnam's ancient leader :)) The tall, imposing statue is surrounded by a broad plaza of stone tiles, bonsai trees, and fresh flowers... The park is very popular among the city's residents, and you can observe all manner of activities here... ladies exercising in the early morning, children & parents enjoying rented toys, families walking and chatting, performers on the covered outdoor stage, etc... Find a seat and observe everyone enjoying this lovely spot in the heart of the capital city :))

author: F4023NZalbertos
title: Nice small park!
original_content: Just in fron of my favourite place in hanoi! Hoàn kiếm lake! I use to come here if no rain, and stay for many hours! Talking to local peoples and even to many of different countries!
highlights: even to many of different countries

author: kathleensantara
title: Good location and nice
original_content: Located in the center of Hanoi, the front is a sword lake. It is a large square with a big statue. This place is suitable for many sports to come here to enjoy the fresh air, because there are many trees and very wide, especially convenient to travel around the main road.There are also many daily activities, suitable for large groups

author: ironian
title: Good place for a stop on your walk around the lake
original_content: If you are having a stroll around the lake this is a good park to rest your weary feet for a while and watch the locals going about daily life.  It also has an impressive monument of an old King
highlights: watch the locals going about daily life

author: Christian O
title: Local meeting point
original_content: During the Chinese New Year celebrations the Ly Thai To Park was transformed into an amusement park and most impressively a book market. There were 1000s of families walking around and entertaining their kids and shopping books. It was a pleasure to see the locals enjoying themselves, and feeling the atmosphere. There were loads of lights during the evening, which made very colourful.
practical_tips: go during Chinese New Year celebrations

author: TheShis
title: A park with a monument.
original_content: This is a small park next to the lake.The park features a monument to Ly Thai To, the emperor of 1000 years ago or so.

author: Linh B
title: Laughing Yoga in the early morning, young vibe in the evening
original_content: Central located and you will pass by for sure during your stay in Hanoi. Best experience can come in the early morning when you can drop by and join the local group practising Laughing Yoga. During the day it's quite quiet, until late afternoon when it filled up with local families, school kids, young artist group rehearsal, tourist... Nice to grab a glimpse of local life.
highlights: grab a glimpse of local life

author: Diego D
title: Nice place for walking
original_content: This palce is near the lake in the old quarter of Hanoi. It is a nice place where walkimg around with the family. All the area is worth of being visited and walking around the lake.
highlights: all the area is worth of being visited

author: Laurent C
title: Rap danse and Childs joyce
original_content: In the evening there are many dancers of rap.They chain the complex figures and it is great!The children play with bright electric scooters.Rollers are in on this!
highlights: children play with bright electric scooters

author: TWal1
title: Small City Park, Imposing Statue
original_content: This park is home to Ly Thai To's statue, which is a recent addition to Hanoi's historical culture. The park is small and is close to Hoan Kiem Lake. It is worth a visit and is popular with local families. Thanks for your vote if you found this review helpful.

author: DelanA82
title: Park with Monument to Ly Thai To
original_content: Small park close in Hoan Kiem district close to the lake with a statue/monument to Ly Thai To.I went past a few evenings and families with young kids skating, playing and enjoying/relaxing there. It is nicely lit up at night.Good place to see what the locals do outside of work and school.
highlights: families with young kids skating, playing and enjoying/relaxing

author: jeff1955malaysia
title: people relaxing
original_content: it is a small park just off the Hoan Kien Lake. It is by the side of the statue of Ly thai To. You will find people just relaxing, dancing, reading or just resting. it is very greenery and calm. nice place to relax and read a book.
highlights: nice place to relax and read a book

author: Nada O
title: People and families
original_content: This is certainly a place to go if you are interested in seeing how the Vietnamese live in their private time.  Many Vietnamese go to parks as the space in their homes do not usually include a garden - this is the place for kids to run around, dance or play while the parents sip tea with friends on the small stools in the minute tea spots.  A delight over weekends in good weather
highlights: place for kids to run around
practical_tips: go on weekends in good weather

author: Susana D
title: Nice park with monument of Ly Thai To
original_content: A medium-sized park. Best seen at night due to the lighting. Lots of locals with families and kids on weekends. Lots of old bonsai trees.

author: Valerie N
title: If you like to people-watch...
original_content: Stumbled upon this place when chasing pikachu there. Happened upon an open air photo exhibition which was a nice surprise. Gets quite crowded at night when the Ly Thai To statue is lit up and there are people blasting music from speakers, street performers entertaining the crowd, live bands rocking out, vendors along the sidewalk hawking their wares, kids playing jump rope & roller skating, families out for a stroll and couples milling about and having their wedding photos taken.

author: JasonNguyen24
title: Very relaxed
original_content: Going with novntravel.com to visit this Park, after a short walk from the lake, sitting there to enjoy the life of local people. Little children play roller skating. iti is funn

author: jemikanne
title: A green haven
original_content: Visiting the lake area in the middle of a hot Hanoi day is like a breath of fresh air.  You are surrounded by green and feel calmer and cooler because of it.  It is a lovely respite in the middle of a hectic city.
extracted_times: middle of a hot Hanoi day

author: phoenix7389
title: Full of people
original_content: Sometime Hanoi Youth held out door event here, but almost time it's like a community place for skate board-er, Zumba dancer etc...

author: JoeG4D
title: Engage with your Hosts
original_content: Many times we would be approached by young kids or students so that they can practice their English, which is taught in schools as a second language. This is a very busy Place!!! Much going on and a great place to stroll and watch how socially interactive the Vietnamese people are in their daily lives. They use technology, technology does use them. The engage each other more than disengage. You see how Happy they are with doing just that

author: HLalani
title: Midnight Rendevous
original_content: I stumbled into this city Central Park at 1am because I kinda got lost on my way home. At this late time of hour were mostly young couples or groups of friends sitting around chatting. From what I hear a lot of local Vietnamese youth don't get much privacy at home so they congregate in these parks and cafes. None of them were rowdy or anti social at all. Actually really well behaved. It was very peaceful. I finished my beer enjoyed the moment and stumbled on into the night. Oh there is a toilet which I really wanted to use but couldn't figure out the instructions. Doh!
drawbacks: Couldn't figure out the instructions for the toilet

author: Daniel_lawgg
title: A place popular for locals and tourists
original_content: This is a popular place for locals and tourists alike. Locals like to exercise around the park and offers tourists a glimpse of the their daily life.

author: Rainie Green
title: Good place for having a nice rest
original_content: We were very surprised at a lot of park in Ha Noi. We are from Ho Chi Minh City which is full of pp, not many park for citizen wlking around, holding activities like this. We appriciate this place.

author: bronvoyage
title: Fun atmosphere
original_content: go there at 6am.  I joined in the Zumba, Laughter Yoga and watched plenty of other dances.  Really great fun way to wake up to the day in Hanoi and very enjoyable to see locals out dancing wearing lovely clothes and dancing as couples and women dancing with their hats. I enjoyed it so much I did it twice, no point sleeping in on holidays.
highlights: watching locals dancing wearing lovely clothes

author: Melvin M
title: Best time is in the evening
original_content: The best time to come to the park is in the evening when the statue commemorating the hero of Vietnam's Lý dynasty is lit up to its full glory. It was a quiet and rainy evening when we were there, but it is just a stone's throw to the Hoan Kiem lake, so definitely a place to stroll around a little on the way to the old quarters.
highlights: statue commemorating the hero of Vietnam's Lý dynasty
practical_tips: stroll around Hoan Kiem lake on the way to the old quarters

author: EarlyRetirementAbroad
title: Wonderful park
original_content: One of the favorite parks is Ly Thai To Park.  This is a place where families come together to enjoy live music, kids play sports, and newlyweds getting ready for the photo shots.

author: pagoda2014
title: Grab some atmosphere
original_content: Go there on a Saturday -may see wedding couples being photographed, people exercising, even dancing. Right by the lake so take a detour while walking around -do some people watching. Sometimes concerts here also.
practical_tips: take a detour while walking around

author: Trypp Adams
title: Festivals, open area... a place to celebrate
original_content: While I was in Hanoi, Ly Thai To Park hosted events... there was music, dancing, and just a general party most times I walked by and it seemed to cater to the locals. If you are walking around the lake, it's hard to miss the park, worth a stroll through if you have a little extra time.
practical_tips: worth a stroll through if you have a little extra time

author: LG_Kay
title: Just a local park
original_content: Located just across the Hoan Kiem Lake, the commanding statue of Ly Thai To stands out in the park. It is an open space area for locals to gather here, be it relaxing, dancing, exercising etc. Though nothing spectacular, it is a good place to hang around to take a break or observe the locals in their daily activities.
highlights: observe the locals in their daily activities

author: hikkaduwa_10
title: Nice area
original_content: good to walk around and sit on the benches, very close to Hoan Kiem lake and the whole territory of Old Quarter

author: diploconcierge
title: Large, paved park next to Hoan Kiem Lake
original_content: At most any time of day, you can find people hanging out in Ly Thai To Park, adjacent to Hoan Kiem Lake.  In the early mornings, I hear you might find a group of Hanoians practising laughing yoga.  In the afternoons, especially on a weekend, you might find many kids running around.  The park could be a stop on a stroll from the Metropole to Hoan Kiem Lake or vice versa.
practical_tips: stop on a stroll from the Metropole to Hoan Kiem Lake or vice versa

author: Paulsphotos
title: Amidst all the tourists, this is the place for local children to play - a real joy to sit and watch.
original_content: Much of the week this urban space is largely empty and of little interest to the visitor. However, after school time and at the weekends, particularly on Sunday afternoon, it fills with the laughs of the colourfully dressed children - roller blading, scooting, cycling, chasing bubbles, etc. You just need to sit, relax and enjoy the fun.
highlights: laughs of the colourfully dressed children
practical_tips: sit, relax and enjoy the fun

author: Agathe F
title: Park with children activities
original_content: If you have child it worth going. There is a place where your children can go play. There is a play ground. There is also a cafe
practical_tips: go if you have a child

author: Jel86
title: Just next to the Hoan Kiem lake, with big Ly Thai To statute
original_content: Just next to the Hoan Kiem lake, with big Ly Thai To statute. Read your guidebook for the part of history. Nice stone flooring. Skaeboarders squat the space, along with women exercising early in the morning and at night on load dance music.
drawbacks: women exercising early in the morning and at night on load dance music
practical_tips: Read your guidebook for the part of history

author: travelnomadNZ
title: Relaxing Environment
original_content: Pleasant surprise. Great use of open space in the middle of a bustling city of Hanoi with 10.9 million people . Can be used as a playground , tai chi classes and much more. Architectural design has made it user friendly for more than two activities at the same time without conflict.Tip : popular with both locals and tourists. Sunset is a good time to be here . Try and avoid the big crowds
highlights: user friendly for more than two activities at the same time
popular with both locals and tourists
practical_tips: try and avoid the big crowds

author: Trường N
title: Great exercise place for the locals
original_content: Many locals takes it as the playground for Taichi, football, biking even though it is little bit small. they know well how to give space to each other. It is crowded at every weekend.
highlights: know well how to give space to each other

author: Bolt T
title: Beautiful at Night!
original_content: A walk around Hoan Kiem Lake and a stop at Ly Thai To Park are a great way to spend an inexpensive night out in Hanoi. Everything was beautifully lit and there were friendly people everywhere.

author: Maria Paalman
title: Bustling children's playground
original_content: Visit this little ground, just off Hoan Kiem Lake, in the (early) evening, when many parents take their small kids here to play, skate, dive around in toy cars etc., while the imposing statue of Ly Thai To is overlooking the action and the whole place is lit up with fancy lighting. Fun to watch. You might also see a group of (mostly) women doing their aerobic exercises on the rhytms of a blaster turned up very loud.
highlights: imposing statue of Ly Thai To

author: sain21
title: My favorite place
original_content: You should  visit the place with kids.They can see the dance practicing teenagers,skating  .You will the culture of Hanoi.Really enjoyable place....

author: Jack E
title: Brilliant hussle and bustle escapism spot
original_content: This is the perfect spot at Hoan Kiem Lake to relax and take in the views and the performing locals. Great to escape here from all of the busy streets and the 2.5 million motorbikes. Some bench seats are available but as in all other Vietnamese localities there are not many (they don't want you congregate). It won't be too long before tourists will have to queue to get a seat on one of the benches to rest their tired feet and limbs.Great spot after dark.
drawbacks: queue to get a seat on one of the benches

author: VNvet2015
title: You're going to go by this park anyway
original_content: so cross the street from Hoan Kiem lake and do some people-watching of Vietnamese rather than more tourists. The end nearest the lake is where kids learn to rollerblade and families gather to let the kids loose, while other end of the park is usually pretty empty and offers places to sit more quietly. I always enjoy walking through the park when I am coming from or going to streets to the east of the lake. Heading east from the lake you will come out very near the Metropole hotel and a short walk to the Opera House, so the park is convenient to many places of interest. It's not an oasis like the former Lenin park, but it is a change of pace from traffic and shopping.
highlights: change of pace from traffic and shopping
practical_tips: go to the end nearest the lake for kids' activities
head east from the lake for convenient access to other places of interest

author: ekeat79
title: Nice place for a walk
original_content: This park is not exactly a green lung per se, but it consists of a wide cemented space surrounded by colorful flower beds. This park provides ample space for the locals to carry out healthy activities such as tai-chi, jogging, skating, etc. The main landmark in this park is a large bronze statue of Ly Thai To, i.e. former Emperor of ancient Vietnam. A nice place for a walk, especially in the morning or evening.
practical_tips: go in the morning or evening

author: seedhunter
title: Very interesting all the time
original_content: Located near Hoan-Kiem Lake, "Ly Thai To Park" is veri live place in the city. In the morning joggers and walkers and in evening cyclist, earobics and many more activities to chill out. Be careful with your bags and valuables.
drawbacks: Be careful with your bags and valuables
highlights: veri live place in the city
many more activities to chill out
practical_tips: Be careful with your bags and valuables

author: Puppy
title: Right next to the lake of the restored sword
original_content: The park has a massive bronze statue of Ly Thai To (founder and first king of the Ly Dynasty) which dominates the entrance, he reigned from 1009 to 1028 AD. It was he who moved the capital to Hà Nội in 1010. The park is not big but is often home to roller skaters and youngsters having fun.
highlights: massive bronze statue of Ly Thai To
roller skaters and youngsters having fun

author: Rich M
title: great for early morning people watching
original_content: To see everyday life in Hanoi, get up early (5:30 - 6:30) and walk around the lake.  Many people exercising, dancing, meditating, lifting weights, jogging, playing games, etc.  Very interesting and fun.

author: Chris101111
title: Entertainment
original_content: Fabulous park to watch the locals going about their everyday lives, early morning it's tai chi or badminton and it's fun to watch.I would recommend you come down early and see it.
highlights: watch the locals going about their everyday lives

author: Vu D
title: Local entertainment
original_content: Facing the Hoan Kiem Lake, this park is a popular place for local people, especially by late night with street dance, cycling, aerobic and even taichi etc. Relax environment and chance to see local life.
practical_tips: go by late night for street dance, cycling, aerobic, and taichi

author: Noisrucxe
title: 【 Morning Gymnastics 】
original_content: "Ly Thai To Park" is located near Hoan-Kiem Lake.This park was built by French colonial government in 1887.You should visit this park in early morning time!Because many people are doing gymnastics at this park.You may be able to know Vietnamese-healthy lifestyle.I recommend this experience.

author: MichaelLau3000
title: Monument of King Le Thai To
original_content: Notice this Monument located near Ly Thai To Park & Hoan Kiem Lake area.It provide some historical background on the national hero Le Loi, the Golden Turtle, The Returned Sword & King Le Thai To.Details are scribbled on the rock in few languages.

author: nObOdY007
title: Great Park Next To The Lake
original_content: Located In Front Of HOAN KIEM Lake, This Park Is Such A Wonderful Place For Relaxing. At The Night Time, Lots Of People Are Gathering And Doing Some Activities. If You're Tired, Just Walk A Fews Minute And You Will Find The Restaurant For Chilling, Having Hanoi Beer And Great Foods.A Must Visit Place.
practical_tips: Walk A Fews Minute And You Will Find The Restaurant For Chilling

author: chavi2015
title: My daughters favourite place
original_content: This is the favourite place of my daughter as in the evening its crowded with the kids and youngesters practising skates and dancing..Sometimes they organize their cultural programme.So you can get to know vietnamese lifestyle.missing....

author: G C
title: Nice park just across the street from Hoan Kiem Lake
original_content: The Ly Thai To Park honors one of Viet Nam's famous leaders, who ruled a thousand years ago.  There are two broad, stone-paved plazas in front and behind his statue that are really popular places with the locals for their outdoor activities... Be sure to check out the shaded paths behind the Emperor and the large open gazebo (with classic Vietnamese architecture, of course -- nice spot for a photo)... there are plenty of benches to sit and rest.  When the paths along the Hoan Kiem Lake get busy, I just head across the road to this nice park... There are also several carnivals with rides for small children nearby (these seem to operate during holidays?)  Beautiful flowers adorn this place of honor as well, and it's a frequently used location for wedding photos.  Enjoy Ly Thai To Park as I do :))
practical_tips: head across the road to this nice park when the paths get busy

author: Erica W
title: Fun for kids
original_content: Rollerskates for rent in front of the statue.  Behind the park in the next block on the left is Hanoi Children Center they have some carouselles and other simple rides for small children. 15-20 K each. Seems to start around 4-5pm  Fun for an hour or so.

author: MsAnnHanoi
title: Small park for rest.
original_content: Statue of King Ly Thai To is located at Ly Thai To park in Dinh Tien Hoang Street, Hoan Kiem District, Hanoi center. Today, Ly Thai To park is a cultural and architectural beauty.In order to honor of King Ly Thai To, in February, 2004 the Department of Information Hanoi Culture organized a competition design King Ly Thai To statue. After that the statue of King Ly Thai To is located at Ly Thai To park.Monument at Ly Thai To park is one of the main cultural projects to celebrate 50 years of liberation of the capital (10/10/1954 – 10/10/2004), and to celebrate 1000 years of Thang Long – Hanoi (1010 – 2010).

author: Leo D
title: special park
original_content: it os a place where every people can come to take a rest as well as enjoy the beauty of Hoan Kiem lake. opposite to Hoan Kiem lake, Ly Thai To park is quite large, airy atmosphere for you to relax. you also cannot ignore the big statue in this park - is of king Ly Thai To who removed the capital of Vietnam from Ninh Binh to Hanoi.
practical_tips: enjoy the beauty of Hoan Kiem lake

author: pinoytraveller2

highlights: We were all alone and no other soul was around

author: BeeJhoii
title: Park

author: konshoe
title: A park opposite of Hoan Kiem Lake
original_content: On our tour around the lake, we spotted this park tucked across the street facing the lake, a square with a majestic statue. Crossing the infamously unruly traffic of Vietnam, we reached Lý Thái Tổ garden,Standing tall and lonely in the middle of the square, the statue held a scroll on his right, suggesting his relationship to scholarly wisdom. And reading his biography during my research for this entry, I was enlightened to his significance and importance to Hanoi in particular, so much so that a statue was erected near to a famous landmark.The statue would get its companions in the form of camera toting tourists and strolling locals. An occasional couple or family would stop by the square to enjoy the spacious ground, a luxury hard to come by in the city center of Hanoi. Twirls of smoke wafted from the bowl of incense holder placed at the foot of the majestic emperor, fluttering to nothing as the wind blow past.

author: SteveJacksonnufc
title: Hanoi - Ly Thai To Park - What a great place for local people
original_content: We were leaving the Hoan Kiem Lake area and heading towards the history museum and passed straight through this park. What a delight it is. It was early evening and the sun was falling but the place was full of local Vietnamese people either dancing, playing games or just generally out with their families enjoying the open space the park has to offer. It is mainly covered in slabs giving a polished flat surface with a few steps in places but it was great to people watch for a while. The kids were loving it and the dancing was superb, even if it was a little dated. I could have sat for an hour or so and watch everyone having a great time. There was no sign of any hassle or trouble and everyone got on brilliantly. At the far end of the park is an impressive statue of Ly Thai To which overlooks everything that is going on. This place was refreshing and an insight into how the locals spend some of their evenings and leisure time.
highlights: local Vietnamese people dancing, playing games, or enjoying the open space

author: Chris101111

author: ChrisMcLaren
title: Stunning views and well worth it.
original_content: How this doesn’t rate in the top 20 “things to do in Hanoi “ is surprising. It has Stunning views, very modern facilities, fun activities and lots of seating just to soak up the 360 degree view. Reasonable pricing (we opted for the drink at the top option). Free of charge high strength binoculars (and we found our hotel). Shops selling drinks , food and tourist options on the level. Our day wasn’t the best viewing day but the nice lady did preview what we would see from her phone before purchasing the tickets. The lift up the 65 th floor was flawless and the 2 see through glass bottom floors were exhilarating and gave me shivers.  worth the visit. Chris (Melbourne) 🇦🇺

author: KEVIN MICHEAL D... G
title: AY, SO WORTH IT! THE WEEKEND DEAL! 🤩
original_content: Grabe, the entrance fee is 230K VND, but we snagged the weekend package for 280K VND which already includes a refreshing drink—sulit much! Taking that high-speed elevator to the 65th floor felt like flying straight to the clouds. Seeing Hanoi at night? Bongga! The whole city below looked like a massive, glittering carpet of tangled lights. The cars moving along the crowded roads, the jumbled bahay (houses), and ponds—it was surreal, like we were floating above a complex, breathing organism. Standing on the glass floor with no shoes on was truly nakakapraning (nerve-wracking), but the view of the hustle and bustle from way up there is just unforgettable!
drawbacks: No shoes allowed on glass floor
practical_tips: Buy weekend package for better value

author: Chris S

author: A W
title: WOW! Hidden Gem
original_content: What a lovely experience. No crowds or waiting.  2 glass platforms on either side of the building for you to experience floating on air above the city.  Plenty of viewing binoculars and we also did a mission X VR game and Hanoi VR gliding which was hilarious with the family shooting ghosts in a castle and then gliding above city sights. You can stroll around the entire 360° area of the building. Afterwards we enjoyed a cool drink at bar. Clean tidy and staff were attentive.

author: simonin78

author: Edokko
title: The tallest observation deck in Hanoi?
original_content: Visit on July 9, 2025.Since it is the tallest building in Hanoi with 65 floors, I climbed to its observation floor. The entrance is on the basement floor, pay 230K VND and take the high-speed elevator to the 65th floor! I visited in the evening, so I could even enjoy the night view. Hanoi, seen from above, was a mix of high-rise buildings, jumbled areas and ponds, with car lights illuminating the crowded road conditions. There is a glass floor where you can stand without shoes. Even though I knew I was fine, it still made my liver cool!

author: johnmichaelo954
title: How to access lotte Skyview observation deck
original_content: This 65th floor viewing deck gives amazing outlook over Hanoi. It is a hidden gem and hard to find good info on. So here goes. The mall is a Vietnam one rather than straight tourist trap. English is not a given. The process to gain access to the sky deck is:Go into the mall and ignore the lifts. You must use the escalator to go down to level B1. This will get you to the supermarket (which is worth a trot round), but leave it via its front entrance. This is done by turning right off the escalator. Then pass food vendors, this is Vietnam after all, in front of you is the up escalator but looking right you will see the neon tunnel entrance. The guy you first sees is a greeter who just points you at the ticket booth. Price is 230000d, and for a little extra, you can add a drink. Go through the turnstiles and onto the actual lift to get to the 65th  floor. Super fast and ear popping!Time your visit with the sunset and take as many photos as you can. The glass floor sections are good for those with the stomach for it. There is a couple of bars up there and is well air conditioned. This is a great stop off the beaten track and should  not be missed!
drawbacks: hard to find good info on
practical_tips: time your visit with the sunset
add a drink for a little extra

author: Mirjam G
title: Beautiful view
original_content: Unfortunately it was cloudy and therefore probably not crowded.We went to do the VR Hanoi Gliding and came out sick (this has been warned in advance)The price included another VR thing but it was broken.We took some pictures and then left. Price quality is fine. It's a shame it's so atmospheric.
drawbacks: price included another VR thing but it was broken

author: Dark C
title: Don't Miss This on Your Visit to Hanoi!
original_content: For some reason, the Lotte Skydeck never showed up in ANY of the "top attractions" websites/blogs we looked at when researching our trip to Hanoi.  It was a bit of happenstance that we learned of it, but once we did, we booked a Grab to get there right away (about a 20 minute ride from the Old Quarter). Similar, but higher than the Bitexco Tower in Saigon (65th floor vs. 49th), it also has an enclosed 360° view, with refreshments and souvenirs available at the top. And admission is about the same price. Unlike Bitexco,  however, the Lotte Skydeck features two large glass floor sections you walk onto and see the entire 65 floors right beneath your feet! We enjoyed both towers, and are glad we discovered the Lotte Skydeck.
practical_tips: book a Grab to get there
admission is about the same price as Bitexco Tower

author: NotTheLastJedi

original_content: I really enjoyed spending some time at the Lotte Observation Deck. Hanoi is a beautiful city particularly to observe from sky high vantage point. They have interesting art and extra experiences such as virtual gliding and games, and a robot trolley delivers drinks.  There's a large supermarket and posh shopping on the ground floor of the complex.

author: Wikumj
title: Expensive but worth it
original_content: This is the best place for views over Hanoi. It is quite expensive to go up relative to Vietnam prices, but once you are up there there is quite a lot to do up there and you could easily spend an hour or two up there if you wanted to. Firstly there are the various view points with some interesting gimmicks - the glass floor, the big heart, the angel wings, which all make for some memorable photos. Then then there are various other things to do, VR rides, and art gallery, small exhibitions, a cafe and bar etc. So it is a comfortable place to spend some time. It is open til late so recommend coming in the evening to catch both the sunset and the city lights at night.

author: LackyTravels

drawbacks: light reflections can be seen everywhere

author: Herbert C
title: Mediocre elevating experience!
original_content: All cities must have one, and South Korean conglomerate Lotte has ensured that Hanoi gets its observation deck. The building itself is not particularly impressive, nor is the relatively mild height of 267m and entrance fees of VND230,000. But Lotte’s attempt to make up for these is by offering visitors an acrophobic experience and unique photo opportunity with 2 heart-dropping glass platforms 65 floors above street level. The night view is just mediocre and unlike other observation decks where night photos can be taken if you place your phone against the glass, this is disappointingly impossible here, possibly due to the thickness and angle of the glass.

author: Liron

author: K W T
title: See the Whole of Hanoi from the Top
original_content: Although it was a bit cloudy, we could still see the whole of Hanoi from the Observation Deck. for VND230,000 per person, it is worth it. There are also many seats available from the several food outlets, allowing visitors to enjoy the beautiful scenery.  There are also 2 glass decks to take photographs but as usual i am afraid of heights, staying clear of that area!!! author: Ev_kka

author: Elizabeth Q
title: Wonderful Experience
original_content: You buy your ticket from the kiosk on the ground floor, accessible by escalator or lift. I was asked to go through an airport-type security test before entering the lift to the Observation Desk. The lift rises rapidly but the lights go out, so if your suffer from claustrophobia don't attempt this. The views from the deck are stunning and you can take as many photos as you wish; there is an area with a glass floor that you can stand on but don't attempt this if you suffer even slightly from vertigo. There are information points all around the deck. There are plenty of places selling food and drink and nice clean loos. The returning lift takes you to the Lotte Supermarket.
practical_tips: don't attempt lift if you suffer from claustrophobia or vertigo

author: Denis Mark

author: Hanzen

original_content: The observation deck is worth a visit, if for nothing else, but the restaurant. The view is great and it's a very nice are of Ho Chi Minh City. The shopping center is also fun with a large restaurant area and an ice rink.

author: hander22
title: Dont go at night
original_content: The view is really not that great at night because some idiot decided to put a lot of lights in to the floor so you get reflections. Also alot ot annoying chinese people, and the windows are dirty.
drawbacks: some idiot decided to put a lot of lights in to the floor so you get reflections

author: Adam_Bang
title: Reasonable value for money if you have some time to kill in Hanoi
original_content: Good attraction to see the skyline (not impressive though) of Hanoi. Highly advisable to go at around 4:30 pm, you'll have a chance to see the city both during the day and during the night
highlights: see the city both during the day and during the night

author: Judit R
title: One of the must-ones in Hanoi
original_content: The observation tower was clean and air-conditioned which was amazing in the hot weather. There were friendly and helpful staff and the tower itself was themed beautifully. The decorations were coordinated really well to maximise photo opportunities. Also, the interactive photo displays  gave a great brief history of the historical places visible on the sky line. Perfect spot.

author: Johan H
title: I must do when u visiting Hanoi
original_content: The building are incredible and contains everything u can imagine. I will especially recommend a visit to the observation-deck located at 65 floor with a 360^ view over Hanoi. Totally worth a visit 👌🏼

author: Deepak DB
title: Sky (walk) High
original_content: Located on the 65th floor of Lotte Centre offeres panoramic view of Hanoi. Added to the attraction is the Glass floor sky deck which could be a nightmare for those with fear of heights.This attraction requires you to buy tickets online or at their basement tickets counter. There are offers during specific time of the day and or also for certain age groups. Not sure if it applies to locals or all. Since we landed there at a very short notice we couldn't opt for any. Add to this it was very cloudy evening hence we missed on getting better views but we were happy to see the cloud rush.One can take a picture with professional cameras which are printed and presented in paper frames. There is a 10% odd discount coupon which comes with the entry ticket.Also available there is a bar and restaurant in case you would like to spend more time enjoying the view.The deck is very popular with all hence plan you visit well to avoid crowds which is likely in evenings and weekend.Must Visit!!Please Note: One needs to take off the foot wear when stepping on the sky deck. Socks, stockings, etc are allowed
drawbacks: nightmare for those with fear of heights
missed on getting better views due to cloudy evening
practical_tips: buy tickets online or at their basement tickets counter
plan your visit well to avoid crowds
take off footwear when stepping on the sky deck

author: murielcsmith
title: Looking down on Hanoi
original_content: The tower was recommended to us and we were not disappointed, We bought tickets on the day which were quite cheap and zoomed up to the 65th floor in the lift. It was a quiet day so plenty of time to take advantage of the very clear 360 degree views. We took a few photos ourselves but there was a photographer there taking photos if required. We were lucky in that it was a clear bright day and the views were quite spectacular. Overall, good value for money but don't expect to spend too long in there.
practical_tips: don't expect to spend too long in there

author: k2711
title: Glass floor
original_content: Amazing 360 view of hanoi, 2 different glass floor observation decks, well worth a visit, cheaper prices for an hour in morning or night too.
practical_tips: cheaper prices for an hour in morning or night

author: Indonesian-Jetset
title: See Hanoi from the sky
original_content: Very nice place to visit on the 65 th floor of Lotte Hotel.Do not for get to go to Top Of Hanoi for some nice roof top drink.
practical_tips: go to Top Of Hanoi for some nice roof top drink

author: Michelle B
title: Worth the ride up
original_content: We bought one of the package ticket deals offered for admission plus beer, pizza and chicken karage, and were happy with that decision. The pizza was good, the karage was delicious, and the beer was fantastic to enjoy with the corner view in the Observation Deck's bar and lounge. They had great photo opportunities all the way around the deck, and fun, interactive experiences. The Lotteria there is a much nicer one than the one in the basement - which I wish I had known earlier. There's also a lovely little ice cream stand that offers uniquely Vietnamese flavors. The Observation Deck is a great to place to go for a whole new perspective on Hanoi. Just prepare yourself to do a lot of waiting for other tourists to give you a chance to take advantage of the photo ops - not all of them were terribly conscious of other people waiting their turn.
drawbacks: lot of waiting for other tourists
not all of them were terribly conscious of other people waiting their turn
practical_tips: prepare yourself to do a lot of waiting
go early to take advantage of photo ops

author: souLondon_england
title: A 360 degree view of the whole city.
original_content: A fantastic place to visit for all. Have your photograph professionally taken standing on the glass floor overlooking the city. We stayed up there until it got dark and the lights all came on. You have full 360 degree views of every part of the city by walking around the 64th floor of this 272 M high building. We caught a taxi there but be careful not to be ripped off and agree the fare 1st. Or get your hotel to book a “ grab” taxi. Only cost us 61,000 d one way from the Old Quarter.
drawbacks: be careful not to be ripped off
highlights: full 360 degree views of every part of the city
practical_tips: get your hotel to book a “ grab” taxi

author: Amy Lopez
title: A good spot to stand
original_content: Although I am not a fan of its price tag, I am happy that I tried. It is not scary to be here as it is sturdy enough with no incidents I suppose. Hanoi isn't small but I does look small and lovelier from this point of view.
highlights: lovelier from this point of view

author: Jochips
title: Great views - well worth the entrance fee!
original_content: Fantastic views of the whole city - we went about 4pm and it was beautiful and pretty quiet. Glass floors for you to stand on for some awesome photos - and the heart in the glass wall shown in all the promotional material.

author: Faith Thong
title: Quick view of Hanoi City from 272m high
original_content: Well this is slightly a bit more expensive but if you wish to see the entire city of Hanoi from above you can come here . You can purchase the ticket on B1 floor and there a lift than bring you up to 65th floor of this building . Inside there some cafe or lounge where you can buy drink and chill while overlooking the city of Hanoi
highlights: see the entire city of Hanoi from above
practical_tips: purchase the ticket on B1 floor

author: grimsbygirlusa
title: birds eye view
original_content: Great place to visit to see over the city old and new.A little difficult to find . Go to floor B1 to buy the tickets to go up to the top.  Amazing views. Some insta. Photo ops.
practical_tips: Go to floor B1 to buy the tickets

author: Laura B
title: Great View of Hanoi
original_content: We went aaround 5pm to get a glimpse of the sunset.  Not crowded and easy to find. Great view of Hanoi from 65 floors up.Is a bit out of the way from central tourist spots. A cab takes 20mins from St Josephs.
drawbacks: A bit out of the way from central tourist spots
practical_tips: Take a cab from St Josephs

author: marwammh
title: Hanoi from the Top
original_content: We went to Lotte Observation Deck, and we enjoyed the view of Hanoi from the top.You can spend around 2 - 3 hours, and they have Lotte burger, some other cafes.
highlights: enjoyed the view of Hanoi from the top
practical_tips: they have Lotte burger, some other cafes

author: Peter H
title: a must visit
original_content: We had heard about this place so got a taxi to here...great view of Hanoi...get your photo taken on the glass floor by a professional photographer...scary if you don't like hights.
drawbacks: scary if you don't like heights
highlights: get your photo taken on the glass floor

author: Adrian Lee
title: Mr. Adrian Lee
original_content: Grateful & Thankful To have the opportunity to experience the Lotte Observation Deck in Hanoi. Situated on the 65th floor, 253 meter, 830ft high. Amazed and mesmerized by the design and architecture of the tower deck with its 3D design lift that brought us up there. At the 65th floor were able to view the whole beautiful city of Hanoi and its nature. Love the place and the ambience of Fine Dine restaurant and cafes over at this floor ☺️
highlights: amazed and mesmerized by the design and architecture
view the whole beautiful city of Hanoi and its nature
love the place and the ambience

author: andrewlofnes
title: Fun Activity for an hour
original_content: Great views from the top and a decent way to spend some time in Hanoi which has very few activities otherwise. Don’t bother with the shopping centre unless you’ve got a fair bit of cash to spend.
drawbacks: Don't bother with the shopping centre unless you've got a fair bit of cash to spend
practical_tips: Don't bother with the shopping centre unless you've got a fair bit of cash to spend

author: _vco_mcivor
title: Superb view and service
original_content: Go to the top of the hotel (roof lounge) and save the cost of the observation deck.  You will find yourself on the roof with stunning views (great at night) and a bar that serves good food and drinks, if pricey by Ha Noi standards.  Would be among my top 5 of things to in Ha Noi, along with Water Puppet Theatre, three museums and wandering and eating in the old quarter.
practical_tips: go to the top of the hotel (roof lounge) and save the cost of the observation deck

author: Lucia.xiii
title: the whole view of hanoi
original_content: I mean you should go there, definitely by night to see the nightlife of hanoi through the see through glass here but the entrance ticket is not that affordable.

author: Silvia U
title: Great City Perspective
original_content: You can really get a sense of the city from the observation deck. It is bigger and more spread out than I thought.
highlights: get a sense of the city

author: Tiffany
title: Best views of Hanoi!!
original_content: This is something that anyone visiting Hanoi must absolutely do. Whilst quite pricey, it is a once in a lifetime experience and really enjoyable. My boyfriend and I only found out about this 2 days before we were leaving, but we found a way to slot it into our itinerary and we are so glad we did.We got to go up 65 storeys into the sky. Whilst we went on a gloomy and cloudy day, the views were still magnificent. I can just imagine what they’re like when it is sunny. Go and observe the whole of Hanoi. Something one should not miss!
practical_tips: go and observe the whole of Hanoi

author: Eduardo B
title: As usual Lotte has an excellent Observation Deck
original_content: Everything when I've visit a city want to see it from skyes,  I've found about Lotte deck this time in Hanoi Vietnam... before I went to Observation Deck in Seoul.My family and myself really love it , you can see Hanoi from different angles and take several pictures inside the glass observatories. Everything pas perfect and the staff was very friendly.I went early morning but definitely at night would be nice to see Hanoi.Keep in mind weather might affect visibility so arrange your visit accordingly.I was staying in the old quarter so it took us less than 25 min to get there by taxi
highlights: Take several pictures inside the glass observatories

author: Lyndsey J
title: Amazing views of the city and not expensive
original_content: Was very quiet in the tower but that meant it was peaceful. Great views of the city and a reasonably priced beer at the top.

author: SherbetMelbourne
title: Worth a visit
original_content: We weren't planning on doing this but decided to do so on  our last day. This is well designed, set out and organised as far as observation decks go. We had fun and had our photo taken. It wasn't busy, we enjoyed the view and the perspective of the city even though the fog / mist / made it hard to see too far off into the distance. There is a great space to sit and enjoy a drink or two. Worth the money.
drawbacks: fog / mist / made it hard to see too far off into the distance

author: Rallyman23
title: A great experience
original_content: You'll get the best view of Hanoi from here (if it's not too hazy) and you'll also have the fun of testing your nerve standing on the glass panel!Compared to most attractions it's a bit of a one-trick pony and it's a bit off the beaten track so you may want to get a cab out to it. If you do then take my advice and use Grab (Asia's answer to Uber) instead of a metered taxi as it could be up to 10x cheaper - you have no idea what speed they've set their meters too!
drawbacks: a bit of a one-trick pony
practical_tips: use Grab instead of a metered taxi

author: Sigalit B
title: the best view point in Hanoi
original_content: a must see during a visit in Hanoi. give good view of all the city. next to fancy shopping mall and great supermarket
highlights: good view of all the city
practical_tips: visit next to fancy shopping mall and great supermarket

author: Bsmip82
title: Great view
original_content: Great view at night but the fair quite expensive compare with other places here. Better should go the roof top bar at lotte.
practical_tips: Go to the rooftop bar at Lotte

author: Steve H
title: Lotte Deck
original_content: Great day, we visited on a clear day during the day, with our son who is teaching in Hanoi.  Great view of the city, at relatively modest cost, about £10 per adult I think. Interesting to get an over view of the city and the mono rail under construction.  Did the glass floor ( gulp), worth doing.  There are 2 glass floors and on a Sunday when we visited, not much of a queue, maybe 5-10 people hovering and they cleared off when they saw us approach.
highlights: Interesting to get an over view of the city

author: Linhchesky N
title: Great view of Hanoi
original_content: Lotte Observation Deck allows you to see different corners of Hanoi without the crowd. The sky walk platform was definitely not for the faint-hearted though but do try it if you are not scared of height.
highlights: see different corners of Hanoi without the crowd
practical_tips: do try it if you are not scared of height

author: Andi H
title: good view of Vietnam without the crowd
original_content: This place gave us literally a bird's eye view of Vietnam.  It was nice to see the place from this vantage point.  It was a different experience from being right in the middle of everything going on.  I was too scared to stand on them, but the kids loved the glass floor observation platforms!  There were hardly any people up there with us, so it was a good change from the crowded experience you usually get when you go around Vietnam.
highlights: nice to see the place from this vantage point
different experience from being right in the middle of everything going on

author: Jennifer Y
title: Just like other observation decks
original_content: I’ve been to Saigon observation deck and I thought that was better. Maybe it’s because of the weather. It was foggy when I visited Lotte observation deck so view wasn’t good. I went to McDonald in this deck and ordered chicken nuggets. They were all burnt. I liked the heart and angel theme areas. They were great to take pictures.

author: woodlucy68
title: Love it
original_content: I and my friend went there last week. Love this space. Nice view and great place to take photos. Will be back again.

author: John E
title: Great Views
original_content: This is a 5 start hotel and shopping mall which also has "The Top of Hanoi" on Level 65 with a bar and restaurant. Good place to go for a drink or meal.
highlights: Good place to go for a drink or meal

author: Girlwholovestotravel
title: Amazing view point
original_content: This view point was absolutely amazing! I think it's the highest view point I've ever been on. It had 65 floors and a lot of areas to take photos with flashing lights, such as the flashing heart or the wings on the walls, as in California. Loved this view point. Highly recommended.
highlights: areas to take photos with flashing lights

author: Sid Rose
title: Fabulous view of Hanoi
original_content: This is great if you want to get an aerial overview of Hanoi without taking a helicopter. There is also a great rooftop bar in the Lotte Tower.

author: Stefan O
title: Great Views!!
original_content: Lotte Observation Deck gives you a Superior look across Hanoi and its surroundings! A Must See while in Hanoi!!

author: youbloodytourist
title: Visit as the sun sets!
original_content: If you want to get the most of your money, visit as the sun goes down. This means you'll be able to get some good photos of the city beforehand and see Hanoi all lit up. at night.
highlights: good photos of the city beforehand
practical_tips: visit as the sun goes down

author: OFB17
title: Great views but not for us
original_content: I wanted to see the Lotte Center and its Observation Deck to get a feel for the "new Hanoi" outside the Old Quarter. The building is a very contemporary high-rise and the department store an upscale one that could be anywhere in the world, but one that surely only very, very few locals can afford. The Observation Deck comes with a corresponding price tag of 230k VND ($10) per person, which really is too much for what it is. The views from the 65th floor could probably be great but we only experienced them on a rather normal and typically hazy day. Outside the two small skywalk platforms there is little else to do than walking around completely and maybe having an overpriced coffee. I would not do it again and recommend the 20th floor of the Pan Pacific Hanoi instead, where 230k VND will buy you a good four beers and you get great views for free...
drawbacks: views from the 65th floor could probably be great but we only experienced them on a rather normal and typically hazy day
highlights: views from the 65th floor could probably be great
practical_tips: go to the 20th floor of the Pan Pacific Hanoi instead

author: Maxi F
title: Top rooftop bar
original_content: Very nice stuff working there ( minh, tdan, hoa & chi) the prices are ok for a sky bar and its not to crowded. Be careful it can be cold in the Winter.
drawbacks: Can be cold in the Winter

author: TheButcherBunch
title: The View
original_content: Something about being able to see for miles. You feel nothing in the elevator going up, just maybe your ears popping. There are no windows so you don't even no your moving except for the numbers flying past on the screen. Once up top you are able to take lots of photos some of which can be on the two see through floors looking down. Have a coffee and take in the view. Lots of information in English to let you know where your looking.

author: Danny Bui
title: Not worth experiencing
original_content: I got some high expectations when visiting because of the skywalk. The price is fairly okay but the experience is not worth it at all. Walking pass the security point the staff was sitting there and doing nothing. We had to wait and ride the elevator to floor 65 by ourselves. We have to share the elevator with this Korean family and as I wondered around to take photos. The Korean family closes the elevator door quickly so they could have a ride up to the observation deck alone. As they closes the door my brother was stepping in while the door was closing and hit his head hard on the elevator door. There was no single apology from the korean family and the staff doesn’t bother to care. I was really pissed at the family and we had a very awkward ride up to the top. As soon as we got up, I got very disappointed. Staff were just sitting around while tourist were bustling on the skywalk. The limit was only for 10 peoples to be on it at once but I saw about 15-20 people stepping and walking around it. The gift shop didn’t really have anything special to offer, just some simple stuff you could easily get from a nearby market. We got our photos taken and quickly head back down. We only spent 15-20 minutes. Disappointing experience, I would never recommend going here. I’d rather go to their restaurant on the 63rd floor and have a dinner or visit Top of Hanoi (65th floor) to have a drink.
drawbacks: Staff was sitting around while tourists were bustling on the skywalk
Elevator door closed quickly without apology from the Korean family
practical_tips: Go to their restaurant on the 63rd floor for dinner
Visit Top of Hanoi (65th floor) for a drink

author: Thuận N
title: Such a lovely place
original_content: I came there several times.One time with my family, my son was very exciting to go and play around. One time I came with my friend in a bar in the evening, so wonderful, delicious food and really nice view. The other time, I came there alone for refresh myself with a cup of drink from Angel in Us in a corner of OD to see a nice Hanoi. It is really a must destination that everyone should go in Hanoi.
practical_tips: try the food at Angel in Us

author: ngocph2610
title: Chill?
original_content: Too much chill I melted away!A little Jazz, a little cocktail and a bit of view from the Observation deck, the whole combination kept me warm on a cold night. I love how peaceful Hanoi looks from up here!

author: Trangthu
title: Stunning place to visit
original_content: I have been here twice with my family. And each time coming, it's like a whole new experience. The view is absolutely perfect and sky walking is a must!!! It's really amazing but not for those who are afraid of heights!!!! ^^
practical_tips: not for those who are afraid of heights

author: Hako
title: Delightful place to visit
original_content: I haven’t been here so I was really excited to see Hanoi in such high tower. My first time here in Vietnam and I think this is the best place to visit. Very romantic and the sightseeing was mind blowing  and amazing. Romantic place for couple also.
highlights: sightseeing was mind blowing and amazing

author: briann
title: Amazing!!!
original_content: Suitable for those who like to see the city from a height. Very clean and the staff was wonderful. I was impressed with friendly and helpful staff. The prices were very reasonable. Time seemed to stop when I was there. Worth visiting if you're in Hanoi. I recommend this place.
extracted_times: Time seemed to stop when I was there
practical_tips: Suitable for those who like to see the city from a height
Worth visiting if you're in Hanoi

author: Trachala N
title: Lotte Observation Desk Hanoi, the high advatage poin in the city!
original_content: I went with my friends in few months ago, amazing views across HA Noi and there is have a nice bar for chill out, we stayed for sunset and got some absolutely great pictures, there are hours afterWe definitely recommend to visit here.

author: Phạm Minh Khuê
title: Best view in Hanoi
original_content: A very inexpensive way to get excellent view of all directions of Hanoi.Many places to sit and relax and enjoy the gorgeous view. Must try coconut coffee at Raku Raku coffee shop.
practical_tips: try coconut coffee at Raku Raku coffee shop

author: pinkachoo10
title: Great Views and Cool Skywalks
original_content: Had a free day in Hanoi so we decided to check this place out.  Took a taxi from the old quarter which was maybe 15 minutes drive.  The fee to get in was a little expensive considering but it was worth it because we got to see the great views, get out of the rain, and the place was not crowded so it was nice.  We also got to eat some Japanese food at the shopping mall and do a little shopping.  Really good bakeries.

author: Nguyễn H
title: Best view in Hanoi
original_content: Best view in Hanoi. Its suitable for dating.You can take pictures with two skywalk in OD. Nice view

author: T_Senaratne
title: Bird's eye view of Hanoi city
original_content: Located in the Lotte Centre which is just a few meters away from the Hanoi Daewoo Hotel.  Unimaginable view of the city from the 65th floor.  Great feeling of walking on air when standing on the glass floor and seeing the vehicles passing beneath your feet.  Better to grab the "happy hour entry" (morning and evening 10pm to 11 pm) when the prices are slashed by 50%.
highlights: Great feeling of walking on air
practical_tips: Grab the 'happy hour entry' for 50% off

author: Tops333
title: Amazing views
original_content: Amazing views food and service , you get a great view of the city served by amazing staff who look after all your needs

author: Heguang Z
title: Glass Floor
original_content: Not on my must do list but if you have a few hours to spend you could go to the Lotte Center in Hanoi. Observation Deck in on the 65th floor and there are two glass floor decks you can walk on. It was scary at the beginning but you get used to it after a little while. The fee is expensive but if you go early in the morning there is 50% discount. There is a coffee shop and a Lotteria fast food outlet on the same deck.

author: AlvinSG
title: Good place to view Hanoi
original_content: At 65th storey 272m, beautiful scenery.Advise to go late afternoon for sunset view.Love the thrill of standing on the transparent floor deck at great height.Wt lower floor, have food street and great shopping of many big brands you can name it.Spent 4hrs including my lunch there.Good place to visit for meals n shopping and good view of Hanoi city.
highlights: thrill of standing on the transparent floor deck
good place to visit for meals n shopping and good view
practical_tips: go late afternoon for sunset view

author: JSTrip_77
title: Pretty Much Always Hazy - But Still Cool
original_content: OK, so this is a really cool option for sightseeing in Hanoi. It is relatively expensive considering the rest of the sights in Hanoi. And yes, there's a pretty obvious price difference for Vietnamese citizens and foreigners. But, that's OK. The real issue is that the views are always hazy because of all of the pollution. But, on the flip side, because the observation deck is so expensive, relatively speaking, there really are no crowds. So, that's nice. And, it's easy to get some good time on the two incredible glass floor outcroppings. Just please, take off your shoes. The signs are obvious but people don't always pay attention.
drawbacks: price difference for Vietnamese citizens and foreigners
people not paying attention to shoe removal signs
highlights: no crowds due to high price

author: Dean W
title: Cloudy views
original_content: I did quick trip to the Lotte centre. The price is 230 k. Expensive for what you get. The good part was there was very few tourists  and you can look out  with no rush. The bad part is the views is blocked from smog

author: Natalia N
title: Fantastic
original_content: You can go up on the 65th floor/272meters by a speed elevator. The ticket was approx 10usd, the accept credit cards and dongs. The have 50% on early morning and after 22hrs. We went there at 16hrs to see Hanoi both during the daylight and after the sunset. You can take great pictures standing on a glass floor!

author: Student Q
title: The Lotte Observation Deck
original_content: The Observation Deck has a great view but there is to much smog to see through. Right bellow it is a shopping mall so you could buy things before going up the Observation Deck
practical_tips: buy things before going up the Observation Deck

author: madamshalet
title: Escape from the heat
original_content: I imagine this would give some amazing views of an ever growing city, however the day we went up it was really cloudy so we could really see too much.  I think that on a sunny day the views would be amazing
drawbacks: could really see too much due to cloudy weather
highlights: would give some amazing views on a sunny day

author: Omzas
title: Go during the non-peak hours
original_content: We've checked and there were 2 non-peak hours (8.30-10.30 and 22.00 to 23.00) where visitors get a 50% discount off its VND230,000 per pax price. Suddenly, it become so much more value for money and you may get to avoid the crowd. Thus, go in the morning for the day view of the entire hanoi city and go in the night for the sunset/night skyline of the city. Worth a try when you got a sufficient dose of museums and monuments in hanoi.
highlights: Day view of the entire Hanoi city
practical_tips: Go when you got a sufficient dose of museums and monuments in Hanoi

author: Minh Thuy T
title: A new adventure in Hanoi
original_content: When we first have this in Hanoi, I was so excited to come. The first time ever I could see Hanoi so close and clear. Maybe people in other countries have had this experience for long but for us, Vietnamese, it's new and a must try one.
highlights: see Hanoi so close and clear

author: b0rn2sh0p
title: Better than I expected
original_content: I went there 8:30am and get 50% off. It was nice I got the iview all by myself. I bought some drinks in Lotte mart before I enter the observatory so I don’t have to buy experience drinks there. There are plenty of chairs and photo spots. It was nice place to visit.

author: Sudesh
title: Bit costly though
original_content: If you are foreigner, you will be charged 230K VND if Vieatnamis 180K VND (elder person), Less people Make sure to go not raining time Any way good experience

author: Gillsholidays
title: Worth the visit great views
original_content: Spent nearly 2hours up here which was not only a relief from the heat but it was also a great place get your bearings of this awesome city
highlights: great place to get your bearings

author: Maddy F
title: Overcoming Fear with a View
original_content: 2 reasons we came here - the view & the Skywalk. Cannot believe the lack of visitors for the amazing view of Hanoi, which proved to be more than just Hoan Kiem Lake & the Old Quarter.  360degree view, just sit down, have a coffee & watch Hanoi unfold below you. For the added bonus 2 Skywalks - free. This was one of my fears & am happy to report I walked out on both a couple of times. I would highly recommend it & one of those rarities where you get 2 experiences for the price of one.
highlights: 2 experiences for the price of one

author: OseEmma
title: Nice spot to get an amazing view of Hanoi!
original_content: This was an exciting experience and I was able to take great pictures and enjoy the view. Note that entry is not free.

author: Ivanof_Bcn
title: Not that great as expected
original_content: I was expecting something better. The two  parts with glass floor are not very big. Plus in one of them they have like a photo stage with a heart so it's often occupied with people making the oficial heart  picture and the other ones can't be at that part. I think this photo thing very "touristy". I'm not sure if it's worth the price you pay (more than 8 euros) but still you have nice views of the city.

author: Ilga U
title: Glass floor
original_content: Breathtaking views of Hanoi! Peacefull, not crowded place.Glass floor not for faint hearted! A must visit
drawbacks: Glass floor not for faint hearted

author: BrisbaneTraveler2009
title: Amazing views of Hanoi
original_content: Awesome view of Hanoi city. Clear glass viewing decks for good pictures. Well worth it. Good aircon.

author: zoe1606
title: Don’t look down
original_content: By Western prices entry is quite cheap at 230k dong. The deck is located on the 65th floor with lift access from the basement of the shopping centre next to the supermarket. 360 degree views but not much information to say what you are looking at. There are two glass decks for the brave to walk out on to with a professional photo available at one - prices started at 90k for a photo in a presentation wallet. There are several drink / snack places on the floor.
drawbacks: not much information to say what you are looking at

author: Judith S
title: WOW
original_content: As soon as you exit the lift it is WOW. What a fantastic view. A great place to sit and have a meal and relax. This is a must see when in Hanoi.
highlights: great place to sit and have a meal and relax

author: Vivek Chauhan
title: Unique Experience
original_content: Now this is a luxury mall with many local luxury brands and some international brands. One needs to visit the SkyDeck on 65th floor which has a complete view of Hanoi. It has a sky deck for interesting pics as well. Be here to spend an hour or two. It has some interesting picture taking worth spots with screens etc. Don’t have anything to eat/ drink up there, it’s not good and is expensive.
practical_tips: Don't have anything to eat/ drink up there

author: edwardcyau
title: Great views and cafe on the 65th floor
original_content: Great day trip to see the skyline of Hanoi West Lake and also enjoy some retail therapy. The entrance is outside the mall on the lower ground floor. Lots of Instagramable photos from above but go on a clear day or after rain so the smoggy atmosphere settles for a better view. Waffle at the cafe was kinda delicious 🤤

author: Kurtis H
title: A great experience
original_content: A very good way to spend half an hour, and also very convenient since it’s on top of a shopping centre. Amazing 360 degree view around Hanoi. Can see everything. The glass floor is also a fun challenge if you are up to it. Much better than the sky deck in Ho Chi Minh

author: rchlwllms
title: A must see view of Hanoi.
original_content: The Lotte building itself is very nice and modern, we went to the supermarket and the food court before going to the observation deck. You get an amazing 360 view of Hanoi!
