author: spktravels
title: Interesting stop
original_content: The Silk Village which is now part of Hanoi is  limited to several streets but it is worth a visit.We stopped at one family owned shop which still operates its own looms. Apparently most of the shops in the Silk Village are merely retailers.We learned the process of making silk fabric from the start, silk worms, to designing patterns, to the actual weaving.Next to the manufacturing area is a nice sized shop. There is a large selection of completed garments such as dresses, pajamas and scarfs all reasonably priced. in addition for those who are so inclined there is a wide array of silk fabrics from which you have have clothes made on your own.This shop is modern and the owners were friendly and helpful.
highlights: learned the process of making silk fabric
practical_tips: visit early to see the manufacturing process
consider making clothes on your own with silk fabrics

author: 175MOM
title: Great silk shopping experience
original_content: I enjoyed the visit to the silk village. The entire area is not big, but I still did not get to see all the stores in 2 hours we had.   I see mixed reviews and I can see why. If you are not interested in silk, you should probably skip it.  All the stores are selling silk fabric/scarves, so I can see why people may get bored if you are not interested.  My husband was...but I loved the place as I love fabrics.   Is this "touristy" place?  Sure, I don't think the  locals would pay those prices.  But entire Hanoi is kind of touristy.  Also some may be disappointed that many products are not made there at the silk village.  "Authentic" or not, this is the place to go for silk shopping. I really wanted to see how silk is made in old fashioned way.  I assumed we could see it right in the middle where a small pond/arch are.  But this courtyard is just surrounded by shops.  At one of the stores we bought a scarf, and asked about it.  The store lady pointed to go to the residential area.  So we did, walked for a while but did not see anything.  Maybe they have closed down, or maybe we would have seen if we wondered off smaller streets.  We went back to the silk village and browsed more stores.  At another store where I bought fabric, a very helpful lady, who also made the fabric I bought (and her father dyed it), said her home where she makes fabric is 30 min away, but told as to go to store called Mao and showed us where.  She also advised us that their fabrics are more expensive.  Mao was a larger store in this area, and there is factory/house right next to it.  The store ladies said we could take a look at the factory, so we did that first.  Our kid thought it was interesting. I am not an expart, but theier fabric seemd to be better quality. Some are 100% silk and some are not, and they are clearly marked.  I bought the one my kid liked.   Also some stores also sell non-silk souvenirs in small quantities.  I found some beautiful fans. We did not bargan.  Coming from the U.S., I thought the price was already reasonable, and felt barganing was not appropriate. But I guess you could if you wanted.  We did "cheap" silk shopping in HCMC, but shopping in Van Phuc Silk village was something compeltely different and I enjoyed it.

author: nickal06
title: A dying place... unfortunately
original_content: Well, well well...This place tries (sadely) to survive with the tourist but there not that much left.Far away, surrounded by the constructions, no need of crytal ball to predict its future...
drawbacks: tries to survive with the tourist

author: elna m
title: Nothing extraordinary
original_content: This was just another commercial outlet, nothing unique about it.  If in the area, worth a visit but do not expect anything authentic.

author: John S
title: Not what I was expecting
original_content: Loads of places selling silk, however they are all selling the same stuff. However we did get to see the old style weaving machines that I would say come from the era of our industrial revolution, very noisy and the health and safety people would have a fit lol.The area for the dyeing of the silks was also available to see, didn't get too close didn't want to inhale the fumes.
extracted_spaces: exhibition of old style weaving machines
practical_tips: be cautious of health and safety concerns
don't inhale fumes from dyeing process

author: WAprof
title: Buying silk fabric
original_content: If you'd like to buy silk fabric then make sure and visit Van Phuc. They also have scarves, and other clothing but one of my goals in visiting was fabric and I found a lovely selection here.
practical_tips: visit Van Phuc if you're looking for silk fabric

author: LaraDay1993
title: Van Phuc Silk village
original_content: If you have some extra time to kill while you're in Hanoi - the silk village is a nice trip. It's not too far away and the drive is a scenic one of the city. I would recommend that you spend 2 hours there. You probably won't need more time than that. There are no real restaurants there, however one cafe for drinks. I'd recommend that if you're keen to know more about the silk village, try and get hold of a tour guide, there are no information centres or plaques up explaining anything (I may have missed them though ).  Everyone is relatively chilled, you can walk straight into the factories with beautiful old looms still in use. You may even be lucky and see them in use. The silk products are stunning , however the shops become repetitive and some products say 100% silk and then when you ask, the shop assistant will tell you that it's actually not 100%.  There is a stunning shop at the top of the street with silk clothing and scarves that are to die for so definitely take your time and shop around. You can buy various types of silk as well, and you can buy it in meters. The prices aren't too bad, you're looking at $10-$20 a scarf and a bit more for a silk shirt. There is a lovely garden and shrine there as well so have a look at that is well. I think that if you have the time, it's a nice place to visit.

author: FaithMY
title: Not worth the visit
original_content: We were greatly disappointed at what the silk village has to offer. Shops all selling almost same things . Poor design and price not great either. Not worth the visit.

author: Kathy K
title: Skip if limited on time
original_content: It was interesting to see how silk is made. I had no idea the amount of labor involved. I wisely left my credit card in the car.This was my second time in Hanoi. I would not recommend this if time is limited. There are far more interesting things to see in the Hanoi area
drawbacks: Not recommended if time is limited
highlights: Interesting to see how silk is made
practical_tips: Leave credit card in the car

author: Annemarie V
title: lots of silk
original_content: it's nice to take a tour, let someone else do the organising, get a bit of info on the area. Lan, our guide was lovely and happy to chat about local culture. we made some nice purchases. some satin silk aud$14 per meter, I have paid 40 at home for lower quality. everyone friendly and no pressure.

author: Grazbee
title: Nice for 1-2hours
original_content: This Silk Village is really beautiful and the people are so nice. It is nice to see it if you are in Hanoi for 1week. :)

author: sally a
title: Disappointed
original_content: My expectations of visiting the silk village as part of the tour I was on were certainly not met. It seemed to be geared to providing a venue for shopping - fair enough -  but some of what was on offer appeared to be cheap reproductions you can find anywhere. There was some nice silk and we did get to see a mechanised weaving set up which showed how the patterns were woven - you could do with ear plugs at this point as it is very noisy. For me it was a very disappointing visit.
drawbacks: seemed to be geared to providing a venue for shopping
some of what was on offer appeared to be cheap reproductions
highlights: mechanised weaving set up which showed how the patterns were woven

author: Kiko
title: Very nice products but not sold in all shops
original_content: We visited the silk village this month and saw some amazing offers for silk ties and pashminas! You just need to check almost every shop in order to find the right quality- really worth the effort going there.
highlights: amazing offers for silk ties and pashminas
practical_tips: check almost every shop in order to find the right quality

author: Justin S
title: Was a good trip. Maybe worth an arranged tour
original_content: Easy to get there by taxi. Approx 190,000 VND from Hanoi Opera House. Bargain given is takes 30-40mins due to traffic. We fancied just wandering around so didn't book any guides/tours. For our needs it worked well. We got to watch a lady working a loom and then wandered the quiet streets, in and out of shops. Some really lovely products. If you want the full run down of the area, how it all works etc, you may want to research in advance or consider a guide. However I don't think it's necessary to spend $$$ on guides. We were there about 70-80 mins. Plenty of time for a leisurely stroll. Our cab driver offered to wait for us, but no need as it's close to a very main road where hailing a cab was easy. Worth a look.
highlights: watch a lady working a loom

author: Jean Ann F
title: Shopping Heaven!!!
original_content: More shops and pretty things to buy than anyone could dream of!!!  Prices are VERY affordable.  I enjoyed the history of silk and watching the looms.

author: Yevgeniya K
title: Good place to buy fabric
original_content: Dont expect to find beautifull silk clothes there. The clothes are not that beautifull and they are not silk. But its the place to find the best silk fabrics ever. Its not that cheap ( the best silk is about 25$ a meter) but still cheaper than in europe. I suggest to come with a lighter so you can check if the fabric is real. They can easily sell you viscose for silk and you will never know, it looks so similar.
drawbacks: The clothes are not that beautifull and they are not silk
They can easily sell you viscose for silk and you will never know
highlights: Its the place to find the best silk fabrics ever
Its not that cheap ( the best silk is about 25$ a meter) but still cheaper than in europe
practical_tips: I suggest to come with a lighter so you can check if the fabric is real

author: Brayden_byn
title: High quality product silk!!!
original_content: From 10km from our hotel in Old Quater, we visited Van Phuc Silk village which is amazing village with helpful and friendly local people and beautiful sightseeings, but impressed thing with me is high quality product silk which is made by hand of local people . It's amazing experiences, thanks Hanoi Free Walking Tours to support us during our trip.You can catch bus 02 and 21 to travel to there.
highlights: high quality product silk made by hand of local people
practical_tips: catch bus 02 and 21 to travel to there

author: Su H
title: Silk village
original_content: The name is Silk village, so I expected to see a variety of silk fabric.  But reality is far from expectation.Nothing much to see, all the shops are selling almost the same items. You need to ask for discount in most of the shops as the shops mark up the price especially to the foreigners.Just 40 minutes drive from Hanoi old quarter.
drawbacks: Shops mark up the price especially to the foreigners
practical_tips: Ask for discount in most of the shops

author: Tania P
title: Nice silks,nice setting
original_content: Nice silks,but most shops all carry same selections, so very repetitive .. The nicer shops were quite expensive & no real bargaining .. Enjoyed seeing silk worms and the looms,but not much else to do. The little park nearby is nice for a wonder.
highlights: seeing silk worms and the looms

author: Adan c
title: Outstanding white silk dress
original_content: Travelling Van Phuc village in lately afternoon, i surprised before the beauty of Van Phuc silk like the rainbow. Furthermore, Hung uncle who is enthusiastic local people told us the history of the village and how to make special of Van Phuc silk. 10km from Hanoi Old Quater, you can travel buy bus or hire moto.
highlights: the beauty of Van Phuc silk like the rainbow
Hung uncle who is enthusiastic local people told us the history of the village and how to make special of Van Phuc silk
practical_tips: 10km from Hanoi Old Quater, you can travel buy bus or hire moto

author: TravelforScuba
title: Silk Scarves, Silk Worms, and That's About It
original_content: Went here looking for inexpensive silk items. Most of what we saw was scarves, a few dresses, and shirts. Most shops have the same items so you can haggle to get the best price. We were a bit underwhelmed there was no one demonstrating the silk weaving just a bunch of old machines set up to show the process. This was interesting but a live demonstration would have been great. It's about a $5 cab ride from old town so cheap to get there. So if you have an hour to kill it's not a complete waste.

author: agrippina1952
title: perhaps the high season is better here
original_content: We visited in winter, and many of the shops were shut. We had been told that we could see silk weaving and manufacturing in process, but that was not to be. The place seemed rather bleak and deserted. All the silk products on display were very similar, and not cheaper than in the Old Quarter or Hang Gai. I wouldn't bother, but then perhaps a visit in summer might be very different.
drawbacks: many of the shops were shut
could not see silk weaving and manufacturing in process

author: KeepMemories
title: Quiet pleasant walk
original_content: The place was really quiet, huge contrast with the busy preparation for Ted New Year in the Old Quarter. The shops sell similar things to Old Quarter silk shops but since it's so quiet, we had a leisurely walk and browse.
extracted_times: busy preparation for Ted New Year
drawbacks: busy preparation for Ted New Year

author: shocar
title: It worth the trip for clothes. Be aware sellers to follow you everywhere
original_content: We had here a nice day with a friend shopping around and checking for nice clothes made in silk.Most fancy shops use to charge more, so expect to find more western designs and prices too.Some sellers are not kind and follow you in all the shop what I found very uncomfortable, but I understand is a culture misunderstanding.If you are big size, XL for Europe or US I suggest better go to Hue to buy clothes where they have more sizes due the lot of tourists there.
drawbacks: Some sellers are not kind and follow you in all the shop
Most fancy shops use to charge more
highlights: found nice clothes made in silk
expect to find more western designs and prices too
practical_tips: If you are big size, XL for Europe or US I suggest better go to Hue to buy clothes

author: annalee2403
title: amazing attraction
original_content: Arrive Van Phuc village I was impressed by typical manner of an ancient village in the north of Vietnam with banyan tree, well, communal house, and the sound of power-looms everywhere. There are very much silk with various products like shirts, ties, crafts, dresses…
highlights: typical manner of an ancient village
various products like shirts, ties, crafts, dresses

author: Beaumaris32
title: A Great Day Out
original_content: At the end of our walking/touring visit to N Vietnam, the 10 of us had to to do a craft village tour.    So, combined with the Bat Trang Ceramic village (see my review) we had a splendid day out - Bat Trang in the morning, back to Hanoi for lunch, then Vin Phuc Silk village in the afternoon.    You start off with a close look at were they spin the silk and make the cloth on looms - very interesting.    Then you can stroll around the large number of places selling all sorts of silk items from scarves to shirts and blouses etc.   Do the usual, expected bargaining and, bingo, souvenir/gift problems solved !   A very pleasant day out.

author: kdk1965
title: Up-thumb on the insight and down-thumb on bargains
original_content: We stopped here as part of a private tour and while we enjoyed seeing how silk is made, the rest of the visit was simply ok.  It felt "canned" and more like an amusement park area in terms of the approach.  Shops were lovely, the ladies selling items in the shop were lovely, but this is not a free market area.
drawbacks: more like an amusement park area
highlights: ladies selling items in the shop were lovely

author: Dylan G
title: Great insight into silk manufacturing
original_content: Friendly locals, free tour through a silk manufactory. Many silk toys and clothes purchasable. There's a small marketplace next door that sells cheaper items, so it's worth shopping around.

author: dccollyer
title: Don't Miss It
original_content: As a lace maker I was keen to buy silk thread which is not something they normally sell.  However the management kindly agreed and I came away very satisfied. This is a wonderful place which needs more promotion!

author: MsAnnHanoi
title: Touristy but still have a story
original_content: Van Phuc silk village , now in Van Phuc ward, Ha Dong disrict, Hanoi, 10km from the city centre, has been the most famous and long lasting silk weaving village in Vietnam with various patterns.Since its first appearance, silk from Van Phuc village became a favorable product thanks to the skilful and sopisticated hans and souls of weavers which were crystallized in each piece of silk. Van Phuc silk was always provided for mandarins to make official clothes. Despite historical changes, Van Phuc silk weaving has still been growing for the last 10 centuries. Itnitially , Van Phus silk was produced only for upper and middle feudal classes. The late 19th century the Nguyen dynasy encouraged people to use domestic products and craftsmen of Van Phuc Viallage quickly collected, learnt, and innovated to “popularize” silk and satin product.
highlights: skilful and sopisticated hands and souls of weavers
long lasting silk weaving village in Vietnam

author: Sebastian L
title: Touristy
original_content: Unless you are very keen to know the intricate process of silk making, the few stalls selling silk products are less appealing than the shops at Old quarters. An optional tour in my opinion.
drawbacks: less appealing than the shops at Old quarters

author: ColinGJ
title: Mostly shopping
original_content: This is mostly a couple of streets of silk shops selling very nice items. At the back of one of the shops, you can go into a room where they are making some silk objects, and watch the old machines working. Mostly of interest if you want to buy clothes or souvenirs, but not that different to what you can buy in the centre of Hanoi, really.
extracted_spaces: room where they are making some silk objects
drawbacks: not that different to what you can buy in the centre of Hanoi

author: pw0867
title: Nice silk and a factory to visit how they make silk clothes
original_content: It would be boring for young kids.  With the exception of the factory that you could visit where they showed you how they made silk garments, it was just a bunch of shops selling silk clothing items.  Some were not cheaper than I could have gotten at home, but the wide variety and selection of items was good.It was better than the ceramic village, but not much to see, unless you were in the mood to buy silk.
drawbacks: not cheaper than I could have gotten at home
highlights: wide variety and selection of items

author: fickle_flower
title: Touristy, but more variety than at the Old Quarter
original_content: Probably a visit is in place if your intention is to buy silk goods in Hanoi. There are more variety in terms of fabric selection than in the Old Quarter. Prices appear more reasonable, although you still have to bargain hard. They close pretty early, around 7pm
highlights: more variety in terms of fabric selection

author: AppreciateAdvice
title: Can't understand the glowing reviews... not worth visiting
original_content: The village is a few streets of "shops" selling silk.  There's nothing interesting, original, compelling or otherwise worthy of spending the time to get there, walk-around and go back to Hanoi.  Sure, there's a working mill where you can learn about how silk is made and watch-it, but it's really not so exciting.  And I didn't find anything that was either special or value-priced or both to make a visit worthwhile.  Pass...

author: happywanderer1954
title: Interesting
original_content: Visited the Village, unfortunately it was at lunch time, so didn't see a lot of activity but it was interesting see the looms and the shopping was good.  Went with a private guide and this was just a cheap as going with an organised tour but we were able to fit in a little more during the day.  Some tour companies advertise an admission fee...don't believe it.  There is not admission fee, you can just walk in.
drawbacks: didn't see a lot of activity
practical_tips: don't believe tour companies about admission fee

author: EmillyStephenie
title: good for shopping
original_content: A place has so much shirt, dress,...which are made from silk by hand made. . everything in here are very cheap and special !

author: GeciDC
title: Nothing much here
original_content: We went here as part of our day tour to Doung Lam Ancient Village. What to do? Nothing much. You just take a peak on how they make silk and then you will visit a shop that sell their finished silk products and you'll realize after that it is cheaper to get them in the Old Quarter.
practical_tips: Go to the Old Quarter for cheaper prices

author: Phua W
title: Not worth the time
original_content: Went there as part of a day tour. Just a short street was shops selling silk products.  Totally not interesting and not worth the time.  I'd you are looking for silk products,  shops in the old quarters are more interesting.
practical_tips: shops in the old quarters are more interesting

author: TravellingMouse2014
title: Interesting program that showed us the process of silk making from the silk worms eating to finished silk
original_content: We watched silk worms eating mulberry leaves, saw the cocoons, saw spinners spinning silk, saw operators winding silk on spools, watched the weavers following elaborate paper cutout patterns on the looms, and saw the beautifully patterned silk emerging from the looms.
extracted_spaces: weavers following elaborate paper cutout patterns on the looms
highlights: watched silk worms eating mulberry leaves
saw the beautifully patterned silk emerging from the looms

author: msinwdc
title: Not Worth It
original_content: Oh how I wish I listened to most of the reviews here on T.A. I just can't hear the word "village" and not think that it will be a charming and quiet locale full of locals working on their handicraft. And after going to Ba Trang pottery village, which is just that, I was hoping Van Phuc would be the silk equivalent.But alas, it is as many previous reviewers have commented - nothing special or interesting. I couldn't even find the shops that actually spin the silk. Perhaps it's less busy in November (I was the only non-Vietnamese person there) and this activity is not done all year?If you must go, it's worth hiring a guide or asking a local Vietnamese friend to take you, just to make sure you see all there is to see. As already noted, you only need an hour or two. I think this place is of most interest to people who want to buy fabric rather than ready-made items, because the latter are more readily available in Hanoi's Old Quarter. While I didn't see a lot of fabric, what I did see was beautiful and soft.
drawbacks: couldn't even find the shops that actually spin the silk
practical_tips: ask a local Vietnamese friend to take you

author: Brenda R
title: Small, not much to see or do
original_content: I expected the silk village to be more like the colorful, bustling center or Hoi An, so it was a bit of a disappointment. There were significantly fewer shops, and the merchandise was rather limited. Primarily only ready made clothing (as opposed to the custom shops you can find in other parts of Vietnam) and scarves. Not really any decorative items for the home. We had intended to spend a few hours here and maybe grab lunch as well, but other than 1 or 2 fruit vendors and a few small pharmacies, there weren't really any other dining options. We were able to pop into the 2 temples and all of the silk kiosks (around 25) in just over an hour. This is definitely not a full day or even half day excursion if you plan to work it into your schedule.
practical_tips: not a full day or even half day excursion

author: Nhu_Phuong
title: Genuine and cheap silk!
original_content: It's very easy to get here. Take xe ôm (motorbike taxi) for about 4-5 dollars each way. A lot more expensive by taxi.Here, you'll get to see how they produce silk products. And you can purchase good quality and cheap silk here. This is my go-to place when I need to by gifts for my international friends. About 5 dollars for a silk scarf, That's a good bargain, right?
practical_tips: Take xe ôm (motorbike taxi) for about 4-5 dollars each way
Purchase good quality and cheap silk here

author: CHUN C
title: LIKE A MARKET - THAT'S ALL
original_content: Go there if your purpose is to buy silk fabrics and scarf. Otherwise, do not come here coz nothing for your visit. The good thing is the price of silk is cheaper than Dong Xuan market and not crowded.
highlights: price of silk is cheaper than Dong Xuan market
practical_tips: go there if your purpose is to buy silk fabrics and scarf

author: lastlyvn
title: A silk village you can see people weaving silk cloth
original_content: This is originally a village people produce silk and silk products.  However, it seems the business has come down and nowadays not so many silk factories.  Most products can be found in Hoan Kiem Area and even cheaper there.  Products not exceedingly cheap and this place is quite far away from the city.  Not a particular attraction for tourists or even local people.  Especially do not go right after lunch, most shops are closed for afternoon sleep.
drawbacks: quite far away from the city
practical_tips: go to Hoan Kiem Area for cheaper products

author: Mervyn C
title: Not interesting enough

The village is not as old and traditional as expected

author: Clare Y
title: Not worth seeing
original_content: Perhaps we missed something but all we could see were the silk shops near the main street. The name is misleading as it isn't a village at all and was just in Hanoi.There was construction on the street which I guess hid the looms and silkworm workshop. The city should put up a map near the 'welcome to Silk vilalge' sign to define some kind of walking path.Disappointing.
extracted_spaces: Silk shops near the main street
drawbacks: Construction on the street hid the looms and silkworm workshop

author: Ann T
title: Listen for the sound of the looms
original_content: This is a village full of silk shops but one which is no longer surrounded by mulberry trees. However, if you can hear the sound of the looms, go in and watch people at work weaving silk. We visited this on an Urban Adventure Village tour which was a great way to get insight into the place.
highlights: watch people at work weaving silk
great way to get insight into the place
practical_tips: go in and watch people at work weaving silk

author: PALTravel
title: Good for purchasing gifts; some shops are more friendly than others.
original_content: You really need to shop around ... and if you want an authentic silk or 'pashmina', then you need to know your stuff as some shops slap labels on polyester and which says pashmina.  So, take the time to look at things in a variety of shops before you purchase.That said, the prices are very good and you can easily find something for everyone back home!  It's fun to walk the streets and, if you're interested, you can actually see the entire process (from silk worm to final, woven product.  We'd seen this in Turkey, so didn't bother on this trip.You can find scarfs in all prices.  The finer silk scarves are around $25usd.  Check out each piece before purchasing to make sure there aren't any snags or an damage to the item.We actually took a taxi to the village and he waited while we shopped.  Nice to not have to find a taxi when we were finished!If you have time to shop, this is a great place to do so!
drawbacks: some shops slap labels on polyester and which says pashmina
snags or an damage to the item
highlights: can easily find something for everyone back home
practical_tips: take the time to look at things in a variety of shops before you purchase
check out each piece before purchasing

author: Rafie K
title: Maybe March is the best time to visit Van Phuc
original_content: I was here last week and my sole purpose is to buy silk fabrics and scarf. My wife suggested this place to buy all things silk as she was here in March 2009.Good things:- You can see the silk worm and the process of making the fabric- Considerably low in price compared to Hanoi (and Don Xuan market)- Not that crowdedNot so good:- Less options of silk fabrics and scarf (Maybe due to the cold season)- The fabric options is more inclined towards the celebration of the lunar new yearDespite, I believe this will be better during hot season on whenever the silk worm is active producing the silk thread. I hope someone travel to this place in March or hotter season to supply with more information. Overall, it's a silk village for sure.
drawbacks: Less options of silk fabrics and scarf
The fabric options is more inclined towards the celebration of the lunar new year
highlights: You can see the silk worm and the process of making the fabric
Considerably low in price compared to Hanoi (and Don Xuan market)

author: beachlady32927
title: Interesting stop over and nice people
original_content: I took a motorbike taxi out of Hanoi just to ride around. I saw the statue and small pond first and didn't know it was the silk village. It was a lovely stop. I have never seen this process or the machines. As a teacher and still a learning child myself I truly immersed myself into the machinery and people. The good we're QUALITY and I literally bought the silk that was on the machine. This was priceless to me. Worth seeing was the granite stones and shrine to the Vietnam war losses for this tiny town. Prices w o haggling were better than old town. I don't haggle much. I look at my life and paychecks and I look at theirs. I can afford 5$ more :)
extracted_spaces: shrine to the Vietnam war losses
practical_tips: Consider buying silk directly from the machines

author: Upperny
title: Great prices for silk scarves, but a small venue
original_content: We found ourselves with mixed feelings.  The scarves were inexpensive and beautiful ($5-10), but the extraoidinary ones were $25 and we should have bought those.  There are many shops ostensibly selling the same class of goods.  The people are lovely and the walk is short.  The demonstration of weaving isn't worth the trip, if you've seen such things before, but the prices are great and the selection is amazing, given the twenty or so shops.
drawbacks: The demonstration of weaving isn't worth the trip, if you've seen such things before
practical_tips: Go early to buy the extraoidinary scarves

author: kandl
title: Recommended for silk fabric lovers.
original_content: As a silk lover, I enjoyed seeing the process from silk worm to silk fabric. The old weaving machines were fascinating. Every type of silk in every colour and pattern available by the meter and some ready made clothes. A pleasant village only a short distance from frantic Hanoi.
highlights: every type of silk in every colour and pattern available by the meter and some ready made clothes

author: DragonCrew
title: not as my expectation
original_content: It's on the way from Mai Chau to Hanoi and sure a good reststop if you want smth strange. There you can see the process of making silk but only at a tiny corner of the village communal house. In contrast, there are hundreds of "modern" things with lots of shops, street hawkers, cars and streetside food stalls. If you are fond of silk, we suggest you go for shopping at Hang Gai "silk" street inside Hanoi old quarter instead.
drawbacks: only a tiny corner of the village communal house
street hawkers, cars and streetside food stalls

author: Anna T
title: Ideal place for buy silk products
original_content: We took private car in around 3 hours from Hanoi centre to the Van Phuc Village. These are many silk products hanging on boutique shops: Crafts, ties, dress, tissus..To be attracted by multiple color of silk products, we bought a lot of things: 10 crafts, 5 ties, somes dress.One thing have to be mentioned that we has made bargaining before settle the payment.It was nice expericence to see how the silkworm makes the fibers and how the spinner makes the tissus.Coming to this village is chance to discover the genuine traditional silk-making industry. Bisides that, this is ideal place for buying vietnamese silk.Recommended for everyone traveling to Hanoi.

chance to discover the genuine traditional silk-making industry
ideal place for buying vietnamese silk

go to Van Phuc Village for buying vietnamese silk

author: BobBonHere
title: Not worth visiting
original_content: This was a bit of a disappointment. Our guide obviously had his preferred shops which were were 'encourage' to buy. Prices were OK but buying anything you didn't really want is expensive.
drawbacks: buying anything you didn't really want is expensive

author: Mike
title: Not worth the hassle
original_content: We got the impression from Lonely Planet that this village this village was out of Hanoi in the country a little bit so hired a driver for the day to see this and the Thay and Tay Phuong Pagodas.The silk village was the big disappointment of the trip.  We felt like we were still in the middle of Hanoi when we turned off a main road and down a non-descript street lined with silk shops and into a courtyard, where we saw a few silkworm cocoons on a screen, what looked like some raw silk that had been unwould from cocoons some time ago, and into an old silk weaving room where there a few old looms, one of which was being operated.  We walked back out through the connected silk shop and down the street trying to find something else of interest, before getting back in the car and driving on to the pagodas.  Perhaps we missed something?
drawbacks: Felt like still in the middle of Hanoi

Go to Thay and Tay Phuong Pagodas

author: pngocduong1
title: Beautiful Silk Village Experience
original_content: We visited Van Phuc Silk Village during our Hanoi trip,  Our driver recommended that we visit, and we’re so glad he did!It was very interesting to walk around the village and see the variety of silk products. highlights: interesting to walk around the village and see the variety of silk products
beautiful silk clothes, scarves, and other items to choose from
great experience and a nice opportunity to see something beyond the typical Hanoi attractions

author: Muriel B
title: Sumptuous clothes for a more than reasonable price
original_content: We don't know what to choose because all the clothes are beautiful and inexpensive. A magical place that can even be discovered by taking the metro (1 km 4 from the metro stop).

author: Dal S
title: See how silk is made, woven, dyed
original_content: Lots of vendors, makers, suppliers with a dizzying array of wares.  From bolts of fabric to finished product.  What a fun place to see weaving to finished product.
highlights: Fun place to see weaving to finished product

author: Adrian Villanueva
title: Handicraft Village
original_content: I really enjoyed this trip. The itinerary was perfect, hotels were comfortable, and the food was delicious. Thank you for such a memorable experience.

author: George E
title: Super great for social media content - but otherwise is mid
original_content: I might have come at the wrong time of day or wrong season - but this was mid. We were there midday, midweek.There was very few sight seers there when we went - despite many of the shops being open. There was a relatively pretty pagoda, and several well-painted murals to get a photo in front of. Overall the silk village made for some colourful and fun Instagram content (with all the umbrellas and murals) but did not necessarily provide a super fulfilling experience in itself. most of the silk shops appeared to carry the same products

author: Ightham1
title: Really enjoyable look into silk making
original_content: We took a Grab from the old quarter, which took 35 minutes. Lots of great shops as well as the sound of the looms producing the silk. The higher end stores were honest about whether an item was 100% silk or a silk linen mix, although they wouldn’t budge on price. author: michelle B
title: WELL WORTH A VISIT
original_content: We really enjoyed our visit to Yan Phuc Silk Village.  It is very pretty as you enter under a sea of suspended pastel coloured umbrellas. author: Mincimoo

original_content: I would avoid visiting on a Sunday, some shops closed. A nice experience to walk through but all the shops have similar fabrics. Nothing special and for tourists.

author: Scott V
title: FAKE FAKE FAKE
original_content: FAKE FAKE FAKE... they should call it "70% Silk Village. And either cotton or polyester blend cuz I don't know Village. Poor quality clothes for dumb tourists. It's all repeat cheap fake Chinese made clothing, some with fake brand names and all the same tags no matter what. It's swap meet and fake market goods made elsewhere. author: Saf Traveler

author: 672highf
title: Just A Shopping Trip

author: spktravels
title: Interesting stop
original_content: The Silk Village which is now part of Hanoi is  limited to several streets but it is worth a visit.We stopped at one family owned shop which still operates its own looms. Apparently most of the shops in the Silk Village are merely retailers.We learned the process of making silk fabric from the start, silk worms, to designing patterns, to the actual weaving.Next to the manufacturing area is a nice sized shop. There is a large selection of completed garments such as dresses, pajamas and scarfs all reasonably priced. in addition for those who are so inclined there is a wide array of silk fabrics from which you have have clothes made on your own.This shop is modern and the owners were friendly and helpful.

author: 175MOM
title: Great silk shopping experience
original_content: I enjoyed the visit to the silk village. The entire area is not big, but I still did not get to see all the stores in 2 hours we had.   I see mixed reviews and I can see why. If you are not interested in silk, you should probably skip it.  All the stores are selling silk fabric/scarves, so I can see why people may get bored if you are not interested.  My husband was...but I loved the place as I love fabrics.   Is this "touristy" place?  Sure, I don't think the  locals would pay those prices.  But entire Hanoi is kind of touristy.  Also some may be disappointed that many products are not made there at the silk village.  "Authentic" or not, this is the place to go for silk shopping. I really wanted to see how silk is made in old fashioned way.  I assumed we could see it right in the middle where a small pond/arch are.  But this courtyard is just surrounded by shops.  At one of the stores we bought a scarf, and asked about it.  The store lady pointed to go to the residential area.  So we did, walked for a while but did not see anything.  Maybe they have closed down, or maybe we would have seen if we wondered off smaller streets.  We went back to the silk village and browsed more stores.  At another store where I bought fabric, a very helpful lady, who also made the fabric I bought (and her father dyed it), said her home where she makes fabric is 30 min away, but told as to go to store called Mao and showed us where.  She also advised us that their fabrics are more expensive.  Mao was a larger store in this area, and there is factory/house right next to it.  The store ladies said we could take a look at the factory, so we did that first.  Our kid thought it was interesting. I am not an expart, but theier fabric seemd to be better quality. Some are 100% silk and some are not, and they are clearly marked.  I bought the one my kid liked.   Also some stores also sell non-silk souvenirs in small quantities.  I found some beautiful fans. We did not bargan.  Coming from the U.S., I thought the price was already reasonable, and felt barganing was not appropriate. But I guess you could if you wanted.  We did "cheap" silk shopping in HCMC, but shopping in Van Phuc Silk village was something compeltely different and I enjoyed it.

author: nickal06

author: LaraDay1993
title: Van Phuc Silk village
original_content: If you have some extra time to kill while you're in Hanoi - the silk village is a nice trip. It's not too far away and the drive is a scenic one of the city. I would recommend that you spend 2 hours there. You probably won't need more time than that. There are no real restaurants there, however one cafe for drinks. I'd recommend that if you're keen to know more about the silk village, try and get hold of a tour guide, there are no information centres or plaques up explaining anything (I may have missed them though ).  Everyone is relatively chilled, you can walk straight into the factories with beautiful old looms still in use. You may even be lucky and see them in use. The silk products are stunning , however the shops become repetitive and some products say 100% silk and then when you ask, the shop assistant will tell you that it's actually not 100%.  There is a stunning shop at the top of the street with silk clothing and scarves that are to die for so definitely take your time and shop around. You can buy various types of silk as well, and you can buy it in meters. The prices aren't too bad, you're looking at $10-$20 a scarf and a bit more for a silk shirt. There is a lovely garden and shrine there as well so have a look at that is well. I think that if you have the time, it's a nice place to visit.

author: FaithMY

author: Beaumaris32
title: A Great Day Out
original_content: At the end of our walking/touring visit to N Vietnam, the 10 of us had to to do a craft village tour.    So, combined with the Bat Trang Ceramic village (see my review) we had a splendid day out - Bat Trang in the morning, back to Hanoi for lunch, then Vin Phuc Silk village in the afternoon.    You start off with a close look at were they spin the silk and make the cloth on looms - very interesting.    Then you can stroll around the large number of places selling all sorts of silk items from scarves to shirts and blouses etc.   Do the usual, expected bargaining and, bingo, souvenir/gift problems solved !   A very pleasant day out.

author: MsAnnHanoi
title: Touristy but still have a story
original_content: Van Phuc silk village , now in Van Phuc ward, Ha Dong disrict, Hanoi, 10km from the city centre, has been the most famous and long lasting silk weaving village in Vietnam with various patterns.Since its first appearance, silk from Van Phuc village became a favorable product thanks to the skilful and sopisticated hans and souls of weavers which were crystallized in each piece of silk. Van Phuc silk was always provided for mandarins to make official clothes. Despite historical changes, Van Phuc silk weaving has still been growing for the last 10 centuries. Itnitially , Van Phus silk was produced only for upper and middle feudal classes. The late 19th century the Nguyen dynasy encouraged people to use domestic products and craftsmen of Van Phuc Viallage quickly collected, learnt, and innovated to “popularize” silk and satin product.

author: msinwdc
title: Not Worth It

And after going to Ba Trang pottery village, which is just that, I was hoping Van Phuc would be the silk equivalent.But alas, it is as many previous reviewers have commented - nothing special or interesting. I couldn't even find the shops that actually spin the silk. Perhaps it's less busy in November (I was the only non-Vietnamese person there) and this activity is not done all year?If you must go, it's worth hiring a guide or asking a local Vietnamese friend to take you, just to make sure you see all there is to see. title: Listen for the sound of the looms
original_content: This is a village full of silk shops but one which is no longer surrounded by mulberry trees. However, if you can hear the sound of the looms, go in and watch people at work weaving silk. We visited this on an Urban Adventure Village tour which was a great way to get insight into the place.
highlights: watch people at work weaving silk
great way to get insight into the place
practical_tips: go in and watch people at work weaving silk

author: PALTravel
title: Good for purchasing gifts; some shops are more friendly than others.
original_content: You really need to shop around ... and if you want an authentic silk or 'pashmina', then you need to know your stuff as some shops slap labels on polyester and which says pashmina.  So, take the time to look at things in a variety of shops before you purchase.That said, the prices are very good and you can easily find something for everyone back home!  It's fun to walk the streets and, if you're interested, you can actually see the entire process (from silk worm to final, woven product.  We'd seen this in Turkey, so didn't bother on this trip.You can find scarfs in all prices.  The finer silk scarves are around $25usd.  Check out each piece before purchasing to make sure there aren't any snags or an damage to the item.We actually took a taxi to the village and he waited while we shopped.  Nice to not have to find a taxi when we were finished!If you have time to shop, this is a great place to do so!
drawbacks: some shops slap labels on polyester and which says pashmina
snags or an damage to the item
highlights: can easily find something for everyone back home
practical_tips: take the time to look at things in a variety of shops before you purchase
check out each piece before purchasing

author: Rafie K
title: Maybe March is the best time to visit Van Phuc
original_content: I was here last week and my sole purpose is to buy silk fabrics and scarf. My wife suggested this place to buy all things silk as she was here in March 2009.Good things:- You can see the silk worm and the process of making the fabric- Considerably low in price compared to Hanoi (and Don Xuan market)- Not that crowdedNot so good:- Less options of silk fabrics and scarf (Maybe due to the cold season)- The fabric options is more inclined towards the celebration of the lunar new yearDespite, I believe this will be better during hot season on whenever the silk worm is active producing the silk thread. I hope someone travel to this place in March or hotter season to supply with more information. Overall, it's a silk village for sure.
drawbacks: Less options of silk fabrics and scarf
The fabric options is more inclined towards the celebration of the lunar new year
highlights: You can see the silk worm and the process of making the fabric
Considerably low in price compared to Hanoi (and Don Xuan market)
practical_tips: Visit in March or hotter season

author: beachlady32927
title: Interesting stop over and nice people
original_content: I took a motorbike taxi out of Hanoi just to ride around. I saw the statue and small pond first and didn't know it was the silk village. It was a lovely stop. I have never seen this process or the machines. As a teacher and still a learning child myself I truly immersed myself into the machinery and people. The good we're QUALITY and I literally bought the silk that was on the machine. This was priceless to me. Worth seeing was the granite stones and shrine to the Vietnam war losses for this tiny town. Prices w o haggling were better than old town. I don't haggle much. I look at my life and paychecks and I look at theirs. I can afford 5$ more :)
extracted_spaces: shrine to the Vietnam war losses
practical_tips: Consider buying silk directly from the machines

author: Upperny
title: Great prices for silk scarves, but a small venue
original_content: We found ourselves with mixed feelings.  The scarves were inexpensive and beautiful ($5-10), but the extraoidinary ones were $25 and we should have bought those.  There are many shops ostensibly selling the same class of goods.  The people are lovely and the walk is short.  The demonstration of weaving isn't worth the trip, if you've seen such things before, but the prices are great and the selection is amazing, given the twenty or so shops.
drawbacks: The demonstration of weaving isn't worth the trip, if you've seen such things before
practical_tips: Go early to buy the extraoidinary scarves

author: kandl
title: Recommended for silk fabric lovers.
original_content: As a silk lover, I enjoyed seeing the process from silk worm to silk fabric. The old weaving machines were fascinating. Every type of silk in every colour and pattern available by the meter and some ready made clothes. A pleasant village only a short distance from frantic Hanoi.
highlights: every type of silk in every colour and pattern available by the meter and some ready made clothes

author: DragonCrew
title: not as my expectation
original_content: It's on the way from Mai Chau to Hanoi and sure a good reststop if you want smth strange. There you can see the process of making silk but only at a tiny corner of the village communal house. In contrast, there are hundreds of "modern" things with lots of shops, street hawkers, cars and streetside food stalls. If you are fond of silk, we suggest you go for shopping at Hang Gai "silk" street inside Hanoi old quarter instead.
drawbacks: only a tiny corner of the village communal house
street hawkers, cars and streetside food stalls
practical_tips: go for shopping at Hang Gai 'silk' street inside Hanoi old quarter instead

author: Anna T
title: Ideal place for buy silk products
original_content: We took private car in around 3 hours from Hanoi centre to the Van Phuc Village. These are many silk products hanging on boutique shops: Crafts, ties, dress, tissus..To be attracted by multiple color of silk products, we bought a lot of things: 10 crafts, 5 ties, somes dress.One thing have to be mentioned that we has made bargaining before settle the payment.It was nice expericence to see how the silkworm makes the fibers and how the spinner makes the tissus.Coming to this village is chance to discover the genuine traditional silk-making industry. Bisides that, this is ideal place for buying vietnamese silk.Recommended for everyone traveling to Hanoi.
highlights: see how the silkworm makes the fibers and how the spinner makes the tissus
chance to discover the genuine traditional silk-making industry
ideal place for buying vietnamese silk
practical_tips: make bargaining before settle the payment
go to Van Phuc Village for buying vietnamese silk

author: BobBonHere
title: Not worth visiting
original_content: This was a bit of a disappointment. Our guide obviously had his preferred shops which were were 'encourage' to buy. Prices were OK but buying anything you didn't really want is expensive.
drawbacks: buying anything you didn't really want is expensive

author: Mike
title: Not worth the hassle
original_content: We got the impression from Lonely Planet that this village this village was out of Hanoi in the country a little bit so hired a driver for the day to see this and the Thay and Tay Phuong Pagodas.The silk village was the big disappointment of the trip.  We felt like we were still in the middle of Hanoi when we turned off a main road and down a non-descript street lined with silk shops and into a courtyard, where we saw a few silkworm cocoons on a screen, what looked like some raw silk that had been unwould from cocoons some time ago, and into an old silk weaving room where there a few old looms, one of which was being operated.  We walked back out through the connected silk shop and down the street trying to find something else of interest, before getting back in the car and driving on to the pagodas.  Perhaps we missed something?
drawbacks: Felt like still in the middle of Hanoi
practical_tips: Hire a driver for the day
Go to Thay and Tay Phuong Pagodas

author: Eli
title: Interesting backstory
original_content: An old pagoda in the center of Hanoi. Quite peaceful and carries that traditional charm. Learning more about its historical backstory was quite interesting and surprising. If you’re traveling solo or on your own, you can use the Travellens app to explore it deeper.
practical_tips: use the Travellens app to explore it deeper

author: Maud M
title: Nice temple
original_content: Very nice temple in Hanoi which for me deserves a look. The temple was little attended at the time we went there.

author: Sonia
title: The sacred temple in the heart of Hanoi
original_content: Quan Su Pagoda is one of the most famous and sacred pagodas in Hanoi. This is the headquarters of the Vietnam Buddhist Sangha, so the space is always imbued with Buddhist culture. The pagoda has traditional architecture with a large three-door gate, spacious courtyard, and solemn Buddha statues. On major holidays, the pagoda is crowded with people coming to burn incense and pray. The peaceful space here creates a sense of purity and comfort for anyone who visits.

author: Betsy S
title: Beautiful Pagoda
original_content: Beautiful and ornate. I was there on Vesak Day, which some consider Buddha’s birthday.  Many locals were there to pay respects.

author: Tc voyageur
title: Peaceful. Oasis that’s seen a lot of history
original_content: Peaceful oasis in a busy city.   Near some grim reminders of inhumanity — “Hanoi Hilton” prison  n the Police Museum Don’t come looking for action.  It’s a majestic temple with a lot of history to it.  My heritage Buddhist traveling companion lit joss sticks for lost family members.

author: TheLeongOhana
title: Beautiful Pagoda on A Busy Street
original_content: I stopped by this Buddhist pagoda on the way to Train Street.It was a good size building with lots of greenery everywhere.  Large urns with burning incense with statues and more plants filled the middle of the stairs. I did not go inside as there seemed to be some preparations going on for a ceremony so I silently observed from the outside.  The altar was a beautiful arrangement around a large golden Buddha statue.  Smaller altars were setup on each side.Towards the back there was a small store and stairs leading up to the next levels.  Very quiet everywhere.Worth a short stop if near the Police Museum or Hoa Loa Prison.
drawbacks: preparations going on for a ceremony
highlights: beautiful arrangement around a large golden Buddha statue
practical_tips: worth a short stop if near the Police Museum or Hoa Loa Prison

author: R M
title: Bit of peace
original_content: I went here to just get a little peace of mind after doing lots of war tourist stuff. Very beautiful space, tranquil and many locals going in and out. Very glad I went.

author: Rachel P
title: Lovely and tranquil
original_content: A lovely tranquil temple which was a wekcome relief after the emotion of visting Hoa Lo Prison nearby.  It's free to enter and well worth a visit.  The decoration is incredible and almost sensory overload but it is offset by the calmness of the place.

author: Mehul Kirit Shah
title: Buddhist Community Headquarter
original_content: The monk who hosted the temple then, had corridors built, statues painted, and bell made. The front palace is dedicated to Buddha and the rear palace is dedicated to the king of the Ly Dynasty.

author: explor246
title: Beautiful and peaceful
original_content: It was great to have a private tour guide. He explained how pagoda and temples vary, the budas, the alters, etc. And answered a lot of our questions. Highly recommend a tour guide (and they are so inexpensive to hire).

author: R K L
title: It survived...
original_content: The Ambassador's Pagoda (also known as Quan Su Pagoda) had a noticeably serene and peacefully atmosphere, even while it was full of worshippers when we visited. Originally, the pagoda was built specifically to welcome ambassadors from neighboring countries who were all Buddhists. It survived over centuries when other pagodas met with destruction and has served as the Headquarters of the Vietnamese Buddhism Association since the mid-18th century. Visitors were welcome and encouraged to purchase some incense and offer prayers. To do so was actually quite liberating.
practical_tips: purchase some incense and offer prayers

author: j-curv
title: Peaceful Find
original_content: A beautiful piece of architecture and cultural history that has survived despite the numerous conflicts over the centuries.This is well worth a visit, for its tranquility alone.  On the day we called in there was some kind of ceremony and access was limited to the external perimeter courtyard nonetheless it was worth a wander around this area.

author: jeff1955malaysia
title: an old buddhist temple
original_content: it is located close to the Hoa Lo prison. its entrance has a pagoda shape and it is dark yellow in colour. you will find a number of monks of a non stop of worshippers doing theirs prayers. it is calm and a strong smell of incense.

author: BrockDaBadger
title: Lady Monks (Sangha) Chanting When I Visited
original_content: This pagoda has some history and is just around the corner from the Hoa Lo Prison (aka the Hanoi Hilton).  When I arrived I could hear chanting and when I looked inside there were probably 40 Sangha monks chanting.  Small area but a pleasant and free attraction.

author: RET2246
title: Lovely little find
original_content: A lovely, quiet temple. If you're visiting the prison which is just up the road this is definitely worth a visit, especially following the gloom of the prison this is a peaceful heaven. There are still monks in the temple and plenty of locals coming in to worship. Depending on your level of religion it takes between 10-30 mins to look around.
highlights: plenty of locals coming in to worship

author: seanworc
title: Little Jewel Box Pagoda
original_content: This is an 17th century temple with an entrance gate in Ha Noi. It was built by visiting Buddhist ambassadors who called on the then emperor of Viet Nam. It is reportedly the central HQ of Buddhism in Viet Nam. It is an active temple so there will be many worshippers paying homage here.  A quick stop , maybe 30 minutes.  It is not a complex such as the Temple Of Literature or the Lama Temple in Beijing. Went in March, 2013.
drawbacks: It is not a complex such as the Temple Of Literature or the Lama Temple in Beijing.

author: Chris101111
title: Peaceful
original_content: Happen to come across the temple when out walking, lovely and serene, locals use it regularly, it's well maintained and the Buddhas are ornate and colourful.I would recommend it to visit.

author: HugoColle
title: Beautiful temple
original_content: A beautiful temple which is very peaceful once you enter. Not that big but very nice statues and ornaments here. Alot of locals using this temple for offerings and prayers. Still monks and nuns living here. Is called the Ambassadors pagode because in the earlier years it was a guesthouse for the ambassadors of the Budhist countries. Worth a stop..

author: Porgester
title: Quiet & peaceful
original_content: Its a little off the beaten track but a very beautiful temple & worth the visit. You can pass by it on your way to the prison & temple of literature
practical_tips: pass by it on your way to the prison & temple of literature

author: Leo D
title: headquarters for the Vietnam Central Buddhist Congregation.
original_content: vietnam has many pagodas and temples and Quan Su is one of the most important temples in the country. Constructed in the 15th century along with a small house for visiting Buddhist ambassadors, in 1934 it became the headquarters of the Tonkin Buddhist Association, and today it is headquarters for the Vietnam Central Buddhist Congregation.Since 1942, the pagoda has been restored and expanded many times with a larger and better architectural structure. It's an active pagoda and usually thronged with worshippers; the interior is dim and smoky with incense.

author: BabyCParis
title: Very nice place
original_content: Nice Pagoda to visit if you have done all the other sightseing sites in Hanoi. Very peaceful, not crowded and mainly locals.
practical_tips: visit if you have done all the other sightseeing sites in Hanoi

author: esopus35
title: A quick stop
original_content: I had my rickshaw driver take me here. It was pretty empty.  I loved the Temple with various shrines. When I was there they had large areas of flower petals spread on the ground. It made for some good photos.

author: PhongTien
title: The heritage of Le dynasty
original_content: The temple was renovated several times, and now both local worshipers and curious visitors can enjoy the calm, the beauty, the bits and pieces of history. If you’re the talkative kind, the locals will tell you stories.

practical_tips: If you’re the talkative kind, the locals will tell you stories

author: unREMb

author: Jinsung, Lee
title: The New Landscape of Vietnam
original_content: A tourist destination near Hanoi. The mountain is high and the road is good. The forest is gorgeous and there are various sights around, including folk villages. You can feel the old way of Vietnam.  An old cathedral that collapsed on the hillside.

author: MichaEu61
title: Short trip from Hanoi
original_content: Reachable by scooter from Hanoi in two hours. Some acceptable accommodation around the national parks. Far from mass tourism, especially during the week when there are no Vietnamese.Scenic beautiful area. Close to the Red River. Two nights are definitely enough. You should definitely take the more than a thousand steps to the two highest peaks to the temples and the pagoda. Great view with clear visibility.

practical_tips: take the more than a thousand steps to the two highest peaks

author: D K W
title: Disappointing guide. Excellent aftercare by agent
original_content: Disappointing tour guide but great aftercare from customer services. Significant refund given after excellent customer service from the agent.Prompt pick up by guide and driver.After 2 hours in the car with the tour ‘guide’ and driver speaking between themselves and very little interaction with us we arrived at a gathering place. The guide said ‘that way walk and that way walk’, then pointed at two different staircases. He said 45 minutes each then we eat lunch. The first steps took us 15 minutes, the second steps took 40 minutes. We were then taken to some church ruins and had less than a minute of ‘information’ to say it’s there because of the french and then asked us if we were religious. When we asked if there was anymore to the trip or if he had any other information he said no. At which point he said ‘we go eat’ but when we said we werent hungry yet he responded saying ‘whatever, you want to go home’.The car ride home was extremely awkward and the guide was even swiping through tinder at one point. On the way back to our hotel the guide said ‘this is close to my home so i am getting out now and the driver will take you the rest of the way’, this left us with a driver that spoke no english. The driver also took a wrong turn, at which point we opted to get out and walk the rest of the way to our hotel.We could have booked a taxi for a lot less money and had the same/better experience. We complained to via tripadvisor and after discussing with the agent and them speaking with the tour guide they agreed to a partial refund. With polite and swift communication I cannot fault the agent.
drawbacks: Guide spoke between himself and driver, very little interaction with us
Guide asked if we were religious without any further information
highlights: Significant refund given after excellent customer service from the agent
Prompt pick up by guide and driver
practical_tips: Book a taxi for a lot less money
Communicate with the tour guide and agent if you have any issues

author: Gertjan V
title: Definitely worth it! Good to do at the end of the trip.
original_content: We stayed just outside Ba Vi national park to take a taxi into the park in the morning. A nice trip style up but a very good road. Views are beautiful, going to the top is already a party. Arriving at 1000 meters with a van to the starting point of the routes we walked. Nice terrace with good man and then the trip to the Ho Chi Minh temple. More than 1200 steps challenging and doable. Stairs are made of stone and very easy to walk.  We don't see any tourists that's a relief after Hanoi. The pagoda is definitely worth it but the temple is really special. People are. Very open and also like to have a chat. If you're lucky like we are, people will offer you tea.  So relaxed.  Down and still to the upper temple some 950. Again locales who are sacrificing and giving unsolicited explanations. Ticket costs 60,000 VNDTrails to run well, reasonable condition required.No bugs or pests bothered. Very special experience and highlight of our trip. No tourists and super friendly local people.  Beautiful nature and impressive temples and customs. Night in the area gives peace, recommended. Also to do from Hanoi in a day but less relaxed and you experience less of the local people in the area. We did it the penultimate day to be able to easily get to the airport the next day (1.5 hours) and not back to busy Hanoi.

author: wendy d
country: Arthur's Pass National Park, New Zealand
title: Worth a visit
original_content: Went as part of a private tour. This is very much a locals location. So we felt honoured to be just a few of the westerners up the mountain. The walk up to Ho Chi Minh is over 1200 evenly sized steps, so although a lot, it is very achievable.The temple and pagoda and views (if the clouds break), are beautiful.abandoned church down the mountain was amazing.Definitely worth a visit. A spectacular day out. One of my highlights of 5 week visit to Vietnam.
highlights: one of my highlights of 5 week visit to Vietnam

author: karunayes
title: EXQUISITE EXPERIENCE
original_content: Nature is the ultimate luxury. Now, Nature plus eastern hospitality full of authenticity and warmth, in the purest 1930’s Indochina setting full of antiques and fine porcelain, wooden floors, high ceilings, indirect lightning, is the perfect way to land and begin experiencing Asia. Tour facilitators recommend you arrive from the west and spend a few days taking it easy to stabilize your body and adapt. Coming here, 90 min drive from hectic Hanoi was a perfect decision. The highlight of my month in SE Asia. A true experience for the senses. Family oriented, kind to the solo traveler, and highly recommended as a romantic setting.
highlights: perfect way to land and begin experiencing Asia
a true experience for the senses
practical_tips: spend a few days taking it easy to stabilize your body and adapt

author: Wander29593119161
title: Explore the Spectacular Beauty of Ba Vi National Park - An Ideal Destination for All Tourists
original_content: Explore the Spectacular Beauty of Ba Vi National Park - An Ideal Destination for All TouristsWe explore Ba Vi National Park through unique experiences, from natural beauty to recreational activities. Ba Vi National Park, one of the most wonderful natural wonders not only of Hanoi but also of the whole country, always an ideal destination for those who love the peace and beauty of the mountains and forests and want to temporarily get away from the hustle and bustle of the city. With this article, join us to explore Ba Vi National Park through unique experiences, from natural beauty to interesting recreational activities.Ba Vi National Park - a destination not to be missedLocated about 60km west of Hanoi center, Ba Vi National Park is part of the majestic Ba Vi mountain range. Known as the "green lung" of the capital, this national park not only impresses with the wild and majestic beauty of the mountains and forests but also with its biodiversity with many precious species of plants and animals. rare.Ba Vi National Forest - paradise for nature loversBa Vi National Forest is a place to preserve many types of ecosystems, from primary forests to regenerated forests, creating a cool, fresh green space. This is a great opportunity for visitors to explore the richness of the plant and animal world, from ancient trees to unique birds and butterflies.Entrance tickets and ticket pricesThe entrance ticket price to Ba Vi National Park is very affordable, suitable for all ages, ensuring an affordable yet experiential tour. Detailed information on ticket prices and how to purchase tickets can be found on the official website or at ticket sales points at the entrance.Traveling to Ba Vi National Park - an unforgettable experienceTraveling to Ba Vi National Park is not simply about exploring nature, but also an opportunity to participate in suburban activities such as picnics, camping, climbing, and even yoga in the middle of the green forest. There's nothing better than relaxing and re-energizing in the heart of nature.What does Ba Vi National Park have?Ba Vi National Park is not only famous for its mountains and forests but also for historical and cultural sites such as Thuong Temple, Jade Emperor Temple, and eco-tourism areas. Each location has its own mysterious and historical stories, creating a meaningful and educational trip.Note when visitingWhen visiting Ba Vi National Park, visitors need to pay attention to protecting the environment, not throwing trash indiscriminately and respecting the regulations of the conservation area. Please bring drinking water and snacks to ensure your health during your exploration.Why is Ba Vi National Park so interested in by many tourists?Ba Vi National Park is not only an ideal destination for those who love nature, but also a place that preserves many historical and cultural values of the nation. Let this tour become an indispensable part of your travel memories.
practical_tips: pay attention to protecting the environment

author: Nhà hàng Dung Tiến Ba Vì
title: Ba Vi National Park is an extremely wonderful vacation destination
original_content: I went to Ba Vi National Park, I really like it here, Ba Vi National Park has fresh air, very cool. Many check-in points to take beautiful photos. Especially the majestic and beautiful mountain view of Ba Vi National Park. Take photos with majestic clouds
highlights: many check-in points to take beautiful photos

author: Aurora princess
title: It's worth going, everyone
original_content: Every year I go to Ba district because of its many landscapes, especially Ba Vi National Park, which is very green and beautiful, suitable for treking and team building. Close to the city center, just over 1 hour to get there.
highlights: suitable for treking and team building

author: HMKaren
title: Beautiful park, check it out!
original_content: Huge, beautiful park with a lot of neat stuff to explore. We didn't have a whole lot of time to spend--we climbed up to Bao Thien Tower and (practically next to it) the Ho Chi Mihn Temple. After we came down we checked out the ruins of the French stone church. So all together, we were there for a few hours.The climb up the big hill to the tower and temple involved many, many stairs. But you are in the shade the whole time! Still, if you have mobility issues or you hate stairs, this one might not be for you. But it was really great once you reach the top! There are other people on the path with you, and there are plenty of benches and other places to stop and rest if you want to. I recommend bringing water.The park is full of beautiful flowers. Everything is so lush and green, and you hear constant bird song. For the record, we did NOT use our bug spray, and we had not trouble. No bug bites.The park is a 90 minute drive (60 km) west of Hanoi. We booked a driver with Golden Holiday Travel. He met us in the lobby of our hotel and took us straight there--no difficulty at all. Cost was $75. Admission cost: 60000 VND ($3) per person. I think your driver is free. There is a ticket booth right at the entrance to the park. Our driver stopped---we ran over and bought tickets. Super easy.
practical_tips: use benches and other places to stop and rest

author: K Wang
title: Good for half-day getaway from Hanoi
original_content: The hike to the temple at the top is quite easy. Good for a quick getaway as the air is refreshing. However nothing much special here so if you want to be properly touristy, maybe this is not your best choice.

author: Tracy Hong
title: An escape from busy city
original_content: Located between Hanoi City & Hoa Binh Province, it's an ideal destination if you want a change of air from busy Hanoi. It's a long col but not too hard even for an amateur bike/ motorbike rider. Just be well noticed about the time when you get down: the sky darkens very quickly with a very thick curtain of fog and totally no light (often happens in winter). Be careful with that.You can have a great view down from the high mountains, see cloud shrouded forest and nice stream on the way, visit Ho Chi Minh Temple on the peak. That's a great feeling of being mixed with nature.If need more advise, you can ask me
drawbacks: the sky darkens very quickly with a very thick curtain of fog and totally no light
highlights: great view down from the high mountains
visit Ho Chi Minh Temple on the peak
practical_tips: be well noticed about the time when you get down

author: GavanFreo
title: Ideal Day trip.
original_content: Just 55km from a Hanoi. The distance from the entrance to the top is about 12 km.... all uphill.  We hiked from the bottom which i only suggest if you are fit. On the way here is beautiful scenery and the ruin of the old church is very special. At the top there are lots of steps to get to a lovely pagoda and the Ho Chi Minh Shrine.
drawbacks: only suggest if you are fit
highlights: ruin of the old church is very special
practical_tips: hike from the bottom only if you are fit

author: Liz S
title: Ride a bike to really explore
original_content: We rode motorcycles out from the city, there isn't much to see unless you research the trip. We found a really nice coffee shop along the way...Once at Ba Vi we found our homestay and ate lunch. There aren't many restaurants so a motel or homestay gives you food and a clean bathroom. We then spent the afternoon and early evening riding and exploring the national park. There are several points of interest but for us it was the old church. We made it to the temple around 4pm so it was dark coming down the mountain... if you want to do the temple perhaps go there first because it has many steps and you need daylight.I had read several posts that talk about the mist, I have included a photo... I personally think it created a cool atmosphere. On another side of the park is the waterpark and the waterfalls. This is a different enterance to the park.
drawbacks: not much to see unless you research the trip
highlights: cool atmosphere created by the mist
practical_tips: go to the temple first because it has many steps and you need daylight

author: Pavluna
title: Nice place in the nature, not far from Hanoi
original_content: We visited Bavi National park by car. It took us 1.5 hours from Hanoi. The entrance fee was 60,000VND/person (12 and older) and 20 000VND per car. There was quite a lot of people as it was Sunday, but most were only there for taking some selfies or to have a picnic. We drove to the uppermost parking lot (#7 on the map), where there are 3 possible ways you can go. We decided to go the the french political prison ruins. It was quite tricky to find as even the locals didn't know where it was but if you follow the signs that point to the toilets and continue down some relatively steep stairs you will reach them. On the way back I recommend visiting the Melia resort in the park just for a coffee. It's a bit pricey but beautiful.
drawbacks: even the locals didn't know where it was
practical_tips: follow the signs that point to the toilets
continue down some relatively steep stairs
visit the Melia resort in the park just for a coffee

author: Babar
title: Disappointing Trip
original_content: We traveled from Hanoi, and I don't feel the drive up was worth it. Make sure you pay attention when you travel, because it's possible with the rain and clouds, you'll get no views at all. There was some climbing of stairs, at the end of which there was a temple, a view completely obscured by clouds (although I'd seen it before, I'd still say it wasn't worth it), some expensive place to eat average food, an uninteresting pine tree farm that for some reason is marked as an area of interest, and some old church ruins (the most interesting part of the trip, but not worth it).

author: Maria Ver
title: 😍😍😍
original_content: Amazing place, park is huge, my tips: go there in the morning because there a long way from center of Hanoi , around 2 hourse by moto ,  evening is perfect time to see a sunset from the cliff
drawbacks: long way from center of Hanoi
highlights: perfect time to see a sunset

author: Too Yi
title: Motorcycle Ride Up To Ba Vi National Park
original_content: We were taking a ride up to Sapa from Hanoi and planned to take two days, with a stop in Yen Bai overnight on the first day. Ba Vi is roughly along the way to Yen Bai and is an easy detour to see some nice mountains and scenic places. Google maps brought us to Ba Vi National Park quite easily, without any problems along the way. The whole trip is at most 2 hours out from Hanoi, going at a reasonable pace on a motorcycle. If you don't have any experience on a motorbike, perhaps you may want to think about going up this place. It has hairpins and some reasonable inclines that might throw a new rider off. That being said, the roads are perfectly paved (as compared to some i have had the misfortune of going on) and the inclines are doable even on a bike with less power (125cc). Entrance Fees were VND65,000 per person, but I can't read or speak a word of vietnamese, so if they charged me extra, i have no idea haha. You pay for the tickets at the foot of the park and then travel uphill from there. We didn't have too much time, so we rode up to the Church and the temple. Interestingly, as it was a weekend, there were many young Vietnamese people at the Church's ruins, all having a wonderful day out and bbqing/picnicking around the area. The path to the Church is steeper than anything else there, so be careful if you're new or are riding a really crappy bike. The temple is right on top of the hill, just keep going upwards and you'll reach it.
drawbacks: hairpins and some reasonable inclines that might throw a new rider off
highlights: many young Vietnamese people at the Church's ruins, all having a wonderful day out and bbqing/picnicking around the area

author: Saf Traveler
title: Worth the mission for a day but go to Nimh Binh rather
original_content: It's a really nice motorbike ride up to the top but the jungle is so thick in the park that really the only place to stop is at the top parking lot. Otherwise it's steep uphill ride with just nice trees and couple stunning views. Then you walk up the stairs to the Pagoda. Nice walk but that's about it really.
