author: Chu H
title: Fantastic national park
original_content: Ba Vi national Park is located near Hanoi, 60 km far from the city. It's seem to be a good trip with our motorcycles, easy to ride, climb up and walk around  the mountain. Good choice for weekend!

author: billyroo
title: Lovely day out away from hustle and bustle of Hanoi
original_content: We did a private motorbike trip to Ba Vi National Park. Great fun ride out took about 90 minutes. Beautiful cool air, lovely scenery, great food in the restuarant. We walked up 600 steps to the top to visit Ho Chi Min Temple well worth the climb, had a lovely cup of green tea up the top, made extra special by our two guides Kim and Ken from Funny Travel  Gia Ngu street Hanoi Old quarter.

author: tuananhhoang
title: Excellent national park, beautiful nature and environment
original_content: I, my wife and some friends love to travel to this attraction and we do it every year. It is simply an excellent national park with amazing trail for driving uphill, beautiful nature and environment. Good for sightseeing, trekking to the sacred Tan Vien temple and Ho Chi Minh temple on top of the mountains.

author: Jitze B
title: Great views, cool air.
original_content: Today we visited Ba Vi national park which is located some 65 kilometers away from Hanoi. Driving there takes around one hour, not counting driving up the mountain. Entrance fee for a car with two adults and two children is 140.000 vnd, just around 5 euro. The road leading to the main car park next to the top is good with some small parts but nothing scary. Once you make it to the car park you can climb another 200 meters on good rock stairs to get to the top. Admire the temple and the stunning views if it's not too cloudy. The temperature at the top is at least 5 degrees lower than at the entrance of the park which makes it quite refreshing. Recommended for a day trip if you did Ha Long bay and have a day extra when you are in Hanoi.
practical_tips: Recommended for a day trip if you did Ha Long bay and have a day extra when you are in Hanoi

author: TallChris51
title: Enjoy the views
original_content: Lovely and under-used national park, with a good mix of scenery and a good road leading up to the summit. Some interesting diversions including ruined church and other buildings. Very atmospheric.  Plan well as there's nothing else around!
highlights: good road leading up to the summit

author: BurmeseDays
title: Hanoi day trips - Ba Vi National Park
original_content: Ba Vi National Park is a common day trip from Hanoi, but it seems to be difficult to find much information about it. We hired a driver for the day (~$50 US) and headed there. Trick 1: Get a map when you enter at the base of the mountain …. because there are none up the top. The map shows a couple of walks. The first one you pass, on the way up the hill, to a cave, was ok … cool to be in the jungle, but beyond the cave it got a bit overgrown. On the other side of the road there was another walking track which we attempted to follow … but this was super overgrown and turned into quite a mission. Trick number 2: Wear insect repellent because there are leaches. There are heaps of butterflies though, which is cool. Don't expect to see animals. We did see a couple of birds though. Lonely Planet had suggested there was an orchid garden and a bird garden, I had the ticket lady mark them on the map, but we did not find them - despite lots of looking around. There were plenty of facilities main parking area, mid way up the mountain. A couple of restaurants, accommodation etc…. although the main restaurant waved us away (possibly because there was another function on, possibly because we were not looking to sharp after our bushwalking adventures). Nevertheless, you can get food there.The main attractions seem to be the ruins of the french summer camp - which are pretty cool, and being overgrown by jungle. The tracks here are pretty good. And at the top of the mountain there is a temple dedicated to Ho Chi Minh. Again, the track is good, so easy enough to get there (if you don't mind the 1000+ steps). You'll either be up in the clouds, or have a good view. We had the former.Finally there are some really old and rare pine trees. There is a sign to these off the road on the way up to the HCM temple. These are also worth the walk (up) for nature nerds. The track was getting overgrown when we visited though.
highlights: cool to be in the jungle
ruins of the French summer camp
temple dedicated to Ho Chi Minh
really old and rare pine trees
practical_tips: Get a map when you enter

author: Patty B
title: Wonderful Place To Visit
original_content: This is a lovely place to see while visiting Hanoi.  We met a couple in Saigon who told us about it.  It was a nice walk from the Capella Hotel.  We walked along the lake went over the red  bridge and found wonderful sights.  We watched a man making a beautiful scroll, the famous turtles, beautiful flowers, birds and more.  A woman was selling small items and I got a nice small bike to use for my summer display,  it even had a real chain.  This is a great way to explore this special area.  I am glad we did not miss it.
highlights: watched a man making a beautiful scroll

author: Andrea L
title: Very characteristic
original_content: The Ngoc Son Temple is one of the classic visits to make in the center of Hanoi, especially for its beautiful location: it is located on a small island in the northern part of Hoan Kiem Lake and is connected to the shore by the characteristic red The Huc bridge, one of the most photographed spots in the city.The temple dates back in its current form mainly to the 19th century and is dedicated to various figures of the Vietnamese tradition, including General Tran Hung Dao, a national hero famous for his victories against the Mongol invasions in the 13th century. The complex reflects an interesting mix of Confucian, Taoist, and traditional Vietnamese religious influences.Inside there are altars, incense, and various rooms dedicated to worship. Particularly curious is the presence of a preserved specimen of one of the enormous turtles that lived in the lake, animals linked to the famous legend of the returned sword that gave its name to Hoàn Kiếm, the "Lake of the Returned Sword."The entrance ticket costs 50,000 VND and during our visit we had to pay in cash.The visit does not take much time, but it is interesting and, above all, allows you to enter one of the symbolic places of Hanoi. It is also very evocative to simply cross the red bridge and observe the lake and the city from there.Considering also that it is located in the heart of Hanoi and a few steps from the Old Quarter, it is a visit that I definitely recommend including during a walk around Hoàn Kiếm Lake.
highlights: interesting mix of Confucian, Taoist, and traditional Vietnamese religious influences

author: sannamoo
title: Small temple in Hoan Kiem
original_content: Ngoc Son Temple in Hanoi is a prominent spiritual site situated on a small island in Hoan Kiem Lake. Accessible by crossing the red Huc Bridge, it venerates national heroes and scholars, offering a peaceful retreat from the bustling city. An entry fee of approximately $2 applies, as it is not a free attraction.Notable features include a glass case displaying a large, taxidermied softshell turtle from the lake, a powerful symbol of national independence, spiritual protection, longevity, and wisdom. This connects the site to the legendary Golden Turtle God, who played a crucial role in defending against foreign invaders.The main shrines feature altars dedicated to the military leader Tran Hung Dao and esteemed scholars, underscoring the site’s historical and cultural importance.

author: William Tan
title: a special pagoda
original_content: Hanoi is a city rich in historical landmarks and stories. This particular pagoda is very special, as it preserves the actual remains of a giant turtle inside. A lot of people come here to pray
highlights: preserves the actual remains of a giant turtle inside

author: The Wandering Pair
title: Culture, History and Serenity on the Lake
original_content: We visited Ngoc Son Temple this afternoon, and our leg covers came in handy again following our earlier excursion to another religious site.Crossing the red bridge over the lake to the island temple, leaving the busy Hanoi streets behind us, made for a beautiful transition to a more spiritual place. The temple itself is wonderfully decorated, with flowing plants and wildlife to see all around. We spotted herons and turtles across the lake, while the courtyard featured huge, brightly coloured floral displays.The external pagoda, with its Vietnamese flag flying proudly above it, made for quite a spectacle. Turning to look out across the water towards the ancient tower was equally stunning.Moving inside the temple, signs highlighting the no-photography rule were not exactly being adhered to by most visitors. Naturally, we respected the request and took no photographs ourselves. The atmosphere inside the main temple was peaceful and reverent, with people actively praying, making it a truly memorable experience.Alongside the main temple is a small outbuilding where two preserved turtles are housed in special display cases. The information boards explained that only six of these turtles remain in the wild, and the story of the turtle providing a sword to an ancient king made for particularly interesting reading.A cultural must when visiting Hanoi. At 100,000 VND (£2.82) for both of us, it was excellent value and well worth the time we spent exploring the island.
drawbacks: no-photography rule not being adhered to by most visitors
highlights: beautiful transition to a more spiritual place
stunning view of the ancient tower
peaceful and reverent atmosphere inside the main temple

author: CarolineLanc

original_content: Iconic temple on Hoan Kiem Lake. Worth a visit but be prepared for crowds. Very scenic setting.

author: Dimenson X
title: So Beautiful 🩷🩷
original_content: The Ngoc Son Temple is located on an island on Hanoi's Hoan Kiem Lake in the middle of the city.Built in the 19th century, the temple is a blend of Confucianism, Taoism, and Buddhism.The temple primarily honors General Trần Hưng Đạo (who led the 13th-century resistance against Mongol invaders), Văn Xương Đế Quân (the God of Literature and Education), and La To (the patron saint of medicine).To access the temple you need to cross the red footbridge, the Húc.

author: Jeremy C
title: Island Temple
original_content: Cross the very pretty Red Bridge which in itself gives excellent views of the lake and enter a compact and typically beautiful temple that is frequented by worshippers and tourists alike. It is a little haven within the bustling city and a chance to get away from it for a little while.

author: Richard T
title: Great to mix with the locals going about their religious beliefs
original_content: Extremely busy during New Year. We were advised by the hotel to take care due to pick pockets but we saw no evidence at all. Worth the wait to go over the walkway to the Temple. Many people doing their New Year picture posing. A very religious facility for the locals, with many making offerings, burning “money” etc, adding to the local emphasis. The local experts were painting their messages on red paper to signify happiness, good luck etc.We were only there 30 minutes or so, but a great local experience.

author: Talant2007
title: Ngoc Son Temple
original_content: The temple is built on Ngoc Island on Hoan Kiem Lake in Hanoi. Originally existing in the 11th century, it later declined. In the present saw built in the 19th century.

author: Francois T

author: GlobetrotterMSK

author: Wanderlustaustralia
title: Beautiful and filled with plants
original_content: This is a really beautiful temple with lots of plants. It is kept really clean, and the entry fee is reasonable. Recommend a visit!

author: TheLush101
title: Famous turtle and temple
original_content: As others have right said, it's busy here day and night. You pay a small amount to be able to cross the red bridge and head to the temple. Inside there is some information about the story of the turtle and the reason that the temple was built to say thank you. The bridge looks more picturesque at night due to the lighting, so probably best to time your visit around dusk so that the temple is still open, grab a drink / food nearby, then take some photos at night.

author: Eli
title: Interesting backstory
original_content: A temple on Hoan Kiem Lake. Quite peaceful and has that classic old charm. Learning more about its historical backstory was really interesting and surprising. If you’re traveling solo or on your own, you can use the Travellens app to explore it deeper.

author: NilsM73
title: Mostly for the evening photo

author: Stanley H
title: Holy Land of Hanoi, Cambridge
original_content: Since ancient times, Hanoi has been the political center of Vietnam. So, most of the things related to ancient dynasties can be found in Hanoi and its surroundings. This time, on New Year's Eve, come to the Old Town of Hanoi. Our team did get to the last attraction of the journey, the Yui Temple. This is a temple in the lake of Tambor. The temple is dedicated to Wen Cheng and the heroes of the 13th-century Dauphin army. Of course, the most important thing is to look at the specimens of reptile already extinct in 2016.The location of the Yuzhou Temple is Yuzhou Lake near the old town of Hanoi. The correct location is one of the lake islands in this lake. There are also two islands in Lake Cambridge. One is the home of the "Yu Mountains" "Yu Mountains", the second is a small island called "Turtle Tower". "Turtle Island" is one only for the wild animals in the lake and swordsmen to enjoy.The former "Yu Mountain Temple", was built during the Chinese dynasty (about the 13th and 14th centuries). But today we are visiting the Yujing Temple, which was built in 1865 during the Mongol Dynasty (about the 19th century) under the supervision of the then Chunxian Chunxian.There is a building called the "peat tower" in "Yu mountain temple". On the tower are inscribed three large words "Writing the sky". A tribute to literature.After passing the "peat tower", there was a door called the "grand tower". This door is a stand. Since there is a "pen", it is necessary to "Ink" so there is such a relative design.After passing through the "Great Canyon", we officially reached the scope of the "Yu Mountain Temple". We go to the lake side to see. That day, it was evening, and it was the evening of Easter. The entire surrounding area of Cambridge has been preparing for the Annual Party. The lights taken and the lights of the surrounding buildings make the night view of Lake Cambridge more colorful.And where we enjoy the lake view, it is located in front of the temple, a building called "Town Booth". There is not much information on this apartment on the Internet. In short, this is the best location to enjoy the whole of Cambridge.And "Toh Moon Building" is the inner gate of "Toh Moon Temple", which means tower that can receive the moonlight.Go to the main temple of "Yu Shan Temple". The first temple on the north side is dedicated to Chen Hengdu and Wen Cheng. In the temple, the knives are believed to be the royal members and generals known for defeating the invasion of the Yunnan army three times.Not very interested in Vietnam's ancient history. So, what we spend the most time admiring is the two remains of the sword that are preserved in the Temple.And the sword, also called Lili. According to the classification of Vietnamese scholars, this is a species of spleen. Today, the last remaining swordfish died in 2016. The same samples as those that died in 1967 were made and kept in the temple. It also means that even swordfish have been extinct.But according to international research, swordfish are the same kind. There are only 4-5 known live spots.A fisherman caught a ancient sword while fishing in the lake of the Rainbow Marine Network, with the words "Good day" inscribed on it, and the fisherman handed it to the leader of the Liberal Army at the time, Li Li Li, and then Li obtained a matching hand of the sword, so they assembled a sword. During the Decade of War, Liu Liu continued to carry the sword around him, eventually defeating the army of the Jin and establishing the post-Li Dynasty. Shortly thereafter, Lili came to the Lake of the Marine to ride the boat to play, and a giant lion emerged from the lake and sank under the sword. Lili believes that this is the sword given to him by the giant during the war against the Ming to help him defeat the enemy, and the giant seems to be willing to take back the sword after the restoration of peace under the sky. Lili decided to rename the Lake of the Navy to "Lake of Cambridge," which meant to return the Sword of God.A pleasant tour. Learn about the ancient history of Vietnam and see the beast of Vietnam. Also in the temple to enjoy the beautiful view of the Cambridge lake. It can be said that it is three. highlights: Learn about the ancient history of Vietnam
enjoy the beautiful view of the Cambridge lake

author: lilybt
title: It's changed a lot.
original_content: This shrine was built on an island in the northwestern part of Hoan Kiem Lake. It started its history as a temple and has continued to exist as Guandi Mausoleum, then as a temple, then as an educational publishing institution. After crossing the red bridge called Asahisashi Bridge, you reach the small main hall, which is scattered with various gates and towers. It displays stuffed turtles decorated with legends of saving the country, giving a sense of the city's history as it developed into a city center. The admission fee, or rather, the admission fee, was raised significantly the year before last to 50 thousand VND (about 300 yen).
highlights: stuffed turtles decorated with legends of saving the country
practical_tips: cross the red bridge called Asahisashi Bridge

author: VoyagerZ5533OA
title: A bubble of peace if you come early
original_content: I was a child when I first heard about the legend of the turtle, the king, and the magic sword. As an adult coming here with my own family, it felt a bit surreal, new yet nostalgic. We came here on the first and last days of our Hanoi visit, and the key is to come when they first open, at 7 am. The tranquility you'll find here in the early hours offers a welcomed reprieve from the Old Quarter's nighttime crowd and cacophony. Take your time, observe the markings engraved in the rocks as you first walk in, and notice other forms of life here. You may even have a cat come sit--just sit--next to you when there's no one around. Also try to spot a (live) turtle or two, and tell yourself that it's a sign of good luck. If you still believe in magic, this is the place to keep it alive.
highlights: observe the markings engraved in the rocks
practical_tips: try to spot a (live) turtle or two

author: BorntocruiseUK
title: Worth a look
original_content: The bridge is beautiful and gives great views over the lake. It’s only a small entrance fee to go in and I believe it’s worth it. You only need about 40 mins to go in and walk all the way around.Unfortunately it was raining whilst we were there but it didn’t really spoil it but made the bridge a tad slippery.The toilet if you need one is on the far side of the island.

author: Kishor D
title: Worth a visit
original_content: Oldest bridge in Hanoi. Beautiful view of the lake from bridge. Very reasonable entrance fee. Beautiful temple inside. Cannot take photos inside the temple but everything surrounding you can. Worth visiting
highlights: Beautiful view of the lake from bridge
practical_tips: Cannot take photos inside the temple but everything surrounding you can

author: CJ
title: Good history and sightseeing and really peaceful
original_content: Very nice temple and a good place to come and learn more about the history of Hà Nội and Ho Kiếm. They have the two turtles displayed which hold a key significance for the people in this region. It costs 50,000VD entry and is a good spot for sightseeing. We visited at night time which is quieter. You get a panoramic view of the city.
highlights: good place to come and learn more about the history

author: akio9jp
title: The Tortoise and the Hero

author: Higuma 2017
title: Try to figure that out.
original_content: This is all about the turtle(s). And worthwhile the visit. A rather average, but reasonably cute temple, displaying two dead turtles, quite massive, to be honest. These poor creatures used to live at the bottom of that lake in the middle of Hanoi. Their kind is gone, forever. Their stories can be found on the wall, available in English. Although Vietnamese scholars like to classify them as a unique local species, they are part of the Yangtze Giant Softshell Turtle species... which does not make the whole survival of the species any more bright, as there are only two known individuals alive in the whole planet - both males. Back to the temple, displayed in each of the two glass boxes, there is an item, quite unrecognisable. Looks like a clawed hand. In one of them there is an explanation that suggests it's the reproductive apparel.  Check that and try to figure it out... If those two specimens on display were indeed males and those things are what is suggested, no wonder all the females are dead and the species is functionally extinct.

author: Dinh Trung-Tin
title: A Cultural Jewel in the Heart of Tourist Bustle
original_content: My visit to Ngoc Son Temple in the middle of Hoan Kiem Lake in Hanoi was a memorable experience despite the crowds of tourists. This temple offers a fascinating insight into Vietnamese history and culture, and there are less crowded corners worth exploring.The temple itself is an architectural gem, with its glazed tile roofs, detailed carvings and elegant pagodas. The view of the lake from the Huc Bridge that leads to the temple is breathtaking, creating an atmosphere of serenity even among the crowds of visitors.One of the disadvantages of this place is indeed the tourist crowds, especially during peak hours. However, I found that as I explored the back part of the temple, there were fewer people and a more peaceful ambiance. This allowed me to better appreciate the spirituality of the place and take wonderful photos without the crowds.The history and cultural significance of Ngoc Son Temple is fascinating, and there are informative signs that provide interesting details. I also enjoyed the collection of historical artifacts on display in the temple.
highlights: fascinating insight into Vietnamese history and culture
practical_tips: explore the back part of the temple for a more peaceful ambiance

title: Beauty in simplicity - visit in the morning
original_content: If you want a more authentic experience at this temple, visit right at opening. Locals come here to make their offerings before continuing their work day, so the morning is when you will witness people releasing birds to the sky, of bags of eels to the lake. You will see piles of incense smoking at every alter, and offering jar in between. You will see the hearth at the back smoldering with the papers of so many students, or symbolic money, or other papers. You will also witness the opening of the temple, the gardeners watering the simple-yet-beautiful gardens surrounding the small island complex. It's a different place than the mid-afternoon tourist destination. I also recommend walking by in the evening, to see the island, and its neighboring red bridge, glowing in the night and reflecting magically on the surface of the water. Quite the sight.

Translated: "Temple of the Jade Mountain" is accessed by the beautiful red, wooden Huc Bridge which spans from the banks of Hoan Kiem Lake, to the Temple on Jade Island. author: digitalroc
title: Temple of the Jade Mountain
original_content: Ngoc Son Temple translates into the Temple of the Jade Mountain and resides on an island in Hoan Kiem Lake in Hanoi.  The temple was built to commemorate the 13th century military leader Tran Hung Dao who was known for battling the Chinese Yuan Dynasty.  The cost was only 30K VND, there was no line up, and it wasn’t too busy.  If you are near the lake, take the time out of your day to check it out, as it makes for some good photo opportunities.

author: Govindan N
title: Beautiful Place
original_content: This temple is located in the old quarter on a small island in the northern part of Hoan Kiem Lake. To enter the temple, we will have to go over The Huc Bridge, a beautiful red-painted wooden bridge. Ngoc Son temple -Pagoda is peaceful and quite. The island on which the temple stands is called Jade Island. This is a Buddhist temple.The turtle displayed inside Ngoc Son Temple is one of 4 giant turtles which lived in Hoan Kiem Lake. The turtle is attached to the legend King Le Loi, who led Vietnamese people to fight back and expel Ming invaders from the national border. According to legend, Le Loi had the sword named Heaven's Will given to him by the Golden Turtle God, Kim Qui. He used this sword in the battle against the aggressors.Not long after Vietnam got independence, Le Loi was out boating on the lake. Suddenly the Golden Turtle God surfaced, prompting Le Loi to return Heaven's Will. The Golden Turtle God got back the sword and disappeared into depths of the lake. Le Loi then renamed the lake Hoan Kiem Lake, meaning “The Lake of the Returned Sword”.Ngoc Son Temple Entrance Fee:Adults: 30.000 VND Children: 15.000 VND Ngoc Son Temple Opening HoursMonday – Friday: 7 am to 6 pmSaturday and Sunday: 7 am to 9 pm
practical_tips: check the entrance fee (Adults: 30.000 VND, Children: 15.000 VND)

author: Laura T
title: Felt tricked as paid entrance fee but whole island was under construction - not worthwhile visiting at the moment
original_content: The temple sits on a small island in the centre of Hoan Kiem Lake and is linked by a beautiful red wooden bridge, which would make a lovely background for photos apart from the never-ending hoards of crowds!! Soo soooo soooo busy! :-SCurrently there is a LOT of restoration work taking place at the temple, so a visit in late December was not worthwhile, we would recommend to wait until the construction has finished before you try to visit. We were annoyed as there were no signs about the maintenance and you are not told when you buy the tickets, so even though the tickets were very little money (about £1 each), we still felt rather ripped off! and certainly wouldn't have bothered buying the tickets if we had known. There are free clean toilets at the rear of the temple if you do buy a ticket. There was really nothing to see at the temple on the island in December, as completely taken over by construction. You could see the giant turtle in the glass display cabinet, but that was all. I was rather annoyed as there is literally nothing to see, except a couple of bonsai and a view across the lake, which you can see from anywhere... That is until my husband discovered a back door through to the temple near to the toilets! There was no-one else inside here, so not sure if we were really allowed! but inside the temple was nice, brightly coloured with fresh coats of paint... Just a shame we couldn't see the flower gardens or large tree garden mentioned in previous reviews or view the temple from the front... and there were still crowds and crowds of people queuing to get across the bridge... to see nothing very much!The bridge that leads to the Ngoc Soc Temple is illuminated at night and very photogenic so just walk around and take photos - most people seem to hang around on the bridge without buying tickets to take photos, which is fair enough... but... the bridge is just crazy crazy busy all the time! :-STickets are purchased from a booth at the left hand side just after crossing the bridge for 30,000VND (£1) each. Open 7am to 6pm weekdays and until 9pm on weekends. We would recommend admiring the stonework and sculptures before the bridge and walking on the red wooden bridge to take photos, but then turning back at the ticket booth - at least until the extensive construction has finished.

author: David B
title: Local History & Legends
original_content: Ngoc Son Temple, or the  'Temple of the Jade Mountain', is Hanoi's most visited temple.It is small island in the northern part of Hoan Kiem Lake, reached  by an elegant red bridge of classical Vietnamese construction. The temple is dedicated to General Tran Hung Dao (who defeated the Mongols in the 13th century), La To (patron saint of physicians) and the scholar Van Xuong.There is also a large taxidermied turtle in a glass case, homage to the legend of King Le Loi returning the sword he used to vanish the Chinese invaders to the turtle in the lake.

author: AMC286
title: The Temple of the Jade Mountain
original_content: The Temple of the Jade Mountain locally known in Vietnam as Den Ngoc Son is located on Hoan Kiem Lake in central Hanoi, Vietnam.  Being built on the Jade Islet and dedicated to Confucian Taoist philosophers and the national hero, Tran Hung Dao, the small temple was expanded in 1865.From the shore, the Welcoming Morning Sunlight Bridge leads to the island.  Buildings of the temple include the Pen Tower, the ink slab, the Moon Contemplation Pavilion and the Pavilion against Waves, all of which have symbolic meaning.Show respect to these temples by dressing appropriately as the locals and tour guides will remind tourists before they go to the place.

author: blackeaglejim
title: Hoan Kiem's island temple
original_content: The island called Jade Mountain, at the top end of Hoan Kiem Lake, now is the site of a temple dedicated to Tran Hung Dao, the 13th century general who led the Vietnamese defeat of three Mongol invasions. It's a good example of how Vietnamese deify their national heroes.  In the 17th-18th centuries the island was the site of a palace of the ruling Trinh Lords, who watched naval exercises on the lake which, at that time, was bigger and still connected to the Red River.  It was cut off from the river in the early 19th century.  The island is accessible via a beautiful, comb-shaped, red wooden bridge, built in the 19th century.  Hoan Kiem Lake used to be the abode of very large turtles that lived for centuries.  A preserved sample of one of these is in the temple compound.

highlights: good example of how Vietnamese deify their national heroes

author: santo t
title: Icon of the lake

This small island is accessible by the iconic Huc Bridge or Rising Sun Bridge, a charming red painted wooden bridge  The pagoda is also guarded by two towering posts decorated with Chinese writing. The lake and temple are probably the most famous places in Hanoi Old Quarter to enjoy the surrounding view and are a great place to sit back and watch the locals.Ticket to visit sold at the left hand side before crossing the bridge for VND 30000 / adult, open from 7am to 6pm. The lake and the temple offer plenty of trees and shaded spots to escape from the surrounding busy city streets. This site is not too far from the other famous attraction, at the opposite side of Thang Long Water Puppet.

This 45 minute indoor show is it is truly a unique Vietnamese art form (depicting scenes from rural life and episodes of national history). The puppets are controlled by puppeteers arge rods and hiding behind a bamboo screen.at the back of the pool. author: The Wandering Pair
title: Chaos in the Foyer, Magic on the Water
original_content: The purchase of the tickets was straightforward through Tripadvisor. However, on arrival, things felt rather chaotic. Organisation appeared to be in short supply and the crowd gathering outside created some concern, particularly for Megan, as there was a real risk of people being crushed in the rush to enter. Thankfully, we made it inside safely in the end.Once seated, we quickly discovered that the theatre makes very efficient use of its available space. The seats are quite cramped, so if you’re particularly tall or broad-shouldered, you may find yourself getting to know your neighbours better than expected.As English visitors, some of the folktales were difficult to follow in detail, and we found the audio guide a little sparse at times. However, this did not detract significantly from the overall experience. The skill and artistry involved in the water puppetry are genuinely impressive, and it is easy to appreciate the tradition even when some of the finer story details are lost in translation.The live music and singing added greatly to the atmosphere and authenticity of the performance. The musicians were excellent, and the cast appeared to be thoroughly enjoying themselves, which helped make the show even more engaging.Overall, we thoroughly enjoyed the performance and would recommend spending an evening experiencing this unique aspect of Vietnamese culture.Audio guides are available in other languages for 50,000 VND per person.Tickets cost us 858,156VND (£24.42), when we collected the tickets from Viator we noticed the price listed was 200,000VND each so for both it was 400,000VND (£11.20) We checked this against the sales desk and can confirm it is cheaper to buy from the theatre than online.
highlights: skill and artistry involved in the water puppetry
live music and singing added greatly to the atmosphere
practical_tips: buy tickets from the theatre for cheaper price

author: Tom&NikkiTravel
title: A Great Experience - Worth It? Seating Tips, Audio Guide & What to Expect
original_content: We purchased our tickets online via GetYourGuide, which was a smooth process overall. However, it’s worth noting that ticket collection is not at the theatre itself—you’ll need to pick them up from a location approximately a 5–10 minute walk away, so allow a little extra time for this.Our show was scheduled for 9:15pm, and we recommend arriving at least 15 minutes early to secure your seat. While we had pre-booked front-row tickets (Rows A–E), seat selection is not assigned in advance. This can be slightly frustrating, as you might expect reserved seating when booking ahead.If you’re not seated within the first two rows, be prepared for potential obstructions. Audience members moving around or using phones and cameras can impact your view. For reference, we were seated in Row D (Seats 7 and 8), and we’ve included a photo to give a realistic perspective of the view.We highly recommend renting the audio guide (50,000 VND per person), especially for English speakers, as the performance is conducted in Vietnamese. It adds valuable cultural context and enhances the overall experience. That said, the audio volume can be quite low compared to the live music and sound effects, which occasionally makes it difficult to follow.The show itself is of a very high standard—engaging, unique, and deeply rooted in Vietnamese culture. At around 45 minutes long, it’s the perfect length, and the seating is reasonably comfortable throughout.Overall, this is a highly enjoyable and worthwhile experience, and we’d absolutely recommend adding it to your itinerary when visiting  Hanoi

Audio volume can be quite low
highlights: Unique and deeply rooted in Vietnamese culture

author: cmtran7393
title: Fun unique experience
original_content: Pretty cheap price for a 50’ culture show.To be honest I’m Vietnamese but I barely understood what they were singing 😅. I think the sound system had some echo it was hard to follow. Also high pitched opera voices added to the difficulty. But the highlight was they were playing all the traditional instruments in sync!The show mostly consisted of short scenes depicting daily life in villages predominantly of rice field culture. People used to fish, swim, play, plow the fields with buffaloes, herding ducks and looted by hungry fox, racing boats, telling lores to each other…However I agree with some comments here that there’s no consistent storyline throughout. Short scenes just told a quick fun snapshot of what the life used to be in the past along with the mythology about Hoan Kiem Lake. Then at the end magical creatures representative of the Vietnamese culture  dancing : Dragon, Turtle, Phoenix and Lion/Tiger. That’s why the show seemed fragmented and random.I admire the hard work and talent of the artisans and musicians. They work very hard behind the scene im telling you!Overall it was a fun and silly show 🥳. I think this was a no bs show as the scenes were very fast paced and lively. I went when I was in primary school and now revisited. I give it 8 out of 10. It was quite enjoyable and unique of Vietnamese communal and agricultural culture.P/S: after that you can walk to the nearby street food and try the papaya salad with beef jerky and some fresh spring rolls 😋 you won’t regret !
drawbacks: hard to follow due to echo in sound system
highlights: unique of Vietnamese communal and agricultural culture

Redemption was simple — just pick up the physical ticket at the Klook counter right in front of the theatre.The performance itself is highly entertaining, showcasing Vietnam’s traditional water puppet art. author: lilybt
title: Advance ticket purchase is recommended
original_content: It is located on the shores of Hoan Kiem Lake, the most prestigious and large-scale facility of several floating puppet theaters in Hanoi. We get information about long lines to buy tickets and pre-purchase them via OTA (kNanchala). It is an advantage to be able to book with a specific performance time, and with so many tourists lining up at the ticket booth on the day, it is a great choice for those who want to put their itinerary together. However, it’s better to understand that you need to visit a local agent about five minutes away from the theater to exchange paper tickets, and that the price is somewhat higher than buying at a ticket booth, whether it’s a commission for the agent. The ticket types are divided into three levels, near-middle and far, toward the stage (or rather, the pool), and the near price is more than twice as much as the far price, but the feeling is so realistic that the doll splashes when diving into the water like a 'sand coat,' and as I said, it costs about 1,300 yen in Japanese currency, so I recommend purchasing the top-of-the-line ticket.The play is a legend of the founding of Vietnam, but you don't have to have an understanding of the language to enjoy it to some extent, and you can kind of understand the story. I felt it was quite a good entertainment.

author: Megan B
title: Unique and Entertaining Experience: Hanoi Water Puppet Show
original_content: The Hanoi Water Puppet Show is a must-see cultural experience when visiting the city. It is a traditional Vietnamese art form that combines puppetry, live music, and storytelling, all performed over water. The show is about an hour long and takes place in a charming theater with comfortable seating and a good view from almost anywhere.The puppets are beautifully crafted, and the skilled puppeteers control them from behind a screen, making them glide, dance, and interact on the water. The stories are based on Vietnamese folklore, legends, and rural life, giving a fascinating glimpse into the country’s traditions. Even if you do not understand Vietnamese, the expressive movements of the puppets and the live music make it easy to follow along.The live traditional music, played with authentic Vietnamese instruments, adds to the immersive experience. The musicians perform on the side of the stage, creating a rich atmospheric soundtrack to the show.Tickets are reasonably priced, and it is best to book in advance as the show is popular, especially in the evenings. It is a great experience for all ages, entertaining, cultural, and something you will not find anywhere else. If you are in Hanoi, the water puppet show is definitely worth checking out.

There are a dozen scenes, the most beautiful is the dance of dragons breathing fire, cute that of children playing in the water, even duck hunting, the most auspicious scene is that of the four celestial animals. The puppets are skillfully moved by horizontal tie rods hidden under the water.
highlights: scenically depicts episodes of rural life
cute that of children playing in the water

author: OnAir38937315268
title: Fun Show, Great Visuals.
original_content: Fun, creative show, you get an interesting view of Vietnamese culture. It's all in Vietnamese, so it's hard to follow. Just enjoy the impressive visual effects. Shows are around 50 minutes.
drawbacks: It's all in Vietnamese, so it's hard to follow

author: Cosmo550
title: Easy to follow show in Vietnamese
original_content: Fun show, all in Vietnamese but for each section an English description is given on the screen beside the stage, could follow the show easily. Amazing musicians

author: S&O
title: Traditionell in Hanoi
original_content: We were in the afternoon performance. Very well attended. Interesting and definitely a little different. Relaxed and relaxing atmosphere.

author: sophiegrace24
title: Great Cultural Experience in Hanoi
original_content: What a fantastic cultural experience while staying in Hanoi. We booked the tickets through Get Your Guide and the pickup process from an office round the corner from the theatre was super easy.The live musicians and performers during the show were incredible.I would highly recommend getting the audio guide for some context on the stories being portrayed as this was really interesting
practical_tips: book tickets through Get Your Guide

author: Clive and Clair... B
title: Wonderful Show 🎪
original_content: We had an evening in Hanoi, so we decided to book tickets 🎟️ for the Water Puppet Theatre. On arrival we also hired the audio guide so we could follow what was going on in English. Overall a unique cultural experience which was thoroughly enjoyable. It lasts slightly less than an hour and is excellent value for money..
practical_tips: hire audio guide for English translation

author: MTAA
title: Unique experience
original_content: Fun experience at the puppet show. Provides interesting insight into Vietnamese culture through this unique artform.

author: Keelyimps
title: Very clever and very good.
original_content: As good as I thought. So cleverly done by the puppeteers. The traditional Vietnamese music was also lovely to hear played on instruments I hadn’t heard before and the singing was very unusual. I really liked this and would recommend anyone to go.

author: Christina W
title: Beyond Boring
original_content: The only people at the show were on vacation tours, because no one else would ever go to see this show. I'm convinced that the tour companies and the puppet people have reached some deal to fill the seats. I wish that I could get my 90 minutes back. The truth is, I spend the time clearing out my email account.

author: Heather S
title: Book early to get tickets!
original_content: When we arrived in the morning, we were lucky to get seats for the last showing at 9.15pm.  There are around 5 showings a day starting at 3pm and we decided to go for the VIP seats at the front for 200k Dong.  You don’t need an audio guide in my opinion.  The show only lasted around 50 minutes and it was lovely to see the clever use of music and puppetry.  A must see in Hanoi.
highlights: clever use of music and puppetry
practical_tips: You don’t need an audio guide

author: Deano1967
title: Traditional Vietnamese culture
original_content: I wasn't sure about going to see the water puppet show, thinking it wouldn't be my kind of thing but am happy to say I was totally wrong.The live music is played by very accomplished musicians who create a wonderful atmosphere for the supremely skilled puppeteers. The tale of legends and history contains humour, drama and pyrotechnics, narrated in Vietnamese with an audio guide available for those who wish to follow the story.Totally recommended and make sure you go for the more expensive tickets towards the front of the theatre.
highlights: live music is played by very accomplished musicians
practical_tips: go for the more expensive tickets towards the front of the theatre

author: jwg2
title: Management should provide guidelines for phone etiquette during the show
original_content: The water puppet show was very good and I'm glad we saw it. However, the experience was badly marred by a young mother in front of us who had a phone on a selfie-stick that she held up over her head to video the show. Many others in the audience also held their phones over their heads, which partially blocked the view of audience members behind them. The disrespectful use of phones was so distracting and annoying that I considered asking for my entrance fee to be refunded, but I did not do that. I think the theater management should provide brief guidelines at the beginning of each show asking the audience to respect the other audience members by not raising their phones above their heads.
highlights: water puppet show was very good
practical_tips: ask theater management to provide guidelines at the beginning of each show

author: Liliane M
title: IT'S WORTH IT TO GET AN IDEA BUT NOTHING MORE
original_content: Before you start if you want to see the show and be able to take pictures I recommend buying front row tickets because further back it is difficult because many people start recording and it is really annoying.The show lasted about 40 minutes. On both sides of the stage are musicians with their instruments, and singers.I personally found the scenarios very childish and a little repetitive.The puppet management is done with a stick that goes from side to side and sinks into the water.It is respectable the effort made to preserve the tradition but it did not finish convincing me.
highlights: respectable the effort made to preserve the tradition

author: Inger B
title: Magical moments on water
original_content: The show was a mesmerizing blend of tradition and artistry. As the puppets danced on the water, we were transported to a world of legends and folklore. The music was enchanting, and the skill of the puppeteers was incredible. We laughed, we cheered, and we were completely captivated. It was a unique experience that brought us closer together, sharing in the wonder of Vietnamese culture.
highlights: mesmerizing blend of tradition and artistry
skill of the puppeteers was incredible

author: Shinester888
title: A great show!
original_content: We dropped in to check out the show. This was fun with historical flavour. Sure, it was not in English; however it did not matter! Weboth enjoined the show and musical backing! The seats towards the front are 200kVD. up the is 100k, and middle 150k. It was fun!

author: Alexandra N
title: Lovely
original_content: A funny cute experience that's not like anything I've seen before. Easy to interpret what is going on, don't think you need to pay extra for the audio guide. Not too long. Very entertaining. Nice to hear and see traditional Vietnamese craft and music.
practical_tips: don't think you need to pay extra for the audio guide

author: Tegan C
title: Water Puppet Show with children
original_content: The puppet show is roughly an hour long - we choose not to have audio translation devices and we're easily able to follow along with the story and enjoy the show. If you have children, make sure you grab the seat booster as you walk in yo take your seats.
highlights: easily able to follow along with the story and enjoy the show
practical_tips: grab the seat booster as you walk in to take your seats

author: Otto S
title: Good visit if you have free time in Hanoi!
original_content: Puppet show in the water. It tells the story of Vietnamese, from its ancestral beginning to traditions of Vietnamese society.I really liked that all the melodies were live and the work quite professional.We didn’t have it in mind to visit but we ended up going and left satisfied I recommend 100%, pay the $2 audio guide since the work is in Vietnamese and without audio guide, nothing is understood.We saw how many people were leaving because they didn't know what was happening. Recommended but also not essential
drawbacks: Nothing is understood without audio guide
People leaving because they didn't know what was happening
practical_tips: Go with an audio guide if you don't speak Vietnamese

author: Sussanne P
title: Enjoyable and worth a visit for the experience
original_content: Worth going , great little show , Seating uncomfortable especially if you have someone tall sitting in front of you .  very hot inside the theater also. Take a fan !Enjoyable overall for the price

author: Ashwini Marathe
title: Don't forget the audio guide!!
original_content: You need to book these tickets in advance as they get sold off quickly. Also we forgot to book our ticket with the English audio guide. In hindsight, I think it would have elevated our experience as the kids got restless since they couldn't understand anything. Anyways, the management needs to make a note that we  had booked deluxe seats but we were made to sit in the standard section. Their ground staff needs to be better trained. The actual show was about the different aspects of life in the ancient times. The puppets were awesome and kudos to the artists. Definitely a must watch but with an audio guide!
drawbacks: forgot to book English audio guide
made to sit in standard section
ground staff needs to be better trained

author: Gareth H
title: Skip the show tickets via Agoda
original_content: The show was fun, the puppetry is very cool even if we couldn't quite follow all of the stories (it is lots of small fables rather than one continuous story). However, getting in was an issue. We booked "skip the line" tickets through Agoda but when we arrived (15 mins early as per the email) there was no-one to give us a ticket and a long queue to buy a new ticket. The show had already sold out for multiple days by this point. Eventually someone came out to take names but there were so many of us from Agoda, Viagogo, etc that they did not have anywhere near enough tickets and the show began before anyone got in. I was one of the lucky few to only miss ~10 mins of the show, others were turned away for different shows, some on different days. Very stressful experience and really coloured our enjoyment of the evening. I would recommend to only buy paper tickets via the box office well in advance of the show. Definitely avoid any skip the queue tickets as you will likely have to skip the show.
drawbacks: Long queue to buy a new ticket
Some visitors were turned away for different shows
highlights: Lots of small fables rather than one continuous story
practical_tips: Buy paper tickets via the box office well in advance of the show

author: Dan H
title: Traditional Vietnamese entertainment
original_content: We went to the theatre, we booked on the day.    This is a popular attraction, so suggest that you book early or in advance.This show is performed excellently and accompanied with live traditional music and spoken in Vietnamese. There is translation devices available but we didn't hire these and   the show was able to be followed.The show lasts about 50 mins and the theatre is very comfortable.Toilets on site and there is a little shop next door where you can get drinks from at reasonable prices and take in the venue.

author: Brett W
title: Rude tourists
original_content: The actual show was good, very informative and very enjoyable and the music was amazing, however the tourist with a serious lack of theatre etiquette (I’ve never seen anything like it; constant picture taking, constant loud talking and overall a few tourists ruined the experience and were very rude to everyone else in theatre) If the theatre could crack down on these individuals then r would become a 5 star experience.
drawbacks: tourists were rude to everyone else
practical_tips: theatre could crack down on individuals with poor etiquette

author: Sandeep B
title: Give it a miss.

I am sure that you can see the whole show of 30 mins in YouTube.

no announcement to tell not to record

Half the people leave the theatre mid-way

author: Mafalda N

author: Hany G

title: Worth a visit even if you don’t understand the language
original_content: It's something you don't see in Greece, plus the live music and the professionalism of those who participate in the show, but the language is only in Vietnamese, without the possibility of subtitling. It is worth visiting, you can buy water puppets at a relatively good price.

author: Mary M
title: Would be better if filming was banned.
original_content: It was interesting and a good way to pass an hour. It would be better if they stopped people filming. I had two people in front of me with their phones up all the time. It spoilt the whole experience, and I was missing much of what was happening on stage. What little I did see looked good.
drawbacks: missing much of what was happening on stage
highlights: What little I did see looked good

author: 5kidsBrisbane
title: Poorly organized
original_content: I really enjoyed the puppets and the musicians were amazing.  What gave it 3 stars is that even 15 minutes into the performance people are still being let into the theatre . We actually had a whole tour group come in 10 minutes in and had to file past everyone to the back of the theatre.  They were talking the whole way to the back and some kept trying to sit in the front row and were redirected back up stairs.  Another family came 15 minutes in to the second row and kept swapping seats with each other.  The man in front of me couldn’t fit into the seat properly and spent the whole performance frantically waving his phone in the air trying to take video or crouched over the seat in front.  There were no staff in the theatre to stop anything.  It was chaos.  Was it a good performance! Not sure as I could only see a quarter of it.
drawbacks: People were still being let into the theatre 15 minutes into the performance
Tour group came in 10 minutes in and had to file past everyone to the back of the theatre
Chaos in the theatre due to lack of staff

author: Wander65765109162
title: Nice and memorable experience
original_content: A fantastic performance. The story was fun and the atmosphere was good with live music. A very nice experience as warmly recommended.

author: Jim B
title: Charming Theatre Experience
original_content: Unique and delightful theatre experience - the puppets themselves were quite spectacular and the musical accompaniment was brilliant. Would highly recommend this to travellers to Hanoi
highlights: the puppets themselves were quite spectacular
practical_tips: Would highly recommend this to travellers to Hanoi

author: christine s
title: Traditional puppet show,but on water.
original_content: This is a water puppet show in a theatre,very popular and useually packed,in a seated theatre,so pre book and come early,The show is in17 acts,and flows along quickly,telling a story bypuppets controlled by artists under water.A superb traditional puppet show,for the youngand older,for families,with story elling entertainment.Skillfully displayed,good family entertainment.

author: Patty B
title: Near The Mausoleum and Nice
original_content: Since this is part of the area where the mausoleum is, we went to see it.  It was worthwhile, but getting busy.  The grounds are nice and so was the pagoda we saw.

author: Andrea L
title: Lacking atmosphere
original_content: The One Pillar Pagoda is certainly one of the symbols of Hanoi and, being located inside the Ho Chi Minh complex, it is worth stopping to see it during your visit.Personally, however, I did not find it particularly evocative. The pagoda is very small and the large number of visitors makes it difficult to appreciate the religious atmosphere and the significance of the place.When we were there, there was practically a continuous line of people waiting for their turn, mainly to take photographs and selfies in front of the pagoda. Seeing a place of worship turn almost into a photo shoot inevitably makes it lose much of its charm and spirituality.The structure remains unique, however, built on a single pillar in the center of a small pond and with a history that dates back to the 11th century.It is worth seeing if you are already visiting the Ho Chi Minh complex, also because it requires little time, but personally I do not consider it among the most exciting places visited in Hanoi.
drawbacks: difficult to appreciate the religious atmosphere
loses much of its charm and spirituality
practically a continuous line of people waiting
highlights: built on a single pillar in the center of a small pond
history that dates back to the 11th century

author: Travel Girl GR
title: Visit after the mausoleum
original_content: The pagoda is in the mausoleum so you will see it as you go out.It's on a pen that makes it special.No entrance required.

author: David B
title: A pagoda on one pillar
original_content: This pagoda is hidden in a little park. It is surrounded by a pond with lotus flowers. The pagoda can be entered after climbing a steep staircase. Coming down is more challenging. The chapel area is quite beautiful.
drawbacks: Climbing a steep staircase can be challenging
highlights: The chapel area is quite beautiful
practical_tips: Be prepared for a steep staircase

author: David L
title: Inspired by the lotus flower
original_content: The One Pillar Pagoda is one of Hanoi’s most iconic monuments, famous for its unique lotus-flower inspired architecture and deep spiritual significance.  This historic Buddhist temple stands on a single stone pillar and symbolizes the purity, enlightenment and cultural heritage of Vietnam.  Highly recommended.

author: Jeremy C
title: Iconic Little Temple
original_content: Located within the mausoleum complex this novel little temple sits like a lotus flower on a small lake. I would imagine that it is often mobbed with tourists but still worth looking out and taking a moment of contemplation.

author: Talant2007
title: Pagoda on one column
original_content: This pagoda was originally built in 1046g and is an iconic Buddhist temple. The original was destroyed during the French occupation in 1954. But in 1955 it was restored.

author: Steve_Grant1
title: Interesting
original_content: This is an interesting structure clearly based on one pillar. Nive to look at when you are in the overall area with its various sites.

author: FyingKiwi
title: An Enigma
original_content: A rather strange pagoda containing a statue of Buddha in a manner never previously observed by this traveller throughout his extensive travels. While clearly a place of worship, perhaps because of its location, it also appears to be a shrine that is more visited by tour groups than used by locals. Even after subsequently sharing with a local about this pagoda after visiting, resulted in a non-cholent response.
drawbacks: visited by tour groups rather than locals
practical_tips: visit early to avoid tour groups

author: sekjr0521

extracted_spaces: behind one of the major buildings

author: Wanderlustaustralia
title: Beautiful to look at
original_content: We spent about two minutes at this pagoda, as it is very small and you won’t have much luck climbing it with the crowds. It was very beautiful and just a short walk from the Ho Chi Minh Museum, definitely worth a look.

author: TheLush101
title: Peaceful pagoda
original_content: Part of the palace and mausoleum grounds, this is a very serene place. The pond with waterlilies surrounds the pagoda itself. There are steps up to the pagoda itself and it's well organised - you walk up one side, a few people can stand at the top, then you walk back down the other side.

author: francisco r
title: Good experience
original_content: Very nice, right behind the Ho Chi Min mausoleum.Watch out for the tangancito and the very bad coffee. The pagoda and the temple are worth visiting.

author: vodka
title: Nice place
original_content: This is a very beautiful place with many stories attached. Not only is it a place with beautiful and unique architecture, I really like this place.

author: doctorfoxtrot
title: Part of the Ho Chi Minh complex
original_content: Nice to go up and observe. And take photos. Made in observance and respect for the Buddha. Part of the Ho Chi Minh complex where there is tight security coming in

author: linece91
title: Beautiful! Soothing site
original_content: Located in the Mausoleum complex Pagoda in the middle of the water like a lotus flower. You can get a little crowded in July but not insurmountable either The site is quiet and soothing.A real moment of disconnection.You can find bamboo sculptures from this pagoda up to the bixtenco tower

author: Stanley H
title: A Pillar Temple
original_content: Beyond the building blocks of the Presidium, we reached a small temple called the "Temple of One Pillar". The temple was built in 1049. According to the legend, Li Tai Song dreamed of watching the Buddha's hand-to-hand baby, standing on the water pool flower table, soon to be born, it was ordered to build a temple like water flower, so that a column of the temple looked like a water flower. Therefore, the one-pillar temple is dedicated to observance Buddha.Although, the whole journey is definitely a horse ride to see flowers. But in a few short hours, I felt that I went to a history class again. And for Vietnam this part of Hong Kong, Western history will not go deep into teaching an era, to learn more.
drawbacks: whole journey is definitely a horse ride to see flowers
highlights: felt that I went to a history class again

author: divya
title: Tiny and interesting pagoda
original_content: * Entrance : no fees* Parking : could not find a designated parking spot . We parked near the shops/cafes. An old lady charges 20,000 and we only paid 15,000 . She verbally abused us in Vietnamese.No receipt. It’s a scam, she isn’t allowed to charge for parking. * Walkable from Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum. It’s in the same compound. * Scooter hire : 1,50,000 per day (Hired close to our hotel)
drawbacks: Verbal abuse by an old lady
highlights: Walkable from Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum

author: Amy B
title: Wow, Just Wow! A Tiny Treasure with a Big Story...
original_content: Okay, so I took a little detour from exploring the charming streets of Hội An (yes, I know it's a bit of a trip to Hanoi!) and I had to see the One Pillar Pagoda. I'd seen pictures, but honestly, they don't do it justice.Standing there, this little gem of a temple just gracefully rising out of the water... it's kind of magical. It feels ancient and peaceful all at the same time. I loved hearing the story about Emperor Lý Thái Tông and the dream. It makes the whole place feel even more special.It's definitely smaller than I expected, but that almost makes it more intimate. You can really take it all in. I spent a few quiet moments just soaking up the atmosphere. It was a really nice contrast to the energy of the markets and the tailor shops.Honestly, even if you only have a short time in Hanoi (or if you're making a bit of a journey like I did!), make the effort to see the One Pillar Pagoda. It's a little piece of Vietnamese history and beauty that really stuck with me. So glad I made the trip!
highlights: feels ancient and peaceful all at the same time
a really nice contrast to the energy of the markets and the tailor shops
practical_tips: make the effort to see the One Pillar Pagoda
even if you only have a short time in Hanoi

author: TravelingAnnK

author: Nikhat Shahin Khan
title: Interesting structure

author: Alberto G

author: Karen
title: Symbol of Vietnamese culture and history
original_content: One Pillar Pagoda is one of the most famous symbols of Hanoi, with its unique and unmistakable architecture. The pagoda was built in the 11th century under King Ly Thai Tong, with the shape of a lotus blooming on the water. Despite its small area, the surrounding space is very peaceful and airy, creating a relaxing feeling in the middle of the bustling city. This is a great stop for those who want to learn more about the history and ancient architecture of Vietnam
highlights: great stop for learning about history and ancient architecture

author: Dr Kulkarni Mohina S

author: MissL219
title: Beautiful temple
original_content: A lovely little temple in Hanoi. Make sure to cover up when you attend. Some lovely photo opportunities so make sure to take your time.
drawbacks: Some lovely photo opportunities so make sure to take your time

author: Yvonne S
title: Interesting location for a photo
original_content: They tell us this is one of Vietnam’s most iconic Buddhist temples.  The structure is built of wood atop a single, four-foot-wide stone pillar and designed to resemble a lotus flower. The temple’s origins date back to the year 1049. This is located close to the Mausoleum of Ho Che Min.

author: Ludo V
title: A legend is kept alive here
original_content: The Chua Mot Cot (Single Column Pagoda), like the Cot Co, is one of the symbols of Hanoi. Originally built in 1049 under Emperor Ly Thai Tong goose in wood. The concept depicts a lotus flower growing towards the sky from a lotus pond.  She is considered important in connection with the legend that the emperor - who was childless - still had a son here. The post of the pagoda has been restored several times over time, with the original wooden post being replaced by a concrete column with a diameter of 1.25 m. Burned one last time by the French during their retreat in 1954..
drawbacks: Burned one last time by the French during their retreat in 1954
highlights: Depicts a lotus flower growing towards the sky from a lotus pond

author: Shelley M
title: If you are in the area
original_content: In the same area as the mausoleum and worth a visit if you are there.  It is very small and my husband called it the pagoda on a stick.  Had a squirrel in a tree that my son was more interested to watch.  It is cute and has a line of people waiting to go up the stairs to pray.  Had to go through the security and they take lighters and cigarettes off you and they had a huge pile on the counter.  My husband went back in to get his when we were leaving and they just smiled.

author: RoverP
title: Attractive but not original
original_content: This is a bit quirky.  It is unusual and attractive but is not original.  Whilst the original pagoda was built in 1049, what you see is a major restoration built by the French in 1955.  There is little else on the site.

author: SEALS
title: It is a rare historic temple built in the middle of a pond.
original_content: This is an old temple built in an unusually shaped pond located very close to the Ho Chi Minh Corridor. It was a one-day tour of Hanoi's tourist spots, but it was full of worshippers and tourists.

author: Alessandro S
title: Nice place
original_content: The Chua Mot chot Pagoda dates back to 1200. It is also called One Pillar Pagoda and is built of wood and rests on a single stone pillar, has a system of curved bars that support the floor and a curved roof. author: LuizDutraNeto
title: A symbol of Buddhist faith in Hanoi!
original_content: Not far from "Ba Dinh Square", "Ho Chi MInh Mausolem" and "Ho Chi Minh Museum", you will find "Chùa Môt Côt", as "One-Pillar Pagoda" is locally known. It was originally built by Emperor Lý Thái Tông, in 1049, and has been restored many many times along the centuries. Its last restoration dates from 1955, as it was severely destroyed by French Union Forces while withdrawing Vietnam after the First Indochina War. The three square meter wooden pagoda stands on a single stone pillar (1,25 m in diameter) in the middle of a pond and is surrounded by beautiful gardens. The pagoda supposedly ressembles a lotus blossom, a Buddhist symbol of purity, enlightenment and rebirth. Inside "One-Pillar Pagoda", Vietnamese Buddhist deity "Quam Am" is enshrined and brings blessings of fertility and health. Visiting the pagoda can be easily combined with other nearby attractions in the "Ho Chi Minh Complex". Dress properly, queue respectfully and be silent, as prayers take place continuously inside this beautiful small temple. Say a little prayer, burn an incense and may "Quam Am" bless your visit to Vietnam. Enjoy!
drawbacks: Severely destroyed by French Union Forces

author: Kim G
title: Revered Eleventh Century Historic Buddhist Temple (Recreation)
original_content: The One Pillar Pagoda is the most highly revered Vietnamese Buddhist Temple, and architecturally unique.  Originally constructed in 1049 by the Emperor Ly Thai Tong for finally being blessed with a son, the temple resembles a lotus flower (the Vietnamese National Flower), standing on one pillar, as seen in his prophetic dream promising the son.  Rising above a small square pond with lotus flowers (Asian Water Lilies), the Temple is accessed by stone steps which reveal a shrine in its small interior. Unfortunately, the French destroyed the original sacred temple upon their withdrawal from Hanoi in 1954. Nearby are the Ho Chi Minh Mausoleum and the Presidential Palace, just a short stroll away and also worth a visit.
drawbacks: The French destroyed the original sacred temple upon their withdrawal from Hanoi in 1954

author: Diverdanperth
title: Love Ba Dinh Square, the One Pillar Pagoda, but not the taxi scam
original_content: For a sense of this area by night, see my review for Ba Dinh Square, "Visit night AND day but beware the taxi scammers". This review continues that review: Two days after photographing the pink lotus and mausoleum by night, on the morning of our departure for Hoi An, our hotel flagged down a 'legitimate' taxi to take us to The One Pillar Pagoda - imagine our surprise at being dropped at Ba Dinh Square - we hadn't realised how close we'd been two nights earlier. In daylight hours, we had to go through security check points and metal detectors - it was quite a different experience to our 'casual' evening visit. Having reinforced our memories and added a few new ones, we had to get back to the hotel. At the southern end of the square, taxis were coming and going regularly. It had cost us 28 000 dong ($2) to get there in a metered taxi, so we grabbed the one that seemed to be at the front of the queue - this is where the taxi scam story begins: this 'taxi' drove past our hotel with us yelling at him to stop. We realised afterwards he's done it on purpose so we couldn't call for help. He pulled over about 200m down the road and I realised the taxi meter was reading 480 000 dong ($30) !!! YEP. We were in a car set up to LOOK like a taxi with the roof light, the meter, a badge on the side, BUT it was NOT A LEGITIMATE TAXI. My family had exited the taxi, we had a flight to catch, and as I argued, the driver just said, "NEW RATE after 12." I thought about it, I felt bitter about it, afterwards I wondered if I hadn't had the pressure of meeting the airport driver (who was waiting for us!) whether I might have opened the door and screamed, "Help, Police". I paid and was bitter about it for two days – it was an unnecessarily unpleasant end to our pleasant memories of Hanoi. There are similar stories all over Trip Advisor - BE WARNED.Hanoi police traffic-controllers could have an inspector standing at the southern end of Ba Dinh square discouraging these ‘illegitimate’ taxis - even seasoned travelers can be duped. I’ve read that the Vietnamese themselves believe they are a country full of thieves and don't trust each other; however, a flourishing tourism industry demands trust i.e. tourists can trust that the government is doing what it can to stamp out the 'illegitimate' thievery, and the government trusts that the flood of foreign money entering the country in the pockets of tourists will grow. The lesson in Hanoi is: wait for a GREEN Mai Linh TAXI.A few days later in Hoi An, I happily coughed up 600 000 dong in a spur of the moment transaction beside a rice paddy; my entire family sat on a water buffalo in memory of a favourite childhood story about a water buffalo called 'Dahbitse’. Only then, did I finally release the tension the taxi incident had caused in me. I'd spent as much as I'd lost on an experience I valued and was happy to pay it.
drawbacks: Unpleasant end to our pleasant memories
practical_tips: Wait for a GREEN Mai Linh TAXI

author: Wildcat7400
title: A Unique Pagoda
original_content: It is located in Ba Dinh Square & next to Ho Chi Minh’s house on stilts.  It is a Buddhist temple & one of Vietnam’s most iconic temples.  The pagoda was built in 1049 during the reign of Emperor Ly Thai Tong of the Ly Dynasty.  Accordingly, the Emperor was childless for a long time. But he dreamt that he was given a baby boy & not long after, his wife became pregnant.  Thus, it could be said that the temple was built out of gratitude & its structure was similar to what he had seen in his dream.  From a single pillar in the middle, the Buddhist temple was built on a square shape platform constructed in the middle of a pond to resemble a lotus flower.  There are steps going up to the temple & in the temple lies a shrine.  The French army had damaged the structure in 1954.  However, restorations have been made in 1955.  Offerings can be made for those who wish to do so but please dress appropriately as a sign of respect.

drawbacks: The French army had damaged the structure in 1954

original_content: It looks wonderful. However, if you plan go just for the Pagoda, you might feel it was a long trip (from the Old Quarter) for not so much.MAJOR TIP:If you plan on going up the steps, you cannot without a long sleeve shirt and pants.

author: ducpham27
title: Most unique structure
original_content: Architecture represents culture: when Vietnamese appreciate the pure beauty of lotus, they built a pagoda symbolizing this flower

author: KPR1955
title: Really isn't a lot to say about it thats not in its title.
original_content: It's a Pagoda, it sits on one pillar and is absolutely tiny. It will only fit 2 people at a time but you can see 100% of it without going up the stairway. If you are in Hanoi then Im sure you will visit the Ho Chi Minh complex of which this forms a part. On its own it would not be worth the trip from your hotel but since you're here!!There are Pagoda guardians around so please be careful and respectful of your dress and attitude as this is a holy site.
drawbacks: only fit 2 people at a time
not worth the trip from your hotel
highlights: see 100% of it without going up the stairway
practical_tips: be careful and respectful of your dress and attitude

author: Randy P
title: Small
original_content: I would not make a special trip to see this site. It is very small. Give it a quick glance if you happen to be in the area.

author: Peter V
title: A bit too thin
original_content: This is a replica from the one destoyed by the french. And , t is a pity to say, disappointing, both in size as in the new reconstruction. You just walk around , have a good look, and continue in your exploits around this area and, there are many gems waiting forvyou
extracted_spaces: The one destroyed by the French

author: WandJs
title: Nice Pagoda, but why so many mice!
original_content: If I know it has so many nice running on the lawn, I will NEVER visit this place. Why so many!! Bcs of world cup?!?!  I can not remember any thing other than the mice is big and scary. They must having a good life there.I quickly take 1 photo and run away.

author: Erica v
title: Ok pagoda poor dove
original_content: The pagoda is beautiful althouh small. 20 minutes there is enough but since it is very near to the hcm mausuleum you might as well combine the two. One of the salesmen standing outside (selling Godess of mercy memorabilia!) Keeps a dove in a tiny tiny cage. It can't even stretch it's wings. The saddest thing. This ruined my whole experience: Going to a pagoda dedicated to the Godess of mercy who is supposed to hear the cries of all sentient beings and then seeing this. I tried to buy the dove to set it free, unfortunately the man wouldn't sell it to me. Maybe if more people tell him he should not keep the poor thing like this, especially  at this temple, he might change his mind.
drawbacks: Keeping a dove in a tiny cage
Not selling the dove to set it free
highlights: Combining the pagoda with the HCM Mausoleum
practical_tips: Combine the pagoda with the HCM Mausoleum
